Amite County is in Mississippi, near Louisiana. In 2010, there were 13, 131 people living there. The county seat is Liberty. The county is named after the Amite River, which goes through it. Amite County is part of the McComb, Mississippi, micropolitan area.

The Whopper is Burger King's famous sandwich and a popular item in their Australian chain, Hungry Jack's. It was first introduced in 1957 and has changed several times, with new bread and portion sizes. Burger King calls itself "the home of the Whopper" and uses this in their ads and stores. Competitors try to make similar sandwiches to compete. Burger King sells different Whopper versions for special times or to fit local tastes. They often make limited-time Whoppers for promotions. The Whopper is a big part of Burger King's advertising and practical jokes. Burger King has registered many trademarks to protect the Whopper.

ibk sundsvall was a floorball club in sundsvall, Sweden, starting in 1986. The men's team played in Sweden's top floorball division during the 1990s. In 2006, the club joined with ibk nordic to become sundsvall city. In 1991, the club also played soccer in division 6 for men.

Vanzone con San Carlo is a municipality in the province of Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, in the Piedmont region of Italy. It is located northeast of Turin and west of Verbania. Vanzone con San Carlo borders the following municipalities: Antrona, Schieranco, Bannio Anzino, Calasca-Castiglione, and Ceppo Morelli.

Giuseppina Bozzacchi, born on November 23, 1853, was an Italian ballerina. At 16, she created the role of Swanhilda in Léo Delibes' ballet "Coppélia" while dancing for the Paris Opera Ballet. She was born in Milan and went to Paris to study with Mme Dominique. Arthur Saint-Léon, the choreographer, and Émile Perrin, the director of the Académie Royale de Musique, were looking for a suitable Swanhilda. They had chosen other dancers before but neither Léontine Beaugrand nor Angelina Fioretti was perfect. In 1868, Saint-Léon was preparing the role, but he fell ill. They asked Delibes to find a Swanhilda in Italy, but he didn't succeed. Bozzacchi was discovered in 1869 and created the role on May 25, 1870, in front of Emperor Napoleon III. She continued to perform Swanhilda for several weeks. In July, France went to war with Prussia. Bozzacchi performed Swanhilda for the last time on August 31, as the Paris Opera closed due to the war. She got sick from lack of food, contracted smallpox and fever, and died on her 17th birthday in the morning. She was buried at Cimetière de Montmartre in Paris.

Dark Souls is an action role-playing game from 2011. FromSoftware made it, and Namco Bandai Games released it. It follows in the footsteps of Demon's Souls, another FromSoftware game. Dark Souls is the second game in the Souls series. The story takes place in a made-up kingdom called Lordran. You play as a cursed, undead character on a quest to find out what will happen to your kind. A Windows version came out in August 2012, adding extra content. In October 2012, new content was also available for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 players. Dark Souls is known as one of the best video games ever. People liked how deep the fighting was, how detailed the levels were, and how the game used text to give background information. Some players found the game too hard, though. The Windows version was less popular due to some technical problems. By April 2013, over two million copies had been sold worldwide. Two more Dark Souls games came out in the middle of the 2010s, and a remastered version was released in 2018.

Three 6 Mafia is an American hip hop group from Memphis, Tennessee. They started in 1991. Initially, they made scary-themed underground rap music. Later, they became popular with mainstream audiences. Their first album, "Mystic Stylez," came out in 1995 and is considered an influential hit. They have worked with labels like Prophet Entertainment, Hypnotize Minds, Relativity, Loud, and Columbia Records. Two of their albums, "The Boss" (2000) and "Most Known Unknown" (2005), were certified platinum by the RIAA. "Most Known Unknown" also included the hit song "Stay Fly." In 2006, they won an Academy Award for best original song for "It's Hard Out Here for a Pimp," from the movie "Hustle & Flow." Their most recent studio album, "Last 2 Walk," was released in 2008. As of 2016, their total album sales worldwide were 5.5 million.

Lewis Michael Eisenberg, born on October 12, 1942, is an American financier and investor. He is the United States Ambassador to Italy. Eisenberg co-founded and led a private equity firm called Granite Capital International Group. He has worked in American political fundraising for many years and held important jobs at the national, state, and bi-state level. In 2001, he was the chairman of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which managed the World Trade Center during the September 11 attack. In July 2017, President Donald Trump nominated Eisenberg to be the United States Ambassador to Italy. He was confirmed by the U.S. Senate on August 3, 2017.

Kublai was the fifth khagan of the Mongol Empire, ruling from 1260 to 1294. He also became the first emperor of the Yuan Dynasty in China in 1271. Kublai was the fourth son of Tolui and a grandson of Genghis Khan. He took over as khagan in 1260 after his older brother Möngke. He had to fight his younger brother Ariq Böke in a civil war that lasted until 1264. This war started the disunity in the empire. Kublai ruled mainly over China and Mongolia, but he still had some influence in other parts of the empire. His realm stretched from the Pacific Ocean to the Black Sea, from Siberia to Afghanistan. In 1271, Kublai created the Yuan Dynasty, which controlled parts of present-day Mongolia, China, Korea, and nearby areas. He became China's first non-Han emperor to rule all of the country by 1279 after conquering the Song Dynasty. Kublai's imperial portrait, part of an album of Yuan emperors and empresses, is now in the National Palace Museum in Taipei. The color white, Kublai's royal color, was also the imperial color of the Yuan Dynasty.
Lisa Latrelle Blunt Rochester (born February 10, 1962) is an American politician. She has been a U.S. representative since 2017. She belongs to the Democratic Party.

The 2003 invasion of Iraq was the start of the Iraq War. This invasion began on March 19 and 20, 2003, with about 177,000 troops from the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Poland invading Iraq. It lasted for about a month, with 26 days of major fighting. The war officially ended on May 1, 2003, when President George W. Bush said the "main fighting" was over. After this, a new government called the Coalition Provisional Authority was set up. This government led to the first Iraqi election in January 2005. American forces stayed in Iraq until 2011. About 177,000 troops entered Iraq during the initial invasion, with 130,000 from the United States alone, 45,000 from the UK, 2,000 from Australia, and 194 from Poland. About 36 other countries also helped after the invasion. The invasion was to disarm Iraq of weapons of mass destruction, stop Saddam Hussein from supporting terrorism, and free the Iraqi people. Some say it was mainly because of the 9/11 attacks and the idea of spreading freedom. President Bush and UK Prime Minister Blair said Iraq failed to disarm itself of alleged nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons, seen as a threat to world peace. In a January 2003 poll, 64% of Americans supported military action against Iraq, but many wanted a diplomatic solution and feared more terrorism. Some long-time US allies, like France, Canada, Germany, and New Zealand, opposed the invasion, arguing there was no proof of weapons of mass destruction. Before the invasion, there were protests, including a huge one in Rome with 3 million people. About 36 million people worldwide joined 2,900 protests between January and April 2003. The invasion began with an air strike on Baghdad's presidential palace on March 20, followed by an advance into Basra. Special forces landed in the Persian Gulf to secure Basra, while the main army moved south. Massive air strikes confused the Iraqi army, making it harder to fight back. By March 26, the 173rd Airborne Brigade was dropped near Kirkuk and joined Kurdish rebels to secure the north. The main coalition forces moved towards Baghdad, which they occupied on April 9. Kirkuk and Tikrit were captured on April 10 and 15, respectively. Saddam Hussein and his leadership went into hiding as the coalition completed its occupation. On May 1, President Bush declared the end of major combat operations, ending the invasion and beginning the military occupation.

The South African Republic, also known as the Transvaal Republic or the Rand, was an independent country in what is now South Africa from 1852 to 1902. It won the First Boer War against the British Empire and stayed independent until the end of the Second Boer War on May 31, 1902. After losing the war, it was forced to surrender. The British used a harsh policy called "scorched earth" and set up camps where they held captured Boer women and children. Over 27,000 civilians died as a result. After the war, the land where the South African Republic was located became the Transvaal Colony. During World War I, there was a failed attempt to revive the republic in the Maritz Rebellion. Now, the area that used to be the South African Republic is mostly in the provinces of Gauteng, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, and North West in northeastern South Africa.
Farid Abedi was born on August 28, 1977, in Firouzabad. He is an Iranian football player. Currently, he plays for Bargh Shiraz in the Azadegan League.
Italy has participated in all Military World Games since the first edition in 1995.

A euphemism is a mild word or phrase used instead of one that might be offensive or uncomfortable. Some are meant to be funny, while others use simple, non-offensive words to downplay something. Euphemisms can replace bad words or talk about difficult topics like disabilities, sex, bathroom needs, or death in a polite way.

The flag of Saint Lucia has a blue background with a yellow triangle in front of a white-edged black triangle. It was adopted in 1967 to replace the British blue ensign with the colony's arms. Since Saint Lucia became an associated state of the UK that year, this has been its flag. While the design stayed the same, some parts were changed over time.

College Station is a city in Brazos County, Texas. It is located in the eastern part of the state, in the heart of the Brazos Valley, near the center of the Texas Triangle region. College Station is northwest of Houston and northeast of Austin. As of the 2010 census, the population was 93,857, which grew to an estimated 117,911 by July 2019. College Station and Bryan together form the Bryan-College Station metropolitan area, which had 273,101 people in 2019. College Station is where the main Texas A&M University campus is located. The city got its name and began because of the university's presence along a railroad. Texas A&M is a special kind of university that gets money to do many types of research from NASA, the National Institutes of Health, the National Science Foundation, and the Office of Naval Research. Due to Texas A&M, College Station was named by "Money" magazine in 2006 as the most educated city in Texas and the 11th-most educated city in the United States.
Giornico is a town in the Leventina district, which is in the canton of Ticino, Switzerland.

The governor of Vermont is the leader of the government in Vermont, United States. The person who holds this job is chosen by people voting directly every two years. Vermont and New Hampshire are the only states that have elections for their governors every two years, while other states have elections every four years. There is no limit on how many terms a Vermont governor can serve. If no one gets more than half the votes, the state legislature picks the governor. The current governor of Vermont is Phil Scott, a Republican. He became governor on January 5, 2017, and is Vermont's 82nd governor.
Great Romania, in Romanian called "România Mare," can mean:

Eino Tamberg was born on May 27, 1930, and died on December 24, 2010. He was an Estonian composer whose music is performed around the world. He wrote operas, including "Cyrano de Bergerac," four symphonies, and several concertos. For many years, he taught composition at the Estonian Academy of Music.
Jefferson County is the name of 26 counties and one parish in the United States.

An editorial, often called a leading article or leader, is written by the main editors of a newspaper or magazine. It is usually not signed. In some big US newspapers like The New York Times and The Boston Globe, editorials are grouped under "opinion." Illustrated editorials can appear as cartoons. The newspaper's editorial board decides which issues are important to discuss and expresses their opinion. Editorials are usually on a special page called the editorial page, which also includes letters from readers. The opposite page is the op-ed page, where writers not connected to the publication can share their opinions. Sometimes, an editorial can be placed on the front page for important topics. Newspapers might not name the writer of an editorial to make readers focus on the issue, but the editor, who is known, is responsible. When a New Zealand newspaper, The Press, changed from broadsheet to compact in 2018, they published editorials showing how their views had changed over time. For example, they once wrote that women preferred staying at home instead of voting. In fashion magazines, the term "editorial" refers to features with big photos on a specific theme, like a designer or model, often without text.
Blingel is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of northern France.

The Citadel Center is a 580 ft (177m) tall building in Chicago's Loop area. It is at 131 S. Dearborn St., Chicago, Illinois 60603. It was designed by Spanish architect Ricardo Bofill. As of fall 2018, it was the 57th tallest building in Chicago, and it soon became the 60th tallest. The building was completed in 2003. It has 37 floors above ground and 3 below ground, making a total of 40 floors. The building is 1,536,548 square feet large. In 2017, it was certified as LEED Gold. A special sculpture, the Winged Victory of Samothrace, was in the lobby for a while but was removed in late 2018. The original sculpture is at the Louvre Museum. The lobby previously had a curved wall made of padauk red wood. The Citadel Center was the first building in Chicago to use a raised-floor pressurized plenum system. This system helps control the climate more precisely with adjustable floor diffusers.

Balaguer is the capital of the "comarca" of Noguera, in the province of Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. It sits by the River Segre, a tributary of the Ebro. The town includes an area to the east. Balaguer was taken from the Moors by Ermengol VI of Urgell in 1106. He made it his new capital, and it stayed the capital for later counts of Urgell. The town has a Gothic bridge called "Pont de Sant Miquel" over the Segre River. This bridge was destroyed during the Spanish Civil War, in a battle called "Cap de Pont" in 1938, and was rebuilt afterward. Another Gothic building is the Santa Maria Church, located on a hill above the city. There is also a well-preserved 15th-century wall nearby. The historic part of the town is on the right side of the Segre River. After the Spanish Civil War, construction began on a modern bridge, leading to the development of a new area on the left side of the river. During the Spanish Civil War, General Franco's forces entered Catalonia through Balaguer's bridgehead in 1938.

Luke Isaac Moore, born on February 13, 1986, is an English former professional footballer who played as a striker. He represented England at the U21 level. Luke is the younger brother of Stefan Moore, who was also a professional footballer.

Percy Bysshe Shelley (4 August 1792–8 July 1822) was a major English romantic poet. He is considered one of the greatest lyric and philosophical poets in the English language. Shelley was also a radical in his poetry and political views, but he did not gain fame during his lifetime. His poetic achievements became recognized after he died. He was part of a group of visionary poets and writers that included Lord Byron, John Keats, Leigh Hunt, Thomas Love Peacock, and his second wife, Mary Shelley (the author of "Frankenstein"). Some of his well-known poems include "Ozymandias," "Ode to the West Wind," "To a Skylark," "Music, when Soft Voices Die," "The Cloud," and "The Masque of Anarchy." Other major works include the play "The Cenci" (1819), and long, visionary poems like "Queen Mab" (later renamed "The Daemon of the World"), "Alastor," "The Revolt of Islam," "Adonais," "Prometheus Unbound" (1820), "Hellas: A Lyrical Drama" (1821), and his final, unfinished work "The Triumph of Life" (1822). Shelley's close friends included progressive thinkers like his father-in-law, philosopher William Godwin (1756–1836), and Leigh Hunt (1784–1859). Most publishers refused to print his work because of the fear of arrest for blasphemy or sedition. His poetry had only a small readership during his time, but his achievements are now widely recognized. His ideas influenced important thinkers like Karl Marx, Leo Tolstoy, and Martin Luther King Jr. Shelley's poetry inspired many poets, including Robert Browning and Dante Gabriel Rossetti. His influence can be seen in the works of admirers like Oscar Wilde, Thomas Hardy, George Bernard Shaw, and others. His writings also influenced Henry David Thoreau's "Civil Disobedience." Shelley's popularity and influence continue to grow in modern poetry.
Saint-Jean-sur-Erve was a small town in the Mayenne department of Northwestern France. On January 1, 2017, it joined with another town called Blandouet to form a new town.

The Flint River is a river in Georgia, the U.S. state. It drains parts of western Georgia. The river flows south from the upper Piedmont region, below Atlanta, to the wetlands in the southwestern corner of Georgia, near the Gulf Coastal Plain. Along with the Apalachicola and Chattahoochee rivers, it forms the ACF basin. In its upper part, through the Red Hills of the Piedmont, the river is particularly scenic, flowing freely for over 100 miles. Historically, it was also known as the Thronateeska River.

drowned in sound, or dis, is a music website based in the UK. It is funded by Silentway, an artist management company. The site was created by Sean Adams. It includes reviews, news, interviews, and discussion forums.

Hydrography is the science that measures and describes the physical features of oceans, seas, coastal areas, lakes, and rivers. It also predicts how these features might change over time. The main goal is to ensure safe navigation. This science supports many other marine activities, such as economic development, security, defense, research, and protecting the environment.
lay-lamidou is a commune in Pyrénées-Atlantiques, a department in southwestern France.

The Amu Darya, also known as the Amu, Amo River, or Amudaryo, is a significant river in Central Asia and Afghanistan. It starts in the Pamir Mountains, north of the Hindu Kush. The Amu Darya is formed by the joining of the Vakhsh and Panj rivers. They meet in the Tigrovaya Balka nature reserve at the border between Afghanistan and Tajikistan. From there, it flows northwest towards the southern part of the Aral Sea. In its upper part, the river borders Afghanistan to the north with Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan. Historically, this river was seen as the boundary between greater Iran and 'Turan', which roughly covers present-day Central Asia.

Tanuja Samarth, known as Tanuja, is an Indian actress who works mainly in Hindi films. She is part of the Mukherjee-Samarth family and is the daughter of actress Shobhna Samarth and producer Kumarsen Samarth. She was married to filmmaker Shomu Mukherjee, and they have two daughters, actresses Kajol and Tanisha. Tanuja won two Filmfare Awards and is famous for roles in films like "Memdidi" (1961), "Chand Aur Suraj" (1965), "Baharen Phir Bhi Aayengi" (1966), "Jewel Thief" (1967), "Nai Roshni" (1967), "Jeene Ki Raah" (1969), "Haathi Mere Saathi" (1971), "Anubhav" (1971), "Mere Jeevan Saathi" (1972), and "Do Chor" (1972). She was popular in the late 1960s and early 1970s with actors Sanjeev Kumar, Rajesh Khanna, and Dharmendra.
The 20th century BC lasted from 2000 BC to 1901 BC.
Rebergues is a town in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in the Hauts-de-France region of France.

A structure is an arrangement and organization of parts in a thing or system, or the thing or system itself organized this way. Material structures are things like buildings and machines, as well as natural things like living things, minerals, and chemicals. Abstract structures are ideas, like how information is organized in computers or the form in music. Structures can be arranged in different ways: like a hierarchy, where parts are connected in a top-to-bottom way; a network, where parts are connected in many-to-many ways; or a lattice, where parts are connected based on their position next to each other.

Hipparchus of Nicaea, also known as Hipparchos, was a Greek astronomer, geographer, and mathematician. He is considered the founder of trigonometry and is famous for discovering the precession of the equinoxes. Born in Nicaea, now in Turkey, he probably died on the island of Rhodes, Greece. He worked as an astronomer from 162 to 127 BCE. Hipparchus is seen as the greatest ancient astronomer and one of the greatest of all time. He created models to explain the movements of the sun and moon. His work likely used techniques and observations passed down by earlier astronomers, including the Babylonians and others like Meton of Athens, Timocharis, and Eratosthenes. Hipparchus developed trigonometry and made trigonometric tables. He solved problems in spherical trigonometry and may have been the first to predict solar eclipses reliably. He also discovered and measured Earth's precession, compiled the first major star catalog, and possibly invented the astrolabe and armillary sphere, which he used for his star catalog.

In meteorology, visibility measures how far you can see an object or light clearly. This is reported in surface weather observations and METAR codes, using meters or statute miles, depending on the country. Visibility affects traffic on roads, sailing, and aviation. Meteorological visibility means how clear the air is. At night, the visibility is the same as during the day for the same air quality.
The Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium are in Brussels, Belgium. They have more than 20,000 drawings, sculptures, and paintings from the early 15th century to today.

Cara McCollum was born on February 6, 1992, and died on February 22, 2016. She was an American journalist and the main news anchor for "SNJ Today." She started working there in July 2015. She was also Miss New Jersey 2013 and competed for the Miss America 2014 title.

On November 14, 2017, parts of the Zimbabwe Defense Forces (ZDF) gathered in Harare, the capital of Zimbabwe. They took control of the Zimbabwe Broadcasting Corporation and some areas of the city. The next day, the ZDF said it was not a coup and that President Robert Mugabe was safe. They said they would only return to normal after dealing with "criminals" around Mugabe who were causing economic problems. The uprising happened because of a disagreement in Mugabe's ruling party, ZANU–PF. Former first vice-president Emmerson Mnangagwa, supported by the ZDF, was fighting against first lady Grace Mugabe, supported by the younger G40 group, over who would replace Mugabe. A week before the ZDF moved into Harare, Mnangagwa was fired and forced to leave the country. On November 19, ZANU–PF removed Mugabe as party leader, replacing him with Mnangagwa, and gave Mugabe until November 20 to resign or face impeachment. Mugabe did not resign, so on November 21, a joint session of parliament met for his impeachment. After the session, Mugabe sent a letter to parliament, resigning as president. Phelekezela Mphoko, the second vice-president, became the acting president. Mnangagwa was sworn in as president on November 24, 2017.

Diomedes, or Diomede, is a hero from Greek mythology known for fighting in the Trojan War. He was born to Tydeus and Deipyle. Later, he became the king of Argos, succeeding his maternal grandfather, Adrastus. In Homer's "Iliad," Diomedes is one of the best warriors, along with Ajax the Great and Agamemnon, after Achilles. This is especially shown in Book 7 when Diomedes, Ajax the Greater, and Agamemnon are chosen by the Achaeans to fight Hector. Diomedes also founded many cities in Italy. After his death, people in Italy and Greece worshipped him as a god under different names.

Charles Henry Scherza was born on February 15, 1923, in Brandon, Manitoba. He played ice hockey professionally for 11 seasons in the American Hockey League. In 1949, he won a Calder Cup championship with the Providence Reds. He passed away on March 16, 2014, at the age of 91.

electromagnetic hypersensitivity (EH) is claimed to be a sensitivity to electromagnetic fields. People who say they have EH say they feel bad after being exposed to these fields. However, there is no scientific proof of EH, and it is not recognized as a real medical condition. Those who say they have EH often report feeling unwell, even at very low levels of electromagnetic exposure, which is below what is considered safe. Many studies have shown that people who think they have EH cannot tell the difference between being exposed and not being exposed to electromagnetic fields. A review in 2011 found no strong scientific evidence that electromagnetic fields cause symptoms. Later studies, called double-blind experiments, showed that people who say they have EH react the same way whether they are exposed to electromagnetic fields or not. This suggests their symptoms might be caused by something other than the fields, possibly because they expect to feel bad. Some people who think they are sensitive to electromagnetic fields try to avoid exposure or use alternative medicine. Some companies that sell devices to shield against electromagnetic radiation have been told their claims are false.

Hannes Schäfer, born on October 2, 1965, in Göttingen, Germany, is a German bass guitarist, singer, and physician. He was a founding member of the German rock band Fury in the Slaughterhouse. After his musical career from 1996, Schäfer studied medicine and became a gynaecologist. He works in his own surgery in Hanover, Germany. In 1982, Schäfer was part of a punk band called "Defekt" in Hanover, where he played bass and sang. From 1985 to 1987, he was in a jazz rock band named Cit, with Mousse T. During this time, he also worked as a studio musician at Stakkato Studio Hannover. In 1987, Schäfer started the rock band Fury in the Slaughterhouse with Thorsten Wingenfelder, Kai Wingenfelder, Rainer Schumann, and Christoph Stein-Schneider in Hanover. He was the bass guitarist until 1996, when he left the band, and Christian Deker took over. Schäfer's band achieved six gold records for their albums "Fury in the Slaughterhouse" (1988), "Mono" (1992), and "The Hearing and the Sense of Balance" (1995). During this time, they sold around three million records and CDs. In 1995, they won Germany's most important musical award, the Comet, as the best rock act of the year. Schäfer played over 1,400 concerts with more than five million spectators. After the band split in 2008, he performed at their farewell concerts. On May 14, 2011, he played a concert with Fury in the Slaughterhouse in front of over 40,000 people in Hanover, celebrating Hannover 96's qualification for the UEFA Europa League. In 1996, Schäfer stopped playing music to start studying medicine. After finishing his studies, he became a gynaecologist and now works in his own surgery in Hanover, Germany.
Erin Richards, born on May 17, 1986, is a Welsh actress, director, and writer. She is famous for playing two roles: Molly Hughes in the TV show "Breaking In" and Barbara Kean in "Gotham."

Fabio Cudicini, born on October 20, 1935, is an Italian former professional goalkeeper. He played from 1955 to 1972. He was very tall, one of the tallest goalkeepers of his time. He never played for Italy's national team, but he is considered one of the best goalkeepers of his era. He is best known for his successful time at A.C. Milan, a very famous football club. He helped the club win the 1969 European Cup, among other titles. He is highly respected by A.C. Milan fans.

Hoyt Patrick "Pat" Taylor Jr. (born April 1, 1924, died April 22, 2018) was an American politician and lawyer. He worked as the speaker of the North Carolina House of Representatives and as the 26th Lieutenant Governor of North Carolina.

Igor Nikolayevich Rodionov, born on December 1, 1936, and died on December 19, 2014, was a Russian general and a Duma deputy. He was known for his strong political views and his role as the head of the Russian Federation's Defense Ministry. Rodionov served as a Soviet army officer in East Germany, Czechoslovakia, the Far East, and other areas around the world. He commanded a motor rifle regiment in the 24th motorized rifle division, known as the "Iron Division," in the Carpathian Military District from 1970 to 1973. Later, he led the 17th motor rifle division in the same district. Rodionov was the commander of the 5th Army in the Far East Military District from 1983 to 1985, and then the 40th Army in Afghanistan from 1985 to 1986. He was the first deputy chief commander of the Moscow Military District from 1986 to 1988, and then became the commander of the Transcaucasus Military District. In 1989, Rodionov was blamed for the violent suppression of demonstrations in Tbilisi during the April 9 protests, where 19 people died and hundreds were injured. He was removed from his position and assigned to the General Staff Academy, a common place for those who lost favor. However, his role as a scapegoat was questioned due to his political stance and career history. The commission investigating the incident found that Defense Minister Yazov gave orders, based on requests from local Communist party officials. Yazov and Rodionov were personal enemies, making it convenient for the Politburo to blame Rodionov. The deaths occurred because the units involved treated the event as a military operation, not corrected for the large number of protesters, and the soldiers were not trained for civil disturbances. From 1989 to 1996, Rodionov served as a People's Deputy and Head of the General Staff Academy. In 1996, President Boris Yeltsin replaced Defense Minister Pavel Grachev with Rodionov. Rodionov published many military doctrinal articles and had experience in analysis, which Grachev lacked. During Rodionov's term, political factors mainly hindered military reforms. Rodionov had ideas for reforms but believed the Cold War outlook should remain. He debated whether the military should be restructured or maintained in the Soviet style. Rodionov was dismissed because he refused to put the Defense Ministry under civilian control and had a dispute with Yuriy Baturin over military spending. Rodionov argued for more funding, while Baturin suggested making do with current spending levels. Rodionov was a member of the Duma from 1999, representing the Rodina faction, and was a member of the Committee on National Security and chairman of the Professional Union of Military Personnel. He was laid to rest at the Federal Military Memorial Cemetery in Moscow Oblast after his death.

Ravi Shankar, born as Robindro Shaunkor Chowdhury (written as Ravindra Shankar Chowdhury in Sanskrit), was born on April 7, 1920, and passed away on December 11, 2012. He was called Pandit, meaning master. He was an Indian musician who composed Hindustani classical music. He became famous for playing the sitar in the latter half of the 20th century and influenced many musicians worldwide. In 1999, he was given India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna. Shankar came from a Bengali Brahmin family in India. He started his career as a dancer, touring India and Europe with his brother Uday Shankar's dance group. In 1938, he stopped dancing to learn sitar playing from a court musician named Allauddin Khan. After finishing his studies in 1944, he worked as a composer. He made the music for Satyajit Ray's "Apu trilogy" and was the music director for All India Radio in New Delhi from 1949 to 1956. In 1956, he began performing Indian classical music in Europe and the Americas. In the 1960s, he increased the popularity of Indian classical music through teaching, performances, and his association with violinist Yehudi Menuhin and Beatles guitarist George Harrison. His influence on Harrison helped introduce Indian instruments to Western pop music in the second half of the 1960s. Shankar also wrote compositions for sitar and orchestra and continued to tour the world in the 1970s and 1980s. From 1986 to 1992, he served as a member of the Rajya Sabha, India's upper house of parliament. He kept performing until the end of his life.
Dhillon is a tribe of Jat people found among Sikhs in Punjab, India. Some famous people with the name Dhillon may or may not be part of this tribe.

Joan Mari Torrealdai Nabea was born on November 24, 1942, and died on July 31, 2020. He was a Basque writer, journalist, and sociologist. He lived in the Basque Autonomous Community in Spain. He was a member of Euskaltzaindia, which is the Royal Academy of the Basque Language.

Cosmology, from the Greek words "kosmos" meaning "world" and "-logia" meaning "study of," is a part of astronomy that looks at how the universe began and how it has changed over time. It also considers what might happen in the future. Cosmology is the scientific study of the universe's origins, its large structures, how it moves, and what might happen to it in the end. The term "cosmology" first appeared in English in 1656 in Thomas Blount's "Glossographia" and was used by German philosopher Christian Wolff in 1731 in his work "Cosmologia Generalis." Religious or mythological cosmology is based on beliefs from creation stories and end-of-the-world tales in religious and mythological texts. Physical cosmology, which is studied by scientists like astronomers and physicists, as well as philosophers like metaphysicians and philosophers of physics, can include both scientific and non-scientific ideas. Sometimes, these theories depend on assumptions that can't be tested. Cosmology focuses on the whole universe, unlike astronomy, which looks at individual stars and planets. Today, the big bang theory is the main idea in cosmology. It combines what we know about the universe from astronomy and particle physics. This theory includes dark matter and dark energy and is called the Lambda-CDM model. Cosmology is considered a "historical science" because when we look at the sky, we are looking at the past. This is because light travels at a finite speed, so the further away we look, the older the light we see.
L'Ile-Saint-Denis is a town in the northern part of Paris, France. It is near the center of Paris. The town is on an island in the Seine River, which is why it is called Ile-Saint-Denis.

El Paso County is one of Colorado's 64 counties. In 2010, it had 622, 263 people. It is the second-largest county in Colorado, after Denver. The county seat is Colorado Springs, which is the second-largest city in Colorado. El Paso County is part of the Colorado Springs metropolitan area. Since 1871, El Paso County has usually voted for the Republican presidential candidate. The last Democrat to win was Lyndon B. Johnson in 1964. Democrats also won four times before, and the Populist Party won in 1892. In 2004, Colorado Springs and El Paso County voters created the Pikes Peak Rural Transportation Authority (PPRTA) and started a 1% sales tax to improve transportation. This, along with state funding for projects like Cosmix in 2007 and the I-25 interchange with Highway 16 in 2008, has improved transportation in the area. In 2012, El Paso County voters legalized marijuana. On March 12, 2019, the county voted to become a Second Amendment sanctuary.
Hand County is in South Dakota, a state in the U.S. In 2010, the population was 3,431. The county seat is Miller.
Mary Ann Mobley was born on February 17, 1937, and passed away on December 9, 2014. She was an American actress and television personality. In 1959, she won Miss America.

Mallory Hagan was born on December 23, 1988. She is an American politician who used to be a beauty queen. She won Miss America 2013 when she was Miss New York in 2012. In 2008, she moved to New York after her first year at Auburn University. Before Miss America, she was Miss Brooklyn in 2010, Miss Manhattan in 2011, and Miss New York City in 2012. She was also a two-time Miss New York first runner-up. When she lived in Alabama, she was the runner-up in the Miss Alabama's Outstanding Teen program. As Miss Chattahoochee Valley in 2007, she was a non-finalist talent winner at Miss Alabama. She won the Miss America competition because she talked about child sexual abuse, which her family experienced. She also talked about gun control, saying she didn't think fighting violence with violence was a good idea. In 2018, she ran for a job in Congress as a Democrat for Alabama's 3rd district, which includes her hometown, Opelika.

Irony is a way of saying something that seems different from what you really mean. It can be divided into three main types: verbal, dramatic, and situational irony. People often use these types of irony to make a point more strongly. In sarcasm, you might say the opposite of what you mean to make a stronger statement. Other forms of irony include dialectic and practical irony.

Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne is an expansion for a real-time strategy video game by Blizzard Entertainment. It was released on July 1, 2003, for Microsoft Windows and Mac OS X. The expansion continues the story from "Reign of Chaos" and shows events after the main game. It features two new heroes, Maiev Shadowsong and Kael'thas, and the returning hero Arthas. It also includes a separate orc campaign released in December 2003 in three parts. The expansion adds new units, buildings, and heroes for each faction, introduces two new races, and includes five neutral heroes, with more added later. It also improves gameplay and has new maps and scenarios. Sea units return after being missing in "Reign of Chaos." Multiplayer features include clans, tournaments, and new maps. Development began in October 2002, after the main game release, and was announced in January 2003. Public beta tests allowed 20,000 players to try new features. Blizzard continues to update the game with new content and hardware support. Critics mostly praised the single-player campaign and new units, though some criticized the graphics and voice-acting. By August 15, 2003, it had sold over one million copies.

Tom Adams was an English actor born on March 9, 1938, and he died on December 11, 2014. He acted in adventure, horror, and mystery films and also appeared in several TV shows. He is best known for playing Daniel Fogarty in "The Onedin Line" series.
Saint-Gervais-en-Belin is a town in Sarthe, which is in Pays-de-la-Loire, a region in northwestern France.

Wood fuel, such as firewood, charcoal, chips, and pellets, is used as a source of energy. The type used depends on factors like where it comes from, how much there is, its quality, and how it will be used. In many places, wood is the easiest fuel to find. You can pick up dead wood without any tools, or you might need a few simple tools. Special machines like skidders and wood splitters can help make the process faster. Wood waste from sawmills and construction sites can also be used. Making fire was one of the most important discoveries for humans. People have been using wood for heating since before civilization began. Today, burning wood is the biggest way we use solid plant material for energy. Wood fuel can be used for cooking, keeping warm, and even powering large machines like steam engines and turbines that generate electricity. You can use wood indoors in stoves or fireplaces, or outdoors in campfires or bonfires.
Daluis is a town in the Alpes-Maritimes area of southeastern France. It is at the end of the Gorges de Daluis and sits by the River Var.

Villedieu is a town in Vaucluse, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region of southeastern France. A local story says that people asked Alice Colonieu to make a statue of the Virgin Mary and place it on the back of a house in Villedieu. This statue, in the Renaissance style and decorated with a king scallop, is known as the "Virgin of the Smile" and can still be seen in Villedieu today.
Abdulhussain Abdulredha was a Kuwaiti actor. He was born on July 15, 1939, and died on August 11, 2017.
Lenox is a city in Taylor and Adams counties, in the state of Iowa. The population was 1,407 in the 2010 census.

The Ontario New Democratic Party (ONDP or NDP) is a social-democratic political party in Ontario, Canada. Led by Andrea Horwath since March 2009, the ONDP is currently the official opposition in Ontario after the 2018 general election. It is part of the federal New Democratic Party. The ONDP was formed in October 1961 from the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation (Ontario section) (Ontario CCF) and the Ontario Federation of Labour (OFL). For many years, it was the most successful provincial NDP branch outside the party's western area. Donald C. MacDonald was its first leader. Under him, the party elected 20 members of provincial parliament (MPPs) to the Ontario Legislative Assembly in the 1967 provincial election. After a leadership change in 1970, Stephen Lewis became the new leader. He helped the party become the official opposition in 1975, the first time since the Ontario CCF did so in the 1940s. Following a poor performance in the 1977 provincial election, Michael Cassidy took over as leader in 1978. However, the party did poorly again in 1981, and Cassidy stepped down. Bob Rae became the leader in 1982. In 1985, under his leadership, the party had an accord with the Liberal minority government. After the 1987 election, the ONDP became the official opposition again. In 1990, surprisingly, the ONDP won its first government, becoming the first NDP provincial government east of Manitoba. However, the party was defeated in 1995 due to unpopular policies, and Rae resigned. Howard Hampton became the leader in 1996. He led the party through three elections. The ONDP lost official party status after the 1999 and 2003 elections. Hampton regained party status after the 2003 election due to a change in the rules and winning a series of by-elections in the mid-2000s. The party kept its status after the 2007 election, and Hampton stepped down as leader in 2009. Andrea Horwath took over as leader after being elected at the 2009 convention. Under her leadership, the party won 17 seats in the 2011 election and 21 seats in the 2014 election. Horwath led the party to become the official opposition with 40 seats after the 2018 election.

Carlos Rojas Hernández, known as Carlos "Cuco" Rojas, was born on March 28, 1954, in San Martín, Meta. He was a Colombian harpist and songwriter of joropo music. He directed the Colombian band Cimarron. He passed away on January 10, 2020.

Hans von Borsody was a German film actor born on September 20, 1929, in Vienna. He came from a family with Hungarian roots and was involved in the arts. His father, Eduard, was a film director, and his uncle, Julius, was a set designer. His daughter, Suzanne, is also an actress. When Hans was three, his family moved to Berlin, and he became a German citizen. He was married four times to Karin Dittmann, Rosemarie Fendel, Alwy Becker, and Heide Keller.

Kiel is the capital and biggest city in Schleswig-Holstein, a northern state in Germany. It had about 249,000 people in 2016. Kiel is north of Hamburg. Because it's in the northern part of Germany, near the Jutland peninsula and the Baltic Sea, Kiel is a big maritime city. It hosts international sailing events like the Kiel Week, which is the largest sailing event globally. Kiel is also famous for a World War I event called the Kiel Mutiny, where sailors refused to board ships to protest fighting. This led to the end of the Kaiser and the start of the Weimar Republic. The city also hosted Olympic sailing events in 1936 and 1972. Kiel is a key shipbuilding and technology center. It has the Geomar-Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research. Kiel is a major sea transport hub thanks to its location on the Kiel Fjord and the Kiel Canal, the busiest artificial waterway in the world. Many ferry services leave from Kiel. Today, it's a popular stop for Baltic Sea cruises. Kiel's history dates back to the 13th century and was originally a Danish village. It became part of Germany in 1871. Kiel was one of the first cities to join the European Green City Award in 2006. In 2005, its average income per person was much higher than the German and European Union averages.

Armungia is a municipality in the province of South Sardinia, which is in Italy. Sardinia is an Italian region. Armungia is near Cagliari. It borders Ballao, San Nicolò Gerrei, Villaputzu, and Villasalto.

The Avenger is the second full-length album by the Swedish death metal band Amon Amarth. It was released on September 2, 1999, by Metal Blade Records. This album included guitarist Johan Söderberg and drummer Fredrik Andersson for the first time. Andersson had left the band before, but this lineup stayed until 2015. The album came in a digipak version with a bonus track, "Thor Arise," which was a re-recording of the title track from their first demo. It was also released as a vinyl album. Later, in 2005, Metal Blade re-released the album on picture vinyl, limited to 500 copies. In 2009, a deluxe edition was released, featuring a remastered version of the album and a bonus CD of the album played live in Bochum, Germany.

Saat bhai champa and sat bhai chompa are popular folk tales from the Bengal region in eastern India. These stories were first published in 1907 by Dakshinaranjan Mitra Majumder in a book called Thakurmar Jhuli. The book's introduction was written by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore. In 1944, Bishnu Dey published a longer version of the story as "Sat Bhai Champa." Several Bengali movies were made based on these tales. The 1968 movie Sat Bhai Chompa is considered one of the top ten films ever made in Bangladesh by the British Film Institute.

Demetria Dyan McKinney, born on August 27, 1979, is an American actress and singer-songwriter. She was in a TV show called "Tyler Perry's House of Payne" from 2006 to 2012. In 2020, there was talk about bringing the show back. She was also in another TV show called "The Ricky Smiley Show" and played regular roles in "Saints & Sinners" on Bounce TV and "Superstition" on Syfy. She acted as Coretta Scott King in an opera called "I Dream" in 2010 and as Deena Jones in "Dreamgirls" in 2012. In 2017, she acted as Whitney Houston in a TV movie called "Bobbi Kristina" and released her first album "Officially Yours" that same year.

Tropical storm Cristobal was a weak storm that moved slowly in the Atlantic Ocean. It formed on August 5 near South Carolina. This storm was the third named storm of the 2002 Atlantic hurricane season. At its strongest, it had winds of 50 mph. By August 8, it no longer had the characteristics of a tropical storm. Its remains brought some rain to Bermuda. The storm combined with a high-pressure system and caused three drownings on Long Island due to strong currents.

The maize weevil, also called the greater rice weevil, is a type of beetle. It lives in many tropical places around the world and in the United States. This beetle is a big problem for maize crops. It eats maize in the fields and in storage. It also damages other crops like wheat, rice, sorghum, oats, barley, rye, buckwheat, peas, and cottonseed. The maize weevil can also attack processed foods such as pasta, cassava, and grains. Sometimes, it even eats stored fruit like apples.
Villeneuve-sur-Fère is a village in Aisne, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in northern France.

Gustav Metzger was born on April 10, 1926, in Nuremberg and died on March 1, 2017, in London. He was an artist and a political activist. Metzger created the idea of auto-destructive art and the art strike. He worked with John Sharkey to start the Destruction in Art Symposium in 1966. Metzger was known for his protests in both politics and art.
Gido Kokars was born on August 16, 1921, and died on March 10, 2017. He was a conductor from Latvia. His twin brother, Imants Kokars, was also a conductor.
Suvarna Sahakari Bank was a private cooperative bank in India. It was in Pune, Maharashtra. The bank started in 1969 and ended in 2009.

Fiorello Henry La Guardia, born Fiorello Enrico La Guardia on December 11, 1882, and died on September 20, 1947, was an American politician. He served as the 99th mayor of New York City from 1934 to 1945, winning three terms. La Guardia was a pro-New Deal liberal progressive Republican. Before becoming mayor, he was elected to Congress in 1916, 1918, and from 1922 to 1930. Short and energetic, La Guardia loved attention. He was one of the greatest mayors in American history. Standing only 5 feet 2 inches (1.57 meters) tall, he was nicknamed "The Little Flower." A Republican who could appeal to many, La Guardia was very popular in New York during the 1930s. He supported President Franklin D. Roosevelt, a Democrat, and Roosevelt helped fund the city and took away jobs from La Guardia's enemies. La Guardia improved New York City. He made the city more fair and clean. He unified the transit system, built low-cost housing, created public playgrounds and parks, and constructed airports. He reorganized the police and fought against the powerful Tammany Hall political group. He also stopped using jobs as favors and started hiring people based on merit. La Guardia hosted a radio show called "Talk to the People" from 1941 to 1945. Known as a strong leader, La Guardia helped New York during the Great Depression and World War II. He supported immigrants and ethnic minorities and was backed by President Roosevelt. He was a mayor who cleaned up corruption, brought in experts, and made the city focus on its citizens. His work opened up new groups to politics, gave New York modern infrastructure, and raised hopes for the city.

Sobek, also known as Sebek, was an ancient Egyptian god with a changing nature. He was linked to the Nile crocodile or the West African crocodile and could be shown as the animal itself or as a human with a crocodile head. Sobek was connected to the power of pharaohs, fertility, and being brave in battle. He was also a protective god, used to keep people safe from the dangers of the Nile.

Charlotte -Jeanne Béraud de la Haye de Riou, born on October 4, 1738, and died on February 6, 1806, was a mistress of Louis Philippe d'Orléans, who was the Duke of Orléans. Later, she became his wife. However, Louis XV would not allow her to be called the Duchess. She wrote and acted in some plays. She is known simply as Madame de Montesson.

VHF omni-directional range (VOR) is a radio navigation system for planes. It helps aircraft find their position and stay on course by receiving signals from ground stations. VOR uses frequencies between 108.00 and 117.95 MHz. Developed in the U.S. starting in 1937 and widely used by 1946, VOR is the main air navigation system globally. By 2000, about 3,000 VOR stations were operating worldwide, with 1,033 in the U.S., decreasing to 967 by 2013 (as GPS became more common). A VOR ground station sends a rotating signal that points north and a fixed reference signal. The difference in signal timing shows the plane's direction from the station, called a "radial." Using two VOR stations, pilots can find their exact position. VOR signals travel line-of-sight and are effective up to 200 miles. Each station broadcasts a VHF signal with navigation, station ID, and voice (if available). The navigation signal helps determine the plane's direction from the station. Station IDs are usually three-letter codes in Morse code. Voice signals can include station names, flight advisories, or live broadcasts.

A cave or cavern is a natural space underground big enough for a person to enter. These spaces often form due to weathering of rock and can go very deep. The term "cave" can also refer to smaller openings like sea caves, rock shelters, or grottos. However, strictly speaking, a cave is deeper than its opening, while a rock shelter is the opposite. Exploring and studying caves is called speleology. Visiting or exploring caves for fun can be called caving, potholing, or spelunking.

The Chevrolet Trax is a small crossover SUV made by Chevrolet since 2013. It is built on the GM Gamma II platform. This platform is also used for the Chevrolet Aveo/Sonic and the Opel Mokka/Buick Encore.

Lev Semyonovich Vygotsky (June 11, 1896 – June 11, 1934) was a Soviet psychologist known for studying how children develop psychologically. He wrote about many topics and his views changed over time. One of his students was Alexander Luria. Vygotsky is famous for his idea of the "zone of proximal development" (ZPD). This is the difference between what a child can do alone and what they can achieve with help from someone more experienced. Vygotsky saw the ZPD as a way to measure skills a child is developing, along with measures that only look at a child's independent abilities. He also wrote about how language and thought are related, how language develops, and a general theory of development through social interactions. There is disagreement among scholars about Vygotsky's work, with some seeing parts of his legacy as distortions and trying to return to his original manuscripts to better reflect his ideas.

Giovanni Boccaccio, born on June 16, 1313, and died on December 21, 1375, was an Italian writer and poet. He was a friend of Petrarch and an important Renaissance humanist. Boccaccio wrote famous works like "The Decameron" and "On Famous Women." He mostly wrote imaginary stories in the Tuscan language, also called the vernacular, and wrote other works in Latin. Boccaccio was known for his realistic dialogue, different from the usual formulas used by other medieval writers.

A Roman legion was a large military group in the Roman army. It was like a small army within the larger army. In the early times, it had about 4,200 foot soldiers and 300 horse soldiers. Later, during the Roman Empire, it grew to have around 5,200 foot soldiers and 120 supporting soldiers.

Bombardier Transportation is a German company and part of Bombardier Inc. It makes and services rail vehicles. Based in Berlin, it has offices and factories all over the world. They produce passenger trains, locomotives, and parts like bogies and propulsion systems. In February 2020, the company had 36,000 workers in 63 locations worldwide.

Glenn "Swampy" Brydson was born on November 7, 1910, and died on December 9, 1993. He was a Canadian ice hockey player who played as a right winger. He played eight seasons in the NHL from 1930 to 1938 for the Montreal Maroons, St. Louis Eagles, New York Rangers, and Chicago Black Hawks. After leaving the NHL, Brydson played five seasons in the International American Hockey League, which later became the American Hockey League. He played for the New Haven Eagles, Indianapolis Capitals, Springfield Indians, and Pittsburgh Hornets. He played senior hockey for a short time before retiring in 1942. Brydson is buried at Park Lawn Cemetery in Toronto.

Meadowbank Stadium, officially called Meadowbank Sports Centre, was a sports place in Edinburgh, Scotland. It replaced the earlier New Meadowbank and Old Meadowbank sports venues. Built for the 1970 Commonwealth Games, it hosted the games again in 1986, making it the first venue to do so twice. The stadium also hosted football matches regularly. From 1974 to 1995, Meadowbank Thistle, a Scottish football league team, played there. After 1996, Edinburgh City, a non-league team, played there. In 2016, Edinburgh City moved back to the stadium after joining the Scottish Professional Football League. The Meadowbank complex also hosted Leith Athletic on the adjacent 3G artificial pitch since 2013. In early 2019, the stadium was demolished to build a new one. Meadowbank Stadium was also used for rugby, hosting Edinburgh Rugby from 2002 to 2004.

Fernando Sebastián Aguilar CMF was a Spanish cardinal in the Roman Catholic Church. He was also the Archbishop Emeritus of Pamplona y Tudela. Pope Francis made him a cardinal on February 22, 2014. He was born on December 14, 1929, and died on January 24, 2019.

Janet Gray Hayes was born on July 12, 1926, in Rushville, Indiana. She later earned her bachelor's degree from Indiana University and attended the University of Chicago. In 1956, Hayes and her husband moved to San Jose, California, where her husband worked as a doctor. Hayes became a city council member in 1971 and was a Democrat. She was elected as the 60th mayor of San Jose in 1975 and served two four-year terms until 1983. Hayes was the first woman to be elected mayor in San Jose and the first woman elected mayor in a major U.S. city with over 500,000 people. She passed away on April 26, 2014, in Saratoga, California, due to a stroke.

Egg donation is when a woman gives her eggs to help another woman have a baby as part of special fertility treatments. For these treatments, doctors use a lab to fertilize the eggs. Sometimes, they freeze unfertilized eggs for later use. This is called third-party reproduction using assisted reproductive technology. In the U.S., the American Society for Reproductive Medicine has made rules for this. The Food and Drug Administration also has guidelines. Similar regulations exist in other countries. However, egg donation agencies in the U.S. can choose to follow these rules or not.

This is a list of important people from Afghanistan. It includes people from different groups in the country. Afghanistan's borders have changed over time. This list usually does not include Pashtuns whose origins are from areas not controlled by Afghanistan at certain times, but there are exceptions for some well-known Pashtuns. It also includes historical figures from within today's Afghanistan, even if they were not Pashtuns. One example is Faridoon Angar.
This article lists cities in Jordan.
farschweiler is a town in the trier-saarburg district. It is located in rhineland-palatinate, Germany.
Feldbrunnen-St. Niklaus is a municipality in the Lebern district of the Solothurn canton in Switzerland.

Nathaniel Dwayne Hale, known as Nate Dogg, was an American singer and rapper who lived from August 19, 1969, to March 15, 2011. He had smooth vocals and wrote hooks for many rap songs, especially during the g-funk era in the 1990s. Nate was part of a trio called 213 with Snoop Dogg and Warren G. After Snoop joined Death Row Records, Nate worked with Dr. Dre on his album "The Chronic" and Snoop's album "Doggystyle." Nate's biggest success came in 1994 with his song "Regulate," which he wrote with Warren G. The song was very popular and reached number two on the Billboard charts. As a featured artist, Nate appeared on 16 songs that reached the Billboard top 100, and in 2003, his voice helped 50 Cent's song "21 Questions" reach number one. In 2007, Nate had two strokes. The first one made his left side weaker, but he could still think and talk. Several months later, he had another stroke. Sadly, Nate died of a heart problem in 2011 at the age of 41.
Inō Tadataka, born on February 11, 1745, and died on May 17, 1818, was a Japanese surveyor and mapmaker. He is famous for making the first map of Japan using new surveying methods.

Hevrin Khalaf, also known as Khelef, was born on November 15, 1984, and died on October 12, 2019. She was a Kurdish-Syrian politician and civil engineer. Khalaf worked in Rojava for many years and then became the secretary general of the Future Syria Party. She was killed by Turkish-backed Ahrar al-Sharqiya fighters near the M4 motorway, south of Tell Abbyad, during the 2019 Turkish offensive into northeastern Syria.

Clarke County is in the northeastern part of Georgia, U.S. In 2010, it had 116, 714 people. Athens is both the county seat and part of the county. Clarke County is part of the Athens-Clarke County metropolitan area, which is also part of the Atlanta-Athens-Clarke County-Sandy Springs combined area.
Sant'Antonio means Saint Anthony in Italian. It usually refers to places named after Saint Anthony of Padua or Saint Anthony Abbot.

Popeye the sailor is a fictional muscular character from an American cartoon. He first appeared in a comic strip called "Thimble Theatre" on January 17, 1929. Popeye became the main focus of the strip in later years. The strip was created by Elzie Crisler Segar and continued by Bud Sagendorf after Segar's death. Today, it is written and drawn by Hy Eisman. Popeye also appeared in cartoon shorts. In 1933, Max Fleischer made the first "Popeye the Sailor" cartoons for Paramount Pictures. These cartoons were very popular and continued until 1957. The cartoons are now owned by Turner Entertainment and distributed by Warner Bros. Popeye has appeared in comic books, TV shows, video games, and advertisements. He has also been in products like spinach and candy cigarettes, and in a 1980 live-action film directed by Robert Altman, with Robin Williams playing Popeye. People think Popeye is a great cartoon character. In 2002, TV Guide ranked him number 20 on their list of the 50 greatest cartoon characters of all time.

Stickney Township is one of 29 townships in Cook County, Illinois, USA. As of the 2010 census, it had 40,772 people. About 71% of these live in the city of Burbank, which has a population of 28,925. The township offices are at 5635 W. State Road in Burbank. Other areas in the township are Stickney, which has about 6,786 people, and Forest View, which has around 698. There are also parts of Bedford Park in the eastern half, as well as some small areas of Bridgeview. Unincorporated communities like Central Stickney and Nottingham Park are also in Stickney Township. The township borders Pershing Road (39th Street) to the north, Cicero Avenue to the east, 87th Street to the south, and Harlem Avenue to the west. It does not include parts of Chicago communities called Garfield Ridge and Clearing, which include Chicago Midway International Airport. However, it does include the area between Laramie and Cicero Avenues up to 35th Street.

The Yalobusha River is a river in north-central Mississippi, United States. It is a main part of the Yazoo River, which connects it to the Mississippi River. The name "Yalobusha" comes from the Choctaw language, meaning "little tadpole." The United States Board on Geographic Names chose this name in 1892. The river has also been called "Yallabusha" and "Yellowbushy River."

A dog of Flanders is a 1872 book by an English writer named Marie Louise de la Ramée, who used a made-up name "Ouida" to publish it. The story is about a Flemish boy called Nello and his dog Patrasche, set in Antwerp. In Japan, Korea, and the Philippines, this book is a beloved children's story for many years. It has been turned into several Japanese movies and cartoons. Starting in the 1980s, the Belgian tourism board noticed this popularity and created two statues to make visitors happy. One statue can be found near a church in a town called Hoboken, and another one is in front of a big church in Antwerp, given by a company called Toyota. Later, a new statue of Nello and Patrasche was put there, covered by small stones.

LVMH Moët Hennessy - Louis Vuitton SE, also known as LVMH, is a big French company based in Paris. It was created in 1987 by combining two famous brands: Louis Vuitton, founded in 1854, and Moët Hennessy. The latter was formed in 1971 after two companies merged: Moët & Chandon, a champagne maker, and Hennessy, a cognac maker. LVMH controls about 60 smaller companies that manage well-known brands. These smaller companies work under six main groups: fashion, wines and spirits, perfumes and cosmetics, watches and jewelry, selective distribution, and other activities. The oldest brand in LVMH is the wine producer Château d'Yquem, which has been around since 1593.

Ross Batty, born on September 20, 1986, in England, used to go to Barnard Castle School. He plays rugby union and is a hooker. Currently, he plays for Bath in the Aviva Premiership. Batty joined Bath from Rotherham in 2010 and has often played in the scrum. He celebrated his 150th game for Bath on February 2, 2018, including cup matches. On April 25, 2019, Batty signed a new contract with Bath. The length of the contract was not disclosed. Batty had played for Bath for nine seasons by the end of the 2018-2019 season.

Bastendorf is a small town in Tandel, which is in north-eastern Luxembourg. The town has 371 people. Until January 1, 2006, Bastendorf was its own commune in the canton of Diekirch. On that date, it joined Fouhren to form the new commune of Tandel, which is in Vianden. The law to create Tandel was passed on December 21, 2004.

Karnes County is in Texas, a state in the U.S. The 2010 census showed the population was 14, 824. The county seat is Karnes City. The county is named after Henry Karnes, a soldier in the Texas Revolution. A railway used to go through Karnes County, connecting San Antonio to Corpus Christi.
corpe is a town in the Vendée department, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of western France.

Sir Run Run Shaw, born in 1907 and died in 2014, was known as Shao Yifu and Siu Yat-fu. He was a big boss in Hong Kong's entertainment business and helped many people. He was one of the most important people in Asia's movie and TV industry. He started Shaw Brothers Studio, a large movie company in Hong Kong, and TVB, a main TV company in Hong Kong. As a kind man, Shaw gave lots of money to schools in Hong Kong and mainland China. Over 5,000 buildings in Chinese colleges are named after him. He also created the Shaw Prize for astronomy, life science and medicine, and mathematical sciences.
Ōshima, Oshima, Ōshima, or Ohshima can mean the same thing.

Swisscom AG is a big telecommunications company in Switzerland. Its main office is in Worblaufen, near Bern. The Swiss government owns 51% of Swisscom AG. According to their own data, Swisscom has 60% of the mobile market, 67% of the broadband market, and 33% of the TV market in Switzerland. Their Italian subsidiary, Fastweb, has 16% of private clients and 29% of corporate clients for broadband in Italy, and is also in the mobile business. Switzerland started its telegraph network in 1852, followed by telephones in 1877. These networks were joined with the postal service in 1920 to form PTT (Postal, Telegraph, and Telephone). Swisscom had trouble making its own digital network. The first digital exchange was launched in 1986, but they were pioneers in the mobile service Natel in 1978 and the GSM-based Natel D in 1993. In 1997, Swisscom was separated from the postal service and rebranded as Swisscom. The Swiss government now owns 51% of Swisscom. Swisscom also owns the protected brand Natel, known only in Switzerland. In 2001, they sold 25% of Swisscom Mobile to Vodafone. Swisscom bought a majority stake in Italy's second-largest telecom company, Fastweb, and invested in areas like hotel support, cloud services, and billing. New digital and IT services are being developed to replace potential losses from traditional businesses.

k's choice is a Belgian rock band from Antwerp. They formed in the mid-1990s. The main members are Sam Bettens and Gert Bettens, who are brothers. Sam sings and plays guitar. Gert plays guitar and keyboard, and also sings. Bart Van Lierde plays bass. Tom Lodewyckx plays lead guitar. Reinout Swinnen plays keyboard. Wim Van Der Westen plays drums. The band has made albums that sold a lot.

Abdullah Hamid Ali Al-Hamid, also known as Abu Bilal, was a Saudi poet, Arabic professor, and human rights activist. He co-founded the Saudi Civil and Political Rights Association (ACPRA). He was imprisoned several times for asking for a constitutional monarchy in Saudi Arabia. In May 2005, Dr. Abdullah Al-Hamid was put in prison for seven years for saying he disagreed with the ruler and called for changes. He was set free on August 8, 2005. In 2008, he spent four months in jail for supporting women who were protesting the arrest of their family members. The women's protest was outside Buraidah prison, in central Saudi Arabia. At times, protests by members of the Shiite minority in Saudi Arabia's eastern region turned violent. In 2018, Al-Hamid was given the Right Livelihood Award, along with other imprisoned activists and Waleed Abulkhair, for their brave and hopeful work to change Saudi Arabia's political system based on human rights.

Observation means actively gathering information from a primary source. In living beings, it uses senses. In science, it also means using tools to see and record data. This term can include any data collected during science. Observations can be qualitative, noting only if a property is present or not. They can also be quantitative, giving a number by counting or measuring.
