UK garage, or ukg, is a type of electronic music that started in England in the early 1990s. It mixes styles like garage house, R&B, jungle, and dance-pop. UK garage has a rhythm with shuffled beats and syncopated hi-hats, cymbals, and snares. Sometimes, it also has unusual kick drum patterns. Vocals in these songs are often chopped up and mixed to fit the rhythm. The tempo is usually around 130 beats per minute. UK garage led to subgenres like speed garage and 2-step. By the mid-2000s, it changed into styles like bassline, grime, and dubstep. During this time, UK garage's popularity decreased, and UK funky emerged, closely related to it.
Fowler is a town in Center Township, Benton County, Indiana, United States. According to the 2010 census, the population was 2,317. It is part of the Lafayette, Indiana metropolitan area.
Oppens is a municipality in Gros-de-Vaud district, which is in the canton of Vaud in Switzerland.

Louis Antoine Godey was born on June 6, 1804, and died on November 29, 1878. He was an American editor and publisher. He founded "Godey's Lady's Book," which was the first successful American women's fashion magazine.

Mikhail Alexandrovich Bakunin (born in 1814, died on July 1, 1876) was a Russian revolutionary and anarchist. He is known as one of the most important figures in anarchism and a key founder of the social anarchist tradition. Bakunin was very famous as an activist in Europe, influencing many radical people in Russia and other parts of Europe. Bakunin grew up in Pryamukhino, a family estate in Tver Governorate. From 1840, he studied in Moscow and later in Berlin, hoping to become a teacher. In Paris, he met Karl Marx and Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, who greatly influenced him. His increasing radical ideas made it impossible for him to become a professor. He was expelled from France for opposing Russia's occupation of Poland. In 1849, he was arrested in Dresden for taking part in the Czech rebellion of 1848 and was sent to Russia. There, he was imprisoned in Saint Petersburg and later in the Schlisselburg fortress from 1854. He was exiled to Siberia in 1857 and escaped via Japan to the United States. From there, he moved to London, where he worked with Alexander Herzen on the journal "Kolokol" (The Bell). In 1863, Bakunin went to Poland to join an uprising but failed to join. Instead, he spent time in Switzerland and Italy. In 1868, he joined the International Workingmen's Association, leading an anarchist group that grew quickly in influence. The 1872 Hague congress was mainly about a fight between Bakunin and Marx. Bakunin and his group argued for a stateless society, while Marx wanted to use the state to bring about socialism. Bakunin could not attend the congress, and his group lost the debate. Bakunin was later kicked out of the association for setting up a secret organization within it. From 1870 until his death, Bakunin wrote several important works, including "Statism and Anarchy" and "God and the State." He continued to be involved in European worker and peasant movements. In 1870, he joined an uprising in Lyon, France. He planned to join an anarchist uprising in Bologna, Italy, but his poor health forced him to return to Switzerland in disguise. Bakunin is remembered as a major figure in the history of anarchism and as an opponent of Marxism, especially the dictatorship of the proletariat. He predicted that Marxist regimes would be one-party dictatorships over the proletariat, not by the proletariat. His book "God and the State" is still widely read. Bakunin has influenced many thinkers, including Noam Chomsky, and continues to be important to anarchists.

The Parliament of Albania, or Kuvendi, is the main group of people who make laws for Albania. It has 140 or more members who are chosen by all citizens in elections. The head of this group is called the Speaker, with a Deputy Speaker helping them. Members use a party-list system to be chosen. The Parliament can change Albania's borders or constitution, make all laws, approve the government, watch over the work of the government, declare war, stop wars, approve budgets, and check the government's accounts. They can also call referendums, perform elections and appointments as required, and forgive criminal offenses. The Parliament also picks the President of Albania. After elections, the first meeting is held within 20 days, with the President as the Speaker. All laws passed by the Parliament are published in the Official Journal of Albania. The oldest Parliament with records was in Lezhë in 1444. This group, called the League of Lezhë, was formed there by Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeu to fight against the Ottoman Empire.
Leslie Orgel, a British chemist, was born on January 12, 1927, and died on October 27, 2007. He is famous for his ideas about how life began.
pittefaux is a commune in the pas-de-calais department, which is in the hauts-de-france region of France.

Tapioca is a starch from the cassava plant, also known as manioc. This plant is native to Brazil's north and central-west regions. It spread to South America, and was taken by Portuguese and Spanish colonizers to the West Indies, Africa, and Asia. Cassava is a perennial shrub that grows well in tropical areas. It can survive in poor soils better than many other crops. Tapioca is a staple food for millions in tropical regions, but it mainly provides carbohydrates and lacks protein, vitamins, and minerals. In other places, tapioca is used as a thickener in foods.
Flavio Bucci was born on May 25, 1947, and died on February 18, 2020. He was an Italian actor, voice actor, and film producer.
Zoran "Bata" Mirković, born on September 21, 1971, is a retired Serbian football player and current manager.
Carhaix-Plouguer is a commune in Finistère, in Western Brittany, France.
Shadow Hills is a neighborhood in the Verdugo Mountains and the northeastern part of San Fernando Valley, in Los Angeles, California.

""With My Own Eyes" is a song by the German group Sash!. It came out on September 4, 2000, as the third single from their third album "Trilenium." Finnish singer Inka Auhagen sang on the song. It was popular in several European countries and reached number 10 on the UK singles chart. This was Sash!'s last top 10 hit on the UK chart until 2008.

"Just a Girl" is a song by American band No Doubt from their album "Tragic Kingdom," released in 1995. It came out as the first single on September 21, 1995. Gwen Stefani and Tom Dumont wrote it, and Matthew Wilder produced it. The song is on their 2003 greatest hits album, "The Singles 1992–2003." The song is about Stefani's life as a woman and her struggles with strict parents. It was the first song she wrote without her brother Eric's help. Critics liked the song because of its strong message and Stefani's singing. "Just a Girl" was a big hit for No Doubt, reaching number 23 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States. It was also popular in other countries like Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, Norway, Scotland, and the United Kingdom. The music video shows Stefani singing in a clean bathroom while the male band members play instruments in a dirty one, separated by a wall. Eventually, they climb over to the ladies' bathroom and start dancing. Stefani wore a popular outfit in the video that people talked about. No Doubt and Stefani have performed "Just a Girl" in many concerts. They played it during their "Tragic Kingdom World Tour" from 1995 to 1997, during part of the 2002 "Rock Steady Tour," and as the encore in the 2016 "This Is What the Truth Feels Like" tour. Stefani named her 2018–2020 Las Vegas concert after the song. It has been covered and sampled by other musicians too.

The anus is an opening at the end of an animal's digestive system, opposite to the mouth. Its main job is to let out feces, which are left-over semi-solid waste after food is digested. This can include undigestible parts like bones, food materials with extracted nutrients like cellulose, things toxic if left in the digestive tract, and extra bacteria. Some animals, like amphibians, reptiles, and birds, use the same opening, called the cloaca, for poop, reproduction, and laying eggs. Monotreme mammals also have a cloaca, inherited from early amniotes. Marsupials have one opening for both poop and liquid waste, and a separate part for reproduction in females. Most placental mammals have separate openings for poop, pee, and reproduction. Males have one for poop and another for pee and reproduction. The anus played a big role in the evolution of animals. It likely developed independently at least twice, in different types of animals. This development went hand in hand with other important changes, like the body plan, coelom, and metamerism, where the body is made of repeating segments that can specialize, like the heads of many insects.

A lawn mower, also called a grass cutter, is a machine that uses blades to cut grass to a uniform height. The grass height can be set by the design, but often can be adjusted by the operator using a lever or wheel nut. The blades can be powered by pushing the mower, a small engine, or electricity. Most common lawn mowers use a small one-cylinder engine. Walk-behind mowers need you to push them, while ride-on mowers allow you to sit and control them. Some mowers can operate automatically, or be controlled by an operator remotely. Two main types of blades are used: rotary mowers have a single vertical spinning blade, while cylinder mowers use a horizontal spinning bar and multiple blades. There are different kinds of mowers for different needs. Small, push mowers work well for small residential lawns. Electric or engine-powered push mowers are for larger lawns. Riding mowers, similar to small tractors, are for very large lawns, though some commercial models are designed for speed on flat areas. Large multi-blade mowers mounted on tractors are for big areas like golf courses, but not suitable for rough terrain.
Alma, formerly known as Mound City and Rantoul, is a small village in Marion County, Illinois, United States. The village had 386 people living there according to the 2000 census.
cyclostome is a biological term (from Greek meaning "round mouth") used in a few different ways.

Emalain Kudo Kabua, born in February 1928, is the former first lady of the Marshall Islands. She was the wife of former Marshall Islands president Amata Kabua and the mother of President-elect David Kabua. Emalain Kabua was the first first lady of the Marshall Islands from 1979 to 1996. She designed the flag of the Marshall Islands.

The Jurassic period lasted about 56 million years, from the end of the Triassic period to the start of the Cretaceous period. It was part of the Mesozoic Era, also called the Age of Reptiles. The Jurassic period began with a major extinction event. Two other smaller extinction events happened during this time. The Jurassic period is split into three parts: early, middle, and late. In geology, it's also divided into three rock layers: the Lower Jurassic, Middle Jurassic, and Upper Jurassic. The word "Jurassic" comes from the Jura Mountains in the Alps, where scientists first found rocks from this time. At the start of the Jurassic, a huge landmass called Pangea began to split into two: Laurasia to the north and Gondwana to the south. This made more coastlines and made the climate wetter. Deserts from the Triassic period turned into rainforests. On land, animals changed. Dinosaurs and their close relatives became the main animals, while other animals like crocodiles became less common. The first birds also appeared, evolving from a group of dinosaurs. Early lizards and the earliest mammals, including some that would eventually give birth to live young, appeared. Crocodiles also started living mostly in water. In the oceans, animals like ichthyosaurs and plesiosaurs became common. Pterosaurs, the flying reptiles, were the dominant flying animals.

Chakotay is a character in the TV show "Star Trek: Voyager," which had seven seasons. He is played by Robert Beltran. Chakotay is the leader on the ship Voyager. He was one of the first Native American characters in a Star Trek show. The people who made the show chose him to inspire Native Americans, like how Uhura inspired African Americans. To create his character, they asked Jamake Highwater for help. Chakotay was first called a Sioux, but later a Hopi. At the start of the show, he didn’t have a specific tribe, which was later fixed. He first appeared in the show's first episode. He stayed in the main cast until the show ended, with his last scene in the final episode. Throughout seasons 7 and 8, he had a love story with Seska, who died in an episode. In "Threshold," Chakotay didn't want to work with the Borg, almost causing Seven of Nine to die. By the end, they were a couple. After the ship returned home, Chakotay became the captain, but broke up with Seven. Critics said Chakotay's Native American background was too simple. They compared him to Tonto from The Lone Ranger. But many liked him as a role model for Native Americans in science fiction. He was seen as a groundbreaking character in this genre.

Desoto is a city in Dallas County, Texas, in the United States. In 2010, it had 49,047 people. Desoto is near Dallas and is part of the South West area, which includes Desoto, Cedar Hill, Duncanville, and Lancaster.

Canillo is a parish in Andorra. It is also the main town in the parish. Canillo is known as the religious center of Andorra. It has a sanctuary and chapel called Our Lady of Meritxell, which is the patron saint of Andorra. The parish also has a well-preserved Romanesque church named Sant Joan de Caselles. In 2011, the population was 4,826. Although it attracts tourists, the parish still has many farms and focuses on agriculture.

A defoliant is a chemical used to make plant leaves fall off. It is often sprayed or dusted on plants. Defoliants are used to remove weeds in farmland and lawns. They helped increase food production during the mid-20th century. Defoliants have also been used in wars to damage enemy crops and hiding places. This happened in the Malayan Emergency and the Vietnam War.

Mount Jackson is a town in Shenandoah County, Virginia, United States. The 2010 census showed the population was 1,994. For travelers on highway I-81, Mount Jackson is easy to spot at exit 273. There is a water tower painted like a basket of apples, recently repainted. For visitors exploring off the highway, Mount Jackson has a history as a commercial and railroad center in the area. It also has ties to the Civil War and is part of a historic district on the National Register of Historic Places.

Washing County is in North Carolina, U.S. In 2010, it had 13,228 people. The main town is Plymouth. The county was created in 1799 from Tyrrell County. It's named after George Washington. There are three towns in Washing County: Plymouth, Roper, and Creswell. Washing County is known for its rich farmland, forests, and lakes. The Roanoke River and Albemarle Sound are in the north. Lake Phelps, 16,000 acres, is in Creswell. It's part of Pettigrew State Park. Somerset Place, a historic plantation, is on Lake Phelps. The southern part of the county has the Pungo unit of the Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge. This area is famous for its large black bears. The North Carolina Black Bear Festival happens in Plymouth each June.

Philip Kotler, born on May 27, 1931, is an American marketing expert. He teaches at Northwestern University, where he was the S. C. Johnson & Son Distinguished Professor of International Marketing from 1962 to 2018. Kotler defined the marketing mix. He wrote over 80 books, including "Marketing Management," "Principles of Marketing," and "Kotler on Marketing." Some of his recent works are "Marketing 4.0," "Marketing Places," and "Marketing of Nations." He describes strategic marketing as a connection between people's needs and industrial responses. Kotler contributed to social marketing, which aims to encourage healthier and safer behaviors. He also introduced the concepts of demarketing, prosumers, atmospherics, and societal marketing. Many scholars consider him the "father of modern marketing." His latest writings focus on economic justice and criticizing capitalism. He published "Confronting Capitalism: Real Solutions for a Troubled Economic System" in 2015, "Democracy in Decline: Rebuilding Its Future" in 2016, and "Advancing the Common Good" in 2019. He also wrote "Brand Activation: From Purpose to Action" in 2018.

Joseph Patrick Kennedy III, born on October 4, 1980, is an American lawyer and politician. He has been representing a district from Boston's western suburbs to the state's south coast since 2013. A member of the Democratic Party, Kennedy worked as an assistant district attorney in Cape and Islands and Middlesex County, Massachusetts, before running for Congress. Kennedy is the son of U.S. Representative Joseph P. Kennedy II. He is also the grandson of U.S. Senator and U.S. Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy, the grandnephew of U.S. President John F. Kennedy and U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy, and the great-grandson of U.S. Ambassador to the United Kingdom Joseph P. Kennedy Sr. Kennedy was born in Boston and grew up there with his twin brother, Matthew Rauch Kennedy. After graduating from Stanford University with a bachelor's degree, he spent two years in the Dominican Republic with the Peace Corps. He then earned a law degree from Harvard Law School in 2009. In early 2012, Kennedy left his job as an assistant district attorney to run for the U.S. House of Representatives seat held by Barney Frank, who was retiring. Kennedy was sworn in as a U.S. Representative in January 2013 and is a member of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. In September 2019, Kennedy announced his candidacy for the Democratic nomination in the 2020 Massachusetts U.S. Senate election, competing against incumbent Ed Markey.

Safety was Coldplay's first public release. It was recorded in May 1998 over a weekend. The band and their manager Phil Harvey paid about £1,500 for it. Only around 50 copies reached record stores, as they gave most to record companies and friends and family. The songs on this EP later appeared unchanged in other releases. "Bigger Stronger" and "Such a Rush" are on "The Blue Room EP," and "No More Keeping My Feet on the Ground" was a bonus track on the single "Yellow." The lead singer Chris Martin's cover photo was taken by John Hilton, a friend of the band.

Shemiranat County is in Tehran Province, Iran. The county's capital is Shemiran, which is part of Tehran City. In 2006, the county had 37,778 people in 11,178 families. For census purposes, Shemiran and Tajrish are considered part of Tehran City. Shemiranat County is divided into two districts: Rudbar-e Qasran and Lavasanat. The county includes four cities: Tajrish, Fasham, Shemshak, and Lavasan.

1600 Penn is an American TV show about a family living in the White House. The family has problems. Jenna Elfman, Bill Pullman, and Josh Gad star in the show. Josh Gad, along with Jason Winer and Jon Lovett, created the main characters and the show's format. NBC decided to make more episodes in May 2012. The show was on TV from December 17, 2012, to March 28, 2013. NBC stopped the show after just one season on May 9, 2013.

The Barents Sea is a part of the Arctic Ocean, located north of Norway and Russia. It is split between Norwegian and Russian waters. In the Middle Ages, Russians called it the Murman Sea, but it is now known as the Barents Sea, named after the Dutch sailor Willem Barentsz. This sea is relatively shallow, with an average depth. It is important for fishing and looking for oil and gas. The Barents Sea borders the Kola Peninsula to the south, the Norwegian Sea to the west, and the Svalbard archipelago to the northwest. Franz Josef Land is to the northeast, and Novaya Zemlya is to the east. Novaya Zemlya, part of the Ural Mountains, separates the Barents Sea from the Kara Sea. Because of global warming, the Barents Sea is getting warmer faster than other parts of the Arctic, leading to less sea ice and changes in water layers. This could affect weather in Europe and Asia.

A migraine is a type of headache that happens often and can be mild to severe. It usually affects one side of the head, feels throbbing, and can last from a few hours to three days. People with migraines might feel sick to their stomach, throw up, or be sensitive to light, sound, or smells. Moving around can make the pain worse. Before puberty, slightly more boys get migraines than girls, but after puberty, twice as many women have them. Migraines are less common during pregnancy and after menopause. No one fully understands why migraines happen, but they seem linked to genes and the brain's nerves and blood vessels. Common treatments include pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen for the headache, medicines for nausea, and avoiding triggers. For some, specific drugs like triptans or ergotamines can help. Adding caffeine might also be useful. Several medications can prevent migraines, such as metoprolol, valproate, and topiramate. About 15% of people worldwide have migraines, and they often start during puberty. By middle age, they can be at their worst. In 2016, migraines were one of the leading causes of disability. An early description similar to migraines can be found in the Ebers Papyrus, written around 1500 BC in ancient Egypt. The word "migraine" comes from the Greek "hemikrania," which means "pain on one side of the head."

Hashish, or hash, is a drug made from the resin of the cannabis plant. People usually smoke it in a pipe, bong, vaporizer, or joint, or they can eat it after a process called decarboxylation. Sometimes, it's mixed with other herbs for smoking. Different names for hashish exist in different places. Hashish is made from parts of the cannabis plant called trichomes. It is defined by international law as "the separated resin, whether crude or purified, obtained from the cannabis plant." It often contains more tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and other cannabinoids than the plant's flowers. In Europe (2011), the THC concentration in confiscated hashish ranges from 4% to 15%. Between 2000 and 2005, about 18% of the cannabis seized was hashish. The consistency of hashish can vary. Pressed hashish is solid, while bubble hash, a type of purified hash, can be a paste-like substance. Its color can range from light to dark brown or even yellow, tan, black, or red, depending on the preparation process. In 2008, hashish was the main form of cannabis used in Europe, while herbal cannabis was more common in North America.

A SIM card is a small chip used in mobile phones and some computers to store information and help identify the user. It is also called a SIM card. SIM cards can hold contact information too. GSM phones always need SIM cards, while CDMA phones only need them for newer models. SIM cards can also be used in satellite phones, smartwatches, computers, and cameras. A SIM card is part of a larger card called a UICC, which is made of a material like plastic and has small metal parts inside. SIM cards can be moved to different devices. The first UICC cards were about the size of credit or bank cards. Over time, they got smaller but kept the same size metal contacts. A SIM card has a unique number, an IMSI number, and some security details. It also lists the services you can use and has two special numbers: one for regular use and one for changing the first number if needed. In Europe, a SIM card sometimes has extra numbers for online registration.

Habib Mohebian, known as Habib, was an Iranian singer-songwriter born on September 27, 1947, in Tehran, Iran. He developed a love for music and guitar in his last years of high school. In a national competition organized by the Iranian radio and TV, he was chosen as one of 16 top candidates. After two years of training, he joined the military and continued performing in clubs and across the country. Habib later lived in the provinces of Western and Eastern Azerbaijan and eventually in Tehran. He moved to the United States but returned to Iran in 2009. Habib died on June 10, 2016, in Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran, due to a heart problem.

Guanajuato is a city and municipality in central Mexico and the capital of the state with the same name. It is in a small valley, making its streets narrow and winding. Most streets are narrow alleys that cars cannot pass through, and some are long sets of stairs up the mountains. Many city streets are partly or fully underground. The historic center has small plazas and colonial mansions, churches, and buildings made of pink or green sandstone. The city grew because of the minerals in the surrounding mountains. During the colonial period, it was very important because one of its mines, La Valenciana, produced most of the world's silver. The city has a mummy museum with naturally mummified bodies found in the cemetery between the mid-19th and early 20th centuries. It hosts the international Cervantino festival, which invites artists and performers from all over the world and Mexico. Guanajuato was the site of the first battle of Mexico's war for independence between new Mexican fighters and royal troops. The city became a World Heritage site in 1988.

Caniformia is a group within the carnivores. It includes animals like dogs, bears, wolves, foxes, raccoons, badgers, seals, and mustelids. Seals, walruses, and sea lions also belong to this group. Caniformia mainly diversified in North America and northern Eurasia. This group is different from feliformia, which includes cats and related animals. Feliformia mainly diversified in Africa and southern Asia.

Florence County is in South Carolina, a state in the U.S. The 2010 census showed 136, 885 people lived there. Florence is the county seat. Florence County is part of the Florence, South Carolina metropolitan area. About 60% of the county's population lives in urban areas.

Adam Lyons Schlesinger was an American singer-songwriter who also played bass, guitar, keyboard, and drums. He won three Emmy Awards, a Grammy Award, and the ASCAP Pop Music Award. He was nominated for Academy, Tony, and Golden Globe awards. He was part of the bands Fountains of Wayne, Ivy, and Tinted Windows. He also wrote songs and produced for the band Fever High. Schlesinger was born in Manhattan and lived in Montclair, New Jersey. He died in the United States during the COVID-19 pandemic from complications caused by the virus.
The Manitoba Liberal Party is a political party in Manitoba, Canada. It started in the late 1800s, after the province was created in 1870.

Jerry Heller, born on October 6, 1940, and died on September 2, 2016, was an American music manager and businessman. He was famous for managing rap groups like N.W.A and Eazy-E. Heller gained attention in the 1960s and 1970s by bringing Elton John and Pink Floyd to America for their first big tours. He also worked with many artists such as Journey, Marvin Gaye, and Van Morrison. In the 1980s, Heller worked with R&B and hip-hop artists including Michel'le, World Class Wreckin' Cru, J.J. Fad, the D.O.C., Egyptian Lover, and La Dream Team. He helped the emergence of West Coast rap music by managing Ruthless Records with Eazy-E and signing groups like N.W.A, the Black Eyed Peas, Above the Law, the D.O.C., and Bone Thugs-n-Harmony. Dr. Dre brought the D.O.C. and Above the Law to Ruthless Records early on, and Eazy introduced Bone Thugs-n-Harmony later.

Dwijen Sharma was born on May 29, 1929, and passed away on September 15, 2017. He was a naturalist and science writer from Bangladesh. In 1987, he received the Bangla Academy Literary Award. In 2015, the government of Bangladesh gave him the Ekushey Padak for his work in language and literature.

Patrick Alan Nunnelee was an American businessman and politician. He served as a U.S. representative from 2011 until he died in 2015. Before that, he worked in the Mississippi State Senate, representing the 6th district from 1995 to 2011. He was a member of the Republican party.

Kathleen Marie Ireland, born on March 20, 1963, is an American model and actress who became an author and entrepreneur. She was a supermodel in the 1980s and 1990s, famous for appearing in 13 straight "Sports Illustrated" swimsuit issues. In 1993, she started a brand marketing company called Kathy Ireland Worldwide (KIWW). Because of her business career, she became very rich. By 2015, she had made a personal fortune of $420 million. In 2012, products from her company were worth $2 billion.

Atal Bihari Vajpayee, born on December 25, 1924, and passed away on August 16, 2018, was an important leader in India. He served as the prime minister three times: for 13 days in 1996, for 13 months from 1998 to 1999, and for a full term from 1999 to 2004. He was a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Vajpayee was the first non-Indian National Congress prime minister to serve a full term. He also wrote poems and books. He was in the Indian Parliament for more than 50 years, winning ten times for the Lok Sabha and twice for the Rajya Sabha. He represented Lucknow and stopped active politics in 2009 because of health issues. Vajpayee was one of the founders of the Bharatiya Janata Samaj (BJS), which later became the BJP. He was its first president. As prime minister, he led India's nuclear tests in 1998. He tried to make friends with Pakistan by traveling to Lahore in a bus and meeting Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. After the 1999 war with Pakistan, he met President Pervez Musharraf to try to improve relations. The government under Narendra Modi declared Vajpayee's birthday, December 25, as Good Governance Day. In 2015, he received India's highest honor, the Bharat Ratna. He died in 2018 from old age.

Mashhad, also spelled Mashad or Meshad, is the second largest city in Iran and the capital of Khorasan-e Razavi province. It is in the northeast part of the country. In 2016, it had about 3 million people, including those from Mashhad Taman and Torqabeh. Mashhad is famous because it has the shrine of Imam Reza, the eighth Shia Imam. People visit the shrine every year. Imam Reza was buried in a village, and the village later became known as Mashhad, meaning "place of martyrdom." The city is also called the city of Ferdowsi after an Iranian poet. Ferdowsi wrote the Shahnameh, an important book. Some famous Iranian poets and artists, like Mehdi Akhavan-Sales and Mohammad-Reza Shajarian, are from Mashhad. On October 30, 2009, Iran's president, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, said Mashhad was Iran's spiritual capital.

Angalifu (pronounced "ang-uh-leef-oo") was a northern white rhinoceros. He lived from around 1970 to December 14, 2014. At the time of his death, there were only six northern white rhinoceroses left in the world. Angalifu was one of the two male rhinoceroses alive, and the only one in North America. He lived at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. Before that, he was in the Khartoum Zoo in Sudan. In 1990, he was moved to the San Diego Zoo Safari Park on loan. Angalifu died of old age at 44 years old.

Central Connecticut State University (CCSU) is a public university in New Britain, Connecticut. It was founded in 1849 as the State Normal School. CCSU is Connecticut's oldest publicly funded university. It has four schools: the Ammon College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences, the School of Business, the School of Education and Professional Studies, and the School of Engineering, Science, and Technology. There are 11,822 students in total. 9,546 are undergraduates and 2,276 are graduate students. More than half of the students live off campus and 96 percent are from Connecticut. CCSU is part of the Connecticut State Colleges and Universities system, which includes Eastern, Western, and Southern Connecticut State Universities. Together, these universities have 32,722 students.

The House of Savoy is a royal family that started in 1003 in a place called Savoy. Over time, they became more powerful, ruling a small area north-west of Italy. In 1713 to 1720, they got the island of Sardinia and ruled it directly. Through a branch called Savoy-Carignano, the House of Savoy helped unite Italy in 1861 and ruled Italy until 1946. They also briefly ruled Spain in the 1800s. The Savoy kings of Italy were Victor Emmanuel II, Umberto I, Victor Emmanuel III, and Umberto II. Umberto II was the last king, ruling for a short time before Italy became a republic in 1946.

In 1976, voters of the Democratic Party chose their nominee for president by going through primary elections and caucuses. Former Georgia governor Jimmy Carter was selected as the nominee. This process led to the 1976 Democratic National Convention in New York City, which took place from July 12 to July 15, 1976.

Georg Solti, born György Stern in Budapest on October 21, 1912, was a Hungarian-born British conductor known for his work with opera companies in Munich, Frankfurt, and London. He was also the long-term music director of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra. Born in Budapest, he studied with Béla Bartók, Leó Weiner, and Ernesto Dohnányi. In the 1930s, he worked as a répétiteur at the Hungarian State Opera and assisted at the Salzburg Festival for Arturo Toscanini. He fled to Switzerland in 1938, where he stayed during World War II. He worked as a pianist to earn a living after being prohibited from conducting. In 1946, he became the musical director of the Bavarian State Opera in Munich. In 1952, he moved to the Opera Frankfurt, where he remained until 1961. He earned British citizenship in 1972. In 1961, he became the musical director of the Royal Opera Company in London, raising its standards to international levels. He became a British citizen in 1972. In 1969, he became the music director of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra, a position he held for 22 years. He also worked as the music director of the Orchestra de Paris from 1972 to 1975 and as the principal conductor of the London Philharmonic Orchestra from 1979 to 1983. Known for his intense conducting in early years, Solti later became more mellow. He recorded many works multiple times throughout his career and made over 250 recordings, including 45 complete opera sets. His recording of Wagner's "Der Ring des Nibelungen" was voted the greatest recording ever made twice. Solti received many awards, including 31 Grammy Awards. He died on September 5, 1997.

Justin Wakeland High School is a public high school in Frisco, Texas, United States. It is a 5A school according to the University Interscholastic League (UIL). It belongs to the Frisco Independent School District and is one of ten district high schools. The school opened on August 14, 2006. Most sophomores and juniors moved there from Frisco High School because the city expanded. New freshmen mostly come from Griffin Middle School, Cobb Middle School, and some from Staley Middle School. In 2015, the school was rated "Met Standard" by the Texas Education Agency.

An oil is a thick, liquid substance that doesn't mix with water and is used for many things. Oils are usually made of carbon and hydrogen and can catch fire. They are usually not mixed with water and are good at mixing with other oils. Most oils are a type of fat-like substance that stays liquid at room temperature. Oils can come from animals, plants, or oil extracted from rocks. They can be used for cooking (like olive oil), heating homes (like heating oil), medicine (like mineral oil), and making machines work well (like motor oil). Oils are also used to make paints, plastics, and other materials. Some oils are used in religious practices to make things feel clean.

Roberto Farias was born on March 27, 1932, and died on May 14, 2018. He was a Brazilian film director, producer, and screenwriter. During his career, he directed 15 films. In 1982, he made a film called "Pra Frente, Brasil" which was shown at the 33rd Berlin International Film Festival. Farias's brother is Reginaldo Faria, who is also a film director and actor. The 's' in Reginaldo's last name was mistakenly added when registering his name.
Bollène (in Provencal, "bouleno") is a village in Vaucluse. Vaucluse is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region of southeastern France.

Sarrebourg is a town in the Moselle department, which is in the Grand Est region of northeastern France. It is near the upper part of the Saar River. In 1895, people found an old temple called a mithraeum at Sarrebourg, where a path goes from the Vosges Mountains.

Keminmaa is a municipality in Finland. It has a population of (number not specified) and covers an area of land, with some water. The population density is not stated. Neighboring municipalities are Kemi, Simo, Tervola, and Tornio.

Noel George Williams, born on September 19, 1943, and known as King Sporty, was a DJ and reggae musician from Jamaica. He also made records for the Tashamba and Konduko labels. King Sporty co-wrote the song "Buffalo Soldier," which became famous when Bob Marley performed it.

In Norse mythology, Niflheim is a place of mist and ice. Sometimes it is connected with Niflhel and Hel. The name "Niflheim" appears in only two sources: "Gylfaginning" and "Hrafnagaldr Óðins". Niflheim was mainly a cold realm with frozen rivers and a great well called Hvergelmir. According to "Gylfaginning," Niflheim was one of the first realms, formed from the ice in Ginnungagap, the space between cold and heat. The other realm was Muspelheim, the place of fire. The mixture of ice from Niflheim and heat from Muspelheim created a "life-creating steam." Later, Niflheim became the home of Hel, a goddess who was the daughter of Loki. It was also where the souls of those who did not die a heroic or notable death went.
A sloppy joe is a sandwich made with ground beef or pork, onions, tomato sauce or ketchup, and seasonings. It is served on a hamburger bun. The dish came from the United States in the early 1900s.
Paul Malékou was born on November 17, 1938, in Fougamou, Gabon. He was the foreign minister of Gabon in 1968. From 1975 to 1983, he worked as the director-general of Asecna.

The Reinheitsgebot is a set of rules about beer ingredients in Germany and former states of the Holy Roman Empire. A well-known version was made in Bavaria in 1516. Earlier rules existed before 1516. Modern rules are different from the 1516 Bavarian version.

John "Ace" Cannon, born on May 5, 1934, and passed away on December 6, 2018, was an American saxophone player. He played with Bill Black's group from Hi Records and began his solo career in 1961 with the record "Tuff." This song reached number 17 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 in 1962. The following single, "Blues (Stay Away from Me)," also did well, reaching number 36 that same year. In April 1965, he released "Ace Cannon Live" and claimed it was the first album recorded live in a studio, not in a concert venue. Ace Cannon was inducted into both the Rock and Soul Hall of Fame and the Rockabilly Hall of Fame in 2000. His hometown, Calhoun City, Mississippi, celebrated him by hosting the first annual Ace Cannon Festival in May 2007. He was also honored by being inducted into the Mississippi Musicians' Hall of Fame in 2008. In the late 1980s, he moved back to Calhoun City and continued playing music. He enjoyed golfing at his local course. Ace Cannon died at home in 2018 at the age of 84.

an Buruk, born on October 19, 1973, is a Turkish football manager and former player. He currently manages Istanbul Başakşehir in Süper Lig. Buruk played as a midfielder for Galatasaray, Inter Milan, Beşiktaş, and Istanbul B.B. He also played for the Turkey national team 56 times.
George Foster Peabody was an American banker and philanthropist. He lived from July 27, 1852, to March 4, 1938.

Michael Corbett Shannon, born on August 7, 1974, is an American actor, producer, director, and musician. He was nominated twice for the Academy Award for best supporting actor for his roles in "Revolutionary Road" (2008) and "Nocturnal Animals" (2016). He got Screen Actors Guild and Golden Globe nominations for his role in "99 Homes" (2014), and a Tony Award nomination for best featured actor in a play for "Long Day's Journey into Night" (2016). Shannon made his film debut in 1993 with "Groundhog Day" and was famous for his role in "8 Mile" (2002). He is versatile, appearing in both comedies and dramas. His films include "Pearl Harbor" (2001), "Bad Boys II" (2003), "Bug" (2006), "Before the Devil Knows You're Dead" (2007), "The Lovely Bones" (2009), "The Iceman" (2012), "Premium Rush" (2012), "Man of Steel" (2013), "The Shape of Water" (2017), and "Knives Out" (2019). He often works with director Jeff Nichols, appearing in all his films: "Shotgun Stories" (2007), "Take Shelter" (2011), "Mud" (2012), "Midnight Special" (2016), and "Loving" (2016). He is also known for playing Nelson Van Alden in the HBO series "Boardwalk Empire" (2010-2014), for which he was nominated for three Screen Actors Guild awards.

Osama bin Laden, the founder of Al-Qaeda, a militant group, was killed on May 2, 2011, around 1:00 AM PKT (20:00 UTC on May 1) in Pakistan. US Navy SEALs, part of a CIA-led operation, carried out the mission. The operation, named Neptune Spear, involved SEAL Team Six and other special forces. Bin Laden's death ended a decade-long search linked to the 9/11 attacks on the US. The raid happened at his home in Abbottabad, Pakistan, which was entered from Afghanistan. The US took his body to Afghanistan for identification, then buried it at sea within 24 hours, as per Islamic tradition. Al-Qaeda confirmed his death and said they would seek revenge. Pakistani militant groups also promised retaliation against the US and Pakistan. Most Americans supported the operation, as did many governments. However, some people criticized not taking bin Laden alive and not sharing evidence. After the incident, a Pakistani commission investigated, revealing the military and intelligence's failure to find him. The report was leaked to Al Jazeera in 2013.

Suzy Delair, born Suzette Pierrette Delaire on December 31, 1917, and passed away on March 15, 2020, was a French actress, dancer, singer, and comedian. She was also a star in vaudeville.

Gary Charles Peters Sr., born on December 1, 1958, is an American politician. He has been serving as Michigan's junior United States Senator since 2015. A Democrat, Peters was a U.S. Representative from 2013 to 2015. His district includes parts of Detroit, Grosse Pointes, Hamtramck, Southfield, and Pontiac. Before Congress, Peters was in the U.S. Navy Reserve, worked as an investment advisor for 22 years, and taught briefly. He joined the Rochester Hills city council in 1991 and represented the 14th district in the Michigan Senate from 1995 to 2002. In 2002, he ran for Michigan Attorney General but lost to the Republican Mike Cox. Peters then worked as the Michigan Lottery Commissioner under Governor Jennifer Granholm from 2003 to 2008 before resigning to run for Congress. In 2014, he was elected to the U.S. Senate seat left by retiring Democrat Carl Levin. Peters won the Democratic primary unopposed and beat the Republican Terri Lynn Land in the general election. He was the only non-incumbent Democrat to win a Senate seat in 2014.
A playwright is someone who writes plays.

A text editor is a computer program used to change plain text. Sometimes, these programs are called "notepad" software, like Microsoft Notepad. Text editors are included in operating systems and software development tools. They can be used to edit files, such as configuration files, documentation files, and programming code.

Hans Gericke was an architect and urban planner from Germany. He was born on July 27, 1912, in Magdeburg, which was in the Province of Saxony, Prussia, in the German Empire. Gericke worked at the Institutes for the Theory and History of Architecture under the Deutsche Bauakademie from 1953 to 1958. In 1965, he became the chief architect of East Berlin, which was then in East Germany. He received awards from many organizations for his work. Gericke passed away on February 15, 2014, at the age of 101.

UNSW, which stands for the University of New South Wales, is a big school in Sydney, Australia. It's in a place called Kensington. In 2012, it had the highest average test scores of any school in New South Wales and got many top students. The university started in 1949 and is ranked fourth in Australia and 43rd in the world according to a list made in 2020. UNSW has nine main parts where you can study different subjects. It offers different types of degrees, like bachelor's, master's, and doctorates. Its main school is in Kensington, near the center of Sydney. The art school, UNSW Art & Design, is in a different part of Sydney called Paddington. There are also smaller schools in the CBD, Randwick, and Coogee. Research places are spread across New South Wales. UNSW is part of a group called the Group of Eight, which includes some of Australia's top research schools. It also belongs to Universitas 21, a network of top research universities worldwide. It has partnerships with over 200 schools in different countries.
Sigourney is a city in Keokuk County, Iowa, United States. The 2010 census showed that it had 2,059 people. Sigourney is also the county seat of Keokuk County.

Hurricane Maria was a very strong category 5 hurricane that hit Dominica, St. Croix, and Puerto Rico in September 2017. It was the worst natural disaster ever recorded in those islands and also the deadliest Atlantic hurricane since 2004. It was one of the ten strongest Atlantic hurricanes on record and the most intense tropical cyclone worldwide that year. Hurricane Maria was the 13th named storm, the 8th straight hurricane, the 4th major hurricane, the 2nd category 5 hurricane, and the deadliest storm of the very active 2017 Atlantic hurricane season. At its strongest, Hurricane Maria caused huge destruction and many deaths across the northeastern Caribbean. This made recovery harder in areas that were already affected by Hurricane Irma. The total damage was estimated at over $91.61 billion in 2017 dollars, ranking it as the third-costliest tropical cyclone on record. Maria developed from a tropical wave and became a tropical storm on September 16, east of the Lesser Antilles. As it approached the islands, it quickly got much stronger. It became the first category 5 hurricane to hit Dominica on September 18, right before making landfall. After briefly weakening over Dominica, Maria reached its strongest point over the Eastern Caribbean with winds of 175 mph and a pressure of 908 millibars. On September 20, an eyewall replacement cycle weakened the hurricane to a high-end category 4 hurricane before it hit Puerto Rico. Further land interaction weakened the hurricane, but it regained some strength as it moved northeast of the Bahamas. By September 28, it was moving slowly to the north and gradually weakened into a tropical storm. After becoming extratropical on September 30, Maria moved east and later east-northeast over the open Atlantic, eventually dissipating by October 2. Maria caused huge damage to Dominica, leaving the whole island without communication. Most buildings and infrastructure were destroyed, and the island's trees were mostly destroyed. St. Martin and Guadeloupe suffered widespread flooding and damaged roofs. Puerto Rico was hit hard, too. The island's population faced flooding and a lack of resources, and the slow relief process made things worse. The storm caused the worst blackout in US history, and by June 2018, thousands of homes and businesses were still without power. This was the third consecutive major hurricane to threaten the Leeward Islands in two weeks, following Hurricane Irma, which hit some of the islands two weeks earlier, and Hurricane Jose, which passed close by, bringing strong winds to Barbuda. After almost a year, Puerto Rico revised the official death count from 64 to 2,975, making the total 3,059. Of these, 2,975 were in Puerto Rico, 65 in Dominica, 5 in the Dominican Republic, 4 in Guadeloupe, 4 in the US, 3 in the US Virgin Islands, and 3 in Haiti. Hurricane Maria was the deadliest hurricane in Dominica since 1834 and in Puerto Rico since 1899. The initial death count of 64 was revised after studies estimated between 1,400 and 5,740 deaths. The final official estimate of 2,975 deaths was based on a study by George Washington University, which used statistical models to estimate both direct and indirect deaths caused by the hurricane.

The bishop is a piece in chess. Each player has two bishops at the start. One bishop begins between the king and the bishop, the other between the queen and the bishop. For white, the bishops start on c1 and f1. For black, they start on c8 and f8.

Alexander Pope, born on May 21, 1688, and died on May 30, 1744, is considered one of the greatest English poets, especially from the early 1700s. He is well-known for his satirical and discursive poetry, including "The Rape of the Lock," "The Dunciad," and "An Essay on Criticism," as well as his translation of Homer. After Shakespeare, Pope is the second-most quoted writer in the English language, with some of his verses becoming common sayings, like "damning with faint praise." He was a master of the heroic couplet. Pope faced many challenges, including his Catholic faith, which led to restrictions on his family's prosperity. Due to these restrictions, Pope was mostly self-educated, learning languages like French, Italian, Latin, and Greek on his own. He discovered Homer at the age of six. As a child, Pope survived a cow trampling incident but began suffering from tuberculosis of the spine at age 12, along with chronic headaches. In 1709, Pope published his first major poems, "Pastorals," which gained him fame. At 23, he wrote "An Essay on Criticism," released in 1711. This essay earned him friends like Joseph Addison and Richard Steele, and a critic, John Dennis, was upset with him. Dennis hated Pope for life and often insulted him, but Pope also wrote satires about Dennis. "Pope's most famous poem, "The Rape of the Lock," appeared in 1712, and a revised version in 1714. It was inspired by an incident where Lord Petre cut a lock of Arabella Fermor's hair, leading to a family dispute. In his poem, Pope humorously criticized the rise of individualism and materialism. In 1717, a collection of Pope's poems was published, including "Verses to the Memory of an Unfortunate Lady" and "Eloisa to Abelard." Pope was never married but had romantic attachments, notably to Lady M. Montagu and Martha Blount. Pope was a satirist who made enemies, carrying pistols for protection. After 1738, he wrote less. He worked on "The Dunciad," with the last revision in 1743, replacing one character with another and targeting politician Robert Walpole. By then, Pope's health was failing, and on his deathbed, his doctor told him he was better, to which Pope replied, "Here am I, dying of a hundred good symptoms."
Macaye is a commune in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department in southwestern France.

Victor Amadeus II, born on May 14, 1666, and died on October 31, 1732, was the Duke of Savoy from 1675 to 1730. He also had other titles like Marquis of Saluzzo, Duke of Montferrat, Prince of Piedmont, and Count of Aosta, Moriana, and Nice. Louis XIV planned his marriage to keep French influence in Savoy, but Victor Amadeus later separated from France. When his father died in 1675, his mother, Marie Jeanne Baptiste of Nemours, ruled as regent for the nine-year-old Victor Amadeus. She remained in control until 1684, when Victor Amadeus took over. Victor Amadeus fought in the War of the Spanish Succession. In 1713, he became King of Sicily, but he had to give up this title and became King of Sardinia instead. Victor Amadeus had a big impact on Turin's culture. He rebuilt the Royal Palace of Turin, the Palace of Venaria, and the Palazzina di Caccia of Stupinigi. He also built the Basilica of Superga, where he is buried.

Antonio Maceda Francés was born on May 16, 1957. He was a Spanish retired football player. Even though he was a central defender, he was famous for scoring goals. He began his career with Sporting de Gijón and ended it with Real Madrid, where he had many injuries. Maceda played for Spain about 40 times and participated in two World Cups and Euro 1984.

Johan Cédric Micoud, born on July 24, 1973, is a former French football player. He mostly played as an attacking midfielder. Micoud was known for his skills and his ability to take free kicks. He had a 16-year career, playing in Italy and Germany, besides France. Micoud played for France about 20 times and was part of the team that won Euro 2000. He also participated in the 2002 World Cup.

The Delaware River is a big river on the eastern coast of the United States. It is in four states: Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania. The river starts in the Catskill Mountains of New York and flows into Delaware Bay. From there, its waters enter the Atlantic Ocean near Cape May in New Jersey and Cape Henlopen in Delaware. The total length of the river, including its two branches, is about 315 miles. The Delaware River is one of nineteen important rivers recognized by the America's Great Waters Coalition. The river has two main branches. One starts near Mount Jefferson in New York and the other begins at Grand Gorge, also in New York. These branches merge in Delaware County and continue as the Delaware River. The river forms borders between several states and meets the tide at the Falls of the Delaware, near Morrisville, Pennsylvania, and Trenton, New Jersey. The river was important for shipping and helped develop cities like Trenton, Camden, and Philadelphia. Native Americans called the river Lenapewihittuk, meaning the Lenape river. In 1609, Henry Hudson, an English explorer, visited the river. After the English took control in 1664, the river was named Delaware, after Sir Thomas West, the 3rd Baron De La Warr.

Noam Chomsky, born on December 7, 1928, is an American linguist, philosopher, and social critic. He is often called "the father of modern linguistics" and is a major figure in analytic philosophy. Chomsky is also one of the founders of cognitive science. He teaches at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of Arizona. Chomsky has written many books about linguistics, politics, and other topics. Born to Jewish parents in Philadelphia, Chomsky grew up interested in anarchism. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania. In 1955, he earned his doctorate with his theory of transformational grammar. That year, he started teaching at MIT. His book "Syntactic Structures" made him famous in linguistics in 1957. From 1958 to 1959, Chomsky was a fellow at the Institute for Advanced Study. He developed important theories like universal grammar and minimalist program. Chomsky criticized behaviorism, especially the work of B. F. Skinner. Chomsky was against the U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War. In 1967, his essay "The Responsibility of Intellectuals" made him well-known. He was arrested for his activism and was on President Nixon's enemies list. Chomsky continued to teach and write, and became involved in debates about linguistics. With Edward S. Herman, Chomsky wrote "Manufacturing Consent," which explained how media operates. He also worked to expose the Indonesian occupation of East Timor. Chomsky supported freedom of speech, even for controversial topics like Holocaust denial, which caused debate. Since retiring from MIT, Chomsky has stayed active politically, opposing the 2003 invasion of Iraq and supporting the Occupy movement. He teaches at the University of Arizona now. Chomsky is one of the most cited scholars today, influencing many fields. He is known for his criticism of U.S. foreign policy, capitalism, and media. His ideas are important to anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist movements but have also faced criticism.

Frederick Nelson Pyatt, born on September 9, 1953, is a former professional ice hockey player from Canada. He was born in Port Arthur, Ontario. In 1973, Pyatt was chosen by the Detroit Red Wings of the National Hockey League and the Minnesota Fighting Saints of the World Hockey Association. He also played for the Washington Capitals and the Colorado Rockies. Pyatt is the father of Jesse and the fathers of former NHL players Tom and Taylor Pyatt.
Higden is a town in Cleburne County, Arkansas, United States. It had 120 people living there in 2010.

The health services functional constituency, once known simply as health, is a group that participates in Hong Kong's Legislative Council elections. This group was first created for the 1988 Legislative Council election. It includes health professionals. This group has a large number of voters among the functional constituencies. It has been mainly supported by pro-democracy candidates, who have held the seat since it was created.
Plougastel-Daoulas is a commune in Finistère, which is in Brittany, a region in northwestern France.

Hara Pattanaik, also known as Hari Patnaik, was an Odia film actor, director, and writer of screenplays. He acted in more than 60 Odia movies and directed about 19 films. Pattanaik helped introduce other actors like Anubhav Mohanty, Sabyasachi Mishra, and Babushaan. He passed away due to cancer on January 13, 2015.

Wandsworth is a borough in southwest London. It is part of inner London. To the east, it borders Lambeth. To the south, it borders Merton and Kingston upon Thames. To the west and north, it borders Richmond upon Thames, Hammersmith and Fulham, Kensington and Chelsea, and Westminster. The local authority is Wandsworth London Borough Council.

The Pauline epistles, also known as Paul's letters, are thirteen books in the New Testament that are attributed to Paul the apostle. Some people doubt who wrote them. These letters are some of the earliest Christian documents. They give us insight into early Christianity's beliefs and problems. As part of the New Testament, they are very important for Christian beliefs and rules. One letter, called Hebrews, doesn't have Paul's name, but it was once thought he wrote it. However, most experts now think he didn't. Paul probably wrote seven of these letters, but four others might not have been written by him. Two more letters are hard to prove came from Paul. Some scholars believe Paul had a secretary who helped write the letters, which may have influenced their style but not the ideas. In most modern Bible editions, the Pauline epistles come after the Acts of the Apostles and before the Catholic epistles. But in many old Greek manuscripts, the General Epistles come first, and in some, the Pauline epistles are at the end of the New Testament.

Halloween is an American horror franchise with eleven films, plus novels, comic books, and merchandise. The main character is Michael Myers, who was put in a sanitarium as a child for killing his sister, Judith Myers. Fifteen years later, he escapes to chase and kill people in the town of Haddonfield, Illinois, on Halloween. The first Halloween film, made in 1978, was written and directed by John Carpenter. It inspired many other horror films. Eight sequels followed, except for one that doesn't connect to the others. In 2007, Rob Zombie made a remake of the 1978 film. A sequel to this remake was released two years later. In 2018, a new film, not connected to the sequels, came out. Two more films, "Halloween Kills" and "Halloween Ends," were announced for 2021 and 2022. Together, the films earned over $640 million. The series is the top-grossing American horror series at the US box office. Both the original 1978 film and the 2018 sequel got good reviews, while other films got mixed or bad reviews.

Francis George Steiner, born on April 23, 1929, and died on February 3, 2020, was a literary critic, essayist, philosopher, novelist, and educator from France and America. He wrote about how language, literature, and society are connected, and he talked a lot about the impact of the Holocaust. An article in The Guardian called him a "polyglot and polymath." Many people think Steiner is one of the greatest thinkers in today's literary world. A.S. Byatt, an English novelist, said he was a "late renaissance man, a European metaphysician who understood the main ideas of our time." Harriet Harvey-Wood, who used to be in charge of literature for the British Council, said Steiner was a great speaker who often showed up with just a few notes and didn't even look at them. Steiner taught at the University of Geneva from 1974 to 1994, was a professor at the University of Oxford from 1994 to 1995, taught poetry at Harvard University from 2001 to 2002, and has been an extraordinary fellow at Churchill College, Cambridge, since 1969.

Anseba Region is one of six administrative regions in northern Eritrea. The region's capital and largest city is Keren. The region is named after the Anseba River, which flows through much of it. Anseba Region has an average elevation around 1,500 meters. It is hottest in May, with temperatures reaching up to 33°C. December to February are the coldest months, with freezing temperatures. Anseba gets about 500 millimeters of rain annually, making the soil good for farming. In 2005, the region's population was 549,000, up from 484,200 in 2001, with a growth rate of 11.80%. Anseba Region covers 23,200 square kilometers, with a population density of 23.66 people per square kilometer. The country and the region are governed by the People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ), formerly known as the Eritrean Liberation Front. Elections are held regularly but under strict control. All men and women, regardless of ethnicity or religion, can vote. Only the PFDJ can contest elections, and PFDJ representatives oversee the voting process.
The following are people who were born, raised, or became well-known while living in the state of New Hampshire, U.S.

Jamstik is a brand of portable, app-connected guitars made by Zivix. Zivix is a music technology company in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Jamstik is made in the United States. It is designed in Minneapolis and manufactured by a contract manufacturer in South Dakota.

The House of Windsor is the royal family ruling the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth countries. In 1901, after King Edward VII took the throne, the family changed its name from Saxe-Coburg and Gotha to Windsor. This happened because of bad feelings towards Germany during World War I. Since then, four British kings and queens from the House of Windsor have ruled: George V, Edward VIII, George VI, and Elizabeth II. Today, the Queen, who is the head of the House of Windsor, is the monarch in sixteen countries, including the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and several Caribbean nations. These countries have separate monarchies. There are also three areas where the Queen is head of state, and fourteen territories and two states in New Zealand where she is represented by governors-general.

Kimberley Gail Marsh, born on June 13, 1976, is an English actress and TV presenter. She became famous in 2001 by joining the band Hear'say after winning on a reality TV show called "Popstars." Hear'say had some success, with two UK number one hits and an album at number one. However, in 2002, Marsh left the band to try singing solo. In 2003, she released an album called "Standing Tall," which reached number nine in the UK and had two top ten hits. From 2006 to 2019, she played Michelle Connor on a TV soap opera called "Coronation Street." She won several awards, including Best Newcomer at the 2007 British Soap Awards and the 2007 National Television Awards, and Best Female Dramatic Performance at the 2017 British Soap Awards. In 2010, she came fourth on the TV show "Popstar to Operastar," where pop stars learned to sing opera.

WWE Raw, also called Monday Night Raw, is an American wrestling show. It airs on USA Network every Monday from 8:00 to 11:00 PM EST in the U.S. The show has two names: WWE Raw and just Raw. It started on January 11, 1993, and is one of the main shows, along with Friday Night Smackdown. WWE Raw is the longest weekly show of its kind. In September 2000, Raw moved to Spike TV from USA Network. It was back on USA Network by October 3, 2005. As of December 9, 2016, you can watch all past episodes on the WWE Network. Recent shows are available 30 days after they air. Since 1993, Raw has been live from 208 places, in 171 cities and towns, and 11 countries: the U.S., Canada, UK, Afghanistan (2005), Iraq (2006-2007), South Africa, Germany, Japan, Italy, and Mexico.

The Animals were an English band that played rhythm and blues and rock music. They were formed in Newcastle upon Tyne in the early 1960s. In 1964, they moved to London after becoming famous. They were known for their strong, bluesy sound and their deep-voiced singer, Eric Burdon. Their most famous songs include "House of the Rising Sun," "We Got to Get Out of This Place," "It's My Life," "Inside Looking Out," "I'm Crying," and "Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood." The band made both tough, rock-edged pop songs and rhythm and blues songs. They were part of the British invasion of the U.S. Later, the band changed members several times and faced poor business management. As Eric Burdon and the Animals, they moved to California and became a psychedelic and hard rock band. They had hits like "San Francisco Nights," "When I Was Young," and "Sky Pilot." They stopped making music at the end of the 1960s. The original members Burdon, Alan Price, Chas Chandler, Hilton Valentine, and John Steel played together again in 1968 for a special concert in Newcastle. They also had brief comebacks in 1975 and 1983. Some original members have played together under different names since then. The Animals were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1994.

Salt Lake County is in Utah, U.S. As of 2010, it had 1,029,655 people, with 1,160,437 by July 1, 2019. This makes it the most populous county in Utah. Salt Lake City is its county seat and largest city, also the state capital. Salt Lake County was created in 1850. It is the 37th most populous county in the U.S. and one of four counties in the Rocky Mountains among the top 100, along with Denver, El Paso, and Clark counties. Salt Lake County is a first-class county, with over 700,000 people. It covers the Salt Lake Valley and parts of surrounding mountains, including the Oquirrh Mountains to the west and the Wasatch Range to the east. The northern part includes part of Great Salt Lake. The county is known for its ski resorts. Salt Lake City hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics. It's the central county in the Salt Lake City metropolitan area.

Charles Edward Daniels was an American singer, songwriter, and musician. He was famous for southern rock, country, and bluegrass music. People remember him most for his top country song "The Devil Went Down to Georgia." Daniels began performing in the 1950s. He was honored in several halls of fame: the Cheyenne Frontier Days Hall of Fame in 2002, the Grand Ole Opry in 2008, the Musicians Hall of Fame and Museum in 2009, and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2016. He was born on October 28, 1936, and died on July 6, 2020.

Sirdavidia is a genus of flowering plants. It belongs to the family Annonaceae. It was described on February 4, 2015, by Thomas L.P. Couvreur from France's Institute of Research for Development, Raoul Niangadouma from the National Herbarium of Gabon, Bonaventure Sonké from the University of Yaoundé, and Hervé Sauquet from Université Paris-Sud. The genus is named after Sir David Attenborough. The type species, Sirdavidia solannona, was found in Gabon at Crystal Mountains National Park on November 15, 2013, between 300 and 600 meters above sea level. The species name comes from the similarity of its flowers to those of the Solanum plants.
Angkaliya Curtis, born around 1928, is an Australian Aboriginal artist. She paints animals from the central Australian desert.
32 is the number that comes after 31 and before 33.

La Bollène-Vésubie is a town in the Alpes-Maritimes department, in the Provence-Alpes-Côte-d'Azur region of southeastern France. The people who live there are called bollénois. In the Niçois dialect, the town's name is La Boulèna, and the inhabitants are called "lu boulenasc."

Silent Hill: Downpour is a survival horror video game. Vatra Games made it, and Konami Digital Entertainment released it. It is the eighth game in the Silent Hill series. It came out in March 2012. The story takes place in Silent Hill, a made-up town in America. The main character, Murphy Pendleton, is in prison. He enters the town and sometimes goes to another world. He finds memories from his past. The game is played from a third-person perspective and can be played in 3D. Some people liked the game because of its atmosphere and story. They enjoyed it returning to the original survival horror style after previous games. But, they criticized the monsters, combat, and technical problems. Since its release, a patch fixed many of these issues.

Toypurina lived from 1760 to 1799. She was a medicine woman from the Tongva people, also called Gabrieliño because of their connection to San Gabriel Mission. She fought against Spanish missionaries who ruled California. Toypurina was involved in a plan to rebel against the mission in 1785. She helped recruit 6 out of 8 villages to join the attack.
"killing me softly" might mean: someone is making me sad in a gentle way.

Wii Music is a music game for the Wii console made by Nintendo. It came out in Japan and North America in October 2008, and in Europe and Australia the next month. This game is part of the Nintendo Touch! Generations brand and the Wii series. In the game, you control the members of an on-screen band to make music arrangements. You choose instruments, like guitars or drums, and play them by moving the Wii Remote and Nunchuk in the right way. Unlike games like Guitar Hero or Rock Band, where you get scores, in Wii Music, you can just play around and experiment with different ways to play songs. Wii Music was shown at E3 in 2006 and 2008. When it came out, some people liked it, but others didn’t. It got good scores from websites, like 64.34% on Gamerankings and 63 on Metacritic. People said it was simple to play, and the songs weren’t very good. Because of this, it’s considered one of the not-so-popular games in the Wii series, selling only 2.65 million copies by March 2009.
drink or the person who drinks may be called a drinker.

Uses and gratifications theory (UGT) helps us understand why and how people choose media to meet their needs. This theory focuses on the audience, looking at what people do with media instead of what media does to people. UGT assumes that media is widely available and that audiences actively choose what to consume. UGT asks why people use media and what they use it for. It suggests that people pick media to learn, relax, stay connected, or have fun. The theory sees audiences as not just passive consumers but as active users who interpret and use media in their lives. Unlike other theories, UGT says that audiences are responsible for choosing media that will give them pleasure. This theory implies that media competes with other sources for people's attention. UGT provides a useful viewpoint for communication scholars to understand media choice, consumption, and even its impact.

Liberty X, originally called Liberty, was a British-Irish group with members Michelle Heatton, Tony Loundon, Kevin Simm, Jessica Taylor, and Kelli Young. They formed after the "Popstars" ITV talent show. Liberty X had ten UK top 20 hits and did better than another group called Hear'say. They changed their name because another band was already using "Liberty." Their first album, "Thinking It Over," came out in May 2002, and their biggest hit was "Just a Little." They released their second album, "Being Somebody," in November 2003 but it was not as successful. After sales dropped, they stopped performing. In 2008, they played one last time together in Belfast. In 2012, they reformed for an ITV2 show called "The Big Reunion," with other former bands. The show was about rehearsing for a big performance. Liberty X said this would be their last appearance together. In 2014, they signed with a new management company for future projects.

'Splosion Man is a 2.5D action platform video game made by Twisted Pixel Games for the Xbox 360. You can download it from Xbox Live Arcade. It came out on July 22, 2009, as part of the 2009 Xbox Live Summer of Arcade. In the game, you control 'Splosion Man, who can explode himself many times. He has to go through obstacles and traps to leave a place called Big Science. 'Splosion Man got good reviews. Players voted it the best original Xbox Live Arcade game of 2009. It was also on IGN’s list of the top 25 Xbox Live Arcade games of all time. The game sold over 487,000 copies by the end of 2011 and ranked 13th in 2009 sales. A sequel called 'Ms. Splosion Man' was released on July 13, 2011.

Hanau is a town in Main-Kinzig-Kreis, Hesse, Germany. It is about 25 kilometers east of Frankfurt am Main and is part of the Frankfurt Rhine-Main area. Hanau has a train station that is a major railway junction and a port on the Main River, making it an important transportation center. The town is known for the birthplace of the Brothers Grimm and Franciscus Sylvius. Since the 16th century, it has been a center for precious metal work, with many goldsmiths. Hanau is also home to Heraeus, one of the largest family-owned companies in Germany. Hanau used to be the seat of the Counts of Hanau, but much of its old architecture was lost in World War II. A British air raid in 1945 caused a firestorm, killing many people and destroying most of the old city. In 1963, Hanau hosted a state festival. Until 2005, Hanau was the administrative center of Main-Kinzig-Kreis. In February 2020, a gunman attacked two hookah lounges in Hanau, killing nine people from outside Germany before shooting his mother and himself.

Joseph René Marcel Pronovost, born on June 15, 1930, and passed away on April 26, 2015, was a Canadian ice hockey player and coach. He played in 1,206 games over 20 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) for the Detroit Red Wings and Toronto Maple Leafs from 1950 to 1970. Pronovost was a top defender and was chosen for four post-season NHL All-Star teams, playing in 11 All-Star games. He was part of four Stanley Cup championship teams with the Red Wings, with his first win in 1950. He also won a fifth Stanley Cup with the Maple Leafs in 1967. Pronovost was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame as a player in 1978. Pronovost started coaching in 1969 and coached junior teams, including the Hull Olympiques and Windsor Spitfires. He was the head coach of the Chicago Cougars in the World Hockey Association's first season in 1972-73. He coached 104 games for the Buffalo Sabres in the NHL from 1977 to 1978 and was an assistant coach for the Red Wings for a short time. From 1990 until 1995, Pronovost worked for the NHL Central Scouting Bureau. He then became a scout for the New Jersey Devils, where he was part of three Stanley Cup championship teams, with the last win in 2003. The 53 years between his first and last championship win set a Stanley Cup record.

Barsha Lekhi, born on May 5, 1993, in Saptari, Nepal, is a beauty queen and environmental activist. She won Miss Nepal 2016. In 2016, she also won the Missosology People's Choice Award. She represented Nepal at the Miss International 2016 contest in Japan on October 27, 2016. Barsha studied environmental science at Patan Multiple Campus. She has worked at the NEFIN-REDD/CC partnership program. Currently, she is studying for her master's degree in environmental science at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

The Standard Model of particle physics explains three of the four fundamental forces in the universe (the electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions) but not gravity. It was created over many years by scientists and finalized in the 1970s after finding quarks. Later, discoveries like the top quark, tau neutrino, and Higgs boson supported this model. It accurately predicts some properties, like those of weak neutral currents and W and Z bosons. While the model is very successful, it can't explain everything. It doesn't explain why there are more matter particles than antimatter particles, nor does it include gravity or dark energy. It also can't fully explain neutrino behavior. Particle physicists worked on the Standard Model because it shows how different phenomena like symmetry breaking can happen, and it helps create new models that include extra particles and dimensions.
