Vincenzo Bettiza was born on June 7, 1927, and died on July 28, 2017. He was an Italian writer, journalist, and politician who was born in Yugoslavia.

Robie Creek is a place in Boise County, Idaho, United States. The population was 1,162 in 2010. Robie Creek has a recreation area with swimming, a playground for children, and a boat launch and dock. There are also vault toilets. However, cell phone service is not available.
His comic books show modern East Asian history, but they mostly present a good view of imperial Japan.

In quantum field theory, the Casimir effect and the Casimir–Polder force are physical forces from a quantized field. These forces are named after Hendrik Casimir, a Dutch physicist who predicted them in 1948. In 1997, S. Lamoreaux conducted an experiment that measured the force, which was within 5% of the theoretical prediction. The Casimir effect happens because the presence of metals and materials called dielectrics changes the energy in the electromagnetic field. This change in energy depends on the shapes and positions of the objects. As a result, there is a force between these objects. This idea is similar in other media that support vibrations, such as beads on a string or plates in water or gas. In modern physics, the Casimir effect is important in understanding how particles behave, especially in the chiral bag model of nucleons. It is also significant in some new technologies like microtechnologies and nanotechnologies.
John Samuel Mbiti was a Kenyan-born Christian philosopher and writer who was also an ordained Anglican priest and a canon.
Babbie is a town in Covington County, Alabama, United States. In 2010, it had 603 people. Babbie became a town in 1957.
The central pier is one of three piers in Blackpool, England. It was built in 1868.

William Friedkin, born on August 29, 1935, is an American director, producer, and writer. He is famous for his work in the "New Hollywood" movement of the 1970s. Friedkin started his career making documentaries in the early 1960s. He is best known for directing "The French Connection" in 1971 and "The Exorcist" in 1973. "The French Connection" won five Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Best Director. "The Exorcist" also got him a Best Director nomination. Other films he directed include "The Boys in the Band" in 1970, "Sorcerer" in 1977, "Cruising" in 1980, "To Live and Die in L.A." in 1985, "Bug" in 2006, and "Killer Joe" in 2011.

"What I've Done" is a song by Linkin Park. It was released in 2007 as the first single from their album "Minutes to Midnight." The song is in the key of G minor. It came out as a radio single on April 1, 2007, as a digital download on April 2, and as a CD single on April 30. A live version of the song was nominated for "Best Hard Rock Performance" at the 52nd Grammy Awards but didn't win. It also serves as the main theme of the 2007 science fiction movie "Transformers." The song was used in the video game "Guitar Hero World Tour" and was included in a Linkin Park DLC pack for "Rock Band 3" in January 2011. It's also a bonus track for the UK single "Iridescent." An instrumental version is used by Sky UK for their interactive services.
Wittmund is a "district" in northwestern Lower Saxony, Germany. It is in East Friesland, by the North Sea. The neighboring districts, going clockwise from the east, are Friesland, Leer, and Aurich.

A combatant is someone who can fight in a war. According to Article 43(2) of Additional Protocol I to the 1949 Geneva Conventions, combatants are members of a country's military, except for medical staff and religious officers. They have the right to fight. Usually, combatants can be attacked by the other side because they are enemies. If caught, combatants are considered prisoners of war. All combatants must follow war rules, but breaking these rules doesn't take away their right to fight or to be treated as a prisoner of war.

Oliver Burgess Meredith (November 16, 1907 – September 9, 1997) was an American actor, director, producer, and writer. He was active in the entertainment industry for over six decades. People called him an excellent actor and one of the most skilled actors of the century. He was a member of the Actors Studio by invitation and won several Emmy awards. Meredith was the first male actor to win the Saturn Award for best supporting actor twice. He was nominated for two Academy Awards. Meredith was famous for his roles in critically acclaimed films like "Of Mice and Men" (1939) and "The Story of G.I. Joe" (1945). He also appeared as the narrator in "A Walk in the Sun" (1945). Later in his career, he was known for his roles on "The Twilight Zone" and as the villain the Penguin in the 1960s TV series "Batman." He also played Mickey Goldmill, a boxing trainer, in the "Rocky" films. For his performances in "The Day of the Locust" (1975) and "Rocky" (1976), he was nominated for an Academy Award for best supporting actor. He starred in the comedy "Foul Play" (1978) and the fantasy film "Clash of the Titans" (1981). Throughout his career, he narrated many films and documentaries, including "Clash of the Titans" (1981). Even though his later performances brought him back into the spotlight, his career was rich and varied. He played many challenging roles in theater, including in plays by Shakespeare, O'Neill, and Beckett.

Melissa Ellen Gilbert, born on May 8, 1964, is an American actress, director, and producer. She was also the president of the Screen Actors Guild. Gilbert started acting as a child in the 1960s, appearing in commercials and TV shows. From 1974 to 1984, she played Laura Ingalls Wilder in the TV series "Little House on the Prairie." During this time, she also appeared in TV movies like "The Diary of Anne Frank" and "The Miracle Worker." As an adult, she continued acting in TV movies and made guest appearances on TV shows. She did voice work for the cartoon "Batgirl." In 2009, she was in the musical version of "Little House on the Prairie." In 2012, she was on a dance competition show called "Dancing with the Stars." Gilbert was the president of the Screen Actors Guild from 2001 to 2005. She wrote her book "Prairie Tale: A Memoir" in 2009. In 2014, she wrote a children's story called "Daisy and Josephine" and a cookbook. In 2016, she tried to become a U.S. representative for Michigan's 8th district but withdrew because of injuries from an accident in 2012.

Eduardo Horacio Laborde was born on October 19, 1967, and died on February 4, 2015. He was an Argentine rugby player. Laborde played three games for the national team, known as "Los Pumas," during the 1991 Rugby World Cup. He died in a car accident near Pinamar, a coastal town.

Actinium is a chemical element with the symbol Ac and atomic number 89. It was first isolated by André-Louis Debierne in 1899. Friedrich Oskar Giesel later found it independently in 1902 and called it emanium, unaware it was already known. Actinium helped name the actinide series, a group of 15 similar elements between actinium and lawrencium in the periodic table. Actinium is a soft, silvery-white metal that reacts quickly with air and moisture. It forms a white coating of actinium oxide, which stops further oxidation. Actinium mostly has a +3 oxidation state in its compounds. This element is rare, found only in small amounts in uranium and thorium ores. The isotope Ac-227 has a half-life of 21.772 years and mostly emits beta particles. The isotope Ac-228 has a half-life of 6.15 hours and emits beta particles. Only a tiny amount of actinium is found in one ton of uranium or thorium ore. Actinium's properties are similar to lanthanum, making it hard to separate from ore. It is produced by neutron irradiation in a reactor. Due to its scarcity and radioactivity, actinium has no major industrial use. It is used in making neutron sources and for radiation therapy.

Churdan is a city in Greene County, Iowa, United States. It had 386 people living there in 2010.

Robert Brown was born on March 19, 1923, and passed away on January 15, 2020. He was from Scotland and played football as a goalkeeper. He played for Queen's Park, Rangers, and Falkirk. He also played five times for the Scotland national team. Later, he managed St. Johnstone and was the manager of the Scottish national team from 1967 to 1971. In 2015, he was added to the Scottish Football Hall of Fame.

West Hanningfield is a small village and civil parish in South Essex, England. It is about southeast of Chelmsford, the county town. The village is in the Chelmsford borough and part of the Rayleigh parliamentary constituency. It is north of Hanningfield Reservoir and surrounded by South Hanningfield, Stock, Rettendon, and East Hanningfield. It is also close to Chelmsford's suburbs of Galleywood and Great Baddow. The local pub is called the Three Compasses. There is also a primary school, village hall, and a hairdresser. Lord Hanningfield, a former Tory peer and ex-Conservative leader of Essex County Council, lives there. The village has a church named St Mary and St Edward. It is a Grade II* listed church from the 12th century, with changes in the 18th and 19th centuries. The tower, built around the 13th century, is made of timber and has recently dated timbers from 1382 to 1414. Bells from 1676 are inside, though not used now. The church is important historically, as noted by Whitechapel Bell Foundry.
Marie Dubois, born Claudine Lucie Pauline Huzé, was a French actress. She was born in Paris and passed away on October 15, 2014.

Charles Joseph Scarborough, born on April 9, 1963, is an American cable news host. He co-hosts "Morning Joe" on MSNBC with his wife Mika Brzezinski. He also hosted "Scarborough Country" on MSNBC. Before his work in cable news, he was a lawyer and a politician. He served in the U.S. House of Representatives from 1995 to 2001 as a Republican for Florida's 1st district. He has also worked as a visiting fellow at the Harvard Institute of Politics at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government. In 2011, he was named in the "Time" 100 as one of the most influential people in the world.

North Mississippi Allstars is an American southern rock/blues band from Hernando, Mississippi, United States. They were founded in 1996. The band has two brothers: Luther Dickinson (plays guitar, lap steel, and sings) and Cody Dickinson (plays drums, keyboards, and electric washboard, and sings). Duwayne Burnside, who used to play guitar for the band, is the son of R.L. Burnside and played on some of their songs.

Alaska Airlines is a big American airline based in Seattle, Washington. It is the fifth largest airline in the United States in terms of planes, passengers, and destinations. Alaska Airlines works with two smaller airlines, Horizon Air and SkyWest Airlines, to connect people mainly from the Pacific Northwest and Alaska to more than 100 places in the United States, Hawaii, Canada, Costa Rica, and Mexico. The airline has five main airports, with its main one in Seattle/Tacoma. Alaska Airlines is not part of any major airline group but plans to join Onward by the end of 2020. In 2020, it employed more than 16,000 people and was rated as having the highest customer satisfaction among traditional airlines for 12 years in a row.
The province of Bari was in the Apulia region of Italy. Its capital was Bari. It had an area and a population of 1,594,109 in 2005. On January 1, 2015, it became the Metropolitan City of Bari.

Gameshark is a brand name for video game cheat cartridges and other products for different video game systems and Windows computers. Currently, the brand is owned by Mad Catz. They made Gameshark products for Sony PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo consoles. Players use these cartridges or discs to put cheat codes into the console's memory. When the game loads, the selected cheats will work.

The 2018 FIFA World Cup qualification UEFA Group B was one of nine groups for the 2018 FIFA World Cup. It included six teams: Portugal, Switzerland, Hungary, Faroe Islands, Latvia, and Andorra. The first round draw was on July 25, 2015, at the Konstantinovsky Palace in St. Petersburg, Russia. Portugal won the group and qualified directly for the 2018 FIFA World Cup. Switzerland came second in the group and qualified for the play-offs. They won against Northern Ireland in the play-offs and also qualified for the tournament.

Jump blues is a fast version of blues music, usually played by small groups and featuring horns. It was popular in the 1940s and helped lead to rhythm and blues and rock and roll. People started listening to jump blues again in the 1990s during a swing music revival.

Edmond Mairé was a French labor union leader. He worked as the secretary general of the French Democratic Confederation of Labour from 1971 to 1988. He did not like strikes and believed workers should share work more equally.

A Hilbert space, named after David Hilbert, is a type of space that expands on the ideas of two- and three-dimensional space. It uses vectors and calculus in spaces with any number of dimensions—finite or infinite. In a Hilbert space, we can measure lengths and angles, and it is complete, meaning it has all the necessary elements for calculus techniques. These spaces are found naturally in math and physics, often as large spaces of functions. They were studied by David Hilbert, Erhard Schmidt, and Frigyes Riesz at the start of the 20th century. Hilbert spaces are very useful in solving partial differential equations, in quantum mechanics, signal processing, heat transfer, and thermodynamics. John von Neumann gave the name "Hilbert space" to this abstract idea. Hilbert spaces include function spaces, sequence spaces, and spaces of generalized functions. In these spaces, the Pythagorean theorem and parallelogram law still hold. We can specify elements by their coordinates, like using a set of axes in a plane. If the set is infinite, we think of it as a space of infinite sequences that add up to a finite number. Linear operators on Hilbert spaces are transformations that stretch the space in different perpendicular directions.
Annapolis is a place in Crawford County, Illinois, United States. It is northwest of Robinson. Annapolis has a post office with the zip code 62413. In 2010, its population was 55 people.

Nelson Lagoon is a small place in Aleutians East Borough, Alaska. Its population was 52 in 2010, down from 83 in 2000. Nelson Lagoon was set up around 1960 and is the newest community in the area. It is the only Aleut settlement near the Bering Sea. The community is located on the northern coast of the Alaska Peninsula. It sits on a narrow sand spit that separates the lagoon from the Bering Sea. Nelson Lagoon is in a good area for fishing salmon. The community got a dock, boat ramp, harbormaster’s office, and warehouse in the late 1990s. It has good places to keep boats and storage for equipment. There is also a state-owned runway that is 4,000 feet long, with lights, allowing planes to land regularly. In March 2016, Nelson Lagoon was covered in ash from a big eruption of nearby Mount Pavlof.

The president of the Republic of Crimea was the leader of the Crimean Republic, Ukraine from February 16, 1994, until March 17, 1995. The position was ended because it went against Ukraine's constitution. In the first round of voting for president on January 16, 1994, no one received enough votes, so a second round was held on January 30. Yury Meshkov, a supporter of Russia, won the election with 72.9% of the votes. He was the only person to be the president of the Republic of Crimea.

Susanna "Susan" Kohner, born on November 11, 1936, is an American former actress who acted in films and TV. She is famous for her role as Sarah Jane in "Imitation of Life" (1959). For this role, she was nominated for an Oscar and won a Golden Globe. In it, she played a light-skinned Black woman who "passed" for white as a young girl and young adult. After marrying menswear designer and writer John Weitz in 1964, Kohner stopped acting to focus on her family. Her two sons, Paul Weitz and Chris Weitz, became film directors, producers, screenwriters, and sometimes actors.

Euro disco, or eurodisco, is a type of dance music from Europe that developed from disco in the late 1970s. It mixes elements of pop and rock with a continuous dance style. Many euro disco songs have English lyrics, but the singers may speak a different language. Euro disco includes other styles like europop and eurodance. Popular sub-genres were space disco in the late 1970s and italo disco in the early 1980s. By 1986, the popularity of euro disco declined, giving way to electronic rock and hi-nrg. However, italo disco had a small revival in the late 1990s.

Quorn is a small town and train station in the Flinders Ranges of northern South Australia, northeast of Port Augusta. In, Quorn had 1,230 people, with 1,131 living in the town center. Quorn is where the Flinders Ranges Council is based. It is part of the Stuart state electoral district and the Grey federal division. Known for its pretty scenery and historic buildings, Quorn is a tourist destination and a place where movies are filmed. It is also the end of the Pichi Richi railway line.

St. Paul is a town in southern Madison County, Arkansas, United States. The 2010 census showed 113 people lived there. It is near the northwest Arkansas region. St. Paul was created in 1887 when a railroad reached that area.

Sometimes written as Gumpei Yokoi, he was a Japanese video game designer who worked for Nintendo for a long time. He created the Game & Watch handheld system. He also invented the cross-shaped control pad. Yokoi was the original designer of the Game Boy. He produced several popular and well-received video game series, including Metroid and Kid Icarus.

The use of toxic chemicals as weapons dates back to ancient times, but the first big use of chemical weapons happened during World War I. These chemicals were mainly used to make defenders feel scared, hurt, or kill them. The slow-moving nature of gas clouds made them very effective against entrenched enemies. Different types of weapons were used, from tear gas to deadly gases like phosgene, chlorine, and mustard gas. Gas warfare was a big part of World War I, which was the first global and total war of the 20th century. While gas could kill, it only caused about 90,000 deaths out of 1.3 million injured by gas attacks. Unlike other weapons of the time, it was possible to create countermeasures like gas masks. As the war went on and gas use increased, its effectiveness decreased. The widespread use of these chemical weapons, along with wartime advances in explosives, led some to call World War I "the chemist's war." The use of poison gas by all major countries during World War I was considered a war crime, as it broke the 1899 Hague Declaration and the 1907 Hague Convention, which banned the use of "poison or poisoned weapons." The widespread horror from gas use led to much less chemical weapon use during World War II.
Dows is a city in Franklin and Wright counties, in the state of Iowa. The population was 538 in the 2010 census.

Metropolis is a city in Illinois, near the Ohio River. It has about 6,537 people living there. Metropolis is the main city in Massac County. It is also part of a larger area called the Paducah, KY-IL micropolitan statistical area, located in southern Illinois.

Thomas Hodgkin was born on August 17, 1798, and died on April 5, 1866. He was a British doctor. People considered him one of the best pathologists of his time and a pioneer in stopping diseases before they start. He is famous for describing a disease called Hodgkin's disease in 1832. This disease affects the lymph nodes and blood. Hodgkin's work started the practice of pathologists being actively involved in patient care. He worked at Guy's Hospital with other doctors like Thomas Addison and Richard Bright.

Chaim Yisroel Belsky, born on August 22, 1938, and died on January 28, 2016, was an American rabbi. He was a leader in Orthodox and Haredi Judaism and lived in Brooklyn, New York. He taught at Yeshiva Torah Vodaas and was the rabbi of a network of summer camps run by Agudath Israel of America. For over 28 years, Belsky worked as a senior kashrut advisor for the OU. He was known for his deep knowledge of the Torah and his vast general knowledge. He was also familiar with practical matters. Some people criticized Belsky for comments he made about accusations of sexual abuse against a Jewish camp counselor.

Football is the most popular sport in Austria. The Austrian Football Association, called ÖFB, was formed in 1904 and is part of FIFA. Although football is very popular in Austria, the national team hasn't done well in tournaments. Austria first joined the European Championship in 2016 but did not advance. Before that, they were in the 2008 tournament, but were eliminated early. In the World Cup, Austria did better, finishing fourth in 1934 and third in 1954. They didn't enter the 1930 World Cup. They also missed out in 1966, 1970, 1974, 1986, 1994, 2002, 2006, 2010, and 2014. They withdrew from the 1938 and 1950 tournaments and were eliminated in the group stages in 1958, 1978, 1982, 1990, and 1998.

Milan Michálek, born on December 7, 1984, is a professional ice hockey player. He plays as a left winger and is currently not signed to any team. He last played for the Toronto Maple Leafs in the National Hockey League (NHL). Michálek was chosen sixth overall in the 2003 NHL Entry Draft by the San Jose Sharks. His older brother, Zbyněk Michálek, is also an ice hockey player. Zbyněk played as a defenceman and last played for the Arizona Coyotes.

Gemiliano "Mel" Campos López, Jr., was born on September 1, 1935, and died on January 1, 2017. He was a Filipino politician. He was the mayor of Manila from 1986 to 1987 and again from 1988 to 1992. He was also an assemblyman in the Batasang Pambansa, the Philippine parliament, from 1984 to 1986. Additionally, he was the former chairman of the Philippine Sports Commission.
Saint-Paul-Mont-Penit is a commune in Vendée, which is in the Pays de la Loire region in western France.

Hainan Airlines Co., Ltd. (HNA) is an airline based in Haikou, Hainan, People's Republic of China. It is the largest civilian airline with a majority state ownership, making it the fourth-largest airline in China by fleet size and the tenth-largest in Asia by passenger numbers. HNA operates scheduled domestic and international flights on 500 routes from Hainan and nine locations on the mainland. It also offers charter services. The main airport for HNA is Haikou Meilan International Airport, with hubs at Beijing Capital International Airport and Xi'an Xianyang International Airport. Several other cities are also important. Hainan Airlines has been awarded Skytrax 5-star status.

The 2000 municipal elections in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada, happened on October 21, 2000. Elections are held every four years since 1996. That year, Halifax, Dartmouth, Bedford, and Halifax County joined to form the Halifax Regional Municipality. The council has 24 members: one mayor and 23 councillors. All positions were up for election. In Nova Scotia, there are no political parties at the local level, so candidates run as independents.

Leonard Norman Cohen, born on September 21, 1934, and died on November 7, 2016, was a Canadian singer, songwriter, poet, and novelist. His work dealt with topics like religion, politics, loneliness, sadness, love, and death. Cohen was recognized with induction into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame, Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame, and Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. He was also honored as a Companion of the Order of Canada, a top civilian award in Canada. In 2011, he received the Prince of Asturias Awards for Literature and the Glenn Gould Prize. Cohen started his career as a poet and novelist in the 1950s and early 1960s. He began his music career in 1967 at the age of 33. His first album, "Songs of Leonard Cohen" (1967), followed by three folk music albums: "Songs from a Room" (1969), "Songs of Love and Hate" (1971), and "New Skin for the Old Ceremony" (1974). In 1977, his album "Death of a Ladies' Man," co-written and produced by Phil Spector, had a different sound from his previous music. In 1979, "Recent Songs" blended his acoustic style with jazz, Asian, and Mediterranean influences. "Hallelujah," one of his most famous songs, was first released on "Various Positions" in 1984. "I'm Your Man" in 1988 marked his move to synthesized productions. In 1992, "The Future" came out, with dark lyrics about social and political issues. In 2001, Cohen released "Ten New Songs," which was a big hit in Canada and Europe. His 11th album, "Dear Heather," was released in 2004. After successful tours between 2008 and 2013, Cohen released three albums in his last five years: "Old Ideas" (2012), "Popular Problems" (2014), and "You Want It Darker" (2016), the last album released three weeks before his death. A posthumous album titled "Thanks for the Dance" was released in November 2019, his fifteenth studio album.

Russian Mission is a city in Kusilvak Census Area, Alaska. A fur trading post of the Russian-American Company was there in 1842. After Alaska was bought by the United States in 1867, the city was officially named Russian Mission in the early 1900s. Alcohol cannot be sold there. In 2000, there were 296 people. By 2010, the population grew to 312.

Ningbo is a city in northeast Zhejiang province, People's Republic of China. It includes Ningbo urban districts, three smaller cities, and several rural counties, including islands in Hangzhou Bay and the East China Sea. The port of Ningbo–Zhoushan, spread across multiple locations, is one of the busiest in the world. Ningbo also has its own special state-planning status. In 2010, the entire area had about 7.6 million people, with 3.5 million in the built-up area of six urban districts. To the north, Hangzhou Bay separates Ningbo from Shanghai; to the east, Zhoushan is in the East China Sea; to the west and south, Ningbo borders Shaoxing and Taizhou. Ningbo is where Chiang Kai-shek, a Chinese nationalist leader, was born.

George Dureau, born on December 28, 1930, and died on April 7, 2014, was an American artist. His long career focused on charcoal sketches and black and white photographs of poor white and black athletes, dwarfs, and amputees. Robert Mapplethorpe was inspired by Dureau's amputee and dwarf photographs. These photos showed the figures as exposed, vulnerable, playful, and in need, and made them seem complex and completely human.

The Boutonne is a long river in western France, in the Deux-Sèvres and Charente-Maritime areas. It starts in a village called Chef-Boutonne. The river goes mostly southwest. It joins the Charente river near Cabariot.

Sewage, or domestic wastewater, is water used by a community. It includes graywater from sinks, bathtubs, showers, dishwashers, and washing machines, and blackwater from toilets and flushes. Soap and paper from toilets are also in it. Sewage goes into a sewer or an onsite facility. In a sewer, it may mix with rainwater. Most global wastewater isn't treated, causing water pollution, especially in poorer countries. In America, "sewage" and "wastewater" mean the same, while "sewerage" is about the pipes that carry sewage.
Athies is a town in the Pas-de-Calais department in northern France.

In Ireland, "gaeltacht" refers to districts where Irish is the main language spoken at home. The term can be used for individual or all such districts. The Irish government officially recognized these districts in the early 1920s, during the Irish Free State, after the Gaelic Revival. The goal was to help restore the Irish language. Today, it is clear that the gaeltacht is facing language decline. A 2015 study found that out of 155 electoral divisions in the gaeltacht, only 21 have Irish spoken daily by at least two-thirds of the population. Some experts say two-thirds is crucial for the language to survive.

Domecy-sur-le-Vault is a commune in Yonne, which is in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, in central France. It is famous for the Château de Domecy-sur-le-Vault.

Cozy Powell, born Colin Trevor Flooks, was an English rock drummer. He lived from December 29, 1947, to April 5, 1998. Powell played drums for many famous rock bands and artists, including the Jeff Beck Group, Rainbow, Gary Moore, Robert Plant, Brian May, Whitesnake, Emerson, Lake & Powell, and Black Sabbath. He appeared on at least 66 albums and contributed to many others. Many rock drummers say Powell was a big influence on their playing.
Strausberg is a town in Brandenburg, Germany. It is 30 km east of Berlin and has 25,594 people living there. Strausberg is the biggest town in the Märkisch-oderland district.

Shawn Colvin, born on January 10, 1956, is an American singer-songwriter. She has been making music solo for many years. Colvin is most famous for winning a Grammy in 1997 for her song "Sunny Came Home."

Jack Hobbs, known as Sir John Berry Hobbs, was born on December 16, 1882, and died on December 21, 1963. He was an English cricket player who played for Surrey from 1905 to 1934 and for England in 61 test matches between 1908 and 1930. Hobbs was called "the master" and is thought by experts to be one of the greatest batsmen in cricket history. He scored 61,760 runs and hit 199 centuries in first-class cricket. Hobbs batted right-handed and sometimes bowled medium-paced right-arm deliveries. He was also good at fielding, especially at the cover position. Born poor in 1882, Hobbs wanted to be a cricket player from a young age. His early batting was not good, but he improved suddenly in 1901 and caught the attention of local teams. In 1903, he joined Surrey with help from England batsman Tom Hayward. His reputation grew, and he scored 88 in his first-class debut and a century in his next match. Over the following seasons, he became a successful county player and made his test debut for England in 1908, scoring 83 in his first innings. Hobbs then scored three centuries against Australia in 1911-12, and critics said he was the world's best batsman. He played attacking, dynamic cricket until 1914. After serving in the Royal Flying Corps during World War I, he continued to be a good player when cricket returned in 1919. His career was troubled by appendicitis in 1921, but he returned to play more carefully and scored a lot in both test and domestic cricket until he retired. Some of his best innings were during this period. Hobbs succeeded because of his quick feet, ability to play many shots, and good ball placement. He was among the first batsmen to do well against difficult googly bowlers and adjusted his technique to meet new bowling styles. He was especially good on hard pitches. Hobbs was a successful opener, forming partnerships with Tom Hayward, Andy Sandham for Surrey, and Wilfred Rhodes and Herbert Sutcliffe for England. His partnership with Sutcliffe remains the best for the first wicket in test history. People thought highly of Hobbs, and he is still considered one of the best batsmen ever. Hobbs was married to Ada for 56 years and lived comfortably later in life from his Surrey salary, commercial deals, and profits from his sporting goods shop. After retiring from cricket, he worked in journalism. In 1953, he became the first professional cricketer to be knighted. He spent his later years caring for his wife and passed away in 1963 at the age of 81, just a few months after her.
Riceville is a city in Howard and Mitchell counties, in the state of Iowa, United States. According to the 2010 census, the population was 785.

A reasonable accommodation is a change made to a system to make it fair for someone based on their needs. These needs can be different. They might be related to religion, physical or mental health, emotions, school, or work. Laws often require these changes. Different countries have their own ways of providing accommodations. The United Nations uses this term in a document called the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. They say not making these changes is unfair. William John "Bulldog" Fairbairn was born on January 7, 1947. He was a Canadian professional ice hockey player who played as a right wing. Fairbairn played in the NHL for 10 seasons. Most of his career was with the New York Rangers. He also played for the Minnesota North Stars and the St. Louis Blues. He retired early in the 1978-79 NHL season. Fairbairn scored 162 goals in his career.

Rockville is a census-designated place and a village in the town of Vernon, Connecticut. It had 7,474 people living there in 2010. Rockville became a city in 1889. Since 1965, it has been part of Vernon.

The Central Bohemian region is an administrative area in the Czech Republic. It is located in the central part of Bohemia, the historical region of the Czech Republic. Prague, the capital city of the Czech Republic, is the administrative center of this region. However, Prague is not part of the region but is considered a separate region. The Central Bohemian region is in the center of Bohemia. It is the largest region in the Czech Republic, covering 11,014 km², which is almost 14% of the country's total area. This region surrounds Prague and shares borders with several other regions: the Liberec Region to the north, Hradec Králové Region to the northeast, Pardubice Region to the east, Vysočina Region to the southeast, South Bohemian Region to the south, Plzeň Region to the west, and Ústí nad Labem Region to the northwest.
Bournos is a commune in southwestern France. It is in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department.

The Berlin State Opera is a famous building on Unter den Linden Boulevard in the center of Berlin. It was built between 1741 and 1743 by Frederick the Great, following plans by Georg Wenzeslaus von Knobelsdorff in the Palladian style. During World War II, it was damaged by bombing. After the war, it was rebuilt from 1951 to 1955 as part of the Forum Fridericianum square. People also call it "Lindenoper." It is special because it is the first theater in a city that is a big, important, and standalone building itself.

Joseph Bonnel was a French football player who played as a midfielder. He was born on January 4, 1939, and died on February 13, 2018. Bonnel played for France in the 1966 FIFA World Cup. He scored 3 goals in that season.

Kieren John Perkins, OAM, was born on August 14, 1973. He is an Australian former competition swimmer. Perkins won four Olympic medals and held world records in three events. He was one of the best long-distance swimmers in the world. He won two Olympic gold medals in 1992 and 1996 for the 1500-meter freestyle event. He also won a silver medal in 2000.

Heidi Alexander was born on April 17, 1975. She is a British Labour Party politician. She works as the deputy mayor of London for transport under Sadiq Khan. She is also the deputy chair of transport for London. Alexander became a member of parliament (MP) for Lewisham East in 2010. She left her job as MP in May 2018 to join Sadiq Khan's team. In 2015, she became the shadow secretary of state for health. However, she left this job in June 2016.

Fernando Bernabé Agüero Rocha was born on June 11, 1917, in Managua, Nicaragua, and died on September 27, 2011. He was a Nicaraguan politician and the founder of the Social Conservative Party in 1988. In 1967, Agüero ran in the presidential election for the Conservative 1966 National Opposition Union (UNO) against the Somoza regime. His campaign faced violence when his political rally in Managua was attacked. In 1971, Agüero signed the Kupia Kumi pact with Anastasio Somoza Debayle.

Ahmed Osman, born on January 3, 1930, was Morocco's prime minister from November 2, 1972, to March 22, 1979. He was married to Princess Lalla Nuzha from 1964 to 1977. Lalla Nuzha is the sister of King Hassan II of Morocco. Ahmed Osman founded the National Rally of Independents. He worked as the secretary general of the Ministry of National Defence from 1959 to 1961. From 1961 to 1962, he was the ambassador to the Federal Republic of Germany. From 1967 to 1972, he was the ambassador to the United States. He served as the under secretary of the Ministry of Mines and Industry from 1962 to 1964. From 1964 to 1967, he was the president of the Moroccan General Navigation Company. He was prime minister from 1972 to 1979. After 1977, he became the president of the National Rally of Independents. He was also the president of the National Assembly from 1984 to 1992.

Binoculars or field glasses are two telescopes next to each other, pointed in the same direction. They help you see distant objects while using both eyes, called binocular vision. Most binoculars are held with both hands, but they come in different sizes, from small ones like opera glasses to larger, heavy models mounted on pedestals. Unlike a single-telescope (monocular) device, binoculars provide a 3D image. For objects that are closer, the two views from each eye, seen from slightly different angles, give a sense of depth.

Tondiarpet taluk is a part of the city district of Chennai, in Tamil Nadu, India. It was created in December 2013 from parts of the old Fort-Tondiarpet taluk. It includes the Tondiarpet neighborhood.

Australian convict sites are a world heritage property. There are 11 remaining penal sites built during the 18th and 19th centuries in Britain. These sites are located on fertile coastal areas in Sydney, Tasmania, Norfolk Island, and Fremantle. They represent "the best surviving examples of large-scale convict transportation and the colonial expansion of European powers through the use of convicts." These sites were first added to the Australian national heritage list before being nominated for the world heritage list. Preparations began in 1995. The nomination was first made in January 2008 but was unsuccessful. The nomination was then reworked.
Brooks County is the name of two counties in the United States.

Joel Murray was born on April 17, 1963. He is an American actor. He has played important roles in TV shows like "Mad Men," "Grand," "Love & War," "Dharma and Greg," and "Shameless." He has also acted in movies such as "God Bless America" and "Monsters University."
Serrières-de-Briord is a commune in eastern France. It is in the Ain department.

The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks is an action-adventure game made by Nintendo for the Nintendo DS. It was part of the Legend of Zelda series and came out in December 2009. Later, it was released on the Wii U Virtual Console in October 2016. Like other games in the series, Spirit Tracks has a cartoon-like art style. The main character, Link, travels around the game world using a steam train with a cannon, similar to how he used a steamboat in Phantom Hourglass. Players can also control phantoms and play the spirit flute. Spirit Tracks is special because it has different endings based on player choices, which affect Link's final outcome.

William Frederick Fraser was born on July 8, 1960, and passed away on June 28, 2019. He was from Northern Ireland and worked to help people hurt by violence from Irish republican groups. Fraser started and led a group called Families Acting for Innocent Relatives (FAIR). He was also a leader in the Love Ulster campaign and the Belfast city hall flag protests. In 2019, journalist Mandy McAuley said that the Ulster Defence Association got weapons from the Ulster Resistance in the late 1980s, and Fraser was in charge of these supplies. McAuley said she had evidence from the police and confirmed by others. The weapons connected to at least 70 people killed by paramilitary groups.

The Terminal is a 2004 American movie. Steven Spielberg directed it, and Tom Hanks, Catherine Zeta-Jones, and Stanley Tucci are in the film. The story is about a man from Eastern Europe who gets stuck in John F. Kennedy Airport in New York. He can't enter the United States, and he can't go back to his country because of a military change. The movie is partly based on a true story about someone named Mehran Karimi Nasseri who stayed in a Paris airport for 18 years. After finishing another film, Steven Spielberg chose to make this movie because he wanted to create something that could make people laugh and feel good. Because no airport was willing to help, they built a whole set inside a hangar. Most of the outside scenes were filmed at Montreal's airport. The movie came out in North America on June 18, 2004. People had mixed feelings about it, but it made a lot of money, earning $77.9 million in the U.S. and $219.4 million worldwide.

Ringmaster is the second album by the American hip hop group Insane Clown Posse. It was released on March 8, 1994, by Psychopathic Records. They recorded it in 1993 at the Tempermill studio. This album is part of their "Dark Carnival" story, where the ringmaster, who judges your soul in the afterlife, comes from your own bad actions. The album was mostly created by producer Mike E. Clark. It also includes guest appearances by Capitol E and Jumpsteady. In 1998, Island Records re-released the album. It got a gold certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). The original version also got a gold certification in 2004.

Cristian Eugen Chivu, born on October 26, 1980, is a former Romanian football player. He usually played as a left back but could also play as a central defender. He started his career with his hometown club FCM Reșița and then moved to FC Universitatea Craiova in 1998. A year later, he joined Ajax in the Netherlands. As captain at Ajax, he inspired an €18 million transfer to Roma in 2003. In his last four seasons at Roma, he won the Coppa Italia. Chivu then moved to Internazionale, where he spent the rest of his career until retiring in 2014. At Internazionale, he won the Italian league, the domestic cup, and the UEFA Champions League in 2010. He played 75 times for the Romanian national team between 1999 and 2010, and was part of Romania's teams for the UEFA European Championships in 2000 and 2008. After retiring, he became a football commentator for Italian TV stations Sky Sport and Fox Sports. He is also a technical observer for UEFA.

Hammurabi was the sixth king of the first Babylonian dynasty, belonging to the Amorite tribe. He ruled from around 1792 BC to 1750 BC (based on the middle chronology). His father, Sin-muballit, gave up the throne because he was not feeling well. During Hammurabi's reign, he conquered Elam and the city-states of Larsa, Eshnunna, and Mari. He forced Ishme-dagan I, the king of Assyria, and his son Mut-ashkur, to pay tribute. As a result, almost all of Mesopotamia was ruled by Babylon. Hammurabi is famous for creating the Code of Hammurabi. He said he got this from Shamash, the Babylonian god of justice. Unlike earlier Sumerian law codes, such as the Code of Ur-Nammu, which focused on helping the victim, Hammurabi’s code focused more on punishing the person who did the crime. It had specific punishments for each crime and was one of the first to assume people were innocent until proven guilty. The punishments were very strict by today's standards, but they were meant to limit revenge by the wronged person. Hammurabi was considered a god during his lifetime. After he died, he was seen as a great conqueror who spread civilization and made everyone respect Marduk, the god of Babylon. His military achievements were later less emphasized, and he was mainly remembered as a fair lawgiver. For ancient Mesopotamians, his rule was a standard for the past. Even after his empire fell, he was still seen as a good ruler, and many kings claimed him as an ancestor. Hammurabi was rediscovered by archaeologists in the late 1800s and is now seen as important in the history of law.

Townsville is a city on the northeast coast of Queensland, Australia. It's the biggest city north of the Sunshine Coast with 180,820 people as of June 2018. Locals call it the unofficial capital of North Queensland. Townsville has many government and business offices. It's in the dry tropics region, near the Great Barrier Reef. Townsville is a big industrial city with a large zinc refinery, a nickel refinery, and other similar activities. The port is growing to handle bigger ships from Asia and the world's largest passenger ships. It's important due to its closeness to Asia and countries like China. People like to visit "The Strand," a long tropical beach, and Riverway, a park by Ross River. They can see many sea animals at Reef HQ, a big tropical aquarium. The Museum of Tropical Queensland shows relics from a sunken British warship. Castle Hill, or Cootharinga, is a big hill and popular for exercise. The town also has a sports reserve and Magnetic Island, a large nearby island mostly a national park.

A resistance movement is when some people in a country try to oppose the government or an occupier and cause disruption. They might use peaceful actions, like protests, or force, like weapons. In some cases, like in Norway during World War II, resistance groups can use both methods. The legal status of armed resistance has been debated since 1899, when international laws of war were first codified. The 1899 Hague Convention included a clause to resolve the dispute. More recently, the 1977 Geneva Convention protocols recognized armed conflicts against colonial rule, but the language is unclear. Depending on a government's view, a resistance movement can be seen as either a terrorist group or a legitimate fight against occupation. This is a political decision.

Schifflange is a town in southwestern Luxembourg. It is part of the canton of Esch-sur-Alzette. The town of Schifflange, located in the west of the commune, has 9,332 people living there. Schifflange became a separate commune on August 15, 1876, by detaching from the commune of Esch-sur-Alzette. The law to create Schifflange was passed on July 6, 1876.

A corroboree is a general term for a meeting of Australian Aboriginal peoples. It can be a sacred ceremony, a festive celebration, or related to war. The word came from the local Dharug language. Usually, it includes dance, music, costumes, and body decoration. Today, it can describe any large, noisy gathering.

Holley is a small community in Santa Rosa County, Florida. As of the 2019 census, it has 2,425 people. A road called Florida State Road 87 goes through Holley. Almost everyone considers Holley a neighborhood in the larger community of Navarre, Florida. Holley and Navarre are part of the same census area and use the same fire and water systems. They also share an election area. Holley has major neighborhoods on Gordon Evans Road, Nelson Street, and Bob Tolbert Road. These areas are growing the fastest.

The new academy prize in literature was created in 2018 instead of the Nobel Prize in Literature, which was not given that year and delayed until 2019. The winner was announced on October 12, 2018. The new academy stopped existing in December 2018. They asked people around the world to vote for 47 candidates chosen by Swedish librarians. The four finalists were Maryse Condé, Neil Gaiman, Haruki Murakami, and Kim Thúy. On September 17, 2018, Murakami asked to be removed from the competition because he wanted to focus on writing without media attention. The new academy prize in literature went to Maryse Condé. In 2018, a non-profit organization called the new academy was formed to give the prize, not connected to the Nobel Foundation or the Swedish Academy.

Mahmoud Abdelrazek Hassan Fadlala, known as Shikabala, was born on March 5, 1986. He is an Egyptian footballer who plays for Zamalek in the Egyptian Premier League and the Egypt national team. Shikabala started playing for Zamalek when he was young and has been with the club for many years. He is considered one of Zamalek's legends. He has also played for other clubs, like PAOK and Sporting CP. Shikabala mainly plays as a right-winger but can also play as a central attacking midfielder or a left winger.
Guerbigny is a commune in the Somme department in Hauts-de-France in northern France.

Merrimack County is in the state of New Hampshire, U.S. As of 2010, it had 146, 445 people, making it the third largest county in New Hampshire. Its main city is Concord, which is also the capital of New Hampshire. Merrimack County was formed in 1823 from parts of Hillsborough and Rockingham counties. It is named after the Merrimack River. Merrimack County includes the Concord, NH micropolitan area, which is part of the Boston-Worcester-Providence, MA-RI-NH-CT combined statistical area. In 2010, the center of New Hampshire's population was in Merrimack County, specifically in the town of Pembroke.

"Time of the Season" is a song by the British rock band The Zombies. It is from their 1968 album "Odessey and Oracle." The song was written by Rod Argent, who played keyboards. They recorded it in August 1967 at Abbey Road Studios. Over a year after it came out, the song became popular in the United States. It reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and number one on the Cashbox chart. It is now one of The Zombies' most famous songs.

Stagecoach is a transport company based in Perth, Scotland. It runs buses and coaches, as well as a tram service in the United Kingdom. It used to operate in many places around the world, including Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and Oceania. Its stock is listed on the London Stock Exchange.

State of Georgia is an American TV show. It stars Raven-Symoné, Majandra Delfino, and Loretta Devine. The show is a half-hour, multi-camera comedy. Raven-Symoné plays Georgia, an actress with a big personality. Her best friend Jo, played by Majandra Delfino, is a science geek. They live in New York City and try to do well in their careers and personal lives. The show was on ABC Family from June 29 to August 17, 2011. The first episode had 1.32 million people watching. On September 16, 2011, ABC Family stopped the show because not many people watched it.

Roman Stanley Gribbs was an American politician born on December 29, 1925, and died on April 5, 2016. He was the mayor of Detroit from 1970 to 1974. Later, he became a judge on the Michigan Court of Appeals. Gribbs was the last mayor of Detroit who was white, as the city was becoming mostly black. Detroit elected Mike Duggan as mayor in 2013.

Loretta Lynn, born April 14, 1932, is an American country music singer and songwriter. She has many gold albums and is famous for songs like "You Ain't Woman Enough (To Take My Man)," "Don't Come Home a-Drinking (With Lovin' on Your Mind)," "One's on the Way," "Fist City," and "Coal Miner's Daughter." She also starred in the 1980 film based on her life. Lynn has won many awards, including from the Country Music Association and the Academy of Country Music. She is the most awarded female country recording artist and the only female ACM artist of the decade (1970s). She has 24 number one hit singles and 11 number one albums. Lynn still tours, performs at the Grand Ole Opry, and releases new albums.

Chiang Ching-kuo, born on April 27, 1910, and died on January 13, 1988, was a Taiwanese politician. He was the son of Chiang Kai-shek, who was a former president. Ching-kuo held many important positions in the government of the Republic of China. He was the Premier from 1972 to 1978 and became the President from 1978 until his death. Ching-kuo was sent to study in the Soviet Union in 1925 when he was a teenager. His father’s party and the Communist Party were allies then. He studied there but was sent to work in a steel factory in the Ural Mountains after the alliance ended. There, he married Faina Vakhreva. When war between China and Japan was likely in 1937, they were sent to China. His father trusted him more during the war and gave him important tasks, including handling administration. After Japan surrendered, Ching-kuo cleaned up corruption in Shanghai. The Communist victory in 1949 forced the Chiangs and their government to move to Taiwan. Ching-kuo was in charge of the secret police from 1965 until 1965, where he used arrests and torture to maintain control. Later, he became the Minister of Defense (1965-1969), Vice-Premier (1969-1972), and then Premier (1972-1978). After his father died in 1975, he became the chairman of the Nationalist Party and was elected President in 1978 and again in 1984. During his time as President, the government of the Republic of China became less strict and more open to different opinions. Ching-kuo also tried to win the support of people from Taiwan, not just those who had come from mainland China after the war. Towards the end of his life, he eased restrictions on the media and allowed more people from Taiwan to hold important positions, including his successor, Lee Teng-hui.

Maizery was a former commune in the Moselle department, located in northeastern France. On June 1, 2016, it became part of a new commune called Colligny-Maizery. In 2017, the population of Maizery was 182 people.

Squash is a game played with a ball and racquets in a court with four walls. Two players take turns hitting the ball against the walls. The goal is to make the ball bounce in a way that the opponent can't return it. Around 20 million people play squash regularly in over 185 countries. A group called the World Squash Federation oversees the sport. They are recognized by the International Olympic Committee, but squash is not in the Olympic Games yet. People are still trying to get it included in future Olympics.

The Eastern Chalukyas, also called the Chalukyas of Vengi, were a dynasty that ruled parts of South India from the 7th to the 12th centuries. They began as governors of the Chalukyas of Badami in the Deccan region. Later, they became independent rulers and controlled the Vengi area in Andhra Pradesh until 1189 CE. They ruled the region for the Cholas for some time before 1189. Their first capital was Vengi (now Pedavegi near Eluru), and later moved to Rajamahendravaram (now Rajahmundry). During their rule, they were often involved in wars with the Cholas and Western Chalukyas over control of Vengi. For about five centuries, Vengi was unified and saw the growth of Telugu culture, literature, poetry, and art, especially in the later part of their rule.

Sidney Sheldon was an American writer, director, and producer. He was important in the 1930s, working on Broadway plays and then in movies. He wrote a successful comedy called "The Bachelor and the Bobby-Soxer" in 1947, which won him an Oscar in 1948. Sheldon later worked in television. He created popular shows like "The Patty Duke Show" (1963-1966), "I Dream of Jeannie" (1965-1970), and "Hart to Hart" (1979-1984). At age 50, he started writing best-selling romantic suspense novels, including "Master of the Game" (1982), "The Other Side of Midnight" (1973), and "Rage of Angels" (1980). His 18 novels sold over 300 million copies in 51 languages. Sheldon is often listed among the top ten best-selling fiction writers of all time.

Rivers that join other rivers are listed based on how close their meeting points are to the sea. Rivers like the Meuse, which don't flow directly through Germany, are mentioned because they have German tributaries. These rivers are shown in italics. Only rivers longer than a certain length are included. An alphabetical list of all German rivers with Wikipedia articles is at the end.
