The University of Costa Rica, or UCR, is a public university in Costa Rica, Central America. Its main campus, Ciudad Universitaria Rodrigo Facio, is in San Pedro Montes de Oca, San José province. It is the oldest and biggest university in Costa Rica, starting as Universidad de Santo Tomás in 1843. UCR is also the most important research university in the country and Central America. It is one of the most prestigious and recognized in Latin America. About 45,000 students attend UCR each year.

On a sailing boat, a forestay is a piece of strong rope or wire that holds the mast from moving backward. It attaches either at the very top of the mast or, in some cases, between 1/8 and 1/4 of the way down from the top. The other end of the forestay connects to the front part of the boat. Often, a sail called a jib or genoa is attached to the forestay. In a cutter rig, multiple jibs can be on stays in front of the forestay, possibly going from the mast to the bow. The sail on the forestay is then called a staysail or stays'l. Modern yachts might have a forestay made of stainless steel wire, a solid stainless steel rod, carbon rod, or ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene like spectra or dyneema. High-performance racing boats use these materials. Older ships or cutters might use galvanized wire or natural fibers.

A video game developer makes video games, like a software developer but focuses just on games. They can work alone or in big teams with people doing different jobs, such as coding, designing, making art, and testing. Many game developers get help from companies that provide money and marketing. Self-employed developers who make their own games are called indie developers. Some developers make games for specific consoles, like the Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, or PlayStation 4. Others make games for computers and mobile devices too. Developers might specialize in certain types of games, such as role-playing games or first-person shooters. Some also help move games from one system to another or change the languages of games. Occasionally, they do regular software development work. Many game publishers have their own development teams, like EA Canada or Square Enix. While they still call these teams publishers, they mainly focus on developing games. Some developers work on their own, like Bungie, which made the Halo series for Xbox.

Paul Gust Vallas, born on June 10, 1953, is an American politician. He used to be the superintendent of the Bridgeport public schools and the Recovery School District of Louisiana. He was also the CEO of the School District of Philadelphia and the Chicago Public Schools. Additionally, he was the budget director for the city of Chicago. In 2002, Vallas tried but failed to become the Democratic governor of Illinois. He then ran for lieutenant governor of Illinois with Pat Quinn in 2014 but lost to Bruce Rauner and Evelyn Sanguinetti, who were from the Republican party. In 2019, Vallas tried to become the mayor of Chicago. He came in ninth place out of fourteen candidates with 5.43% of the vote. Since he didn't advance to the second round, he supported Lori Lightfoot.

Devonté Hynes, born David Joseph Michael Hynes on December 23, 1985, is an English singer, songwriter, record producer, and director. He was in a band called Test Icicles from 2004 to 2006. Hynes played guitar, synth, and sometimes sang. They made one album in 2005. Later, he released two solo albums as Lightspeed Champion. Then, from 2008 to 2018, he made four albums as Blood Orange. Hynes has also written songs or produced for artists like Tinashe, Solange Knowles, Connan Mockasin, Tei Shi, Sky Ferreira, FKA Twigs, HAIM, Florence and the Machine, Carly Rae Jepsen, Diana Vickers, The Chemical Brothers, Kylie Minogue, ASAP Rocky, Mac Miller, Blondie, and Mariah Carey.

James Henry Hammond was born on November 15, 1807, and died on November 13, 1864. He was an attorney, politician, and planter from South Carolina. Hammond was a U.S. representative from 1835 to 1836. He was South Carolina's 60th governor from 1842 to 1844. Later, he served as a U.S. senator from 1857 to 1860. He was known as a strong supporter of slavery before the American Civil War. Hammond owned a lot of property through his marriage. He had 22 square miles of land, several plantations, and houses. He also owned over 300 slaves. Through his wife's family, he was related to Wade Hampton II and was an uncle to Wade Hampton III. Hammond faced a scandal when it was discovered that he had raped four teenage nieces of Wade Hampton II. This was a close family connection. The scandal initially seemed to hurt Hammond's political career, but he was later elected to the U.S. Senate.

Shawnee is a city in Pottawatomie County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, it had 29,857 people, up 4.9% from 28,692 in 2000. Shawnee is part of the Oklahoma City-Shawnee area. It is also the main city in the Shawnee micropolitan area. Shawnee is about 45 minutes east of downtown Oklahoma City. To the east and northeast, it is 112 miles from the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System, which connects to the Gulf of Mexico.

Pleasant Hill is a city in Polk County, Iowa, United States. According to the 2010 census, its population was 8,785. It is part of the Des Moines–West Des Moines metropolitan area. In July 2005, Pleasant Hill got a zip code, which is 50327.

The monarchy in Belgium is a constitutional, hereditary, and popular system. The current king or queen is called the "King or Queen of the Belgians." The king or queen serves as the head of state. Belgium has had seven kings or queens since 1830. The current king, Philippe, became the king on July 21, 2013, after his father stepped down.

Hoyerswerda is a big town in the Bautzen district in Saxony, Germany. It is in the Upper Lusatia region where some people speak Sorbian and German. Hoyerswerda has two parts: the old town and the new town. The old town has many old houses and is the historical center. The new town is newer and colorful. Before renovations, many prefab apartment buildings were there. The town has many lakes, marshes, and waterways around it because it's in Lusatia. This attracts holidaymakers. It's also good for cyclists and inline skaters, who can use new paths that go through the lakes.

Aurelius Ambrosius, known as Ambrose in English (397), was a bishop of Milan, theologian, and one of the most influential church leaders in the 4th century. Ambrose became bishop unexpectedly in 374 after people chose him. As bishop, he fought against arianism and tried to help the emperor Theodosius I deal with Magnus Maximus. Ambrose is credited with promoting "antiphonal chant," a singing style where choir sides take turns. He also wrote "Veni Redemptor Gentium," an Advent hymn. Ambrose greatly influenced Augustine of Hippo. Western Christianity considers him one of its four main church teachers. The Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox Church, Anglican Church, and some Lutheran groups believe Ambrose is a saint. He is also seen as the patron saint of Milan.
Burgistein is a town in the Thun area of the Bern canton in Switzerland.
Kellinghusen is a town in the Steinburg district, which is in Schleswig-Holstein.

Cearbhall Ó Dálaigh was born on February 12, 1911, and passed away on March 21, 1978. He was an Irish politician, judge, and lawyer. He became the fifth president of Ireland from December 1974 to October 1976. Before that, from 1973 to 1974, he worked at the European Court of Justice. From 1961 to 1973, he was the Chief Justice of Ireland. He was also a Supreme Court judge from 1953 to 1973 and Attorney General of Ireland from 1946 to 1948, and again from 1951 to 1953. Sometimes, his name is written as Carroll O'Daly, and he used this spelling during his legal career.

The Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARM) was a special region in the Philippines. It covered five mainly Muslim provinces: Basilan (excluding Isabela City), Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi. ARM had its own government. Its main city was Cotabato, though it wasn't part of ARM's area. The region was renamed to Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao in 2012. In 2018, President Rodrigo Duterte signed a new law, the Bangsamoro Organic Law (BOL), creating the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao. ARM ended officially after BOL was ratified on January 25, 2019, and was replaced by BARM.
Michel Jeury, born on January 23, 1934, and died on January 9, 2015, was a French writer of science fiction. He was famous in the 1970s. He also wrote under the name Albert Higon.

The flag of Myanmar, also known as Burma, was adopted on October 21, 2010. This new flag replaced the one used since 1974. The flag was introduced along with changes to the country's name, as outlined in the 2008 constitution. The flag has three horizontal stripes: yellow, green, and red, with a white five-pointed star in the middle. The yellow stripe means solidarity, the green one means peace and tranquility, and the red one means courage and decisiveness.

The Song of Songs, also known as the Song of Solomon or Canticles, is a special book found in the Ketuvim, or Writings, part of the Tanakh. It is in the Old Testament too. Unlike other books in the Hebrew Bible, it does not talk about laws or covenants or the God of Israel. It also does not teach wisdom like Proverbs or Ecclesiastes. Instead, it talks about love between two people, celebrating their desire and joy in each other. The book includes the voices of the two lovers praising and longing for each other. In Jerusalem, women join as a chorus, acting like an audience for the lovers' romantic scenes. This helps the readers to connect better. In modern Judaism, it is read on Sabbath during Passover, which celebrates the start of the harvest and also remembers leaving Egypt. In Jewish tradition, it is seen as a story about God's relationship with Israel. Christians see it as an allegory of Christ and his church.

The G7 is a group of seven major developed countries: Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. These countries are the largest economies in the world according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF). In 2018, these seven countries made up 58% of the world's total wealth ($317 trillion) and over 46% of the global GDP based on current prices. They also represented more than 32% of the global GDP when measured by purchasing power. The European Union is invited to join G7 meetings. Every year, the G7 holds a summit with the leaders from these seven countries.
Ayub Awista (born around 1979) is an Afghan writer who started the Afghan Youth Sports Exchange in the United States.
Page County is in Iowa, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 15, 932 people. Clarinda is the county seat. The county was named after Captain John Page, who was badly hurt in the Battle of Palo Alto.

Orestes "Minnie" Miñoso (born Saturnino Orestes Armas Miñoso Arrieta) was a professional baseball player from Cuba. He started playing in the Negro Leagues in 1946 and became an All-Star third baseman for the New York Cubans. In 1949, he joined the Cleveland Indians of Major League Baseball and later played for the Chicago White Sox, becoming an All-Star left fielder. Miñoso was the first black Cuban in the major leagues and the first black player for the White Sox. As a rookie in 1951, he played in an MLB All-Star game. He was an American League All-Star for seven seasons and won three Gold Gloves in his 30s. Miñoso batted over.300 for eight seasons and led the league in triples and stolen bases three times each. He also led in hits, doubles, and total bases once each. Willie Mays and Miñoso are credited with bringing speed back as an offensive weapon in the 1950s. Miñoso was very good at getting on base, leading the American League in times hit by pitch ten times. He was also a great defensive player, leading left fielders in assists six times and in putouts and double plays four times each. He was popular and dynamic, helping the White Sox become one of the best teams in the 1950s and 1960s. Miñoso set the White Sox record for home runs from 1956 to 1974. He left the major leagues after the 1964 season but continued to play and manage in Mexico until 1973. He came back to the White Sox as a coach and made brief appearances in 1976 and 1980. He was the third player to get a hit after 50 and the second to play in the majors in five decades. Miñoso's White Sox uniform number 9 was retired in 1983, and a statue of him was unveiled at U.S. Cellular Field in 2004. He was elected to the Cuban Baseball Hall of Fame in 1983 and the Mexican Professional Baseball Hall of Fame in 1996. In 2014, Miñoso was considered for the National Baseball Hall of Fame but was not elected.

Maaloula, or Maʿlūlā, is a town in Syria. It is in the Rif Dimashq governorate. Maaloula is about 56 kilometers northeast of Damascus. The town sits in the mountains, more than 1,500 meters above sea level. It is famous because people still speak Western Neo-Aramaic there. Two nearby villages, Jubb'adin and Bakhah, also have this ancient language.

Barrie is a city in central Ontario, Canada, near Lake Simcoe. It's a separate city from Simcoe County but part of it. Barrie is in a historically important area called Huronia and is part of a busy region called the Greater Golden Horseshoe. In 2016, Barrie had about 141,000 people, and the larger area had about 197,000. Barrie grew a lot in recent years because people from Toronto moved there to live. They like it because houses are cheaper, and there are good jobs. Barrie has train service to Toronto. Barrie is north of Toronto, northeast of Detroit, and west of Ottawa. It's easy to get to other big places. The city was first settled during the War of 1812 as a supply area. It was named after Sir Robert Barrie in the 1830s. Barrie grew quickly in the 1980s and 1990s, with the population tripling. In the late 1980s, there were 38,000 people, and by 2006, there were about 128,000. Now, Barrie is a popular place to visit because of its beaches and nearby ski areas. It's called the 'gateway to cottage country'. The city has different types of jobs, like education, healthcare, technology, and making things. The biggest employer is the Royal Victoria Regional Health Centre, with nearly 3,000 workers. There are also many shops in Barrie. Barrie's weather is cold and snowy in winter, with January temperatures around zero. In summer, it's hot and humid, with July temperatures around 30 degrees.
Lie Sang Bong is a Korean fashion designer. He has designed clothes for singers like Beyoncé, Rihanna, Lady Gaga, and Lindsay Lohan.

The River Shannon is the longest river in Ireland. It covers an area of one-fifth of Ireland's total land. The river separates the western part of Ireland (mainly Connacht) from the eastern and southern parts (Leinster and most of Munster). County Clare, which is west of the Shannon but part of Munster, is an exception. The Shannon acts as a significant natural barrier, with fewer than thirty-five places to cross between Limerick City in the south and Dowra in the north. The river is named after "Sionna," a Celtic goddess. The Shannon has been a crucial waterway since ancient times, first mapped by Ptolemy, a Greek-Egyptian geographer. The river flows south from a place called Shannon Pot in County Cavan, then turns west and empties into the Atlantic Ocean through a long estuary. Limerick City is where freshwater from the river meets salty water from the estuary. East of Limerick, the Shannon becomes tidal up to the base of the Ardnacrusha dam.
Faverolles is a commune in Aisne, which is in Hauts-de-France in northern France.

Irma Schultz Keller, born on October 1, 1965, is a Swedish actress and pop singer. She has acted in many Swedish movies and TV shows. She also appeared in American productions like a horror movie called "The Resurrection of Michael Myers Part 2" and a miniseries called "Xerxes." Keller studied at the Swedish National Academy of Mime and Acting and graduated in 1999. On March 3, 2007, Irma and Uno Svenningsson performed the song "God Morgen" in Melodifestivalen 2007. They performed as a duo called Uno & Irma and moved to the second chance round. However, they lost to Sonja Alden in the first round of voting and were eliminated from the contest.
Afrodisiac can mean: A substance or food believed to increase sexual desire.

The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature scale created by physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit in 1724. It uses the degree Fahrenheit (symbol: °F) as its unit. Fahrenheit set 0°F as the freezing point of a brine made from water, ice, and ammonium chloride. He estimated the average human body temperature at 96°F, which is about 2.6°F less than today's value. He also set 32°F as the temperature of ice water. Now, the Fahrenheit scale is officially defined by freezing and boiling points of water: 32°F for ice and 212°F for boiling water, both at sea level and under standard pressure. Fahrenheit was the first widely used standardized temperature scale, but its use is now limited. It is the official scale in the United States, its territories, and some other countries like Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Marshall Islands. In some British overseas territories, both Fahrenheit and Celsius are used. The United Kingdom uses both scales occasionally. Most countries now use Celsius, renamed from the centigrade scale in 1948 to honor Anders Celsius.

Diana Serra Cary, also known as Baby Peggy, was born Peggy-Jean Montgomery on October 29, 1918, and passed away on February 24, 2020. She was an American child actress, vaudevillian, author, and silent film historian. Baby Peggy was one of the most famous child stars of Hollywood during the silent film era, alongside Jackie Coogan and Baby Marie. She starred in over 150 short films from 1921 to 1923 for the Century Film Corporation. By 1922, she got more than 1.2 million letters from fans. In 1924, she earned $1.5 million a year, making her the "million dollar baby." However, she later became poor and worked as an extra in the 1930s. Later in life, she wrote books and became a historian of silent films. She also supported the rights of child actors.

In 1685, King James II met Chinese man Michael Shen Fu-tsung during his visit to England. The king liked Michael so much that he asked Godfrey Kneller to paint his portrait, which was put in the king's bedroom. This painting is still at Windsor Castle. Michael Shen Fu-tsung also visited Oxford, helping to organize the Chinese books at the Bodleian Library. In 1681, Michael left for Europe with Philippe Couplet, a Jesuit, to promote their mission and meet Pope Innocent XI. Couplet planned to take five Chinese men, including Michael and Wu Li, to join him. However, only Michael and another young man left with Couplet. They had a delay in Batavia, and only Michael continued with Couplet on his journey. Michael's meeting with King James II was possible because the king was a Roman Catholic and Jesuits were welcome at court. In 1688, King James II was overthrown by William III, who was Protestant. This change meant their meeting could not have happened otherwise. Despite this, the encounter resulted in a famous painting, "The Chinese Convert," by Godfrey Kneller.

Knott's Berry Farm is a theme park in Buena Park, California, run by Cedar Fair. In 2018, it was the twelfth-most-visited park in North America, with about 4 million visitors a year. The park has 40 rides, like roller coasters, family rides, dark rides, and water rides. Knott's Berry Farm began in the 1920s as a roadside berry stand owned by Walter Knott. By the 1940s, a restaurant, shops, and other attractions were added for more visitors, including a fake ghost town. Over the next few decades, the place changed into a modern amusement park, and in 1968, they started charging for entry. In 1997, Cedar Fair bought the park for $300 million. Two years earlier, in 1995, Knott's food business was bought by Conagra, Inc.
Ahmed Ben Bella was an Algerian politician, soldier, and revolutionary. He was born on December 25, 1916, and died on April 11, 2012. He served as Algeria's first president from 1963 to 1965.
Enrique Floriano Millán was born on October 9, 1982, in Lorca, Murcia. He is a swimmer from Spain. Enrique has vision impairment and swims in B2/S12 category.

Suvā, the capital and biggest city in Fiji, is on the southeast coast of Viti Levu, in the Rewa Province. In 1877, Suva became the capital because the old European settlement, Levuka, was too small. In 1882, the government moved from Levuka to Suva. In 2017, the city had 93,970 people. When including nearby areas, the greater Suva area had 185,913 people. Together, Suva and nearby towns like Lami, Nasilu, and Nausori had about 330,000 people, which is more than one-third of Fiji's population. Suva is very important for politics, business, and culture in Fiji. It's also a big center for business and culture in the South Pacific. Many big companies and international organizations have their offices there. Suva also has a lively arts and fashion scene.

In the United States, state courts handle most civil and criminal cases. They have jurisdiction over disputes connected to a U.S. state. The smaller and fewer federal courts deal with different types of cases. State courts are common law courts, using their state’s laws and procedures. They follow their state’s constitution, laws, and decisions from other courts in the state. When needed, they also apply federal laws. Usually, one judge decides cases by presiding over trials. Lower court decisions can be reviewed by a state court of appeals. The highest court is the state supreme court, which oversees the entire system. For cases involving federal law, the state’s highest court decision, including when they refuse appeals, can be appealed to the United States Supreme Court, which can also choose not to hear the case.

Vancouver is a big city in western Canada, located in British Columbia. It has over 631,000 people and was more populous in 2016 than in 2011. The Greater Vancouver area had 2.5 million people in 2016, ranking third in Canada for the largest metropolitan area. Vancouver is the most crowded city in Canada, with over 5,400 people per square kilometre. It's the fifth-most crowded city in North America, behind New York, Guadalajara, San Francisco, and Mexico City. Vancouver is very diverse, with over half of its people not speaking English at home, and more than half belonging to minority groups. It's often called one of the top five livable cities in the world. In 2011, Vancouver aimed to become the greenest city by 2020. The city's planning idea is called "Vancouverism." Vancouver started as Gastown, with a tavern built on July 1, 1867. It got its current name in 1886 because of a deal with the Canadian Pacific Railway. The railway reached the city by 1887, and the city's large seaport became important for trade. Vancouver hosted several big events, like the 1954 Commonwealth Games and the 2010 Winter Olympics and Paralympics. Vancouver is the fourth-largest port in the Americas by tonnage, and the busiest and largest in Canada. While forestry is a big industry, tourism is the second-largest. Vancouver and nearby Burnaby are a major film production area, earning it the name "Hollywood North."

Snow Patrol is a British rock band. Their third studio album and first major-label album, called "The Final Straw," was released on August 4, 2003, in the UK and Ireland. It came out in the US in 2004. This album was very successful for the band outside their home countries of Northern Ireland and Scotland. After 14 months, five singles were released from this album. "The Final Straw" was the first album with lead guitarist Nathan Connolly and the last with bassist Mark McClelland. In 2004, the album was re-released in the UK with two extra songs, but not in the US. It was also released in SACD and Dualdisc formats with 5.1 surround mixes.

Sorel Etrog was born in Romania and later became an Israeli-Canadian artist, writer, and philosopher. He was known for making sculptures. His work focused on modern art and contemporary sculpture. He lived from August 29, 1933, to February 26, 2014.

Naughton is a village in Suffolk, England. It is now part of the civil parish called Nedging-with-Naughton, which was formed in 1935 when Naughton joined with Nedging. In 1931, the village had 98 people living there. Naughton is near Ipswich to the north-east and Stowmarket to the south-east. Historically, it was in the Cosford Hundred of Suffolk. The village is at the meeting point of two roads. One road comes from the south-west and goes to Nedging Tye and New Road. The other road comes from the south-east. Near the center of the village, just west of where these roads meet, stands St. Mary's Church, a 14th-century flint-built church.

Washing County is in the state of Maine, U.S. In 2010, it had 32, 856 people, making it one of the least populated counties in Maine. Its main town is Machias. It was created on June 25, 1789. It shares a border with New Brunswick, a part of Canada. People sometimes call it "Sunrise County" because it has the easternmost point in the U.S. and is said to be where the sun first rises over 48 states. Many small fishing towns depend on fishing for their income. Tourism is also important along the coast but isn't as big as in other parts of the state. Blueberries are very important for the local economy.
Rubén Galván can be about: One person Multiple people

The Camp David Accords were signed on September 17, 1978. Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin negotiated secretly for twelve days at Camp David, a U.S. president's retreat in Maryland. President Jimmy Carter witnessed the signing of two framework agreements at the White House. The second agreement, titled "A Framework for the Conclusion of a Peace Treaty between Egypt and Israel," led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty. Sadat and Begin shared the 1978 Nobel Peace Prize for this agreement. The first agreement, "A Framework for Peace in the Middle East," which covered Palestinian territories, was not agreed with Palestinian involvement and was criticized by the United Nations. Historian Jørgen Jensehaugen says that by January 1981, when Carter left office, this first agreement was not fully accepted.

Richard Lester Liebman, born on January 19, 1932, is known as Dick Lester. He is an American film director who lives in the United Kingdom. He worked with The Beatles in the 1960s and directed films in the "Superman" series in the 1980s. Lester is also associated with London Film School as an honorary associate.
The Royal New Zealand Navy (RNZN) is part of New Zealand's defense force. It is called "Warriors of the Sea of New Zealand." Currently, it has eight ships.

The Detroit Pistons are an American basketball team. They play in the NBA and are in the Eastern Conference Central Division. Their home games are at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit. The team started in Fort Wayne, Indiana, as the Fort Wayne Pistons in 1941. They won two championships in 1944 and 1945. In 1948, they joined the Basketball Association of America. In 1949, the NBL and BAA combined to form the NBA, and the Pistons became part of it. In 1957, the team moved to Detroit. The Pistons have won three NBA championships: in 1989, 1990, and 2004.

Maximilian Kolbe, born Rajmund Kolbe on January 8, 1894, and later known as Saint Maximilian Kolbe, was a Polish Catholic priest and Franciscan friar. He volunteered to die in place of a stranger at Auschwitz, a German death camp during World War II, in German-occupied Poland. Kolbe had worked to promote the worship of the Virgin Mary, founded a monastery near Warsaw, and set up an amateur-radio station. He also started several organizations and publications. On October 10, 1982, Pope John Paul II made Kolbe a saint and called him a martyr of charity. The Catholic Church honors him as the patron saint of amateur-radio operators, drug addicts, political prisoners, families, journalists, prisoners, and the pro-life movement. John Paul II named him the "patron saint of our difficult century." His feast day is August 14, the day he died. Because of his efforts to encourage devotion to Mary, he is known as the "apostle of consecration to Mary."

The Renault FR1 was a single-decker bus made by Renault Trucks in France from 1987 to 1997. It had a 6-cylinder Renault engine with 9,834 cc displacement. There were three types: TE, TX, and GTX. You could choose between 1 or 2 doors. In 1997, it was updated and renamed Renault Iliade to replace the FR1 model.

Snakes are long, legless, meat-eating reptiles. Like other reptiles, they are cold-blooded and have scales. Many snake species have more flexible jaws, allowing them to eat prey larger than their heads. Their organs are stacked instead of side by side, and most have just one working lung. Some snakes still have tiny hind legs. Lizards have become legless, or nearly legless, many times independently, similar to snakes. Most legless lizards can close their eyes and have ears, unlike snakes. However, there are exceptions. Snakes live on every continent except Antarctica, and on most smaller land masses. Sea snakes are common in the Indian and Pacific Oceans. There are over 3,600 snake species, ranging from very small to very large. Fossils show snakes might have evolved from burrowing or aquatic lizards, possibly during the Jurassic period. Most snakes are not venomous. Venom is used to catch prey, not defend themselves. Some venom is strong enough to hurt or kill people. Nonvenomous snakes either swallow prey alive or suffocate them.

Kambaata is a highland East Cushitic language, part of the Afro-Asiatic family. It is spoken by the Kambaata people. There are different dialects, including Kambaata, Tambaro, Alaba, and K'abeena. Kambaata is one of the official languages of Ethiopia. The language has many verbal affixes. When added to verbal roots, these affixes cause many sound changes. Kambaata follows a SOV order (subject–object–verb). Its phonemes consist of five vowels (which are either long or short), ejectives, a retroflexed implosive, and a glottal stop. The New Testament and some parts of the Old Testament have been translated into Kambaata. Initially, these translations were published using the Ethiopian syllabary (in 1992). Later, they were republished using Latin letters, in line with new policies and practices.

Sandpipers are a large family of waders or shorebirds, called Scolopacidae. They include species called sandpipers, as well as those called curlews and snipes. These birds mostly eat small insects found in mud or soil. Different bill lengths allow various species to feed in the same area without competing for food, especially on the coast. Sandpipers have long bodies and legs, and narrow wings. Their bills are sensitive, helping them find food by feeling the mud. Most have dull, brown, grey, or streaked feathers, but some show brighter colors during mating season. Most sandpipers nest in open areas, and protect their territory with aerial displays. They lay 3 to 4 eggs in simple ground scrapes. The chicks are well-developed when they hatch.
Lantsch/Lenz is a municipality in the Albula region of Graubünden, Switzerland. Most people there speak Romansh.

Denis Farkasfalvy was born on June 23, 1936, and died on May 20, 2020. He was a Hungarian-American Catholic priest and monk from the Cistercian order. He served as an abbot and was also a theologian, author, and translator.

Olga Maria Elisabeth Schwarzkopf, born on December 9, 1915, and died on August 3, 2006, was a German-born singer who became known as an Austro-British soprano. She was famous for singing lieder and performing in Viennese operettas, as well as in operas by Mozart, Wagner, and Richard Strauss. After stopping performing, she taught voice internationally. People consider her one of the greatest sopranos of the 20th century.

The Sri Lankan civil war lasted from 1983 to 2009. It began on July 23, 1983, when Tamil Tiger rebels, led by Velupillai Prabhakaran, started fighting against the government. They wanted to create an independent Tamil state called Tamil Eelam in the north and east of Sri Lanka. The Tamil Tigers were fighting because Sri Lankan Tamils faced discrimination from the Sinhalese majority government. There were several violent events, like the 1956, 1958, and 1977 anti-Tamil attacks, and the 1981 burning of the Jaffna Public Library. The war ended when the Sri Lankan military defeated the Tamil Tigers in May 2009. Over 25 years, the conflict caused many deaths and hardships. Around 100,000 people died, including civilians. The Sri Lankan forces tried to take back areas the Tamil Tigers had captured. The Tamil Tigers were listed as a terrorist organization in several countries. The Sri Lankan government faced accusations of human rights abuses. After a ceasefire in 2002, fighting continued. In 2006, the Sri Lankan military launched major attacks on the Tamil Tigers, driving them from the east of the island. By 2009, the Sri Lankan forces controlled all the areas previously held by the Tamil Tigers. The Tamil Tigers admitted defeat. The pro-LTTE Tamil National Alliance then dropped their demand for an independent state. In 2010, President Rajapaksa appointed a commission to assess the conflict. Since the end of the war, Sri Lanka has been criticized for human rights violations, including genocide and ethnic cleansing of Tamils. The Tamil Tigers were known for suicide bombings. Mullivaikkal Remembrance Day is observed on May 18, marking the end of the civil war. In January 2020, President Rajapaksa said that about 20,000 abducted Tamils were likely dead.

The team captain in association football is a player chosen to lead the team on the field. They are often one of the older or more experienced players, or someone who can strongly influence the game. The team captain usually wears an armband to show who they are.
Mitrović comes from the name "Saint Demetrius" or "Sveti Dimitrije" (in Cyrillic, it is written as "Свети Димитрије"). This name might be used for: A person A place

A rhetorical question is one where the person asking doesn't expect a direct answer. Often, it's used to start a conversation or to share an opinion. An example is "Can't you do anything right?" When asked, this question doesn't really want to know if the listener can do things well, but rather to suggest that they can't.
Morcourt is a commune in Aisne, which is in Hauts-de-France in northern France.

Piedmont blues, also called east coast or southeastern blues, mainly refers to a guitar playing style known as the piedmont fingerstyle. This style uses a rhythmic pattern where the thumb plays the bass strings, while the fore-finger picks the melody on the treble strings. This gives a sound similar to ragtime or stride piano. The term was created by blues researcher Peter B. Lowry, who gave credit to Bruce Bastin, another folklorist. Piedmont blues is different from other styles, especially Mississippi Delta blues, because of its ragtime-inspired rhythms.
Moore Haven is a city in Florida, United States. It is the county seat of Glades County. The population was 1,680 in the 2010 census. Moore Haven is on the southwest shore of Lake Okeechobee.

In the 1980 Democratic presidential primaries, voters chose the party's nominee for the U.S. presidential election. President Jimmy Carter was chosen as the nominee through primary elections and caucuses. This happened at the 1980 Democratic National Convention in New York City from August 11 to 14. Senator Ted Kennedy from Massachusetts was Carter's main challenger. He won 12 contests and got over seven million votes. He refused to give up the nomination until the second day of the convention. This was the last election where an incumbent president's party nominee was still contested at the convention.

Sin City is a series of comics by Frank Miller. The first story came out in "Dark Horse Presents Fifth Anniversary Special" in April 1991. It continued in "Dark Horse Presents" issues 51 to 62 from May 1991 to June 1992. The stories are in thirteen parts and are set in a city called Basin City. There have been other stories too. A film version of Sin City, directed by Robert Rodriguez and Frank Miller, came out on April 1, 2005. A sequel called "Sin City: A Dame to Kill For" was released on August 22, 2014. Dimension Films is making a new TV series based on Sin City. It will have new characters and timelines, more like the original comics than the films.

Villach is the seventh-largest city in Austria and the second-largest in the state of Carinthia. It is an important traffic hub for southern Austria and the Alpe-Adria region. The city has 61,887 people. Together with other mountain towns, Villach works in an association called Alpine Town of the Year. This group helps make sustainable development happen in the Alpine Arc. Villach was the first town to win the Alpine Town of the Year award in 1997.

Lindsey Nelson was born on May 25, 1919, and died on June 10, 1995. He was an American sportscaster who was famous for his long career broadcasting college football and New York Mets baseball games. Nelson worked for the Mets for 17 years and for the San Francisco Giants for three years. For 33 years, Nelson covered college football games. He broadcast 26 Cotton Bowls, five Sugar Bowls, four Rose Bowls, and Notre Dame games for 14 years. Nelson was inducted into 13 different halls of fame. Fans remember Nelson as a talented broadcaster, a great storyteller, and a true sports lover. His colorful jackets and lively broadcasts made him a leading sportscaster in the industry.

Brooke Shields, born on May 31, 1965, is an American actress and model. She started as a child model and became famous at 12 for her role in the movie "Pretty Baby" (1978), where she played a child prostitute in early 20th century New Orleans. Shields continued modeling until her late teens and acted in dramas during the 1980s, including "The Blue Lagoon" (1980) and "Endless Love" (1981). In 1983, she stopped modeling to go to Princeton University, where she earned a degree in romance languages. In the 1990s, Shields acted in small roles in movies. She was also in the NBC sitcom "Suddenly Susan" from 1996 to 2000, where she was nominated for two Golden Globes, and in "Lipstick Jungle" (2008-2009). In 2017, she had a bigger role in an NBC show during its 19th season. Since 2014, Shields has been the voice of Beverly Goodman in the animated series "Mr. Pickles" and its spinoff "Momma Named Me Sheriff."

Lorenzo Cherubini, born on September 27, 1966, is known as Jovanotti. He is an Italian singer-songwriter and rapper. Jovanotti's name comes from "giovanotti," which means "young men" in Italian. He first used the stage name "Joe Vanotti," but a poster for a nightclub误写了他的名字为 "Jovanotti," and the name stuck. Jovanotti is called "Jova" by his fans, and he often uses this name in his promotional materials and on his TV channel Jova.tv, which started on October 2, 2014. Jovanotti's music style changed over time. He began with hip hop, rap, and disco but later added funk, world music, classical, and ska elements. His lyrics also changed, becoming more focused on philosophy, religion, and politics. This is common for cantautore, a type of Italian singer-songwriter. Jovanotti's commitment to social and political issues grew stronger. Some of his earlier work sounds more like 1980s pop music. Most of Jovanotti's songs are in Italian, but he also made an album with Spanish songs. He included a short version of "Rapper's Delight" by the Sugarhill Gang in his live album. Jovanotti appears in several international collections. One notable one is "Red Hot + Rhapsody," a 1998 tribute to George Gershwin, where he performed "I Got Rhythm." He also took part in a charity concert with Luciano Pavarotti in 1996.
Vallorbe is a municipality in the Jura-Nord-Vaudois district, which is in the canton of Vaud in Switzerland.

Bettlach is a commune in Haut-Rhin, which is in the Grand Est region of northeastern France.
Colcannon is a traditional Irish dish. It consists of mashed potatoes with kale or cabbage.

Potsdamer Platz is a big square in the center of Berlin, Germany. It is south of the Brandenburg Gate and the Reichstag, which is the German parliament building. It is near the southeast corner of Tiergarten park. The square is named after Potsdam, a city to the southwest. Potsdamer Platz used to be where a road from Potsdam used to pass through Berlin's old city wall. After changing from a small rural intersection to a busy traffic spot in over a century, it was completely destroyed in World War II. During the Cold War, it was empty because the Berlin Wall split its area. Since Germany became one country again, Potsdamer Platz has been rebuilt.

Sir John Grant McKenzie Laws lived from May 10, 1945, to April 5, 2020. He was a lord justice of appeal. He worked from 1999 to 2016. He also taught as the Goodhart visiting professor of legal science at the University of Cambridge. Additionally, he was an honorary fellow of Robinson College, Cambridge.

Massimo Mattioli, born on September 25, 1943, and passed away on August 23, 2019, was an Italian artist and cartoonist. He started his career in 1965 by publishing "Vermetto Sigh" in the comic book "Il Vittorioso." Later, he was also featured in "Corto Maltese" and "Frigidaire." In 1968, he moved to London and made comics for "Mayfair" magazine. In the early 1970s, he created "Pasquino" for "Paese Sera" newspaper. In 1973, he began working on "Il Giornalino," where he created the character "Pinky." In 1977, he collaborated with Stefano Tamburini to create the underground magazine "Cannibale." The same year, "Cannibale" published the first adventure of "Joe Galaxy." In 1982, he created the "Squeak the Mouse" series, which was a parody of "Tom and Jerry." Mattioli received several awards, including the French Prize Phenix in 1971 and the "Romics d'oro" in 2009.
Kensington is a town in Montgomery County, Maryland, United States. It had 2,213 people in 2010. Greater Kensington includes the whole area with the zip code 20895 and has 19,054 people.
Patrick Dennisoun McGorry, born on September 10, 1952, is an Australian psychiatrist. He is known for creating early intervention services for young people with mental disorders.

Fratton Park is a football stadium in Portsmouth, a city in England. Portsmouth Football Club was founded in 1898. Fratton Park is special because it is on an island, Portsea Island, rather than the mainland. It was built in 1899 on land that used to be a potato field. The stadium opened to the public on August 15, 1899, and had its first match on September 6, 1899. A friendly game against Southampton FC was won 2-0, with 4,141 people watching. The stadium is named after Fratton Railway Station, which is nearby. The name was chosen to make fans think the stadium was close to a railway station. Fratton Park could hold up to 58,000 people in 1935, but it has fewer people now. Since 1996, only people who bought seats can watch games there. Portsmouth fans call the stadium "the old girl." In recent years, it has been called "Fortress Fratton" because of how many people come to watch games and the exciting atmosphere. The stadium is part of the Anglican St. James parish in Milton, Portsmouth.

Naomie Melanie Harris, born on September 6, 1976, is an English actress. She began her career as a child, appearing in the TV show "Simon and the Witch" in 1987. She acted as Selena in the zombie movie "28 Days Later" in 2002. She also played Tia Dalma, the witch, in the second and third "Pirates of the Caribbean" movies. In 2013, she was in the film "Winnie Mandela." She played Eve Moneypenny in the James Bond movies "Skyfall" in 2012 and "Spectre" in 2015, and will return to the role in "No Time to Die" in 2020. In 2016, she starred in the movie "Moonlight," which was very well-received. Her performance earned her several nominations, including for the Golden Globe, BAFTA, and Academy Award for best supporting actress. In 2017, she was given an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) for her contributions to drama.

The grand tour was a tradition in the 17th and 18th centuries where wealthy young European men, usually around 21 years old, traveled through Europe. They often went with a family member to ensure they behaved properly. This journey was an important part of their education and helped them learn about the culture and art of ancient Greece and Rome. Men from countries like Britain, other Northern European nations, and some from North America also took these trips. By the mid-18th century, the grand tour was common among the upper class in Central Europe too. This tradition ended when trains started traveling widely in the 1840s. By then, a guide or tutor called a "cicerone" often accompanied travelers. The grand tour helped young men show others that they had seen important works of art and learned about different cultures. The tour could last from a few months to a few years. The grand tour left a lasting influence, and its ideas about travel and culture are still seen today. Even though it started as a way for the rich to see art, it helped make travel more popular among all social classes. People still choose certain places to visit because of the grand tour's legacy. For artists, the tour was still important for learning painting and sculpture, though most could not afford the full experience. Guides and books, like the one by the Richardson父子, helped more people make such trips. Tourists would buy souvenirs like coins and statues from places like Rome and Naples. Few ventured to southern Italy or Greece, which was still controlled by the Ottoman Empire.

The banker horse is a breed of wild horse living on islands in North Carolina's Outer Banks. These horses are small, strong, and calm. They came from domesticated Spanish horses brought to America in the 1500s. Some may have become wild after surviving shipwrecks or being left on the islands by explorers. These horses live on islands like Ocracoke, Shackleford Banks, Currituck Banks, Cedar Island, and the Rachel Carson Estuarine Sanctuary. While they are not originally from these islands, they are allowed to stay because of their history. They eat marsh grass for food and water. The horses are controlled to stop overpopulation and protect their habitat. The National Park Service, North Carolina state, and some private groups manage the horses. They check for illnesses like equine infectious anemia and keep them safe from traffic. Horses are adopted and their numbers controlled with birth control. Horses trained from the wild can be used for riding and driving.

Miriam Margolyes, born on May 18, 1941, is a British-Australian actress and comedian. She started her career in theater. Later, she had supporting roles in films and TV shows. For her role in "The Age of Innocence" (1993), she won a BAFTA award. She also played Professor Sprout in the "Harry Potter" movies. Margolyes spends time in England, Australia, and Italy. She starred in plays in both countries, including the Australian premiere of a 2013 play. In 2013, she became an Australian citizen.
Chavenon is a commune in the Allier department, which is in Auvergne, a region in central France.

An eagle is a common name for many large birds of prey in the family Accipitridae. Not all eagles are closely related. There are about 60 species of eagles. Most of these species are found in Eurasia and Africa. Outside this area, only 14 species of eagles can be found—2 in North America, 9 in Central and South America, and 3 in Australia.

A chemical substance is a type of matter with a fixed composition and specific properties. Some say it cannot be divided into its basic elements without breaking chemical bonds. Chemical substances can be simple elements, compounds, or alloys. Sometimes, chemical elements are included in the definition, but not always. Pure substances are called 'pure' to distinguish them from mixtures. Pure water is an example; it remains the same whether from a river or a lab. Other pure substances include carbon (diamond), gold, salt (sodium chloride), and sugar (sucrose). In practice, substances are nearly pure for their intended use. Chemical substances can be solids, liquids, gases, or plasma, and change form with temperature or pressure. Chemical substances can turn into others through reactions. Energy forms like light and heat are not considered substances.

NBC is an American TV and radio network. It is owned by NBCUniversal, a company under Comcast. NBC's main offices are in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, and Philadelphia. NBC is one of the main TV networks. Its logo, a peacock, was first used in 1956 and became its official emblem in 1979. NBC was founded in 1926 by RCA, which was owned by General Electric at the time. General Electric had to sell RCA and NBC in 1932 due to antitrust issues. General Electric later bought NBC back in 1986. Bob Wright became CEO in 1986 and left in 2007, when Jeff Zucker took over. In 2003, NBCUniversal was formed by merging NBC and Vivendi's entertainment assets. Comcast bought a controlling stake in 2011 and fully owned NBCUniversal in 2013. NBC has 13 owned stations and many affiliates across the US, some also in Canada and Germany.
Multiple cameras are used in filmmaking and video production. Several cameras record or broadcast a scene at the same time. This is called a multicam setup. It's different from using just one camera.

Lopp Lagoon is a tidal lake northeast of Cape Prince of Wales, the westernmost point of the Seward Peninsula, in Alaska. Many creeks flow into it, but most of the water comes from the Mint River. Some salt water from the Pacific Ocean also enters the lagoon through several channels between it and the Bering Strait. It was named in 1900 after William Thomas Lopp, a missionary and leader for Inuit people, and an overland relief expedition in 1897-98. Historically, Lopp Lagoon has provided important food sources, such as salmon and waterfowl, for people living in the Wales, Alaska area.

Paulo César Wanchope Watson, known as Paulo Wanchope, was born on July 31, 1976. He is a former Costa Rican footballer and former head coach of the Costa Rica national football team. Wanchope is the second top scorer for the Costa Rica national team, with 45 goals in 73 international matches, after Roland Fonseca. He scored against Brazil in 2002 and scored two goals against Germany in 2006. Wanchope is the top goalscorer for Costa Rica in the FIFA World Cup, sharing this record with Rónald Gómez.
Adams is a city in Adams County, Wisconsin. The population was 1,967 in 2010. Adams city is in the town of Adams.
Clay County is in Indiana, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 26,890 people. The county seat is a city called Brazil. Clay County is part of the Terre Haute, Indiana area.
Poygan is a town in Winnebago County, Wisconsin, United States. In 2010, it had 1,301 people living there.

Port Vila, or simply Vila, is the capital and largest city of Vanuatu. It is on the island of Efate. In 2009, its population was 44,040, up from 29,356 in 1999. That year, Vila's population made up 18.8% of Vanuatu's total population and 66.9% of Efate's population. Located on the south coast of Efate, in Shefa Province, Port Vila is Vanuatu's economic and commercial center. Erick Puyo Festa, from Vanua'aku Pati, became mayor in January 2018. His deputy is Jenny Regenvanu, from the Graun Mo Jastis Pati. In March 2015, Port Vila suffered damage from Cyclone Pam.

Rolf Leeser was born on June 4, 1929, in Essen, Germany. He played football for Ajax in the Netherlands from 1948 to 1954. Leeser, who was Jewish, joined Ajax's youth academy at age 12 and made his first professional game on September 19, 1948. He became a regular player during the 1951-52 season and continued to play until April 1954, scoring six goals in 34 total appearances. Outside of football, Leeser worked as a fashion designer. He started his own women's fashion company called Leeser B.V. and helped redesign the Ajax logo, which has been used since 1990. Leeser passed away on March 21, 2018, at the age of 88. He was married to Anita B. Leeser-Gassan.
Brisbane is an Australian electoral district in the state of Queensland.

Municipalities, or "municipios" in Spanish, are the second-level administrative divisions in Mexico. The first-level division is the "state," or "estado" in Spanish. As of September 2017, there are 2,448 municipalities in Mexico, not counting the 16 "delegaciones" of Mexico City. The way municipalities are organized and their responsibilities are described in Article 115 of the 1917 constitution and in the constitutions of the states they belong to. Municipalities are different from cities. Some municipalities can be as large as states. Cities are smaller and can be measured in blocks.

Equivalent weight, also called gram equivalent, is the mass of a substance that reacts with or combines with a fixed amount of another substance. The equivalent weight of an element is the mass that combines with or displaces 1.008 grams of hydrogen, 8.0 grams of oxygen, or 35.5 grams of chlorine. These values are found by dividing the atomic weight by the usual valence; for example, for oxygen, it is 16.0 grams divided by 2. In acid-base reactions, the equivalent weight of an acid or base is the mass that provides or reacts with one mole of hydrogen ions (H+). For redox reactions, the equivalent weight is the mass that provides or reacts with one mole of electrons (e-). Equivalent weight has the same units as mass, unlike atomic weight, which has no units. In the past, equivalent weights were found through experiments, but now they are calculated from molar masses. The equivalent weight of a compound can be found by dividing its molecular mass by the number of positive or negative charges formed when the compound dissolves.

Pegomastax, meaning "strong jaw," is a type of heterodontosaurid dinosaur. It was found in South Africa. Based on a partial skull, including parts of the lower jaw and a beak-like bone, Pegomastax was about 60 cm long. It lived in the early Jurassic period, around 200 to 190 million years ago, in a place called Voyizane, Joe Gqabi district, in the Cape Province. The dinosaur was first recognized by Paul Sereno in the 1980s, but not officially named until 2012. The type species is called "P. africana." Unlike other dinosaurs of its kind, Pegomastax had a robust lower jaw with a short beak. It also had a large tooth at the beginning of its lower jaw, which might have been used for protection.

Andrés Muschietti, born on August 26, 1973, is an Argentine filmmaker. He gained fame with the 2013 film "Mama," which he made with his sister, Barbara Muschietti. "Mama" attracted the attention of Guillermo del Toro, who then became an executive producer. Muschietti became more well-known for directing the "It" film series. The first film, based on Stephen King's novel, was released in 2017 and was the highest-grossing horror film ever. Its 2019 sequel, "It Chapter Two," was also successful. Both films were produced by New Line Cinema and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures. Muschietti will direct two upcoming films for Warner Bros.: "The Flash" and a live-action version of "Attack on Titan." He is also set to direct a remake of "The Howling" for Netflix.
Chamely Khatun, born on November 11, 1988, is a Bangladeshi cricketer. She plays for the Bangladesh national women's cricket team. She is a right-handed batswoman and a right-arm slow bowler.

Karl-Heinz von Hassel was a German actor born on February 8, 1939, in Hamburg. He died on April 19, 2016, in Hamburg at the age of 77. He appeared in over 100 films and TV shows from 1960 to 2012. He started his career with acting lessons and worked in theaters from 1960. From 1966, he frequently appeared on TV. He also had important roles in movies directed by Rainer Werner Fassbinder. Von Hassel was tall and often played police officers. He also acted as industrial workers.

Uddingston is a small town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland. It is located on the north side of the River Clyde, southeast of Glasgow city center. Uddingston serves as a place where people live but do not work, helping Glasgow.
Ismael Gómez Falcón was born on April 24, 1984. He is a Spanish football player who plays as a goalkeeper for Hércules CF.
Anizy-le-Grand is a commune in the Aisne department of Hauts-de-France, in northern France. It was formed on January 1, 2019, by combining the communes of Anizy-le-Château, Faucoucourt, and Lizy.

The Hanshin Tigers (Japanese: 阪神タイガース "hanshin taigāsu") are a professional baseball team in Japan. They play in the Central League. The team is based in Nishinomiya, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. They are owned by Hanshin Electric Railway Co., Ltd., which is a part of Hankyu Hanshin Holdings Inc. The Hanshin Tigers are one of the oldest professional baseball teams in Japan. They started playing in 1936 as the Osaka Tigers. In 1961, they changed their name to the Hanshin Tigers.

Dokaor toongtong is a Thai singer from the Isan region. She sings in the luk thung and mor lam sing styles. Her most popular songs are "Ber Tho Jao Choo," "Oak Hak Wan Hae Tiean," "Miea Kao," and "Rak Phay Thee Kaeng Saphue." She is also known as Aor or "Sao Sieng Sor."

Bad Doberan was a former district in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany. It was named after its biggest town, Bad Doberan. In German, "bad" means "spa." The district was near Rostock, close to the Baltic Sea in the north. It also bordered the former districts of Nordvorpommern, Güstrow, and Nordwestmecklenburg. In September 2011, the district was dissolved. Its area is now part of the Rostock district.

Cylinder is a city in Palo Alto County, Iowa, United States. The population was 88 in 2010.
Trévoux is a town in the Ain area of France, in the east. People who live there are called Trévoltiens. It is near Lyon and is on the slope of the Saône River.

The Forlì-Cesena province is in the Emilia-Romagna region of Italy. Its capital is Forlì. As of 2016, it had 394,273 people and covered an area. It includes 30 "comuni." Davide Drei is the provincial president. Even though it is close to San Marino, Forlì-Cesena does not share a land border with the country.

Efficiency measures how well input is used for a task. It's about using as little waste, expense, or extra effort as possible to get a specific result. Efficiency can be a percentage of ideal performance, like using all the fuel for the best outcome. Effectiveness is about achieving desired results, often simpler to measure than efficiency. Efficiency and effectiveness are sometimes mixed up, but they are different. Efficiency is about doing things correctly, while effectiveness is about doing the right things. Both are important. Choosing goals well is as crucial as doing the work well. In business, the saying "efficiency is doing things right; effectiveness is getting things done" clarifies these concepts. Effectiveness can still be achieved through inefficient processes, like working longer hours or using more energy. Efficiency is calculated as the ratio of useful output to total input. For example, in engines, efficiency is the work output divided by the heat input. Efficiency can never be more than 100% due to energy conservation.

In 2000, Louise, a UK singer, released her 10th solo song. This song is from her third solo album called "Elbow Beach." It uses a part of another song called "Different Strokes" by Syl Johnson, which the Wu-Tang Clan also used. The song reached number 13 on the UK singles chart.

The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an international group that makes rules about trade between countries. It started on January 1, 1995, after a big meeting in Marrakesh, where 123 countries agreed. This replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which began in 1948. The WTO helps countries make agreements and solve problems about buying and selling things, services, and ideas. It has more than 600 people working in Geneva, Switzerland, led by the Director-General, Roberto Azevêdo. In 2013, all members agreed on a Trade Facilitation Agreement, the first big deal in the WTO's history. In 2017, the WTO made a change to its rules about protecting inventions and creations, which is important for developing countries. Research shows that the WTO has increased trade between countries. Without it, trade barriers would be much higher. The WTO's rules are often used in trade agreements, sometimes word-for-word in some parts.

Julian Clare May, born on July 10, 1931, and passed away on October 17, 2017, was an American writer. She wrote stories in science fiction, fantasy, horror, science, and children's genres. She used different pen names. She was famous for her "Saga of Pliocene Exile" and "Galactic Milieu Series" books.

Maurice Petty was born on March 27, 1939, and died on July 25, 2020. He was an American. Maurice worked as a crew chief and engine builder for Petty Enterprises, and he also owned part of the company. In 2011, he was inducted into the International Motorsports Hall of Fame. He was later honored by being enshrined into the NASCAR Hall of Fame in 2014. Maurice was the first engine builder to receive this distinction.
Saint-Julien-de-Mailloc was a town in Calvados, in Normandy, France. On January 1, 2016, it became part of a new town called Vorbiquet.

West Palm Beach is a city in Palm Beach County, Florida, United States. It is right next to Palm Beach, which is on an island across Lake Worth Lagoon. In 2010, it had 99,919 people living there. West Palm Beach is part of the Miami metropolitan area, which had about 6,158,824 people in 2017. It was the first officially incorporated city in South Florida, becoming a city two years before Miami in 1894. West Palm Beach is roughly north of Miami's downtown area.

Andromeda is one of the 48 constellations listed by the ancient astronomer Ptolemy and is still one of the 88 modern constellations. It is named after Andromeda, the daughter of Cassiopeia in Greek mythology, who was chained to a rock to be eaten by the sea monster Cetus. Andromeda is best seen during autumn evenings in the northern part of the sky. It can be seen only north of 40 degrees south latitude and covers a large area of 722 square degrees, which is about 1,400 times the size of the full moon. Andromeda has bright stars like Alpha Andromedae and Gamma Andromedae, which are popular targets for amateur astronomers. The most famous object in Andromeda is the Andromeda Galaxy, the closest spiral galaxy to our Milky Way and one of the brightest in the sky. Other galaxies like M110 and M32, and distant NGC 891, are also found within Andromeda. The Blue Snowball Nebula, a planetary nebula, can be seen with a telescope. In Chinese and Hindu astronomy, Andromeda's stars were part of different constellations with their own meanings. The Andromedids, a weak meteor shower, also occur in November.

NCAA Division II (D-II) is a middle-level division in the National Collegiate Athletic Association. It offers a choice between the larger Division I, which has more funding, and Division III, which doesn't give scholarships. Before 1973, smaller schools were in the College Division. In 1973, the College Division split into two. Those who wanted to offer scholarships or compete against teams that did became Division II. Those who didn't offer scholarships became Division III. ESPN televises the football championship game. CBS shows the men's basketball championship. ESPN2 broadcasts the women's basketball championship. Stadium shows six Thursday football games during the regular season and one men's basketball game each Saturday. The official slogan for NCAA Division II is "Make it yours."
Bartholomäberg is a town and a popular place for tourists in the area of Bludenz, in the Austrian state of Vorarlberg.

A steel mill or steelworks is a factory where steel is made. It might include all steps, from melting iron ore to creating finished steel products. Alternatively, it can refer to places that make steel semi-finished products from molten pig iron or scrap.

The Screen Actors Guild (SAG) was a union in America that represented more than 100,000 film and TV actors. In March 2012, SAG decided to join with the American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (AFTRA) to form SAG-AFTRA. SAG-AFTRA aimed to negotiate fair contracts, protect members' performances, and ensure work opportunities. SAG was created in 1933 to stop unfair contracts that forced actors to work long hours without breaks and gave studios too much control. SAG belonged to a larger group called AAAAA, which connects many actors' unions. SAG focused on movies, while AFTRA covered radio, TV, and new media. They shared some members. SAG had offices in Hollywood and many big cities like Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, and New York. Since 1995, SAG gave out awards that often predicted success at the Oscars, and now these awards are still given by SAG-AFTRA.

Thomas P. Tiffany was born on December 30, 1957. He is an American businessman and politician. Since 2020, he has been representing Wisconsin's 7th congressional district in the U.S. Congress. Tiffany is from the Republican Party. He was previously in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 2011 to 2013 and then in the Wisconsin Senate from 2013 to 2020. He took Sean Duffy's seat in Congress after winning a special election against Tricia Zunker.

Ronald Gabriel Palillo was an American actor and teacher. He was born on April 2, 1949, and died on August 14, 2012. He is best known for playing the character Arnold Horshack in the TV show "Welcome Back, Kotter" from 1975 to 1979. Arnold Horshack was a funny, not very smart character that people liked.

Arch Enemy is a Swedish melodic death metal band. They were formed in 1995 in Halmstad. Some of their members were from other bands like Carcass, Armageddon, Carnage, Mercyful Fate, Spiritual Beggars, The Agonist, Nevermore, and Eucharist. The band was started by Michael Amott from Carcass and Johan Liiva, who were from Carnage. They have made ten studio albums, three live albums, three video albums, and four EPs. The band's first lead singer was Johan Liiva. In 2000, he was replaced by Angela Gossow from Germany. Angela left in March 2014 to manage the band, and was replaced by Alissa White-Gluz from Canada.

The Canadian National Railway (CN) is a big freight railway company in Canada. Its main office is in Montreal, Quebec. CN serves Canada and parts of the United States, especially in the Midwest and South. CN is the largest railway company in Canada in terms of money earned and the size of its tracks. Its tracks stretch from the Atlantic coast in Nova Scotia to the Pacific coast in British Columbia, covering about 25,000 miles of track. In the late 20th century, CN expanded its capacity in the United States by taking over other railways, like the Illinois Central. CN is a public company with about 24,000 workers. As of July 2019, it was worth about $9 billion Canadian. Before 1995, CN was owned by the government and was called a crown corporation. As of 2019, Bill Gates was the biggest shareholder of CN's stock. CN was called "CNR" from 1919 to 1960 and "Canadian National" or "Canadien National" (CN) since 1960.

Jefferson County is in the state of Iowa. In 2010, there were 16, 843 people living there. The county seat is Fairfield. Jefferson County was created in January 1839 and was named after President Thomas Jefferson.

Lester Bruce McDonald was born on September 19, 1914, and died on July 26, 1971. He played American football as an end in the NFL. He played for the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, and Philadelphia Eagles. He went to the University of Nebraska for college and was chosen as the eighth player in the first round of the 1937 NFL draft.
