Princeton is a city in Mercer County, West Virginia, United States. It is also the county seat. People often call it the "jewel of the south" or the "heart of Mercer County." In 2010, the city had 6,432 people. Princeton is part of the Bluefield, WV-VA micropolitan area with 107,342 people. The city has a baseball team called the Princeton Rays that plays in the Appalachian League.

The Inca civil war, also called the Inca war of succession, was a conflict between half-brothers Huáscar and Atahualpa. They were sons of Huayna Capac and fought over who would become the new Inca king. The war started in 1529 and ended in 1532. Huáscar first declared himself king, thinking he should be the next ruler because he was pure Inca. Atahualpa, who was better at fighting, had more soldiers from their father's northern army. Different accounts give different details. After Atahualpa won, Spanish forces led by Francisco Pizarro arrived. Pizarro captured and eventually killed Atahualpa after he paid a ransom to be freed.

Raymond Poulidor, nicknamed "Pou-Pou," was a French cyclist who rode his whole career. He lived from April 15, 1936, to November 13, 2019. Poulidor's career was special, even though he competed against great riders like Jacques Anquetil and Eddy Merckx. People liked Poulidor because he was seen as an underdog. He was called "the eternal second" because he never won the Tour de France but came in second place three times and third place five times, including when he was 40 years old. He finished 12 out of 14 Tours de France, but never wore the yellow jersey as the race leader. Poulidor won one big race, the 1964 Vuelta a España.

Electronic paper, also called electronic ink or electrophoretic display, is a type of display that looks like regular ink on paper. Unlike regular screens that give off light, electronic paper reflects light, which might make it easier on the eyes and offer a wider view than most screens. By 2008, the contrast in electronic paper was close to that of a newspaper, and some newer displays were even better. An ideal electronic paper display can be read clearly even in bright sunlight. Many electronic paper technologies can show text and images without needing power. Flexible electronic paper uses plastic to make the display, allowing it to be bendable. Electronic paper is used in things like shelf labels, signs, bus timetables, phone screens, and e-readers that display books and magazines.
Torcy is a town in the Pas-de-Calais region of northern France.

Tali Tali Pompey was an Aboriginal artist from Central Australia. She started painting in 2002. During her short career, her work was included in important public galleries. She was born around 1945 or 1947 and passed away on November 16, 2011.

The Bridgeport Sound Tigers are a professional ice hockey team. They play in the American Hockey League (AHL). The Sound Tigers are linked to the New York Islanders, which are in the National Hockey League (NHL). The Sound Tigers began playing in the 2001-02 season. The New York Islanders bought them in 2004. The team is in Bridgeport, Connecticut, and plays its home games at Webster Bank Arena.

Rutgerus Johannes Martinus van Nistelrooy, born on July 1, 1976, is a Dutch football coach and former player. He is now the coach of PSV Eindhoven's under-19 team and an assistant manager for the Netherlands national team. Van Nistelrooy, a former striker, is often considered one of the best strikers of his generation. He scored the most goals in three UEFA Champions League seasons and is the sixth-highest goalscorer in the competition's history with 56 goals. He was also the top scorer in three different European domestic leagues. Van Nistelrooy started his career with Den Bosch, then moved to Heerenveen. He became well-known playing for PSV Eindhoven, where he won two Eredivisie titles. His goal-scoring at PSV caught the attention of Manchester United. A deal was made in the summer of 2000, but due to injuries, his move to Manchester United was finalized a year later for a then-record fee of £19 million. His time at Manchester United was successful; he won the Premier League, FA Cup, Football League Cup, and FA Community Shield, and won the Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year twice. He scored 150 goals in 219 games for Manchester United, becoming their all-time European goalscorer. However, he fell out of favor towards the end of his time there. Real Madrid signed him in 2006. Although he was injured at the end of his time with Real Madrid, he won La Liga twice and the Supercopa de España. He then moved to Hamburg SV in January 2010 and returned to Spain with Málaga in the summer of 2011. He retired from football on May 14, 2012. Internationally, van Nistelrooy played for the Netherlands 70 times and scored 35 goals. He was part of the 2004 Euro, 2006 World Cup, and 2008 Euro squads.

Fana Hlongwane is a South African politician and businessman. He advised the Defence Minister, Joe Modise, from 1995 to 1998. Hlongwane's companies, including Ngwane Defence, Truvelo, and Les Amis (PTY) Ltd, are linked to an alleged arms deal. People think these companies received about 200 million rand from British Aerospace, which may have been bribes to the ANC. Swedish authorities claim Hlongwane received 24 million Swedish kronor in 2003. In 2007, a British Aerospace manager named Bernard Collier paid Hlongwane 7 million rand through a company called IVEMA, which Hlongwane partly owned.

Gopinath Pandurang Munde (born December 12, 1949, died June 3, 2014) was an Indian politician from Maharashtra. He was called a 'lokneta', a popular leader in the state. Munde was a senior leader in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and served as the Minister for Rural Development and Panchayati Raj in Narendra Modi's cabinet. However, his time in the cabinet was short because he died in a road accident. He was a Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) of Maharashtra for five terms from 1980 to 1985 and from 1990 to 2009. He was the leader of the opposition in the assembly from 1992 to 1995. Munde was also the deputy chief minister of Maharashtra from 1995 to 1999. He was elected to Lok Sabha twice in 2009 and 2014 and was the deputy leader of the BJP in Lok Sabha. He joined Modi's cabinet on May 26, 2014, but died in New Delhi a week later due to a road accident. According to media reports, he died in a road accident. However, in January 2019, a US hacker said Munde was murdered. Munde is the shortest-serving cabinet minister in Indian history.

Mazdak, also known as Mazdak the Younger, lived until about 524 or 528. He was a Zoroastrian priest and an Iranian reformer. Mazdak gained power during the time of King Kavadh I. He believed he was a prophet of Ahura Mazda and started programs to help people. Some people see him as an early socialist.

Jan Persson, born on October 3, 1947, in Gothenburg, Sweden, is a Swedish pianist and singer. He had several hit songs in Sweden during the 1970s and 1980s. In 1980, he sang "Växeln Hallå" in the Melodifestivalen, coming in second place. The following year, he sang "Rocky Mountain" and placed third. Janne Lucius, his stage name, came from being a member of a pop band called Lucas in the late 1960s. This band won Sweden's pop band competition in 1967 and had a hit song called "Anti-Social Season." They also had a song called "Go Now" that was successful. Janne Lucius was a pianist for a group called Vi i Femman for many years. He also played piano for a vocal group called Noviserna, where Anna-Lisa Cederquist was a member. In 2009, he performed "Växeln Hallå" at Doobidoo on SVT. Janne Lucius is also a choir director for the Onsala and Mölnlycke Gospel Choir.
Bulgarians are a group of people from Bulgaria and nearby areas. They are part of the South Slavic ethnic group.

My Family is a British sitcom created by Fred Barron. It was produced by DLT Entertainment and Rude Boy Productions. The show aired on BBC One for 11 series from 2000 to 2011, with Christmas specials starting in 2002. In 2004, it was ranked 24th in BBC's "Britain's Best Sitcom." In 2008, it was the most watched sitcom in the United Kingdom. By 2011, it was one of only twelve British sitcoms with over 100 episodes. The series is set in Chiswick, West London. Robert Lindsay plays Ben Harper, Zoë Wanamaker is his wife Susan, and Kris Marshall, Daniela Denby-Ashe, and Gabriel Thomson play their children Nick, Janey, and Michael. Janey left in 2002 but returned in 2004 and stayed until the end. Nick left in 2005 but made occasional guest appearances. The character of Abi, played by Siobhan Hayes, joined in 2002 and left in 2008. Roger and Alfie, played by Keiron Self and Rhodri Meilir, were introduced in 2003 and 2005, respectively.

James Barnes Wyngaarden was born on October 19, 1924, and died on June 14, 2019. He was an American doctor, researcher, and school leader. Wyngaarden helped edit "Cecil Textbook of Medicine," an important book about internal medicine. He worked as the director of the National Institutes of Health from 1982 to 1989. Wyngaarden had four daughters and one son. He was part of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

Pashupati Sharma is a Nepalese folk singer born on October 31, 1982, in Putalibazar Municipality Ward 3, Syangja District, Nepal. In 2003, he moved to Kathmandu for further studies. He started singing in a duet folk singing club called Saptakoshi Dohori Sanjh that same year and released his first official song in 2003. Sharma has sung more than 1000 songs during his career. His songs are about patriotism, love, and satire. One of his recent satire songs, "Lutna Sake Lut," was removed from YouTube. He is known as a living legend in Nepal's folk music industry. In 2018, he released a song called "Chhata Harayo" with Devi Gharti Magar.

Sahibzada Mohammad Shahid Khan Afridi, known as Shahid Afridi or Boom Boom, was born on March 1, 1975. He is a famous Pakistani cricketer and used to lead the Pakistan national cricket team. As a skilled all-rounder, Afridi was known for his steady bowling, which depended on varying the speed of the ball rather than spin. His aggressive batting style also drew a lot of attention. He holds the world record for the fastest century in one-day internationals (ODIs) and is the player with the most sixes in ODIs. Afridi considers himself a better bowler than a batsman and has taken more than 350 wickets in ODIs and 48 wickets in Test matches. He is second on the list for the most wickets in T20 internationals (T20Is), with 98 wickets from 99 matches. Afridi retired from international cricket on February 19, 2017, but returned briefly to play in a charity match in 2018. He officially retired from international cricket on May 31, 2018, at Lord's cricket stadium. On June 13, 2020, Afridi announced on Twitter that he tested positive for COVID-19 after experiencing severe body pain since June 11, 2020. During the country's lockdown, he was actively helping people in remote areas of Balochistan.
Saul Asael Martinez Alvarez, born on January 29, 1976, is a Honduran football player. He plays as a forward for Miami United, a fourth-tier team in the USA.

The Rolling Stones released their album "Their Satanic Majesties Request" in December 1967. It was their sixth British album and eighth American album. Decca Records released it in the UK, and London Records did so in the US. This was the first album released the same way in both countries. The album title is a joke, based on the British passport text. The Rolling Stones tried many new sounds on this album. They used unusual things like mellotron, sound effects, strings, and African rhythms. They made the album without their usual manager and producer, Andrew Loog Oldham. The long recording process was hard for the band members. They used drugs, went to court, and even spent time in jail. The album's cover shows a lenticular image by photographer Michael Cooper. Critics had different opinions about the album. Some said it copied the Beatles' "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band." However, it has been more highly regarded in recent years. After this album, The Rolling Stones stopped using psychedelic music. They went back to their blues roots.

Hadrian, born on January 24, 76, and died on July 10, 138, was Roman emperor from 117 to 138. He came from a Roman family with roots in Spain. His father was a high-ranking official and a cousin of Emperor Trajan. Hadrian married Trajan’s cousin early in his career, likely with Trajan’s wife’s approval. Trajan and his close friend Lucius Licinius Sura favored Hadrian. When Trajan died, Trajan’s wife claimed he named Hadrian as his successor right before he passed away. Rome’s army and Senate agreed Hadrian should be emperor, but four leading senators were later punished for opposing Hadrian. This made the Senate angry at Hadrian and they never forgave him. Hadrian changed Trajan’s expansionist policies and stopped taking land in places like Mesopotamia, Assyria, Armenia, and parts of Dacia. Instead, he focused on strengthening borders and making the empire more unified. He is known for building Hadrian’s Wall, marking the northern boundary of Britain. Hadrian traveled widely across the empire, accompanied by experts and administrators. He supported the military and promoted building projects. In Rome, he rebuilt the Pantheon and built the Temple of Venus and Roma. In Egypt, he might have rebuilt the Serapeum of Alexandria. He admired Greek culture and wanted to make Athens the cultural center of the empire, so he built many temples there. His relationship with a Greek youth named Antinous and Antinous’s death led Hadrian to start a new religious practice late in his reign. Hadrian suppressed the Bar Kokhba revolt in Judaea but generally ruled without major conflicts. His health deteriorated in his final years. He had two more senators executed for alleged plots against him, which made people resent him. His marriage to Vibia Sabina was unhappy and childless. He adopted Antoninus Pius as his successor, asking Antoninus to adopt Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus as well. Hadrian died at Baiae in 138. Antoninus was later declared a god, even though the Senate was against it. Some historians consider Hadrian one of the "five good emperors," but his own Senate found him distant and controlling. He is described as mysterious and complex, capable of great kindness and cruelty, driven by curiosity and ambition.

The dram is the money used in Armenia and Artsakh, a nearby country. Historically, it was split into 100 luma. The word "dram" means "money" in English and is related to the Greek drachma, Arabic dirham, and the English weight unit dram. Silver coins called dram were first used from 1199 to 1375.

Rosemary Clooney, born on May 23, 1928, and died on June 29, 2002, was an American singer and actress. She became famous in the early 1950s with the song "Come On-a My House." Other popular songs she sang include "Botch-a-Me," "Mambo Italiano," "Tenderly," "Half as Much," "Hey There," and "This Ole House." She was also known for her jazz singing. Her career slowed down in the 1960s because of depression and drug problems. However, in 1977, her career revived when Bing Crosby, her co-star in "White Christmas," asked her to perform with him at a show celebrating his 50th anniversary in show business. She kept singing until she died in 2002.

Eupen, a city in Belgium, is near the German border (Aachen), the Dutch border (Maastricht), and the High Fens nature reserve (Ardennes). It was first mentioned in 1213 as part of the Duchy of Limburg. Over time, possession passed to Brabant, Burgundy, the Holy Roman Empire, and France before being given to Prussia in 1815, which later became part of the German Empire in 1871. After World War I, the Treaty of Versailles transferred Eupen and nearby Malmedy from Germany to Belgium. German is the official language, and Eupen is the capital of Belgium's German-speaking community. The city has a small university that offers degrees in education and nursing. In 2010, Eupen's soccer team, K.A.S. Eupen, became the first team from the German-speaking community to play in the Belgian Pro League. As of January 1, 2006, Eupen had a population of 18,248, with 8,892 males and 9,356 females. The population density was 175.90 people per square kilometer. Eupen is considered a Roman Catholic region with conservative views.
The name Ana has been used for seven tropical cyclones in the Atlantic Ocean and one in the Central Pacific.

Alan Abel, born on August 2, 1924, and passed away on September 14, 2018, was an American man who made up false stories and wrote books. He is known for creating hoaxes that got a lot of attention from the media.

Lodano is a village and used to be a separate municipality in Vallemaggia, which is in Ticino, Switzerland. It was first mentioned in 1224 as "Lodino." The village had 70 people in 1709. By 1801, the population grew to 85. In 1850 and 1900, there were 140 and 141 people, respectively. The population then decreased to 134 in 1950 and 86 in 1970. It increased again to 171 people in 2000 and 191 in 2003. Lodano had an area of 13.76 square kilometers. In 2004, Lodano became part of the nearby village Maggia.
Salavre is a town in the Ain area of France, which is in the east of the country.

A volcanic belt is a large area where volcanoes are active. Smaller active areas are called volcanic fields. These belts appear where the earth's temperature is very high, around 700 to 1400 degrees Celsius, causing magma to form. They are usually found along tectonic plate boundaries, about 10 to 50 kilometers below the surface. For instance, in Mexico and western North America, volcanoes are in volcanic belts like the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt and the Northern Cordilleran Volcanic Province. Old volcanic belts are found in inactive areas too. The Canadian Shield, for example, contains more than 150 ancient volcanic belts that are now flat, after being deformed and eroded over time. These belts are millions of years old, ranging from 600 to 1200 million years. They consist of rock layers formed by volcanic activity and related sedimentary rocks, known as greenstone belts. These formed at ancient spreading centers and island arcs. One big greenstone belt is the Abitibi in Ontario and Quebec, Canada. Volcanic belts are like mountain ranges, but instead of mountains formed by faulting and folding, they are made up of volcanoes.

Ellen Schwiers was a German actress who performed on stage, in films, and on television. She was born on June 11, 1930, and died on April 26, 2019. She was in plays by Dürrenmatt and Frisch at the Schauspielhaus Zürich. She acted as Buhlschaft in "Jedermann" at the Salzburg Festival. Over her career, from 1949 to 2015, she appeared in more than 200 films and TV shows, including popular series like "Tatort." She directed plays and started a touring theatre company in 1982. She was also in charge of a festival from 1984.

Deinocheiridae is a family of dinosaurs called ornithomimosaurians. They lived in Asia and North America from a time called the Albian until the Maastrichtian. This family was first named in 1970 by Halszka Osmólska and her colleague. At first, it only included a genus called Deinocheirus. In 2014, a study by Yang-nam Lee and others found Deinocheiridae to be a valid family. They looked at new skeletons of Deinocheirus and other dinosaurs, including Garudimimus and Beishanlong, and found that Deinocheiridae included these genera. The family Garudimimidae, named in 1981, is now considered part of Deinocheiridae. This group of dinosaurs lived between 115 and 69 million years ago. Beishanlong lived from 115 to 100 million years ago, Garudimimus from 98 to 83 million years ago, and Deinocheirus from 71 to 69 million years ago. Other dinosaurs possibly included in this family are Paraxenisaurus, Harpymimus, and Hexing.

Italian (or "italiano") is a Romance language from the Indo-European language family. It is closely related to Latin and descends from it through Vulgar Latin. Italian is an official language in Italy, Switzerland, San Marino, and Vatican City. It also has an official status in some parts of Croatia and Slovenia. Formerly, it was an official language in Albania, Malta, Monaco, Montenegro, and Greece. It is understood in Corsica and Savoie due to similarities with the local languages. In former Italian colonies in Africa, Italian still plays an important role. Italian is spoken by large communities in the Americas and Australia. In some European countries, like Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania, Italian is recognized under the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages, but it is not co-official or protected in these places. Many Italians are bilingual, speaking both Italian and other regional languages. Italian is a major European language, used in the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe and the Council of Europe. It is the second most spoken native language in the European Union with 67 million speakers (15% of the EU population), and 13.4 million EU citizens speak it as a second language (3%). Globally, about 85 million people speak Italian. Italian is the main working language of the Vatican, serving as the common language in the Catholic Church hierarchy and the official language of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta. It is known as the "language of music" due to its use in musical terminology and opera. Many musical terms are Italian. Italian is used in arts, food, and luxury goods. It became the official language of Italy after unification, based on Tuscan speech. Its development was influenced by other Italian languages and some Germanic languages. Italian also borrowed words from Latin, its ancestor language. Throughout history, Italian retained Latin's distinction between short and long consonants. Almost all native Italian words end with vowels, making it easy to rhyme. Italian has a 7-vowel sound system, unlike Latin, which had 10 vowels.

Chen Meng, born on January 15, 1994, is a Chinese table tennis player. She won the women's singles title in the ITTF World Tour Grand Finals three times: in 2017, 2018, and 2019. She also got a silver medal in women's singles at the 2019 World Championships. Additionally, she won the girls' singles title at the 2011 World Junior Table Tennis Championships.

Jõgeva county, or Jõgevamaa, is one of Estonia's 15 counties. It is in the eastern part of the country. Jõgeva county borders Ida-Viru county to the northeast, Lake Peipus to the east, Tartu county to the south, Viljandi county to the southwest, Järva county to the northwest, and Lääne-Viru county to the north.
Eastland is a city in Eastland County, Texas, United States. According to the 2010 census, it had 3,960 people. Eastland is also the county seat of Eastland County.

Grand Island is a town in Erie County, New York, United States. As of 2010, it had 20,374 people, which was 9.41% more than in 2000. The town's name comes from the French "La Grande Île," as it is the largest island in the Niagara River and the third largest in New York. "La Grande Île" is on the town's seal. The town has a history connected to the Attawandaron nation and French and English colonial times. In 1945, there was a plan to make Grand Island a World Peace Capital near the border with Ontario, Canada. The United Nations headquarters would have been on nearby Navy Island. The proposal was not accepted and the UN headquarters was built in New York City instead. Grand Island is in the northwest corner of Erie County and is near the Canada–US border, though there is no bridge to cross. It is to the northwest of Buffalo and south of Niagara Falls. Interstate 190 and New York State Route 324 go through the town.

Margaret Higgins Sanger, born Margaret Louise Higgins on September 14, 1879, and later known as Margaret Sanger Slee, was an American activist for birth control, educator, writer, and nurse. Sanger made the term "birth control" popular, opened the first birth control clinic in the United States, and helped found organizations that turned into the Planned Parenthood Federation of America. She used her writings and speeches to spread her ideas. In 1914, she was in trouble for her book "Family Limitation" and had to go to Britain until it was safe to return to the U.S. Sanger's work led to legal changes that allowed contraception in the U.S. She was often criticized by those who oppose abortion, but she strongly believed in birth control, not abortion. Sanger opened the first birth control clinic in the U.S. in 1916, which got her in trouble. She wanted women to have more equal rights and healthier lives by choosing when to have children. She also wanted to stop dangerous back-alley abortions. In 1921, Sanger started the American Birth Control League, which later became Planned Parenthood. She set up clinics in New York and Harlem. In 1929, she created the National Committee on Federal Legislation for Birth Control to push for legalizing contraception. From 1952 to 1959, she led the International Planned Parenthood Federation. She died in 1966 and is seen as a founder of the modern birth control movement.
coustaussa is a commune in the aude department, which is in the occitanie region of southern france. The people who live there are called coustaussans.

Ștefan Andrei was a Romanian politician. He was born on March 29, 1931, and died on August 31, 2014. He worked as the Minister of Foreign Affairs in Romania from 1978 to 1985. He was arrested after Nicolae Ceaușescu's government fell in 1989.

Vulcanodon means "volcano tooth" and is a type of extinct dinosaur. It belongs to the sauropod family and lived in southern Africa during the early Jurassic period. The only known species is called Vulcanodon karibaensis. It was found in what is now Zimbabwe in 1969. For many years, it was considered the earliest known sauropod and remains one of the most primitive ones discovered. As a four-legged plant-eater, it had the typical sauropod features, like long necks and tails and pillar-like legs. It was smaller than most other sauropods, measuring about 20 meters long. Only part of its skeleton has been found, including parts of its legs and tail. At first, scientists thought it was a prosauropod because of the knife-shaped teeth near its fossils. They believed prosauropods ate both plants and animals. Now, we know the teeth belonged to a different dinosaur. Scientists have unified Vulcanodon with Tazoudasaurus in the family Vulcanodontidae, but this is not universally accepted.

The Texas Ranger division, often called the Texas Rangers or "Los Diablos Tejanos" (the Texan Devils), is a statewide law enforcement agency in Texas. Based in Austin, they have the power to investigate crimes statewide. Over the years, the Texas Rangers have worked on many cases, from murders to political corruption. They have also helped control riots and acted as detectives, protected the Texas governor, and tracked down wanted people. Sometimes, they even worked like a military group. The Texas Rangers started in 1823 when Stephen F. Austin wrote a call to arms. Captain Morris led the first group. In 1835, Daniel Parker proposed a resolution to create a ranger unit to protect the border. This unit was dissolved after the Civil War but quickly came back. Since 1935, they have been part of the Texas Department of Public Safety. By 2019, there were 166 Rangers. The Texas Rangers played a big part in important events in Texas history, like stopping the assassination attempts of Presidents William Howard Taft and Porfirio Díaz. They were also involved in famous cases from the Wild West, such as those of gunfighter John Wesley Hardin, bank robber Sam Bass, and outlaws Bonnie and Clyde. Many books have been written about the Rangers, from serious history books to fun novels. The Rangers are important to Texan culture and are legally protected. There's a museum in Waco, Texas, called the Texas Ranger Hall of Fame and Museum, which honors the Rangers' significance. The Lone Ranger, a famous fictional character, got his name from being a Texas Ranger. Other famous works, like a radio and TV show, also feature Texas Rangers.

Santa Rosa is a city in New Mexico, United States. It is the county seat of Guadalupe County. In 2010, the city had 2,848 people. Santa Rosa is between Albuquerque and Tucumcari. It is on the Pecos River where Interstate 40, U.S. Route 54, and U.S. Route 84 meet. The city is at the edge of the Llano Estacado, also known as the "Staked Plains," in eastern New Mexico and western Texas.

Yeager is a town in Hughes County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, it had 75 people. The town was developed early in the 1900s and grew because of oil and gas. However, it has always had few people.
Here is a list of Guinea's presidents since the country became independent from France in 1958, after saying no to joining the French community in a vote.

Johnnie Lee Cochran Jr. (born October 2, 1937, died March 29, 2005) was an American lawyer and civil rights activist. He was famous for helping O.J. Simpson during his trial. Simpson was accused of killing his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ron Goldman. Cochran used rhymes in court, like "If it doesn't fit, you must acquit!" He also worked with other famous people like Sean Combs, Michael Jackson, and Tupac Shakur. Cochran represented athletes, singers, and victims of police brutality. He defended Marion Jones, an athlete, during doping charges from her high school days. Cochran was known for his skills in court and his efforts to help people hurt by police.

Grandview Heights is a city in Franklin County, Ohio, United States. The population was 6,536 in 2010. It was once part of Marble Cliff, one of Columbus's first suburbs. Marble Cliff became a community in 1890 and was called "Hamlet of Marble Cliff" when it was incorporated in 1901. Grandview Heights became a separate village in 1906 and a city in 1931. It has its own police and fire departments and its own school district. Marble Cliff contracts with Grandview Heights for these services.

Uppsala City IBK was a floorball club in Uppsala, Sweden. The men's team played in Sweden's top division during the 1990s. During the same time, the women's team replaced Storvreta IBK in the Swedish league system. The women's team did well in the Swedish championship playoffs during the 1996-1997 season. They won the first semifinal game against Högdalen IBF, but lost the series in the end.

Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle, also known as Bernard Le Bouyer de Fontenelle, was a French writer. He lived from February 11, 1657, to January 9, 1757. Fontenelle was an important member of three academies in the Institut de France. He is especially famous for making science easier to understand during the Enlightenment.
Hohentannen is a municipality in Weinfelden district, which is in the canton of Thurgau in Switzerland.
Neuenhof is a municipality in the Baden district of Aargau, Switzerland. It is situated in the Limmat Valley.

Hurricane Hortense was the first strong hurricane to hit Guadeloupe and Puerto Rico since Hurricane Hugo in 1989, and it was the second strongest hurricane of the 1996 Atlantic hurricane season. It developed from a tropical wave in the central Atlantic Ocean on September 3. It took four days to become a tropical storm on September 7 after moving westward without growing much. It hit Guadeloupe on September 8, crossed into the Caribbean Sea, and became a hurricane on September 9. It struck Puerto Rico and briefly hit the Dominican Republic before entering the Atlantic again. Here, it grew stronger, reaching category 4 strength on September 13. By September 15, it weakened as it moved north-northeast and hit Nova Scotia as a minimal category 1 hurricane. It continued weakening and entered the Atlantic south of Newfoundland. The storm produced heavy rain and strong winds in the Lesser Antilles. In Guadeloupe, over 50% of banana crops were destroyed. In Puerto Rico, 11,463 houses were damaged, and about 1.4 million people lost power, which was 40% of the island's population. Damage in Puerto Rico was estimated at $153.4 million. There were 19 deaths, mostly from drowning during floods. In the Dominican Republic, strong winds damaged buildings and cut power lines, flooding some roads and harming crops. In the Bahamas and Turks and Caicos, the storm brought strong winds. In Nova Scotia, it caused heavy rain and winds, with power outages and road damage. New Brunswick, Newfoundland, and Prince Edward Island were also affected, though less severely. Overall, damage in Atlantic Canada was about $3.64 million.

Mark Alan Webber, born on August 27, 1976, is an Australian former racing driver. He last competed in the FIA World Endurance Championship for Porsche in 2015, winning the championship that year. Webber won nine Formula One races and finished third in the championship in 2009 and 2011, driving for Red Bull Racing. Before that, he had racing success in Australia, competing in Formula Ford and Formula Holden. In 1995, he moved to the UK to further his career. Webber partnered with fellow Australian Paul Stoddart, who owned a racing team, and they eventually moved into Formula One. In 2000, Webber beat future Formula One world champion Fernando Alonso in the International Formula 3000 season. Webber made his Formula One debut in 2000, scoring Minardi's first points in three years at a home race. In 2009, he won his first Formula One race at the German Grand Prix. Over the next few years, he scored eight podium finishes, including a victory in Brazil. He added ten more podiums in 2011, winning races in Spain, Monaco, Britain, and Hungary. In 2010, Webber finished third in the season, leading for a long time but losing out to teammate Sebastian Vettel in the final race. In 2011, he won another race in Brazil and finished third again behind Vettel and Jenson Button. Webber continued with Red Bull in 2011, outperforming Vettel in the early season but not winning any races in the second half. His last race victory came in the British Grand Prix. By the end of 2011, he was in sixth place. Webber was also a long-term director of the Grand Prix Drivers' Association, the Formula One drivers' union. In 2013, he announced he would retire from Formula One at the end of the season. He began racing for Porsche in 2014, competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship. In November 2015, he became the world endurance champion with the #17 car, driving alongside Timo Bernhard and Brendon Hartley. He raced in the #1 car in 2016. After retiring from driving, Webber joined the BBC's Formula One team as a pundit and reporter from 2014 to 2015 and joined Channel 4's team in 2016 as a full-time pundit. On October 13, 2016, he announced he would retire from driving at the end of the 2016 season to take up a role with Porsche and focus on media work with Channel 4.

Hämeenkoski is a former municipality in Finland. It merged with Hollola on January 1, 2016. Hämeenkoski is in Southern Finland and part of the Päijänne Tavastia region. The municipality had a population of (not specified) and covered an area of which 95% was land. The population density was not specified. Hämeenkoski spoke only Finnish. Lake Pääjärvi is at the border with Hämeenlinna (formerly Lammi).

The M65 is a motorway in Lancashire, England. It starts just south of Preston and goes through the main junctions of the M6 and M61 motorways. It passes east of Darwen, Blackburn, Accrington, Burnley, Brierfield, and Nelson before ending in Colne.

Al Jazeera is a Qatari broadcaster based in Doha. It is part of Al Jazeera Media Network. Initially, Al Jazeera was an Arabic news and current affairs TV channel. It later expanded to include the internet and other language channels. Al Jazeera has 80 offices worldwide. Its Arabic channel often showed different opinions, which caused disagreements in some Arab countries. It became well-known during the war in Afghanistan, as it was the only channel to broadcast the war live. Al Jazeera gets money from the Qatari government but keeps its own editorial rules. Some say it supports the Qatari government, but it also has content that criticizes Qatar. Al Jazeera is seen as mostly supporting Islamist views, being pro-Sunni and against Shia. However, it claims to present all sides equally. It has aired videos from Osama bin Laden. In 2017, some countries, including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Egypt, asked Qatar to close Al Jazeera as part of demands during a conflict. Other media outlets supported Al Jazeera. According to The Atlantic, Al Jazeera appears more moderate and Western than some Islamist groups. It has very little religious content.

Jimmy Wayne Jamison was an American musician, singer, and songwriter. He lived from August 23, 1951, to September 1, 2014. Jamison was the lead singer of the rock band Survivor from 1984 to 1989, again in 1992, from 2000 to 2006, and from 2011 until his death. He also wrote and performed the theme song "I'm Always Here" for the TV show Baywatch in the 1990s.

Ace of Base is a Swedish pop group. It originally had siblings Jonas Berggren, Linn Berggren, and Jenny Berggren, plus Ulf Ekberg, who joined in 1990. Their first album, "Happy Nation," came out in 1992. It later became known as "The Sign" and sold nine million copies in the U.S., being the best-selling album of 1994. This was one of the most successful first albums ever, producing three No. 1 hits: "All That She Wants," "The Sign," and "Don't Turn Around." They kept making hit songs in the 1990s, like "Beautiful Life," "Lucky Love," "Cruel Summer," and "Life Is a Flower." By 2002, they had sold 30 million copies of their first four albums, making them the third most successful Swedish group after ABBA and Roxette. Although they haven't been very active since 2012, the group hasn't officially broken up. They've released some demo tracks recently, first through their Facebook page, then in 2015 on the album "Hidden Gems." In 2020, a boxset with an expanded two-disc version of "Hidden Gems" came out. Jenny Berggren continues to perform the group's songs in solo concerts worldwide.
Waltenschwil is a municipality in the Muri district of the Aargau canton in Switzerland.

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) is the main group that runs the Democratic Party in the United States. It organizes the Democratic National Convention every four years. This convention picks a candidate for president and makes the party's rules. While it helps party candidates, it doesn't control elected officials. The DNC's leader is chosen by its members. It also raises money to help with its work. The DNC was formed at the first Democratic National Convention in 1848. Its main partner is the Republican National Committee.

The title is a German translation of an old Norse phrase. In Norse mythology, this phrase refers to a prophesied war involving various beings and gods. This war leads to the world being burned, immersed in water, and then renewed. However, Wagner's version in his "Ring" cycle differs a lot from the original Norse stories.

Jumanji is a 1995 American fantasy comedy adventure movie. It came from a 1981 children's book by Chris Van Allsburg. The movie is the first in the Jumanji series. It was written by Chris Van Allsburg, Greg Taylor, Jonathan Hensleigh, and Jim Strain. The main actors are Robin Williams, Kirsten Dunst, David Alan Grier, Bonnie Hunt, Bradley Pierce, Jonathan Hyde, and Bebe Neuwirth. The movie is about a magical board game. It can hurt people when they play. In 1969, a boy named Alan Parrish got stuck inside the game with his friend Sarah Whittle. Twenty-six years later, two kids, Judy and Peter Shepherd, find the game. They start playing and accidentally free the grown-up Alan. They look for Sarah and decide to finish the game to undo the damage and go back to normal. The movie came out on December 15, 1995. Some people liked it, some didn't. It made a lot of money, over $263 million worldwide. It was the 10th most popular movie that year. It led to an animated TV show from 1996 to 1999. Later, there were more movies in the series: Jumanji (2005), Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle (2017), and Jumanji: The Next Level (2019). Columbia Pictures took over making and showing these later movies.

Extratropical cyclones, sometimes called mid-latitude or wave cyclones, are low-pressure areas that help drive weather over much of the Earth. They can cause various weather conditions, from mild showers to heavy storms, including thunderstorms and blizzards. These cyclones are large-scale weather systems found in middle latitudes. Unlike tropical cyclones, extratropical cyclones create rapid temperature changes along lines called weather fronts around the center of the cyclone.

Mathieu Pierre Flamini was born on March 7, 1984. He is a French professional footballer who also started an environmental business. Flamini plays as a midfielder. He has played for several teams, including Marseille in France, Arsenal and Crystal Palace in England, Milan in Italy, and Getafe in Spain. He has also played for the French national team three times. Flamini co-founded GF Biochemicals, the first company to produce levulinic acid in large quantities.

The Althingi is Iceland's national parliament. It is the oldest surviving parliament in the world, founded in 930. It met at Thing Fields until 1800, when it was discontinued. In 1844, it was revived and moved to Reykjavik, where it remains today. The current parliament building was constructed in 1881 using Icelandic stone. The Althingi has 63 members and holds elections every four years. They use a proportional representation system based on party lists. Steingrímur J. Sigfússon is the current speaker. Iceland's constitution sets up six electoral constituencies, which can increase to seven. The number of seats per constituency is determined by legislation, with each constituency having at least six seats. Parties with more than 5% of the national vote receive additional seats to ensure proportional representation. If voter representation varies too much between constituencies, the Icelandic National Electoral Commission adjusts the seat allocation to balance it.

Mneme is a small moon of Jupiter. It was found by astronomers from the University of Hawaii in 2003 and given the temporary name s/2003 J 21. Mneme is about 2 kilometers in size and takes 640.769 days to orbit Jupiter, at a distance of 21,427,000 kilometers. Its orbit is tilted 148° to Jupiter’s equator, and its path is somewhat elliptical, with an eccentricity of 0.2214. It moves at an average speed of 2.43 km/s. In March 2005, Mneme was named after Mneme, one of the original muses. People sometimes mistake Mneme for Mnemosyne, the mother of the muses, who was Zeus’s (Jupiter’s) wife in some stories. Mneme is part of the Ananke group, a group of small, orbiting moons of Jupiter that move in retrograde paths between 19.3 and 22.7 million kilometers away, with inclinations around 150°.

Sigma Octantis, also written as σ Octantis, is called Polaris Australis. It is the current south star. Because it is close to the southern celestial pole, it serves as the southern pole star. It is a single star in the southern circumpolar constellation of Octans. It is about 281 light-years away from Earth. Sigma Octantis is a giant star with a spectral type of F0 III. It is a Delta Scuti variable, with its brightness changing by about 0.03 magnitudes every 2.33 hours.

Matthew Nagy (born April 24, 1978) is an American football coach and former quarterback. He is currently the head coach for the Chicago Bears in the NFL. As a quarterback, he played college football at the University of Delaware from 1997 to 2000. There, he set several school passing records. After not getting an NFL contract, he joined the Arena Football League (AFL). He played for four teams: the New York Dragons, Carolina Cobras, Georgia Force, and Columbus Destroyers, for six seasons. After his playing career, Nagy worked as an assistant coach for the Philadelphia Eagles from 2009 to 2013, under head coach Andy Reid. In 2013, when Reid moved to the Kansas City Chiefs, Nagy followed him, becoming the quarterbacks coach. He was promoted to offensive coordinator in 2016. In 2018, Nagy became the head coach of the Bears. In his first year, he led the team to their first NFC North championship and playoff appearance since 2010.

Potosí is a department in southwestern Bolivia. It covers 118,218 km² and has 823,517 people (2012 census). The capital is the city of Potosí. Most of the area is a barren, mountainous region. There is a large plateau to the west where the world's largest salt flat, Salar de Uyuni, is located. In the past, Potosí was the richest province in the Spanish Empire. It provided a lot of silver sent to Europe. Today, Potosí is home to the San Cristóbal silver, zinc, and lead mines. These mines were developed by the U.S. company Apex Silver Mines Limited from Colorado. In November 2008, they were sold to the Japanese Sumitomo Corporation.

Pind Dadan Khan tehsil is a subdivision in Jhelum district, Punjab, Pakistan. It is based in a town of the same name, near the Jhelum River, about 22 kilometers from the M2 motorway. The area is famous for the Khewra Salt Mines, the largest salt mines in Asia, which have been used for more than 2,000 years and include an underground mosque. There is a long history in this area, going back to the time of Alexander the Great's invasion (see Punjab, Pakistan). The town of Jalalpur Sharif, close to Pind Dadan Khan, is said to be where Alexander the Great's horse, Bucephalus, is buried. Pind Dadan Khan town is named after Dadan Khan, a devoted Sufi saint from the Awan tribe.

Bellaire is a village in Belmont County, Ohio, United States. It is part of the Wheeling, West Virginia metropolitan area, and Wheeling is east of Bellaire across the Ohio River. In 2010, the population was 4,278. The village reached its highest population in 1920. Bellaire is near the Ohio River. The Bellaire Toll Bridge, which is now closed, was used in the 1991 movie "The Silence of the Lambs." The curved railroad bridge over the Ohio River and the B&O Railroad Viaduct are featured in the 2010 film "Unstoppable" and are historic structures. A logo with the historic stone bridge is on official village documents and police uniforms. It was designed by Michael A. Massa, who also created the Belmont County seal, under the former mayor's administration.
Lionel Guérin is a French CEO and politician.

An antimicrobial is something that kills tiny living things or stops them from growing. Antimicrobial medicines can be grouped based on the tiny living things they target. For example, antibiotics fight bacteria, and antifungals fight fungi. These medicines can also be sorted by their job. Those that kill tiny living things are called microbicidal, while those that just stop their growth are called biostatic. Using antimicrobial medicines to treat an infection is called antimicrobial chemotherapy. Using them to stop an infection from happening is called antimicrobial prophylaxis. There are mainly three types of antimicrobial agents: disinfectants, which kill many tiny living things on non-living surfaces; antiseptics, which are used on living tissue to reduce infection during surgery; and antibiotics, which fight tiny living things inside the body. Now, "antibiotic" can also mean synthetic agents like sulfonamides or fluoroquinolones. The term "antibacterial" is often used for antibiotics, especially in medical contexts. Antibacterial agents can be further divided into two: those that kill bacteria (bactericidal) and those that slow down bacterial growth (bacteriostatic). New advancements have led to solutions that can kill microbes immediately upon contact, going beyond just stopping their growth.
In June 2011, Shibasaki was chosen to be part of the Japan team that played against Peru. However, he did not get to play in the match.

In September 1944, a strong hurricane hit the east coast of the United States. It caused the most damage in New England but also affected areas like the Outer Banks, Mid-Atlantic states, and Canadian Maritimes. This storm was very fierce and was compared to the 1938 Long Island Express, which is known as one of the worst storms in New England history. The hurricane was first noticed east of the Lesser Antilles on September 4. It became a tropical storm northeast of the Virgin Islands on September 9. The storm moved northwest and strengthened, reaching its strongest on September 13 near the Bahamas. It then curved northward. On September 14, the storm passed the Outer Banks and hit Long Island and Rhode Island as a weaker hurricane on September 15. After landfall, the storm changed into an extratropical cyclone. It kept moving northeast and merged with another extratropical system off Greenland on September 16.

Mostafa Pour-mohammadi was born on March 9, 1960, in Qom. He is an Iranian politician and prosecutor. He has held different positions and cabinet posts. Pour-mohammadi served as the Minister of Interior from 2005 to 2008 and as the Minister of Justice from 2013 to 2017. He is reportedly involved in the 1988 massacre of Iranian prisoners.

The office of the prime minister in Prussia existed from 1848. This was when King Frederick William IV created the position during the 1848–49 revolution. The office ended in 1947, when Prussia was abolished by the Allied Control Council.
Sarat Pujari was an actor, director, and producer in the Odia film industry. He lived from August 8, 1934, to May 12, 2014. He came from a place called Jhaduapada in Sambalpur.

John Dixon was born on February 20, 1929, and died on May 7, 2015. He was an Australian comic book artist and writer. He is famous for creating the comic strip "Air Hawk and the Flying Doctors," which was published from 1959 to 1986.

Wind power uses wind to make electricity through wind turbines. It is a clean and renewable source, better for the environment than burning fossil fuels. Wind farms have many turbines connected to the power network. Onshore wind farms are cheaper than coal or gas plants, but can change the landscape. Offshore wind farms are stronger but cost more to build and maintain. Small onshore farms can feed energy to the grid or provide power to remote areas. Wind is sometimes unreliable and can change quickly, so it needs other power sources or storage to ensure a steady supply. In 2018, wind provided 4.8% of global electricity, with 591 gigawatts installed. Wind supplied 15% of electricity in Europe in 2019, and at least 83 countries use wind power.

Jon Llewellyn Kyl, born on April 25, 1942, is an American politician who served as a U.S. Senator for Arizona. He was a Republican and held Arizona's Senate seats from 1995 to 2013, and again in 2018. During his first term, he served with John McCain. Kyl was Senate minority whip from 2007 to 2013. Kyl was born in Nebraska and lived in Iowa for some time. He studied at the University of Arizona and worked as a lawyer and lobbyist in Phoenix. He joined the U.S. House of Representatives in 1987 and served there until 1995. He won a U.S. Senate seat in 1994 and kept getting re-elected until he retired in January 2013. In 2006, he was named one of the best U.S. senators by Time magazine. In 2007, he was ranked as the fourth most conservative U.S. senator by National Journal. He was involved in important Republican roles, including chairing the Republican Policy Committee and the Republican Conference. Kyl said in February 2011 that he would not run for re-election in 2012 and planned to retire after his third term. He ruled out running for any other office, except maybe the vice presidency. After leaving the Senate in 2013, he worked as a lawyer and helped nominate Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court. In September 2018, Kyl was chosen by Governor Doug Ducey to fill the Senate seat left by John McCain, who had passed away. He announced he would not run for the remaining term after the 2020 election. Kyl is the first person to return to the Senate through an appointment since 1975. He left the Senate in December 2018 and was replaced by Martha McSally.
Andlonsheim is a town in Haut-Rhin, which is in Grand Est, in northeastern France.

Quintana Roo, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Quintana Roo, is one of Mexico's 32 states. It has 11 municipalities and its capital is Chetumal. Located on the eastern part of the Yucatán Peninsula, Quintana Roo is bordered by Campeche to the west, Yucatán to the northwest, and Belize districts to the south. It also has a coastline with the Caribbean Sea to the east and the Gulf of Mexico to the north. Quintana Roo used to share a small border with Guatemala but this ended in 2013 when the Supreme Court of Justice of Mexico decided the boundary dispute in favor of Campeche. Quintana Roo includes cities like Cancún, islands such as Cozumel and Isla Mujeres, and towns like Bacalar, Playa del Carmen, and Akumal. There are also ancient Mayan ruins in the state, including Chacchoben, Cobá, Kohunlich, Muyil, Tulum, Xel-Há, and Xcaret. The Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve is also located here. The state's population is growing quickly because of hotel construction and job demand. Many people move from Yucatán, Campeche, Tabasco, and Veracruz. Quintana Roo often experiences severe hurricanes because of its location. In 2007, Hurricane Dean hit with strong winds.

Geoffrey L. Duncan, born on April 1, 1975, is an American businessman and politician. He is the 12th Lieutenant Governor of Georgia. Before that, he was a member of the Georgia House of Representatives. Duncan played college baseball for the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets. He then played professional baseball for six years. He stopped playing due to a shoulder injury. After retiring from baseball, Duncan started a business. He was elected to the Georgia House in 2012.

recruitment is about finding and choosing people for jobs in a company. This involves identifying suitable candidates, attracting them, screening them, shortlisting, and interviewing them. Recruitment can also cover choosing people for unpaid roles. Managers, human resources specialists, and recruitment experts can do this work. Sometimes, public agencies or commercial recruitment firms help with parts of the process. Online tools and even artificial intelligence are now commonly used in recruitment.

The Belize Barrier Reef is a series of coral reefs along Belize's coast. It is in the northern and southern parts of the country. It is part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, which stretches from Cancún in Mexico to Honduras. This makes it the second largest coral reef system in the world after Australia's Great Barrier Reef. It is Belize's top tourist attraction, popular for scuba diving and snorkeling, and attracts almost half of the country's 260,000 visitors each year. It is also important for the country's fishing industry. Charles Darwin called it "the most remarkable reef in the West Indies" in 1842. The reef includes three distinct atolls: Turneffe Atoll, Glover's Reef, and Lighthouse Reef. Lighthouse Reef, the easternmost area for diving, has the Great Blue Hole, famous since 1970 by Jacques Cousteau. Turneffe Atoll is located east of Belize City and is the closest atoll to the capital. These different reefs offer various scuba diving areas, including walls, pinnacles, and reef flats in a large sea area.

Wesley Allison Clark was born on April 10, 1927, and died on February 22, 2016. He was an American physicist known for designing the first modern personal computer. Clark was also a computer designer and worked with Charles Molnar to create the Linc computer, which was the first minicomputer. The Linc computer inspired the development of personal computers, similar to other computers like the PDP-1. Clark grew up in Kinderhook, New York, and northern California. He was born in New Haven, Connecticut, and his parents, Wesley Sr. and Eleanor Kittell, moved to California. Clark studied physics at the University of California, Berkeley, graduating in 1947. His career started as a physicist at the Hanford site. In 1981, Clark received the Eckert–Mauchly award for his work on computer architecture. In 1984, he got an honorary degree from Washington University. Clark was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1999. He received the IEEE Computer Society Computer Pioneer Award, becoming one of the first recipients for "first personal computer."

In physics, the center of mass is a special point in space where the weighted average of the positions of all the parts of an object or a system is zero. This point is important because applying a force here will cause the object to move straight without spinning. Mechanics problems are often easier to solve when considering this point. The center of mass can be thought of as where the whole mass of an object can be imagined to be concentrated for understanding its movement. For a single, solid object with uniform mass, the center of mass is at the centroid. However, it can be outside the object, like in a horseshoe. For groups of separate objects, such as planets, the center of mass is not necessarily where any individual object is located. The center of mass is crucial for calculations involving how masses move in space, including their motion and rotation. In space, the movement of planets is often calculated by considering them as point masses at their centers of mass. The center of mass frame is a reference point where the overall mass of a system is not moving.

Eight Cousins, or The Aunt-Hill, was published in 1875 by American author Louisa May Alcott. The book tells the story of Rose Campbell. Rose is a lonely and sick girl who recently lost her parents. She now lives with her great aunts, who are her wealthy family's leaders in Boston. Her guardian, Uncle Alec, comes back from a trip. He takes care of Rose and has new ideas about raising children. These ideas help Rose feel happier and healthier. She joins her family, which includes seven boy cousins and many aunts and uncles. Rose also befriends Phebe, the young housemaid of her aunts. Phebe's cheerful attitude helps Rose appreciate her own good fortune.

Cristina Deutekom was a Dutch operatic coloratura soprano who lived from August 28, 1931, to August 7, 2014. She performed with many famous tenors of her time, such as Carlo Bergonzi, José Carreras, Franco Corelli, Plácido Domingo, Nicolai Gedda, Alfredo Kraus, Luciano Pavarotti, and Richard Tucker.

The Wiener Sport-Club, often shortened to WSC, was founded in 1883 in Vienna, Austria. It is one of the country's oldest sports clubs. They have a traditional home in the Dornbach area of the city, which is in the 17th district.

The Battle of Leipzig, also known as the Battle of the Nations, took place from October 16 to 19, 1813, in Leipzig, Saxony. The coalition of Austria, Prussia, Sweden, and Russia, led by Emperor Alexander I and Karl von Schwarzenberg, defeated Napoleon's French army. Napoleon's army included Polish, Italian, and German troops from the Rhine Confederation, mainly Saxony and Württemberg. This battle ended the 1813 German campaign and involved about 500,000 soldiers, 2,200 cannons, and resulted in 127,000 casualties. It was the largest battle in Europe before World War I. After this defeat, Napoleon had to leave for France, and the Sixth Coalition continued to invade France the following year. Napoleon was forced to give up and was sent to Elba in May 1814.

Helene & Gänget was a dansband in Kristianstad, Sweden. The band was formed in 1990 by members of Färmarna dansband. In 1995, they became successful with the album "Segla Din Båt I Hamn." The band stopped performing in 2002. Its singer, Helene Persson, started acting as the host of the Kristianstad programme. Some famous songs by the band include "Segla Din Båt I Hamn," "En Korg Med Blommor," and "Nåndans Så Finns Du."
Sheringham is a town in Norfolk, United Kingdom. It has 7,367 people living there. The town's motto, given in 1953 to the Sheringham Urban District Council, is "The sea enriches and the pine adorns."

A château is a large house or residence. It was usually owned by nobles or the wealthy. In the past, and still often today, especially in French-speaking areas, châteaux can be both fancy homes and places with defensive features.

Phoenix is a small constellation in the southern sky. It was first shown on a map by Johann Bayer in 1603. Nicolas Louis de Lacaille later mapped its brighter stars in 1756. Phoenix, along with Grus, Pavo, and Tucana, is known as the southern birds. The brightest star, Alpha Phoenix, is called Ankaa. It is an orange giant. Beta Phoenix is a pair of yellow giants. Nu Phoenix has dust around it. There are ten star systems with planets in Phoenix, and it includes two big galaxy clusters called El Gordo and the Phoenix cluster. Phoenix is where two meteor showers begin: the Phoenicids in December, and the July Phoenicids.

Calfreisen was a former municipality in the Plessur district of the Graubünden canton in Switzerland. On January 1, 2013, Calfreisen joined other former municipalities—Castiel, Langwies, Lüen, Molinis, Peist, and St. Peter-Pagig—to form the new municipality of Arosa.

County Armagh, named after its town Armagh, is one of Ireland's traditional counties. It is part of Northern Ireland and one of six counties there. Situated next to Lough Neagh's southern shore, County Armagh has an area of about 1,326 km² and around 174,792 people live there. It's called the "orchard county" because it has many apple orchards. County Armagh is in the historic province of Ulster.

Chini Modi, also known as Irshad (born September 30, 1939, and died March 19, 2017), was a poet, novelist, short story writer, and critic who wrote in Gujarati. He was born and worked in Gujarat, India. Educated in languages, he taught at different schools and colleges. He became known as a poet and writer. He received several awards, including the Sahitya Akademi Award, the Vali Gujarati Award, and the Narsinh Mehta Award.

Bell Canada, often called Bell, is a big phone company in Canada. It has offices in Montreal, Quebec. Bell is the main phone company in Ontario and Quebec. It is part of a group called Stentor. In western Canada, Bell competes with other companies like Telus and Shaw. Bell also provides mobile services through its Bell Mobility and Virgin Mobile brands. It offers TV through Bell Satellite TV and Bell Fibe TV. Bell's main competitors in Ontario are Rogers Communications, while in Quebec, it faces competition from Videotron and Telus. Bell serves over 13 million phone lines and has its main offices in the Bell complex in Montreal. BCE Inc., formerly known as Bell Canada Enterprises, owns Bell Canada. BCE also owns Bell Media, which runs TV networks like CTV. BCE has stakes in sports teams, including the Montreal Canadiens and Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment. In 2011, BCE ranked 262 on Forbes Global 2000 list.

Lager Norderney was a Nazi concentration camp on Alderney, an island in the Channel Islands. It was named after the island of Norderney. The German Organisation Todt (OT) built four labor camps on Alderney to house workers for planned fortifications. Lager Norderney was located at Saye. Lager Borkum was at Platte Saline, Lager Sylt was near the old telegraph tower at La Fouleré, and Lager Helgoland was in the northwest corner of the island. From March 1943 to June 1944, the control of Lager Norderney changed. It was run by the SS-Baubrigade, and from June 1944, Lager Norderney became a subcamp of the Neuengamme concentration camp, which was in Hamburg, Germany.

Portage la Prairie is a small city in the central part of Manitoba, Canada. As of 2016, it had 13,304 people living there. The city is west of Winnipeg, on the Trans-Canada Highway, between Saskatchewan and Ontario. It is near the Assiniboine River, which used to flood the town frequently. However, a flood control channel was built to divert the water to Lake Manitoba. The city is surrounded by the Rural Municipality of Portage la Prairie. According to Environment Canada, Portage la Prairie has the most sunny days during warm months in Canada. It is also the administrative center for the Dakota Tipi First Nations reserve.

Khunjerab Pass is a high mountain pass in the Karakoram Mountains. It is in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region, specifically in Hunza and Nagar districts. The pass is also on the border between Pakistan and China's Xinjiang region.

A photoreceptor cell is a special type of cell in the retina that turns light into signals. These signals help start biological processes. Photoreceptor cells have proteins that absorb light, changing the cell's membrane potential. In mammals, there are three main types: rods, cones, and intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs). Rods and cones are the most common. Rods are sensitive and work in very low light. Cones need brighter light to work and there are three types, each sensitive to different colors. ipRGCs don't help see, but affect circadian rhythms and pupil reactions. Rods are very sensitive, while cones detect colors. In humans, there are about 120 million rods and 6 million cones. The number of rods and cones differs between animals that are mostly active during the day or night. Some owls, which are nocturnal, have many rods. The human visual system has about 2.4 to 3 million ganglion cells, with about 1 to 2% being photosensitive. These ganglion cells form the optic nerves. Photoreceptors are arranged in a hexagonal pattern called the retinal mosaic. In humans, only rods and cones are photosensitive. Some animals, like birds, have light-sensitive neurons in their cerebrospinal fluid. Insects and molluscs have different types of photoreceptors.

Ahmed Jibril is the founder and leader of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine – General Command (PFLP-GC). During the Syrian civil war, Jibril supported the Assad government. PFLP-GC members helped government forces fight against the Syrian opposition. However, in Yarmouk camp in Damascus, there were clashes with rebels. The PFLP-GC lost some members and had to leave the camp. Jibril had to leave the city.

Homa Rousta, born on September 26, 1946, and died on September 26, 2015, was an Iranian actress who worked in films and on stage. She was married to Hamid Samandarian, a stage director. Rousta studied theatre at a school in Bucharest and began her acting career in 1971. Her most famous role was in the 1992 film "From Karkheh to Rhine," for which she was nominated for the Best Actress award at the Fajr Film Festival. She passed away from cancer in a hospital in Los Angeles, California. Her body was later sent back to Iran and buried at Behesht Zahra cemetery, next to her husband's grave.

Saint-Étienne is a city in eastern central France, in the Massif Central region, southwest of Lyon. It's in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes area and lies on a road connecting Toulouse with Lyon. Saint-Étienne is the capital of the Loire department. As of 2017, the city has 172,565 people, and the urban area has over 520,000. In recent years, Saint-Étienne has changed a lot. It is working to go from an old industrial city to a modern "European Capital of Design." This effort led to big changes in the city's main areas.

Elliott County is in Kentucky, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 7,852 people. By 2018, the number was 7,508. The main town is Sandy Hook. The county was created in 1869 from parts of Morgan, Lawrence, and Carter counties. It's named after John Lyle Elliott, who was a U.S. congressman and a Confederate justice of the Kentucky Court of Appeals. Elliott County does not allow selling alcohol anywhere in the county.
Saint-Jouin is a town in Calvados, which is in Normandy. Normandy is in northwestern France.

In cellular biology, active transport moves molecules from an area with less concentration to an area with more concentration—against the concentration gradient. This process needs energy from the cell. There are two types: primary active transport uses ATP, and secondary active transport uses an electrochemical gradient. An example in the human body is how the intestines absorb glucose.
The Akrisios is a tragedy written by Sophocles, an Athenian playwright from the 5th century BCE. Only fragments of this play survive.

Bob Beckwith, born on September 21, 1933, is a former New York City Fire Department member. After the September 11, 2001 attacks, he stood next to President George W. Bush at the World Trade Center ruins. Photos of Beckwith and the president appeared on the front page of the "New York Daily News" and the cover of "Time" magazine. This made him famous, leading to more press and interviews. Since then, Beckwith has met President Bush several times, given many public speeches, and helped raise money for charities.

The ECW World Heavyweight Championship was a professional wrestling title used in Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW) and later in World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE). It started in 1992 with ECW's predecessor, Eastern Championship Wrestling. The first champion was Jimmy Snuka. ECW stopped operating in 2001, and WWE bought it in 2003. In 2006, WWE brought back the championship as the main title for their ECW brand. It was one of three world titles in the promotion, alongside the WWE Championship and the World Heavyweight Championship on Raw and SmackDown. In 2008, the ECW Championship became the sole world title on Raw. When WWE stopped the ECW brand in 2010, the title was retired with Ezekiel Jackson as the last champion.
Carlos Oscar Reichenbach Filho was a Brazilian filmmaker. He was born on June 14, 1945, and passed away on June 14, 2012.
Örkelljunga is a place and the main town in Örkelljunga municipality, in Skåne county, Sweden. In 2020, it had 10,300 people living there.

Cory Scott Gardner, born on August 22, 1974, is an American lawyer and politician. He has been serving as Colorado's junior United States senator since 2015. Gardner is a Republican. Before becoming a senator, he was a U.S. representative for Colorado's 4th congressional district from 2011 to 2015 and a member of the Colorado House of Representatives from 2005 to 2011. Gardner won a close election against Democratic incumbent Mark Udall in 2014 to become a senator. From 2017 to 2019, he was the chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee. After the 2018 midterm elections, Gardner and Heidi Ganahl, a University of Colorado regent, were the only Republicans holding statewide elected offices in Colorado. In 2020, Gardner was considered one of the senators most likely to lose his seat.

The Fulbright Program, including the Fulbright-Hays Program, is one of many cultural exchange programs in the United States. It aims to improve understanding between people from the U.S. and other countries by sending and receiving students, scholars, teachers, professionals, scientists, and artists. Americans and citizens from other countries can apply to study, research, teach, or share their skills abroad or in the U.S. Senator J. William Fulbright started the program in 1946, and it is well-known and highly respected worldwide. About 8,000 grants are given each year, mostly to U.S. students, scholars, and teachers, and to foreign students and visiting scholars. The program is run by organizations like the Institute of International Education and operates in more than 160 countries. It gets funding from the U.S. Department of State, which is part of the Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs. Funding also comes from governments, foundations, corporations, and local institutions both in the U.S. and abroad. In 49 countries, a joint U.S. and foreign commission manages the program, while in other countries, the U.S. embassy oversees it. Over 370,000 people have taken part since it began, and many Fulbright alumni have won important awards, like 60 Nobel Prizes and 86 Pulitzer Prizes.

The first United States Congress, which included the Senate and the House of Representatives, met from March 4, 1789, to March 4, 1791. This was during George Washington's first two years as president. The first meetings took place at Federal Hall in New York City, and later at Congress Hall in Philadelphia. When the first Congress met, the United States government started operating under the new Constitution from 1787. The number of seats in the House of Representatives was decided according to the Constitution. Both the Senate and the House mostly supported the president. This Congress sent twelve proposed changes to the Constitution to the states. Ten of these changes were accepted and became part of the Constitution on December 15, 1791. They are known as the Bill of Rights.

Colonel Reginald Edward Harry Dyer, CB, was a military officer who served in the Bengal Army and later in the Indian Army. His career started with the British Army, then he moved to work with the Indian army. As a temporary brigadier-general, he was in charge when the Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened in Amritsar, Punjab. He is known as "the butcher of Amritsar" because he ordered soldiers to shoot at peaceful people. The official report said that at least 379 people were killed and over a thousand were injured. Some people who testified suggested even more deaths. Dyer was taken out of duty and widely criticized in Britain and India. However, some people from the British Raj considered him a hero. Some historians believe this event was a significant step toward ending British rule in India.

The Millennium Dome, simply called the Dome, was a big round building used for the Millennium Experience exhibition. This exhibition celebrated the start of the third millennium. It is one of the ninth largest buildings in the world by space used. Located on the Greenwich Peninsula in southeast London, the Dome was open to the public from January 1, 2000, to December 31, 2000. The project and exhibition were political and did not get as many visitors as expected, so the press considered it a failure. All parts of the original exhibition were sold or taken apart. In a 2005 report, the cost to sell the Dome and surrounding land (which increased to 170 acres from the initial 48 acres) and manage the Dome until the deal was closed was £28.7 million. The 48 acres occupied by the Dome were estimated to be worth £48 million, but it was decided to keep the Dome instead of demolishing it. The Dome still exists and is now part of the O2. The Prime Meridian goes through the western edge of the Dome, and the nearest London Underground station is North Greenwich on the Jubilee Line.

Gene Autry is a town in Carter County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, the town had 158 people, which was more than in 2000 when there were 99 people. It is part of the Ardmore, Oklahoma micropolitan area.

Sabayon Linux is an Italian Linux distribution based on Gentoo. It was previously called RR4 Linux and RR64 Linux. Created by Fabio Erculiani and the Sabayon development team, Sabayon follows the "out of the box" philosophy. This means it comes with many applications ready to use and a self-configured operating system. Sabayon uses a rolling release cycle, has its own software repository, and uses a package management system called Entropy. Available for both x86 and AMD64, with ARMv7 support for BeagleBone in development, it’s named after the Italian dessert zabaione, made from eggs. The Sabayon logo is an image of a chicken’s foot.
Patrick Barnabas Burke Mayhew, Baron Mayhew of Twysden, was born on September 11, 1929, and died on June 25, 2016. He was a British lawyer and politician.

Alumpeedika is a small village in Oachira, Kollam district, Kerala, India. It is part of Clappana Panchayath and is in South Kerala. Alumpeedika is 31 km north of Kollam, the district headquarters. It is about 1 km from Oachira and 101 km from the state capital, Thiruvananthapuram. Nearby towns include Kayamkulam, Oachira, and Karunagappalli. Alumpeedika is close to the border of Kollam and Alappuzha districts. It is near the Arabian Sea.

He is known as a Japanese professional wrestler who worked for All Japan Pro Wrestling (AJPW) most of his career. He won three major titles, becoming the first Triple Crown Heavyweight Champion. These titles were the PWF Heavyweight Championship, the NWA United National Championship, and the NWA International Heavyweight Championship. He also teamed up with Yoshiaki Yatsu and won the NWA International Tag Team Championship and the PWF Tag Team Championship, unifying both.

Clean and Sober is a 1988 American drama film. Glenn Gordon Caron directed it. Michael Keaton stars as a real estate agent with a substance abuse problem. This was Keaton's second dramatic role after "Touch and Go." Kathy Baker, M. Emmet Walsh, Morgan Freeman, Luca Bercovici, and Tate Donovan are in the supporting cast. Ron Howard, who directed Keaton in comedies like "Night Shift" and "Gung Ho," served as a co-producer.

Conficker, also called Downadup and Kido, is a computer worm targeting Microsoft Windows. It was first found in November 2008. It spreads by using Windows software flaws and guessing passwords. While spreading, it forms a botnet. It is hard to stop because it uses many advanced techniques. Conficker infected millions of computers in over 190 countries, more than any other computer worm since 2003's Welchia. Even though it spread widely, it didn't cause much damage. This might be because the people who made it—thought to be Ukrainian criminals—didn't want to draw attention. Four men were arrested, and one pleaded guilty, getting 48 months in prison.

Seattle Sounders FC is an American soccer team in Seattle, Washington. They are part of Major League Soccer's Western Conference. The team started in 2007 and played their first game in 2009. It's called a phoenix club, named after an earlier team from the 1970s. Adrian Hanauer owns the club, and Paul Allen, Drew Carey, and 11 Seattle families also have shares. Brian Schmetzer became the head coach in 2016. They play at CenturyLink Field, which has about 37, 722 seats. A band called Sound Wave supports them. They play against Portland Timbers and Vancouver Whitecaps for the Cascadia Cup. Their first game was a win against the New York Red Bulls. The Sounders have won the U.S. Open Cup four times, the Supporters' Shield in 2014, and the MLS Cup in 2016 and 2019. They've made the playoffs every year and reached the semifinals of the CONCACAF Champions League five times. They have the highest average attendance in MLS for five years. The team has famous players like Clint Dempsey, Fredy Montero, Osvaldo Alonso, and Nicolás Lodeiro. They also have a player academy and lower league teams.

Darrell Clayton Hammond was born on October 8, 1955. He is an American actor, comedian, and impersonator. He was a regular cast member on "Saturday Night Live" from 1995 to 2009. Since 2014, he has been the announcer for the show. When he left, Hammond was the oldest cast member in the show's history at 53 years old. He made more appearances on "SNL" than any other cast member and impersonated more than 107 celebrities, with Bill Clinton being his most frequent impression. On September 19, 2014, Hammond was chosen as the new announcer for "Saturday Night Live," replacing Don Pardo, who had passed away the previous month.
