Peristeri is a suburb in the northwest part of Athens, Greece. In Greek, "peristeri" means "pigeon" or "dove." The municipality had 139,981 people living there in 2011. It is the seventh-largest municipality in Greece by population.
The national emblem of Algeria is a seal used by the government. It is like the coats of arms used by other countries.

Ana Lila Downs Sánchez, born on September 9, 1968, is a Mexican singer-songwriter and actress from Oaxaca. She performs her own songs and those by other artists in various genres, including traditional and popular Mexican music. She also includes indigenous influences and has sung in languages like Mixtec, Zapotec, Mayan, Nahuatl, and Purépecha. Born and raised in Oaxaca, Downs studied at the Institute of Arts in Oaxaca for a while and briefly attended the University of Minnesota, but then focused on music. She started performing in Oaxaca City and released her first album, "Ofrenda," in 1994. In 1999, her album "La Sandunga" gained her fame and was successful. Her 2001 album "Border" made her popular internationally. Downs’s seventh album, "Pecados y Milagros," in 2011, was very successful. Her 2015 album "Balas y Chocolate" followed, and "Salón Lágrimas y Deseo" came out in 2017. Downs began performing in school, showing her ability to sing traditional and modern Mexican music with her own style. She speaks Spanish, Mixtec, and English. Downs is an activist who helps protect Mixtec language and other indigenous languages in Mexico. She was influenced by artists like Chavela Vargas, Mercedes Sosa, Lucha Villa, and Amparo Ochoa. Downs is known for her unique and diverse music, which often features traditional Mexican styles. She has won one Grammy and three Latin Grammy awards. Besides music, she works on helping people and fighting for indigenous rights in Latin America.

Stephen Wochy, born Wojciechowski on December 25, 1922, is a Canadian retired ice hockey player. He played 54 games for the Detroit Red Wings in the National Hockey League. He was born in Fort William, Ontario. After Jim Conacher died in April 2020, Wochy became the oldest living former NHL player. Before joining the NHL, Wochy was part of the Port Arthur Bearcats in 1942 and played in the 1942 Allan Cup. Wochy played 10 seasons in the American Hockey League with the Indianapolis Capitals, Philadelphia Rockets, Cleveland Barons, and Buffalo Bisons. In 1952, he was named a first-team AHL all-star.

Diving Machine G5 is a roller coaster at Janfusun Fancyworld in Taiwan. It was built in 2000 by Swiss company Bolliger & Mabillard. It is the second dive coaster they made; the first was Oblivion at Alton Towers in the UK. The ride is in the Sky Plaza area of the park and looks like Oblivion but upside down. Diving Machine G5 got its name because it creates a lot of G-forces during the drop. Like Insane Speed, it doesn't have a theme. It’s one of three roller coasters at the park, along with Ku Ku Roller Coaster. Diving Machine G5 is near the entrance. It has long lines in the morning but shorter waits in the afternoon and evening.

Patmos is a town in Hempstead County, Arkansas, United States. It had 64 people in the 2010 census. The town has the same name as a Greek island where the Book of Revelation was written. Patmos is part of the Hope micropolitan statistical area.

James W. Hardy III was born on December 24, 1985. He played American football as a wide receiver. He was chosen by the Buffalo Bills in the second round of the 2008 NFL draft. He also played for the Baltimore Ravens. He played college football at Indiana University until about June 7, 2017.

Mackenzie Christine Foy, born on November 10, 2000, is an American actress and model. She played Renesmee Cullen in a 2012 movie, earning a nomination for best supporting young actress in a feature film. She also acted as young Murphy in the 2014 space movie Interstellar, where she received a Saturn Award for best performance by a younger actor. Additionally, she played Clara in Disney's The Nutcracker and the Four Realms.

The 1935–36 NHL season was the 19th year of the National Hockey League. The St. Louis Eagles left the league, leaving eight teams. The Detroit Red Wings won the Stanley Cup. They beat the Toronto Maple Leafs in four games.
Koenigsegg Automotive AB makes fast sports cars. They are based in Ängelholm, Skåne County, Sweden.

Jonsered is a small town in Partille municipality, Västra Götaland county, Sweden. It had 930 people living there in 2010. Jonsered is an old industrial town near the Säve River outside Gothenburg. In 1834, a man named William Gibson, from Scotland, started factories here. One of the first products was sail canvas. In 1856, the first Swedish state railway was built between Gothenburg and Jonsered, later continuing to Stockholm. The Gibson family owned and ran the company for many years, until the 1920s. Even after that, the company remained a big part of the town, as the main landowner until the 1970s. By the 1880s, the company began making machines for processing wood, and continues to make these products today. In the 1950s, they started making chainsaws, which became very popular worldwide. This helped the company when the textile industry closed down in the late 1960s. After Jonsereds fabriker closed in 1984, the community changed. Many people in Jonsered now live there to work in Gothenburg or Partille. You can reach Jonsered by train, which has a station that opened in 2000.

Alfredo Félix Alcón was an Argentine actor born in Buenos Aires on March 3, 1930. He died on April 11, 2014, at 84 years old. He acted in over 50 movies, starting with "El Amor Nunca Muere" in 1955. He was one of the best and most important Argentine actors of the 20th century. He won many awards, including the Silver Condor, the Martin Fierro Award, and the 1981 Diamond Konex Award.

Uzbekistan first joined the Olympic Games as an independent country in 1994. Since then, they have sent athletes to every Olympics. Before that, Uzbek athletes competed as part of the Soviet Union from 1952 to 1988. After the Soviet Union ended, Uzbekistan was part of the Unified Team in 1992. Uzbek athletes have won 26 medals in summer Olympics, mostly in wrestling and boxing. They have also won one medal in winter Olympics. Uzbekistan's Olympic committee was formed in 1992 and recognized by the IOC in 1993.

Richard Andrew Gephardt, born on January 31, 1941, is an American politician. He was a United States representative from Missouri from 1977 to 2005. A Democrat, Gephardt was the House Majority Leader from 1989 to 1995 and Minority Leader from 1995 to 2003. He tried but failed to become the Democratic presidential nominee in 1988 and 2004. Gephardt was considered for the vice presidential nomination in 1988, 1992, 2000, 2004, and 2008. After leaving politics, he became a lobbyist. He started a public affairs firm called Gephardt Government Affairs in Washington and a labor consultancy called The Gephardt Group in Atlanta. He also worked for DLA Piper, Fti Consulting, and Goldman Sachs. He is part of the Reformers Caucus of Issue One.

Brendan Halligan was born on July 5, 1936, and died on August 9, 2020. He was an Irish economist and politician. Halligan started and led the Institute of International and European Affairs (IIEA), a think tank that discusses European and international issues. He also led the Ireland China Institute, an independent think tank based in Dublin, which was officially opened in October 2019. Throughout his career, Halligan worked in Irish public sector bodies and in the private sector. He held several important positions, including being the general secretary of the Labour Party, a Teachta Dála (TD), a senator, and a Member of the European Parliament (MEP).

Robert Costanza, born on September 14, 1950, is an ecological economist from the United States and Australia. He teaches public policy at the Crawford School of Public Policy in Australia. Costanza is also a fellow of the Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia and a member of the Club of Rome.

Ofter schwang is a town in southern Germany, in Oberallgäu, Bavaria. It is known for hosting professional winter sports events, like World Cup alpine skiing. The town is also popular for skiing and other sports. Traditionally, the area is agricultural. Ofter schwang has a church with a World War II memorial and some small chapels. Tourism is now very important. People come to ski in winter and do activities like hiking, mountain biking, and paragliding in summer. Visitors also enjoy the "dorfsabend," a traditional village evening with Bavarian costumes, dancing, food, and beer.

José Sarney de Araújo Costa, born José Ribamar Ferreira de Araújo Costa, was born on April 24, 1930. He is a Brazilian politician, lawyer, and writer who was the 31st president of Brazil from April 21, 1985, to March 15, 1990. He is the oldest living former Brazilian president. Before that, he was part of the "bossa nova generation" of UDN politicians in the 1950s, trying to clean up the government and remove corruption. During the military dictatorship in Brazil, Sarney joined the government party Arena. When Arena split, he became part of the new Liberal Front Party. Sarney became vice president under Tancredo Neves, and when Neves died, Sarney became president. His term was popular at first, but he faced problems like the debt crisis and failed economic plans. He is seen as having caused many problems and created a system where family members had a lot of power. He owns important newspapers and TV stations in his home state of Maranhão. Sarney has also faced many accusations of being unfair and dishonest. He is known as an important writer and a member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters.

The Louisville/Jefferson County Metro Government (balance) is a statistical area in Kentucky. It represents the part of the consolidated city-county of Louisville-Jefferson County that doesn't include the 83 separate towns inside. It consists of the old city of Louisville and a large area outside the incorporated places. In 2010, the balance had 597,337 people, while the whole area had 741,096 people. It is part of the Louisville-Jefferson County, KY-IN Metropolitan Statistical Area.
Frank Fakaotimanava Lui was born on November 19, 1935. He was once the premier of Niue, a Pacific island country.

Selhurst Park is a football stadium in the London suburb of Selhurst, part of Croydon. It is where Crystal Palace football club plays. The club is in the Premier League. The stadium was built in 1924 by Archibald Leitch. It has hosted one international match and games for the 1948 Summer Olympics. Some of the stadium includes a Sainsbury's store. From 1985 to 1991, Charlton Athletic shared the stadium. Wimbledon shared it from 1991 to 2003.

The Cheongyang chili pepper, also known as Dang Jo Cheongyang, is a medium-sized chili from the Capsicum annuum species. It has a heat intensity of 10,000 Scoville units. It looks similar to regular Korean chili peppers but is much spicier. This chili is a speciality of Cheongyang County in South Korea. However, it was named after Cheongsong and Yeongyang counties. It was developed by Dr. Yoo Il-Woong by combining local Jejudo chili with Thai chili. The peppers are light purple or green when unripe and turn deep red when ripe. They stay dark red when dried.
grimbosq is a commune in Calvados, which is in Normandy, a region in northwestern France.

Saliva, often called spit, is a liquid made by glands in the mouth. In humans, it is mostly water with a little salt, mucus, cells, enzymes, and agents that fight germs. Saliva contains enzymes like amylase and lipase that start breaking down food, especially starches and fats. It also helps protect teeth by breaking down food stuck between them and fighting bacteria. Saliva keeps food moist, makes swallowing easier, and keeps the mouth from drying out. Some animals use their saliva for special purposes. Swifts use sticky saliva to build nests. Cobra and viper saliva has venom used to hunt. Some caterpillars make silk from saliva.
Schortens was an independent municipality and is now a town in the Friesland district of Lower Saxony, Germany.

The British Rail class 52 were 74 diesel-hydraulic locomotives made for the western region of British Rail between 1961 and 1964. Each locomotive had a two-word name, starting with "Western." Because of this, they were called Westerns.
Springdale is a city in Hamilton County, Ohio, United States. It is a suburb of Cincinnati. In 2010, the population was 11,223.

Larkana district is in the Sindh province of Pakistan. Its main city is Larkana. Two former Pakistani prime ministers, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Benazir Bhutto, are from this district. Mumtaz Ali Bhutto, a former chief minister of Sindh, is also from here. Actress Sohai Ali Abro and folk singer Abida Parveen are from Larkana. The Larkana Bulls cricket team was created in 2013. Other towns in the district are Ratodero, Dokri, Bakrani, and Naodero. In 2005, the government split Larkana district into two new districts called Qamber and Shahdadkot.

The Cat in the Hat is a children's book written and illustrated by Theodor Geisel, known as Dr. Seuss. It was first published in 1957. The story is about a tall cat wearing a red and white-striped hat and a red bow tie. One rainy day, the cat visits the house of Sally and her brother when their mother is out. Despite their fish's objections, the cat tries to entertain them by doing tricks. The cat and his friends, Thing One and Thing Two, end up wrecking the house. The children and the fish become worried until the cat cleans everything up using a machine and leaves before the children's mother returns. Geisel wrote the book to help children learn to read better. A man named William Spaulding, who met Geisel during World War II, asked him to write a more fun primer. Since Geisel was already working for Random House, Houghton Mifflin published the book for schools, while Random House sold it to the public. Geisel said he was frustrated with the word list and started writing a story with the first two rhyming words, "cat" and "hat." The book was very popular and successful, selling over a million copies in three years. In 2001, it was ranked ninth on the list of best-selling children's books. The book led to the creation of Beginner Books, which makes similar books for young readers. In 1983, the story was made into an animated TV special and a live-action film in 2003.

The Eurocopter (now Airbus helicopters) EC120 Colibri was a five-seat, single-engine light utility helicopter. It was jointly designed and developed by Eurocopter, China National Aero-Technology Import & Export Corporation (CATIC), Harbin Aviation Industries (Group) Ltd (HAIG), and Singapore Technologies Aerospace Ltd (ST Aero) in France. The EC120B was assembled in France and Australia. In China, the helicopter is produced by Harbin Aircraft Manufacturing Corporation (HAMC) as the HC120. In 2004, HAMC started making HC120 helicopters in Harbin, in northern China. In China, the People's Liberation Army and several police forces bought HC120 helicopters.

nigel john taylor ( born 20 june 1960 ) is an english musician , singer , songwriter , producer , and actor , who is best known as the bass guitarist for new romantic band duran duran , of which he was a founding member . duran duran was one of the most popular bands in the world during the 1980s due in part to their revolutionary music videos which played in heavy rotation in the early days of mtv . taylor played with duran duran from its founding in 1978 until 1997 , when he left to pursue a solo recording and film career . he recorded a dozen solo releases ( albums , eps , and video projects ) through his private record label b5 records over the next four years , had a lead role in the movie `` sugar town '' , and made appearances in a half dozen other film projects . he rejoined duran duran for a reunion of the original five members of the group in 2001 and has remained with the group since . the current permanent members of duran duran are simon le bon ( singer ) , john taylor ( bass guitar ) , nick rhodes ( synthesizer ) and roger taylor ( drums ) .taylor was also a member of two supergroups : the power station and neurotic outsiders .

Last of the Summer Wine is a British sitcom created by Roy Clarke and first broadcast by the BBC from 1973 to 2010. It started as part of a comedy show in 1973 and the first series aired in 1973. Alan J. W. Bell produced and directed the show from 1983 to 2010. The BBC stopped making new episodes in 2010, and the final episode aired on August 29, 2010. All 295 episodes have been released on DVD. The show is shown on TV in the UK on Gold, Yesterday, and Drama channels. It is also broadcast in over 25 countries, including some PBS stations in the U.S. and VisionTV in Canada. "Last of the Summer Wine" is the longest-running comedy on British TV and the longest-running sitcom worldwide. The show is set in and around Holmfirth, West Yorkshire, England. It follows the adventures of three older men and their friends. Initially, the main trio included Bill Owen as Compo Simmons, Peter Sallis as Norman Clegg, and Michael Bates as Cyril Blamire. After Bates left, the roles were played by Brian Wilde as Foggy Dewhurst, Michael Aldridge as Seymour Utterthwaite, and Frank Thornton as Herbert Truelove. These men never seemed to age and viewed their townspeople with unique perspectives through their stunts. Over time, the show included many supporting characters, making it an ensemble piece. Characters like Tom Owen, Billy Hardcastle, and Alvin Smedley also appeared. For the final episodes, a new trio of younger actors was introduced, including Russ Abbott, Luther Hobdyke, and Brian Murphy. Despite some feeling the quality had declined, the show was popular and won awards. Many royal family members enjoyed it. There were 21 Christmas specials, three TV films, and a documentary about the series. The show inspired other adaptations, including a prequel and stage productions.

The museum about Japanese currency is located in front of the Bank of Japan building in Chuo, Tokyo. It opened in November 1985. In 2010, they showed wallets from the Edo period (1603-1867) and Meiji era (1868-1912).

Charles Henry Pitman Sr. was born on October 20, 1935, and died on February 13, 2020. He was a lieutenant general in the United States Marine Corps. He worked as deputy chief of staff for aviation. He retired in 1990. He passed away in 2020 because of cancer. He was also part of the 1980 Operation Eagle Claw.

The Mercator projection is a map made by Gerardus Mercator in 1569. It is a cylindrical projection used for navigation. This map shows north as up and south as down everywhere, and it keeps local directions and shapes true. As a result, it is conformal. However, the Mercator projection also enlarges the size of objects as you move away from the equator. This enlargement is small near the equator but grows faster towards the poles. Therefore, places like Greenland and Antarctica appear much larger than they really are compared to areas near the equator, such as Central Africa.

Shakargarh is the capital of Shakargarh tehsil and is a city in the northeast part of Narowal district in Punjab, Pakistan. It is near Jammu to the north and Sialkot to the west. The city has a very high literacy rate, over 85%. Shakargarh is at 32°16' north latitude and 75°10' east longitude, on the western side of the Ravi River. Shakargarh tehsil is divided into 35 union councils, with three of them being the capital city.

Madeleine Vionnet was a French fashion designer born on June 22, 1876, in Loiret, France, and died on March 2, 1975. She trained in London before returning to Paris in 1912 to open her first fashion house. Her house had to close in 1914 because of World War I but reopened after the war. Vionnet became one of the top designers in Paris during the 1920s and 1930s. She had to close her fashion house in 1939 and retired in 1940. Known as the "queen of the bias cut" and the "architect among dressmakers," Vionnet is famous for her elegant Greek-style dresses and for making the bias cut popular in fashion. She also inspired many modern designers.
Kuthwal is one of 51 union councils in Abbottabad district in Pakistan's Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa province. It is situated northwest of Abbottabad city, which is the district capital.

Whidbey Island, also spelled as Whidby, Whitbey, or Whitby, is the biggest island in Island County, Washington, in the United States. Another large island nearby is Camano Island, located to the east. Whidbey Island is about north of Seattle and sits between the Olympic Peninsula and the I-5 corridor in western Washington. It forms the northern edge of Puget Sound. Naval Air Station Whidbey Island is on the island. As of the 2000 census, Whidbey Island had 67,000 people living there, with about 29,000 in rural areas. The island is roughly long if measured along roads from north to south and about wide, covering a total area of. This makes it the 40th largest island in the United States. It is the fourth longest and fourth largest island in the contiguous United States, after Long Island, New York; Padre Island, Texas (the world's longest barrier island); and Isle Royale, Michigan. In Washington state, Whidbey Island is the largest, followed by Orcas Island.

Blount County is a county in Alabama. As of 2010, it had 57, 322 people. The county seat is Oneonta. Blount County is a moist county, meaning it allows alcohol sales. In 2012, voters narrowly rejected allowing alcohol sales county-wide. However, Blountsville, Cleveland, and Oneonta have sold alcohol since 2013. Blount County is known as the "Covered Bridge Capital of Alabama." It has more historic covered bridges than any other county in the state. Every autumn, Oneonta hosts a covered bridge festival to celebrate its three remaining covered bridges.

Hermann Baumann was born on January 23, 1921. He is a retired Swiss wrestler who competed in freestyle wrestling. In the 1948 Summer Olympics in London, he won a bronze medal in the lightweight class.

John Norman Haynes was born on October 17, 1934, and died on October 18, 2005. He was an English football player. He played for his national team 56 times, and 22 of those times he was the team captain. He was chosen for three World Cup teams, playing in the latter two. Haynes was called "the maestro" because of his excellent attacking skills, ability to pass with both feet, and clever play. He played for Fulham for 20 years but never won a major trophy. He made it to the FA Cup semi-finals twice. He was the first player to earn £100 a week after the £20 wage limit was removed in 1961. Haynes also played for Toronto City on loan in 1961 and finished his career at Durban City, where he won the only trophy of his career.

Yoshihide Kozai, born on April 1, 1928, and passed away on February 5, 2018, was a Japanese astronomer who studied celestial mechanics. He discovered the Kozai mechanism, which he shared with Michael Lidov. For this, he got the Imperial Prize from the Japan Academy in 1979. Kozai was the president of the International Astronomical Union from 1988 to 1991. In 1989, he received the Brouwer Award from the American Astronomical Society. In 2009, the Japanese government honored him with the Decoration of Cultural Merit. Kozai died from liver failure. An asteroid named 3040 Kozai honors his memory.
Planomicrobium flavidum is a type of bacteria from the Planomicrobium group. It was found in a saltwater pond.

Joshua Reynolds, born on July 16, 1723, and died on February 23, 1792, was an English painter who mostly painted portraits. John Russell said he was one of the best painters in Europe during the 18th century. He believed in using idealization to improve imperfect paintings. Reynolds started the Royal Academy of Arts and became its first president. King George III knighted him in 1769.

Chicka Chicka Boom Boom is a popular children's book. Bill Martin, Jr. and John Archambault wrote it. Lois Ehlert illustrated it. The book came out in 1989 and features letters that can act like people. It was on The New York Times bestseller list for children's books in 2000.

This list includes current cities, towns, and communities in New York, the state in the U.S. It also gives the county names and numbers where each place is located. If there are zip codes, it shows the lowest and highest ones.

Andrus Ansip, born on October 1, 1956, is an Estonian politician. He became a member of the European Parliament in 2014. Before that, Ansip was the European Commissioner for Digital Single Market and vice president of the European Commission from 2014. He was also the prime minister of Estonia from 2005 to 2014 and the chairman of the Liberal Estonian Reform Party from 2004 to 2014. Before entering politics, Ansip trained as a chemist and worked in banking and business. He joined the parliament in 2004, became the minister of economic affairs, and then became prime minister in April 2005. He was appointed to the European Commission on November 1, 2014.

Lynching is when a group of people kills someone without a fair trial. It usually happens when a mob wants to punish someone they think has done something wrong. Sometimes, it is to scare people. Lynching can also be a way for a group to control others. Often, it includes a public event, like hanging, to make others afraid. This kind of violence can happen anywhere. In the United States, lynchings of African Americans became common in the South after the Reconstruction era, especially during times when race relations were very bad. This kind of violence still happens in some countries today, like Brazil, Guatemala, and South Africa.

The King and I is the fifth musical by Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein. It is based on Margaret Landon's novel, "Anna and the King of Siam," which is from Anna Leonowens' memoirs. Anna, a British teacher, came to Siam to teach the king's children and help modernize the country. She had a difficult but loving relationship with the king. The musical first showed on Broadway on March 29, 1951, and ran for almost three years. It won several Tony Awards. Gertrude Lawrence played Anna and Yul Brynner played the king. Brynner later starred in the 1956 film version. The musical has been performed many times, including in London and on tours. Christopher Renshaw directed successful Broadway and West End revivals. The King and I is still popular for professional and amateur performances worldwide.

Illapel is a city in Chile. It is the capital of the Choapa province in the Coquimbo region. The city is next to the Illapel River and is the narrowest part of the country along that line. It is east of Los Vilos.

Michael Jagmin is an American singer. He was the main singer of a band called A Skylit Drive, which plays post-hardcore music. He used to sing for a metal band named Odd Project. Jagmin is famous for his high-pitched voice. He can sing very high and has a range that covers about three octaves.

Gillingham Football Club is a professional soccer team in Gillingham, a town in Kent, England. They play their home games at Priestfield Stadium. Gillingham is the only Kent-based club in the Football League. They play in League One, which is the third level of the English league system. The club was founded in 1893 and joined the Football League in 1920. In 1938, they left the league but came back in 1950 when the league had more teams. In the 1980s, they nearly moved up to the second tier but then their performance dropped. In 1993, they narrowly avoided going to the Football Conference. From 2000 to 2005, Gillingham was in the second tier for the first time in their history, finishing 11th in 2002-03.

Universal Studios Japan is in Osaka and is one of six Universal Studios theme parks. It is owned by NBCUniversal, which is also owned by Universal Studios. The park opened on March 31, 2001. Over 11 million people visited in its first year, making it the fastest amusement park to reach 10 million visitors. Each year, around 8 million people visit. Most visitors are from Japan and nearby Asian countries like South Korea and China. Many Western tourists and expats also visit. In 2005, Goldman Sachs became the park's largest shareholder. The park celebrated its 10th anniversary in 2011 with 88 million total visitors. In June 2012, there were 700,000 annual passport holders. In 2012, 9.75 million people visited, and in 2013, 10.5 million visited. This growth was due to new rides and areas, like the Hollywood Dream roller coaster and the new Spider-Man ride. The family area, Universal Wonderland, also opened in 2012. In 2014, the Wizarding World of Harry Potter opened, attracting many visitors. In 2012, Universal Studios Japan welcomed its 100 millionth visitor. In 2014, it ranked fifth among the top 25 amusement/theme parks worldwide, with 11.8 million visitors. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the park closed from March to June 2020.

Antony Passage is a small village in southeast Cornwall, England, UK. It is near the tidal part of the River Lynher. This river is a smaller stream that flows into the River Tamar. Antony Passage is on the other side of the River Lynher from Antony Village.

Daniel Hudson Burnham, born on September 4, 1846, and died on June 1, 1912, was an American architect and urban planner. He was a key figure in the Beaux-Arts movement. Burnham might have been the most successful person who could get things done in American architecture. He was a well-known architect in Chicago and managed the 1892-93 World's Columbian Exposition, known as "The White City." Burnham played important roles in creating plans for several cities, including Chicago, Manila, Baguio, and Washington, D.C. He also designed famous buildings, such as skyscrapers in Chicago, the triangular Flatiron Building in New York City, Union Station in Washington, D.C., Selfridges department store in London, and the Merchants Exchange in San Francisco. While he is famous for his skyscrapers, city planning, and "The White City," he also designed many shopping buildings, nearly one-third of his total work.

Lexington is the second-largest city in Kentucky and the 60th-largest in the United States. Known as the "horse capital of the world," it's at the heart of Kentucky's bluegrass region. Notable places in the city include the Kentucky Horse Park, Red Mile and Keeneland race courses, Rupp Arena, Transylvania University, the University of Kentucky, and Bluegrass Community and Technical College. Lexington has a high rate of college education, with 39.5% of residents having at least a bachelor's degree. In the 2019 U.S. census estimate, the city had 323,152 people, with a metropolitan area of 517,056 and a combined statistical area of 745,033. By land area, Lexington is the 28th largest city in the United States. The city is fully within Fayette County, and vice versa. It uses a mayor-council government with 12 districts, and three members elected at large, with the top vote-getter becoming the vice mayor.

Ramón Gómez Castillo, often called Ramón Valdés, was a Mexican actor born on September 2, 1923, and passed away on August 9, 1988. He was best known for playing Don Ramón. He was also recognized as one of Mexico's top comedians. Born in Mexico City, Ramón came from a large family and moved to Ciudad Juárez when he was two. He began acting in movies at age 16 in "Tender Pumpkins," alongside his brother Germán, who was famous as "Tin-tan." This helped Ramón start his acting career. During the golden age of Mexican cinema, Ramón appeared in several films with supporting roles. Ramón and Germán had two other brothers who were also actors: Manuel, known as "Manuel El Loco Valdés," and Antonio, known as "El Ratón Valdés." In 1968, Ramón met Roberto Gómez Bolaños, known as "Chespirito." They worked together on shows like "Los Supergenios de la Mesa Cuadrada" and "El Chapulín Colorado." Ramón gained worldwide fame for his role as Don Ramón on "El Chavo del Ocho." He left the show in 1979 but returned in 1981 for his final year. In 1982, Ramón starred in "Federrico" in Venezuela with Carlos Villagrán. He also appeared in "Ah Que Kiko" in 1987, but neither show was as successful as expected.
Vezot is a commune in Sarthe department, which is in the Pays de la Loire region of northwest France.

The secretary of defense (SecDef) leads the United States Department of Defense, an executive department managing the armed forces. This position is next in command after the president. It's like a defense minister in other countries. The president chooses the SecDef with Senate approval, and the SecDef is part of the cabinet and the National Security Council. The SecDef has the authority, direction, and control over the Department of Defense, following the president's direction. They are also the main assistant to the president for matters related to the Department of Defense. The SecDef cannot be appointed within seven years of being a regular armed force officer. They are the only one who can authorize the transfer of military forces between the army, navy, air force, space force, and the U.S. coast guard (when its command is transferred). Only the SecDef, president, or Congress can make such transfers. The SecDef has more power than any regular military officer and is second only to the president. Sometimes, they are unofficially called a "de facto" deputy commander-in-chief. The chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff advises the SecDef and president on military matters but is not in the command chain. The SecDef, along with the secretaries of state, attorney general, and treasury, are considered the top department heads. Mark Esper became the 27th SecDef on July 23, 2019.

The Richmond football club, known as the Tigers, is a professional Australian rules football team that plays in the Australian Football League (AFL). The club started in 1885 in Richmond, a suburb of Melbourne. Between 1885 and 1907, Richmond played in the Victorian Football Association (VFA) and won two championships. In 1908, Richmond joined the Victorian Football League, which is now called the AFL, and has since won twelve championships, the last one in 2019. The club's main home is the Punt Road Oval, where it has been based since 1965, next to the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Richmond wears black shirts with yellow stripes. Their team song, "We're from Tigerland," has a famous "yellow and black" line. The coach is Damien Hardwick, and the team captain is Trent Cotchin. Five Richmond players are in the Australian Football Hall of Fame as "Legends": Kevin Bartlett, Jack Dyer, Royce Hart, Kevin Sheedy, and Ian Stewart.

"Right Behind You (Mafia)" is a song by the Canadian alternative rock group Our Lady Peace. It came out in July 2001 as their third and last single from their fourth album, "Spiritual Machines." The single didn't do well, so they stopped its release and music video. This was also their last single with founding guitarist Mike Turner. During the making of the song, Matt Cameron from Pearl Jam played drums because Our Lady Peace's drummer Jeremy Taggart was injured.

Rascal Flatts is an American country music group formed in Columbus, Ohio, in 1999. The members are Gary Levox (lead vocals), Jay DeMarcus (bass guitar, background vocals), and Joe Don Rooney (lead guitar, background vocals). Jay DeMarcus is Gary Levox's second cousin and a brother-in-law of country music singer James Otto. He used to be in a Christian music duo called East to West. From 2000 to 2010, they were with Disney Music Group's Lyric Street Records. They made six albums during that time, and all were certified platinum or higher by the Recording Industry Association of America. Their albums are "Rascal Flatts" (2000), "Melt" (2002), "Feels Like Today" (2004), "Me and My Gang" (2006), "Still Feels Good" (2007), and "Unstoppable" (2009). After Lyric Street closed in 2010, they moved to Big Machine Records. There, they released five studio albums and one Christmas album: "Nothing Like This" (2010), "Changed" (2012), "Rewind" (2014), "The Greatest Gift of All" (2016), and "Back to Us" (2017). They had forty hits on the charts, sixteen of which reached number one. Their longest-lasting number one hit was "Bless the Broken Road," which stayed at number one for five weeks in 2005. "What Hurts the Most" was also a big hit, reaching number one on the Hot Country Songs and Adult Contemporary charts, and peaked at number six on the Billboard Hot 100. On January 7, 2020, the band said they would disband after a farewell tour, which lasted 21 years. However, the farewell tour was postponed indefinitely due to the coronavirus in May 19, 2020.
Bizen's original center was in modern Okayama. Bizen was an early important place for making swords in Japan.
Phillipsburg is a city in Kansas, United States. It is also the county seat of Phillips County. According to the 2010 census, the city has 2,581 people living there.

The Coral Sea is a part of the South Pacific Ocean, located off the northeast coast of Australia. It is considered an interim Australian bioregion. The Coral Sea stretches along Australia's northeast coast. During World War II, the Coral Sea was the site of a major naval battle between Japan and the United States and Australia. The sea has many islands and reefs, including the Great Barrier Reef (GBR), the world's largest reef system. In 1981, UNESCO declared the Great Barrier Reef a World Heritage Site. Oil exploration projects were stopped there in 1975, and fishing is limited in some areas. The Coral Sea is rich in bird and marine life and is a popular tourist destination both nationally and internationally.

A drumstick is a type of percussion mallet used for playing the snare drum, drum kit, and some other percussion instruments. Drumsticks are especially used for unpitched percussion. Other specialized beaters, like the metal beater for a triangle or the mallets for a xylophone and timpani, are not called drumsticks. Drumsticks typically have these features:

Michael Lawrence Marrow, known as Phase 2 and Lonny Wood, was an American artist who used aerosol paint. He lived from August 2, 1955, to December 12, 2019, and worked in New York City. Phase 2 is famous for creating the "bubble letter" style of aerosol writing, also called "softies." He was also important in the early days of hip hop.

Yandobinskoye is a rural settlement in Alikovsky District, Chuvash Republic, Russia. It is in the center of the district. The administrative center is Yandoba, another rural locality. In 2006, Yandobinskoye had about 1,081 people. Yandobinskoye has twelve rural localities. There is a road that goes through its area.

A rectifier changes alternating current (AC), which switches direction, into direct current (DC), which flows in one direction. This process is called "rectification." Rectifiers come in various forms, such as vacuum tube diodes, wet chemical cells, mercury-arc valves, copper and selenium oxide plates, semiconductor diodes, silicon-controlled rectifiers, and other semiconductor switches. Historically, even mechanical switches and motors have been used. Early radio receivers, called crystal radios, used a small piece of wire (cat's whisker) on a crystal of lead sulfide to act as a rectifier or "crystal detector." Rectifiers are used in many places, especially in direct current power supplies and high-voltage direct current systems. They can also serve other roles, like detecting radio signals or flames in gas heating systems. The output voltage may need smoothing to become steady. For devices like radios and computers, which need a steady DC voltage, the rectifier's output is smoothed with filters. More complex circuits convert DC back to AC, which is called an inverter.

Virginia City is a town in Montana, United States. It is also the main town in Madison County. In 1961, Virginia City and the area around it became a National Historic Landmark. The landmark is called the Virginia City Historic District. As of 2010, the town had 190 people living there.

Emily Bishop is a fictional character from the British TV show "Coronation Street." She has been played by Eileen Derbyshire since January 1961 and is the longest-standing female character in the show. Emily first appeared on December 21, 1960, in a short scene without credits. Derbyshire took a break from the show in November 2015 and returned briefly on October 9, 2019, for Ken Barlow's 80th birthday celebration.

A nuclear submarine uses a nuclear reactor for power. It has many advantages over conventional submarines. Unlike conventional submarines, which need to surface often to get air, nuclear submarines can stay underwater for a long time. They can travel at high speeds for long periods because they generate a lot of power. This means they can go almost anywhere without needing to stop for fuel for 25 years. Conventional submarines can only stay underwater for a few days and a few hours at top speed because they use batteries. However, newer air-independent propulsion systems have improved this. The cost of nuclear technology is very high, so not many countries have nuclear submarines. Some of the worst nuclear and radiation accidents happened in Soviet nuclear submarines.

Septimia Zenobia, also known as Bat-zabbai in Palmyrene (240–274 AD), was a queen in the third century. She was probably from a noble family and married Odaenathus, the ruler of Palmyra. Odaenathus became king in 260, making Palmyra very powerful in the area by defeating the Sassanians and stabilizing the Roman east. After Odaenathus died, Zenobia ruled her son Vaballathus and had control over the region. In 270, Zenobia started a war that brought much of the Roman east under her control, including Egypt. By 271, her empire stretched from Ancyra in central Anatolia to southern Egypt, though she remained formally loyal to Rome. However, when Emperor Aurelian attacked in 272, Zenobia declared her son an emperor and called herself empress, breaking away from Rome. The Romans defeated her forces; Zenobia was captured and sent to Rome, where she spent the rest of her life. Zenobia was a learned ruler who supported scholars and philosophers. She treated her subjects kindly and protected religious minorities. She kept a stable government in her diverse empire. Zenobia died after 274, and many stories exist about her. Her life and fall have inspired many historians, artists, and writers, and she is seen as a national hero in Syria.
This is a list of rivers in Saint Lucia. The rivers are listed going around the island, starting from the northern part.

Jabalpur, formerly known as Jubbulpore, is a city in Madhya Pradesh, India. It is the third-largest urban area in Madhya Pradesh and the 38th-largest in the country. Known for the Dhuandhar Falls and white marble rocks at Bhedaghat, Jabalpur is also famous for being where snooker is said to have started. Jabalpur is a major administrative, industrial, and business center in Madhya Pradesh. It is an important educational hub. The city has a large high court and many state government department headquarters. It also has major military and industrial bases, providing employment. Jabalpur is a key trading center and forest product producer, growing rapidly. The city is the main administrative center of Jabalpur district, which is the second-most-populous in Madhya Pradesh. Historically, Jabalpur was part of the Kalachuri and Rajgond dynasties. It became part of British India in the early 1800s and was renamed Jubbulpore. Since India’s independence, there have been calls for a separate state of Mahakoshal, with Jabalpur as its capital. Jabalpur is the headquarters for the West Central Railway, Madhya Pradesh Electricity Board, and the Tropical Forest Research Institute. It also hosts army headquarters for five states and training centers for military regiments.

In chemistry, an ester is a compound made from an acid, where one hydroxyl group is replaced by an alkoxy group. Usually, esters come from a reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol. Glycerides, which are fatty acid esters of glycerol, are important in biology as they form the main classes of lipids, found in animal fats and vegetable oils. Some esters, with low molecular weight, are used as fragrances and found in essential oils and pheromones. Phosphoesters are part of DNA molecules. Nitrate esters, like nitroglycerin, are explosive. Polyesters are important plastics. Esters generally have a sweet smell and are good solvents for plastics, plasticizers, resins, and lacquers. They are also a large class of synthetic lubricants.

The division of northern Melbourne was an Australian electoral district in Victoria. It covered parts of inner northern suburbs like Carlton, North Melbourne, and Fitzroy. In 1906, it was changed to Batman. The area had one member, H. B. Higgins. He was attorney general from 1904 to 1905. Higgins stopped running in Batman in 1906 because he became a justice of the High Court of Australia that year.

cultured meat is made by growing animal cells in a lab, not from killing animals. It is a type of cellular agriculture. The idea was first popularized by Jason Matheny in the early 2000s after writing about it and founding New Harvest, the world's first organization focused on in vitro meat research. In 2013, Mark Post from Maastricht University created the first lab-grown burger patty. Since then, a few companies have made news about their lab-grown meat prototypes, but it is not yet available in stores. Companies like Memphis Meats and SuperMeat hope to sell lab-grown meat in 2020. People aren't sure if they will like it. The process can be improved, and lab-grown meat could have many benefits or drawbacks in terms of ethics, health, environment, culture, and economy compared to traditional meat.

John Guillermin, born on November 11, 1925, and passed away on September 27, 2015, was a British film director, writer, and producer. He worked mostly on big, exciting movies. Some of his famous films include "I Was Monty's Double" (1958), "Tarzan's Greatest Adventure" (1959), "Never Let Go" (1960), and "King Kong" (1976). In the 1980s, he made less famous movies. His last works were smaller budget films shown in theaters and on TV. People said that Guillermin was very strict and often yelled at actors and crew. He could be a bit scary. But he was very good at filming both small and big scenes. Even though he could be difficult, his ability to make great movies usually made up for it.

Wake up! Pope Francis released a music album on November 27, 2015, through Believe Digital. The album has speeches from Pope Francis recorded in different places worldwide between 2013 and 2015. There are also music tracks of prayers and hymns by Italian artists and producers.

Blanco County is in Texas. It is part of the Edwards Plateau. In 2010, there were 10, 497 people living there. The county seat is Johnson City. Blanco County got its name from the Blanco River, which goes through the county. Texas created Blanco County in 1858 from parts of Burnet, Comal, Gillespie, and Hays counties. Blanco was the county seat from 1858 to 1890. Then, it moved to Johnson City.
Peoria County is in Illinois, a state in the U.S. The 2010 census said it had 186, 494 people. Peoria is the county seat. Peoria County is in the Peoria, IL metropolitan area.

Belkin International, Inc., is an American company that makes consumer electronics, especially devices for connecting things. It is based in Playa Vista, Los Angeles, California. The company sells many types of products for home and work, including routers, iPod and iPhone accessories, computer accessories, surge protectors, network switches, hubs, cables, KVM switches, racks, enclosures, and other peripherals. Belkin International owns brands like Belkin, Linksys, and Wemo, as well as a smart home company called Phyn.

Irrigation is the process of giving plants water at the right times. It helps grow crops, keep gardens healthy, and grow plants in dry areas or when it doesn't rain much. Irrigation can also protect crops from frost, control weeds, and stop the soil from becoming too compact. Without enough rain, farming that depends only on it is called rain-fed farming. Irrigation systems are used for more than just farming. They can cool animals, reduce dust, deal with waste, and help in mining. Irrigation and drainage, which removes extra water, are often studied together. People have used irrigation for over 5,000 years in different cultures around the world. It has been important for many economies and societies, from Asia to the southwestern United States.

X-Men: The Last Stand is a 2006 superhero movie about the X-Men team from Marvel Comics. It follows the 2003 film X2 and is the third movie in the X-Men series. Brett Ratner directed it, and Simon Kinberg and Zak Penn wrote it. The main actors are Hugh Jackman, Halle Berry, Ian McKellen, and others. The story is based on two comic book stories. It talks about a cure for mutants that causes problems for mutants and humans, and about Jean Grey coming back to life. Bryan Singer, who directed the first two films, stopped working on this one to make Superman Returns. John Ottman and Dan Harris and Michael Dougherty, who worked on X2, also left. James Marsden, a character actor, had a small part. Matthew Vaughn was supposed to direct but left, and Brett Ratner took over. Filming lasted from August 2005 to January 2006, costing about $210 million, which was a lot for its time. The movie came out on May 26, 2006. It made about $459 million worldwide, being the seventh biggest film of 2006. It was the highest-grossing X-Men movie at the time. People liked the acting, music, and action scenes, but didn't like some parts of the script and story.

Rudi van Dantzig was born on August 4, 1933, and passed away on January 19, 2012. He was a Dutch choreographer, company director, and writer. He played a very important role in making Dutch ballet famous all over the world in the second half of the 20th century.

Parma is a city in northern Italy, in the region of Emilia-Romagna. It is known for its architecture, music, art, prosciutto (ham), cheese, and beautiful countryside. Parma has a famous university, one of the oldest in the world. The city is split by a stream. The area on the other side of the stream is called "oltretorrente." Parma's ancient Etruscan name was used to describe a round shield. The Italian poet Attilio Bertolucci, born in a small village, said, "As a capital city, it had to have a river. As a small capital city, it received a stream, which is often dry."

A bottle cap seals the top of a bottle. It is usually decorated with colorful logos from the brand. Plastic caps are used on plastic bottles. Metal caps with plastic backing are used on glass bottles. The metal is often made of steel. Some plastic caps have a pour spout. Flip-top caps help control the release of dry products. Bottle caps are sometimes made from a different type of plastic than the bottle.

Dwight Griffith, born on January 22, 1875, and died on July 23, 1948, was an American film director. He is known as one of the most important filmmakers of his time. He helped make long movies possible. His movie "The Birth of a Nation" (1915) made investors money but also caused a lot of problems because it showed African Americans in a bad way and praised the Ku Klux Klan. His film "Intolerance" (1916) was made to answer critics but did not apologize for the negative views of African Americans. Some of Griffith's later films, like "Broken Blossoms" (1919), "Way Down East" (1920), and "Orphans of the Storm" (1921), were successful. However, the high costs for making and promoting these films often meant they did not make money. He made about 500 films in total. Griffith, along with Charlie Chaplin, Mary Pickford, and Douglas Fairbanks, started United Artists. This allowed them to control their own films instead of working with big movie companies. He was also part of founding the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

A mathematical proof is an argument that shows a statement is true based on logical reasoning. It uses previously proven statements, like theorems, but can be built from basic assumptions called axioms and rules of logic. Proofs provide certain certainty, unlike other types of reasoning that only offer a strong expectation. To be a proof, it must work in all possible cases, not just many examples. An unproven but believed statement is called a conjecture or a hypothesis. Proofs mix symbols and words, with informal logic being common. Formal proofs use only symbols. The difference between these types of proofs has sparked interest in how math is done and studied. This includes examining historical practices and the role of language and logic in mathematics.

This list includes world heritage sites in France, which have cultural or natural importance and are on UNESCO's world heritage list or France's tentative list. France joined the UNESCO world heritage convention in 1975. Since then, 44 sites in France have been added to the world heritage list. Of these, 39 are cultural, 4 are natural, and 1 is both cultural and natural. Three sites are shared between countries. The first site was added in 1979, and the most recent in 2019. Five sites were nominated in 1979. France's tentative list has 37 properties. The names are as shown on the UNESCO website. Sites can be cultural, natural, or mixed. Criteria I to V are for cultural sites, and VI to X are for natural sites. The dates for sites on the world heritage list are when they were added, and for the tentative list, they are when they were proposed. Each number links directly to the UNESCO site with more details.

Kimble County is in Texas. It is on the Edwards Plateau. In 2010, there were 4,607 people living there. The county seat is Junction. Kimble County was created in 1858 and set up in 1876. It is named after George C. Kimble, who died in the Battle of the Alamo.
Gagny is a town in the eastern part of Paris, France. It is situated near the center of Paris.

The Salt Fork of the Arkansas River is a smaller river that joins the Arkansas River. This river is in southern Kansas and northern Oklahoma in the United States. Through the Arkansas River, it is part of the Mississippi River's water system.

Elizabeth Bonnin, born on September 16, 1975, is an Irish presenter of science, wildlife, and nature programs. She has worked on TV in Ireland and the UK. She is also a biochemist and a wild animal biologist. In the early 2000s, she hosted morning and music shows. She is well-known for hosting wildlife and science programs like "Galapagos," "How the Earth Works," "Animals in Love," "Stargazing Live," "Blue Planet Live," "Cats v Dogs: Which is Best?" and "Should We Close Our Zoos?" From 2009 to 2014, she co-hosted the BBC show "Bang Goes the Theory." Since 2013, she has co-hosted "Countrywise" for ITV. In 2019, she hosted "Meat: A Threat to Our Planet?"

Don Améche (born Dominic Felix Amici, May 31, 1908 – December 6, 1993) was an American actor and comedian. He started performing in college shows and then in stock and vaudeville. In the early 1930s, he became a popular radio star. In 1935, 20th Century Fox offered him a movie contract. For 14 years, he appeared in 40 films, mostly comedies, dramas, and musicals, as a handsome, charming leading man. In the 1950s, he worked in Broadway shows and on television. From 1961 to 1965, he hosted NBC's "International Showtime." Later, he returned to films and had a successful career revival, starring in "Trading Places" (1983) and winning an Academy Award for best supporting actor in "Cocoon" (1985).

Didier Yves Drogba Tébily, born on March 11, 1978, is a retired professional footballer who played as a striker. He is the all-time top scorer and former captain of the Ivory Coast national team. He is best known for his career at Chelsea, where he scored more goals than any other foreign player and is currently the club's fourth highest goal scorer of all time. Drogba was named in Chelsea's team of the 2010-2020 decade by the club's fans. He won the African Footballer of the Year award twice, in 2006 and 2009. Drogba started his professional career at Le Mans in France at the age of 18. He moved to Guingamp, where he scored 17 goals in 34 appearances in the 2002-03 season. He then joined Olympique de Marseille, where he finished as the third highest scorer in the 2003-04 season with 19 goals. He helped the club reach the 2004 UEFA Cup final. In July 2004, Drogba moved to Chelsea for £24 million, becoming the most expensive Ivorian player in history. In his debut season, he helped Chelsea win their first league title in 50 years. A year later, he won another Premier League title. His performance in 2007 saw him named in the FIFA World XI. In March 2012, he became the first African player to score 100 Premier League goals. Two months later, he scored in Chelsea’s 2012 FA Cup final win over Liverpool, becoming the first (and, the only) player to score in four separate FA Cup finals. He also played in the 2012 UEFA Champions League final, where he scored an 88th-minute equalizer and the winning penalty in the deciding shootout against Bayern Munich. After spending six months with Shanghai Shenhua in China and one and a half seasons with Turkish club Galatasaray, where he scored the winning goal in the 2013 Turkish Super Cup final, Drogba returned to Chelsea in July 2014. With a career record of 10 goals in 10 finals and 10 trophies at the club level, he was referred to as the "ultimate big game player." He joined the Canadian club Montreal Impact as a designated player in 2015, playing 41 matches and scoring 23 goals over two seasons. Drogba became a player-owner for Phoenix Rising of the United Soccer League in 2017 and retired a year later at 40. Drogba played for Ivory Coast from 2002 to 2014, captaining the national team from 2006 until his retirement. He is the nation's all-time top goalscorer with 65 goals from 105 appearances. He led Ivory Coast to their first FIFA World Cup appearance in 2006 and later captained the team at the 2010 and 2014 FIFA World Cups. He was part of the Ivory Coast teams that reached the final of the Africa Cup of Nations in 2006 and 2012, but they were beaten on penalties both times. On August 8, 2014, he announced his retirement from international football. In 2018, Drogba retired from professional football at 40 and became the vice president of the International Organization for Peace and Sport on December 11.

Robert Ray "Rod" Roddy was an American radio and TV announcer, born on September 28, 1937, and died on October 27, 2003. He was famous for his work as an offstage announcer on game shows. He announced shows like "Whew!" and "Press Your Luck" on CBS. Roddy took over the role of announcer from Johnny Olson on "The Price is Right" in 1986 and stayed until his death in 2003. He is the longest-serving announcer on the current version of the show as of 2020. Roddy appeared on camera on many episodes of "Press Your Luck" and "The Price is Right." He was also the voice of Mike the Microphone in "Disney's House of Mouse" from 2001 until his death.

Travers was a town in the Val-de-Travers district of the Neuchâtel canton in Switzerland. On January 1, 2009, Travers and several other towns—Boveresse, Buttes, Couvet, Fleurier, Les Bayards, Môtiers, Noiraigue, and Saint-Sulpice—combined to form Val-de-Travers.

Hurricane Dora was the first hurricane to hit the Florida coast at full strength. It was the sixth tropical storm and second hurricane of the 1964 season. Dora developed from a tropical wave near Senegal on August 28. On September 1, it became a tropical storm. By September 3, it had become a Category 1 hurricane and strengthened to a Category 2 six hours later. It became a Category 3 hurricane on September 5, then peaked as a Category 4 with winds of 130 mph on September 6. At 18:00 on September 6, it weakened to a Category 3 and then to a Category 2 as it curved westward. On September 7, it maintained Category 2 intensity as it approached Florida. Dora made landfall near St. Augustine with winds of 110 mph on September 10. By September 11, it weakened to a tropical storm. Dora affected Florida, causing tides up to above sea level. Strong winds hit north Florida, with a wind speed of 125 mph in St. Augustine. In Jacksonville, about 156,000 customers lost electricity and 19% of phones in Duval County were out of service. Much of the damage was to old buildings and those in coastal areas. Some parts of the city had river flooding near the St. Johns River. Heavy rain damaged crops and roads. Dora flattened 74 houses and damaged 9,374 others in Florida. It destroyed 14 mobile homes and severely damaged 218 others. About 50 farm buildings and 423 small businesses were severely damaged. Three deaths and $230 million in damage occurred. In Georgia, 1,135 homes were damaged, and five were destroyed. Eighteen trailers suffered major damage, and 43 small businesses were destroyed or severely damaged. One death and $9 million in damage occurred. The storm affected a few other states, with minor damage. Overall, Dora caused $280 million in damage and five deaths.
An icon is a religious painting in Eastern Christianity. The word "icon" comes from the Greek word for image. Icons may also refer to:

The Samsung Galaxy S6 is a type of smartphone made by Samsung. It was released after the Galaxy S5. There were actually two models: the Galaxy S6 and the Galaxy S6 Edge. The Edge had a curved screen that extended along the sides. Both models were shown to the public on March 1, 2015, at a Samsung event in Barcelona. They came out for sale on April 10, 2015. At another event on August 13, 2015, Samsung added a third model, the Galaxy S6 Edge+, which had a bigger screen and more memory but didn't have the same remote control feature. The Galaxy S6 was made differently, with a metal body and glass back. It had better cameras and a nicer look than before. It could charge wirelessly and pay for things like a credit card. Critics mostly liked it, saying it was better than previous models. But some said taking away the ability to add storage or swap the battery made it less useful for heavy users. The Galaxy S6 Edge was also criticized for not using its curved screen enough to make it worth more money. The Galaxy S7 came out in March 2016 to replace the S6.

Sir John Elliot was born on May 6, 1898, and died on September 18, 1988. He was a British transport and railway manager. His full name was John Elliot Blumenfeld. His father was R. D. Blumenfeld, who worked as the news editor for the "Daily Mail." Later, R. D. Blumenfeld became the managing editor of the "Daily Express." John changed his last name to Elliot in March 1923, following advice from Lord Beaverbrook.

irredentism refers to movements that claim and try to take back territory considered lost or unredeemed by the movement's members. This territory is often based on history or legend. Sometimes, there are debates about the exact boundaries, especially if the nation or people are not clearly defined in history.

The KGB, or Committee for State Security, was the main security agency of the Soviet Union from 1954 until 1991. It was like the Cheka, NKGB, NKVD, and MGB before it and was part of the Council of Ministers. The KGB was responsible for internal security, intelligence, and secret police tasks. Other republics had similar agencies, often with their own names. The KGB worked like the army and had special rules. Its main tasks included foreign intelligence, counter-intelligence, and protecting the Soviet leadership. It also guarded borders and kept the country safe from dissent. In 1991, after the Soviet Union ended, the KGB split into the Federal Security Service and the Foreign Intelligence Service of the Russian Federation. In the early 1990s, with Russian help, South Ossetia created its own KGB. Belarus also set up its own security agency, called the State Security Committee.
Tagsdorf is a commune in Haut-Rhin, which is in Alsace, a region in northeastern France.
Brienzwiler is a municipality in the Interlaken-Oberhasli region of the canton of Bern, in Switzerland. It includes the village of Brienzwiler and the settlement of Balmhof.

Parker Brothers was an American company that made toys and games. In 1991, it became part of Hasbro. Over 1,800 games were published under the Parker Brothers name since 1883. Some of their famous games include Monopoly, Cluedo (known as Clue in North America), Sorry!, Risk, Trivial Pursuit, Ouija, Aggravation, Bop It, and Probe. After Parker Brothers ended, their games were marketed under the Hasbro Gaming label. In 2017, Hasbro brought back the Parker Brothers brand by releasing new games that are similar to some of their well-known older games.
The epicenter in seismology is the point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake or underground explosion starts. This point is also called the epicentre or epicentrum.

Elephant polo is a type of polo played on elephants. It is played in Nepal, Rajasthan (India), and Thailand. Teams from England and Scotland also play. The game uses a standard polo ball and sticks about six to ten feet long, made of cane (similar to bamboo). The playing field is shorter than usual because elephants move slower. Two people ride each elephant. The elephant is steered by a mahout, while the player gives directions. Elephant polo began in Meghauli, Nepal. Tiger Tops in Nepal is the main place for elephant polo and hosts world championships. In Nepal and Thailand, matches follow rules set by the World Elephant Polo Association (WEP). Other places like India and Sri Lanka manage their own tournaments. Sri Lanka had an annual tournament in Galle. In 2007, an elephant went wild during a game, injuring players and damaging a minibus. People who care about animal welfare said the elephants were treated poorly, leading to matches being canceled and sponsors withdrawing. The records in the Guinness Book of World Records also removed mentions of elephant polo. In October 2018, the Thailand Elephant Polo Association said they would stop elephant polo matches. Previously, an annual tournament was held at the Anantara Hotel Bangkok.
Stapleton can mean: A surname A place name

Lily Chloe Ninette Thomson, born on April 5, 1989, is known professionally as Lily James and is an English actress. She studied acting at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama in London. Lily began her acting career in a British TV series called "Just William" in 2010. After playing a supporting role in the period drama series "Downton Abbey" from 2012 to 2015, she became famous for her lead role in the fantasy film "Cinderella" in 2015. Lily then acted as Natasha Rostova in the period TV series "War & Peace" in 2016. She went on to star in several films, including "Baby Driver" (2017), "Darkest Hour" (2017), "The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society" (2018), "Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again" (2018), and "Yesterday" (2019).

Barley (Hordeum vulgare) is a type of cereal grain from the grass family. It is grown in many places with cooler climates around the world. People started growing barley very early, around 10,000 years ago, especially in Eurasia. Barley is used for different things. It can feed animals, make beer and alcoholic drinks, and is sometimes part of healthy foods. People also eat barley in soups and stews, and in bread from various cultures. In 2017, barley was the fourth most produced grain, after maize, rice, and wheat.

In physics, Gauss's law for magnetism is part of four important equations known as Maxwell's equations. This law says that magnetic fields have no sources or sinks. In other words, magnetic fields are always closed loops. It means there are no magnetic charges, like there are electric charges. If magnetic charges were found, the law would need to change. Gauss's law for magnetism has two ways to express it: one using small parts of the field (differential form) and one using the whole area (integral form). Both mean the same thing because of a mathematical rule. Not everyone calls it "Gauss's law for magnetism." Some just say there are no free magnetic poles. One source even says it has no name. It is sometimes called the "transversality requirement" because it says the direction of wave polarization must be perpendicular to the wave's direction of travel.
glinde can refer to several places in Germany. See also: glynde.
Fabien Eboussi Boulaga was a philosopher from Cameroon. He was born on January 17, 1934, and died on October 13, 2018.

Michael Francis McCormack, born on August 2, 1964, is an Australian politician. He has been the leader of the National Party and deputy prime minister since February 2018. McCormack is in charge of infrastructure, transport, and regional development. Before that, from 2017 to 2018, he was the minister for defense personnel and minister for veterans' affairs. He has been a member of the House of Representatives since 2010, representing Riverina in New South Wales. Before politics, McCormack was a newspaper editor.

Eldorado is a city in Saline County, Illinois, United States. The 2010 census showed its population was 4,122. In 1980, the population was higher, with 5,198 people. The city's name, which looks Spanish, originally had different spellings. It combined the names of its founders: Judge Samuel Elder, his son William, his grandson Francis Marion, and his neighbor Joseph Reed. A signpainter for the railroad changed the spelling and pronunciation to "Eldorado" in 1880. This changed the spelling and pronunciation forever. Eldorado is part of the Illinois–Indiana–Kentucky area and is a place where people live but do not work much in Harrisburg.
