Affoltern district, also called Knonauamt or Säuliamt, is one of the twelve districts in the German-speaking part of the canton of Zurich, Switzerland. The capital of this district is the city of Affoltern am Albis.

The Co-operative Party is a centre-left political party in the UK that supports co-operative values. It was founded in 1917 by co-operative societies to campaign for fair treatment of co-operative businesses and to elect 'co-operators' to parliament. The party's history goes back to 1881, when a parliamentary committee was set up within the Co-operative Union. Since 1927, the Co-operative Party has had an agreement with the Labour Party, where they don't compete against each other in elections. Instead, they use the description "Labour and Co-operative Party" when putting up candidates. The Co-operative Party is legally separate from the Labour Party and is registered as a political party with the Electoral Commission. Co-operative Party members cannot be members of any other UK political party, except for the Labour Party or Northern Ireland's Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP). While it has 26 members of parliament, the Co-operative Party is not a separate group in the House of Commons, as all its MPs belong to the Labour Party group. It has representatives in the House of Lords, the Scottish Parliament, the Senedd, the London Assembly, and local government. The Co-operative Party doesn't have a leader. Instead, Joe Fortune serves as the general secretary, and Jim McMahon is the chair of the Co-operative Party group of parliamentarians.
Rickenbach is the name of several places. In Germany, there is a place named Rickenbach. In Switzerland, there is also a place named Rickenbach.

Jessie Lawrence Ferguson was an American actor. He was born on June 8, 1941, and passed away on April 26, 2019. He is best remembered for playing a police officer who was very hard on himself in the movie "Boyz n the Hood," which was directed by John Singleton and was nominated for an Academy Award.
ebnat-kappel is a municipality in Toggenburg constituency, which is in the canton of St. Gallen, Switzerland.

The movie "Riding in Cars with Boys" is from 2001 and is an American biographical film. It is based on the autobiography by Beverly Donofrio. The story is about a woman who had a hard life, including becoming a teenager with a baby, but later got a master's degree. The film covers the years 1961 to 1986. Drew Barrymore, Steve Zahn, Brittany Murphy, and James Woods are the main actors. This film was directed by Penny Marshall and was her last movie as a director. The movie and the book are not exactly the same.

Dargai is an administrative area in the Malakand District of Pakistan's North West Province, along with Batkhela. It lies on the main highway connecting Peshawar, Swat, Dir, and Chitral. Dargai is economically important as a trade hub between the northern and southern regions of Pakistan. It is known for its timber market and historically as the last train station before entering northern Pakistan. Dargai was part of the Malakand Agency Tribal Area until 1970. In that year, Chitral, Dir, and Swat were combined into the Malakand Division, which was later divided into districts, including the Malakand Protected Area, now known as Malakand District. In 2000, the Malakand Division was abolished. Despite constitutional changes since 1970, "Malakand Agency" is sometimes still used to refer to the entire former agency area.

A gravitational singularity is a place in spacetime where gravity is predicted to become extremely strong, based on general relativity. The strength of gravity is measured by something called the curvature of spacetime, which also measures the density of matter. At a singularity, these measurements become very large or infinite, and the normal rules of spacetime do not apply. Scientists think singularities might exist in the middle of black holes and at the start of the universe during the big bang. They're not sure if these predictions mean singularities actually exist or if our current understanding is not complete. According to general relativity, if a massive object, like a star, collapses beyond a certain point, it forms a black hole with a singularity inside. The singularity is covered by an event horizon. In this case, a singularity is a point where the paths of light and matter cannot be extended smoothly. Scientists believe the universe started as a singularity at the beginning of the big bang. Unlike a black hole, the big bang did not form from a collapsed object, so the usual rules for black holes may not apply. Currently, we can't describe the earliest moments of the big bang using general relativity or quantum mechanics. However, quantum mechanics suggests that particles cannot exist in a space smaller than their wavelength.

Mirosława Litmanowicz, born Kałęcka on September 6, 1928, was a Polish chess player. She won the Polish women's chess championship in 1968. She was also a FIDE Woman International Master in 1967. She passed away on August 18, 2017.

Throckmorton County is in Texas, United States. In 2010, it had 1,641 people. The county seat is Throckmorton. It was created in 1858 and organized in 1879. The county is named after William Throckmorton, an early settler. Throckmorton County is one of six dry counties in Texas.

Dmitry Vladimirovich Strakhov, born on May 17, 1995, is a Russian racing cyclist. He currently rides for a UCI team. In 2017, he competed in a men's point race at the UCI Track Cycling World Championships. In May 2019, he was included in the list for the 2019 Giro d'Italia. On March 11, 2020, it was reported that Strakhov had been infected with SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19. He was hospitalized in an Abu Dhabi hospital after being put in quarantine following the 2020 UAE Tour.

The Limbourg brothers (Herman, Paul, and Johan) were famous Dutch painters who made small pictures called miniatures. They lived and worked from about 1385 to 1416 in Nijmegen. They were active in France and Burgundy during the early 15th century. Their art style was called International Gothic. They are well-known for creating a very famous book with pictures, called the "Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry."

A hypodermic needle, from Greek words meaning "under" and "skin," is a thin, hollow tube with a sharp point used to inject or extract liquids. It's often used with a syringe to put medicines or other liquids into the body or take blood out. It helps in drawing blood from veins. Large needles can be useful in serious blood loss or when treating shock. These needles are used for quick liquid delivery, especially when the liquid can't be taken by mouth, like insulin. People can get injections in their arm or other parts of the body. In labs, hypodermic needles are crucial for keeping things clean. They prevent dirt from getting into samples. This is because their smooth surface stops tiny germs from sticking, and their sharp edge makes the hole small, stopping bigger germs from entering.

Melissa Suzanne McBride, born on May 23, 1965, is an American actress and former casting director. Her big break came when she played Carol Peletier in the AMC series "The Walking Dead," which started in 2010 and is still ongoing. She has been highly praised for her role and has won several awards and been nominated for many more. At first, she was only in a small role and not credited until the end of the episodes. However, her role grew over time, and she became a main cast member. As of 2020, she is the second person credited in the opening titles of the show. She has appeared in every season, alongside Norman Reedus, who is the only other cast member to have done so.

A.C. Moore was an American store that sold arts and crafts. It was owned by Nicole Crafts. A.C. Moore had 145 stores in the eastern United States. Its main office was in Berlin, New Jersey. On November 25, 2019, A.C. Moore said it would close all its stores and sell some of its property to a competitor called Michaels.

Pori is a city and municipality on Finland's west coast. It is near the Gulf of Bothnia, at the mouth of the Kokemäenjoki River, west of Tampere, north of Turku, and northwest of Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Pori was founded in 1558 by Duke John, who later became John III of Sweden. The city has about 45,000 people and covers an area of which 40% is water. Its population density is high. Pori speaks only Finnish. It is Finland's largest city and the 7th largest urban area. Pori is the capital of the Satakunta region with 224,028 people and the Poris sub-region with 136,905 people.

Clannad is a Japanese visual novel by Key. It came out on April 28, 2004, for Windows computers. Unlike Key's earlier works, "Kanon" and "Air," which were first for adults and then for younger audiences, Clannad was made for all ages right from the start. It was later released on other game systems like PlayStation 2, PlayStation Portable, Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, PlayStation Vita, PlayStation 4, and Nintendo Switch. An English version was released in 2015 on Steam by Sekai Project. Clannad tells the story of Tomoya Okazaki, a regular high school student in his last year. He meets several people, including five girls, and helps solve their problems. The game has different paths depending on your choices. It focuses on the five main female characters. Clannad was very popular. It was the best-selling PC game in Japan at the time. It also made it into the top 50 games several more times. In 2005, Key made a game called "Another" which continues the story of one of the main girls, Tomoyo Sakagami, from Clannad. Clannad has been turned into many other things. Four manga adaptations were made by different companies. There are light novels, art books, and audio dramas. An animated movie and two anime series were also produced by Toei Animation and Kyoto Animation, respectively. Both were released in North America by Sentai Filmworks. These adaptations were very successful in Japan and got good reviews overseas.

The national flag of Bolivia was first used in 1851. It has three horizontal colors: red, yellow, and green. In the middle, there is a coat of arms. Some say the red color represents brave soldiers. Green stands for fertility. Yellow symbolizes mineral wealth. Bolivia, along with six other countries, has a flag that includes a depiction of its own flag. Since 2009, the wiphala flag is also considered Bolivia's official flag.

The Saturn Relay is a minivan made by General Motors. It was first introduced in 2005 and was built alongside other vehicles like the Buick Terraza, Chevrolet Uplander, and Pontiac Montana SV6 in Georgia. The Relay was the first Saturn minivan without plastic side panels. It was also the first to be a rebadged Chevrolet or Pontiac. For 2005, it came with a 3.5-liter engine that went from 0 to 60 mph in about 9 seconds. In 2006, a faster 3.9-liter engine was added. The 2007 model dropped the 3.5-liter engine, keeping the 3.9-liter as the base engine. This engine required all-wheel drive, which was not available. Instead, a flexible-fuel engine was added for fleet use in 2007. In crash tests, the Relay got high scores. It had good fuel efficiency in city and highway driving. The base price was $22,850. There were three trim levels: 1, 2, and 3. The Relay 3 came with front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. All models had seven seats, with removable second-row seats and a folding third-row bench. OnStar and a DVD rear entertainment system were standard. A navigation system was optional, as were side airbags. The Saturn Relay ended in 2007, replaced by the Saturn Outlook.
Willis David Gradison Jr. was born on December 28, 1928. He is an American politician from Ohio. He worked in the United States House of Representatives from 1975 to 1993.

The Samsung Galaxy Note 10 is a line of Android phones. Samsung Electronics made and sold these phones as part of the Samsung Galaxy Note series. They were shown to the public on August 7, 2019. These phones replaced the Samsung Galaxy Note 9. People knew a lot about the phones before they were announced. In 2020, Samsung also made a less expensive version called the Galaxy Note 10 Lite.

Companion planting in gardening and agriculture means planting different crops close together for various reasons. These reasons include keeping pests away, helping with pollination, attracting helpful insects, using space more efficiently, and increasing crop productivity. Companion planting is a type of polyculture. People in both developed and developing countries use companion planting for many reasons. This practice has been around for centuries, dating back to traditional cottage gardens in England and forest gardens in Asia, and even thousands of years to ancient Mesoamerica.
Melano is a municipality in the Lugano district, which is in the Canton of Ticino, Switzerland.

The 1983-84 NHL season was the 67th season of the National Hockey League. The Edmonton Oilers beat the New York Islanders, who had won the Stanley Cup four times in a row, in the finals, winning four games to one.

In physics, angular velocity describes how quickly an object rotates or revolves around another point. It is about how fast the orientation of an object changes over time. There are two kinds of angular velocity: spin and orbital. Spin angular velocity measures how fast a rigid body turns around its center. Orbital angular velocity measures how fast a point moves around a fixed point, or the rate of change of its angle over time. Spin angular velocity doesn't change with the choice of the fixed point, but orbital angular velocity does. Angular velocity is typically measured in angles per unit time, such as radians per second. Its SI unit is radians per second, often just stated as 1/s or 1/second. Angular velocity is usually represented by the symbol ω. Generally, positive ω indicates a counterclockwise rotation, and negative ω indicates a clockwise rotation. For instance, a geostationary satellite orbits the Earth once every 24 hours. Its angular velocity is 360 degrees per 24 hours, or about 15 degrees per hour, which is also approximately 0.26 radians per hour. If the angle is measured in radians, the linear velocity is the radius times the angular velocity, or v = r × ω. For a satellite at a radius of 42,000 km from the Earth's center, its speed through space is about 11,000 km/h. The angular velocity is positive because the satellite moves eastward, following the Earth's rotation (counterclockwise when viewed from the north pole). In three-dimensional space, angular velocity is a vector quantity, with its size showing the speed of rotation and its direction pointing perpendicularly to the plane of rotation. Its direction is conventionally determined by the right-hand rule.
Hinton is a town in Caddo County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, the town had 3,196 people, which was more than in 2000 when there were 2,175 people. Hinton is roughly west of Oklahoma City.

Ronald Sidney Tauranac, born on January 13, 1925, and died on July 17, 2020, was a British-Australian engineer and racing car designer. In 1962, he and Formula One driver Jack Brabham created the Brabham racing team. After Brabham stopped driving in 1970, Tauranac managed the team until 1972, when he sold it to Bernie Ecclestone. Tauranac then worked with Frank Williams on redesigning a racing car and helped Trojan create a Formula One car. After a brief time in Australia, he returned to England to start the Ralt marque. The first Ralt car, the RT1, was used in different racing categories and was successful, winning championships in 1975 and 1983. Tauranac also designed the Theodore F1 car in 1978. For 1979, he created two new designs: the RT2 for Formula Two and the RT3 for Formula Three. The RT3 won the 1983 European F3 championship and five British F3 titles. A joint project with Honda resulted in the RH6, which won championships in 1981, 1984, and 1985. In 1988, Tauranac sold the Ralt business to March Engineering for £1.25 million. He continued to work in the racing world, consulting for teams and racing schools. Tauranac was honored as an Officer of the Order of Australia in 2002 for his contributions to motor racing. He died at the age of 95 in 2020.
Lovelock is the biggest town in Big Horn County, Wyoming, United States. The population was 2,360 in the 2010 census.

Gustavo José Joaquín Noboa Bejarano was born on August 21, 1937, in Guayaquil, Ecuador. He is an Ecuadorian politician. Noboa was the president of Ecuador from January 22, 2000, to January 15, 2003. He was also the vice president during Jamil Mahuad's government.

Vandervoort is a town in Polk County, Arkansas, United States. It had 120 people living there in 2000. The town is named after the mother of an important railway businessman from early in the 20th century. Her name was Jan de Goeijen, and her maiden name was Van der Voort.

Jock Sturrock, born on May 14, 1915, in Melbourne, and passed away on July 11, 1997, in Noosa Heads, was an Australian yachtsman. He won more than four hundred yachting races, including international, national, state, and club championships.

The bleating tree frog, also called Keferstein's tree frog, is a tree frog in the family Pelodryadidae. It is native to coastal areas in eastern Australia, from South-Eastern Queensland to around Eden, New South Wales.

The National Symphony Orchestra (NSO), started in 1930, is a symphony orchestra in the United States. It is based in Washington, D.C. Their main place to perform is the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The NSO played in the National Memorial Day concert and the Capitol Fourth event.

A neural network is a system made up of nodes, or artificial neurons, designed to solve problems in artificial intelligence. It can be either a real biological network of neurons or an artificial version. In an artificial neural network, connections between nodes are represented as weights. Positive weights show excitatory connections, while negative weights show inhibitory connections. Inputs are changed by weights and then added together. This is called a linear combination. An activation function then controls the final output. Outputs usually range from 0 to 1, or from -1 to 1. These networks can be trained using a dataset. They can also learn from experience and find patterns in complex information.

On July 15, 2020, between 8 PM and 10 PM UTC, around 130 important Twitter accounts were hacked. Hackers promoted a Bitcoin scam. Twitter and other sources said that the hackers got control of Twitter’s tools to change the accounts and send tweets directly. They might have used social engineering to trick Twitter workers. On July 31, 2020, three people were arrested for wire fraud, money laundering, identity theft, and unauthorized computer access related to the scam. The scam tweets asked people to send Bitcoin to a wallet, promising the money would be doubled. Within minutes, over 320 transactions happened, and the Bitcoin value in one account was high before Twitter removed the scam messages. Also, data from eight non-verified accounts was taken. Dmitri Alperovitch, who co-founded a cybersecurity company, called this the worst hack of a major social media platform. The FBI and other agencies are looking into the scam and Twitter’s security. Security experts worry that the social engineering could affect important discussions on social media, like before the 2020 U.S. presidential election.

Madeline Gail Kahn, born Madeline Gail Wolfson, was an American actress, comedian, voice actress, and singer. She was known for her funny roles in movies directed by Peter Bogdanovich and Mel Brooks, including "What's Up, Doc?" (1972), "Young Frankenstein" (1974), "High Anxiety" (1977), "History of the World, Part I" (1981), and "Blazing Saddles" (1974), for which she was nominated for an Academy Award. Kahn first appeared on Broadway in "Leonard Sillman's New Faces of 1968" and was nominated for a Tony Award for the play "In the Boom Boom Room" in 1974 and for "On the Twentieth Century" in 1978. She starred in the short-lived sitcom "Oh Madeline" (1983-84) and won a Daytime Emmy Award in 1987 for an ABC afterschool special. Kahn received another Tony Award nomination for the play "Born Yesterday" in 1989 and won the 1993 Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play for the comedy "The Sisters Rosensweig." She appeared in other films such as "The Cheap Detective" (1978), "City Heat" (1984), "Clue" (1985), and "Nixon" (1995).

An oar is a tool used to move boats in water. It has a flat side at one end, and rowers hold the other end. Oars are used for rowing, while paddles are not. In rowing, the oar is attached to the boat through a pivot point, like an oarlock or a thole. The oar is mostly outside the boat, and the rower pulls on the shorter end, moving the longer end through the water. The oar acts as a second-class lever, with the water as the fulcrum, the oarlock as the load, and the rower as the force. Though unusual, the oar multiplies the small movement of the rower's hand into a larger movement of the boat in the water. The rower pushes hard over a short distance, while the water pushes the boat over a longer distance, so the work done by the rower equals the work done by the water. In contrast, paddles are held in both hands and are not connected to the boat. Rowers face the back of the boat, reach towards the back, and place the oar blade in the water. As they lean back towards the front of the boat, the blade pivots in the oarlock, and the longer end moves towards the back, providing forward movement. For many years, boats were moved by sails, rowers, or paddlers. Some old boats used both oars and sails, depending on the wind direction and speed.

A medical abortion, also called a medication abortion, happens when pills are used to end a pregnancy. First, a person takes mifepristone. Then, they take misoprostol. This combination is both safe and effective for abortions at different stages of pregnancy. If mifepristone is not available, misoprostol alone can be used.

Ji Guobiao was born on March 1, 1932, and passed away on September 5, 2019. He was a Chinese chemical engineer and a member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. Ji Guobiao was an important pioneer in chemical fiber engineering technology in China.
The Berowra division is an Australian area where people choose their representative. It is in the state of New South Wales.

phosphorus pentafluoride, or PF, is a type of phosphorus halide. It is a colorless, toxic gas that produces fumes when it is in the air.

Ksenia Arturovna Tripolitova was born on May 7, 1915, in Vilna, Russian Empire, and passed away on April 9, 2020, in Paris. She was a Russian-born French ballet dancer. She studied at the studio of Lyubov Yegorova. Ksenia and her husband toured together in the 1930s and 1940s. During World War II, she performed in France when Nazis were fighting there. In 1949, she performed in Switzerland. At the end of the 1950s, she and her husband formed a vocal and dance ensemble called "Troika." In 1954-1955, she worked in the opera theater in Tunis. In 1957, she performed with the Ural Cossack choir in Spain. Ksenia turned 100 in 2015.

The Allen Telescope Array (ATA), previously called the One Hectare Telescope (1HT), is a radio telescope used for astronomical observations and searching for signs of extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI). It's located at the Hat Creek Radio Observatory in Shasta County, northeast of San Francisco, California. The project began as a partnership between the SETI Institute and the Radio Astronomy Laboratory (RAL) at the University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley), with funding from an initial $11.5 million donation by the Paul G. Allen Family Foundation. Paul Allen, a co-founder of Microsoft, later contributed an additional $13.5 million to support the construction of the first and second phases. Construction was completed on October 11, 2007, when the ATA started operating with 42 antennas (ATA-42). Allen has donated more than $30 million in total, but the project couldn't build the originally planned 350 6.1 m (20 ft) dishes. The ATA faced a brief operational pause due to lack of funds between April and August 2011. Observations resumed afterward. In April 2012, UC Berkeley left the project, and management was transferred to SRI International (formerly Stanford Research Institute), an independent, nonprofit research organization. As of 2016, the SETI Institute uses the ATA from 6 PM to 6 AM daily. In August 2014, the installation was temporarily shut down due to a nearby forest fire but was largely unaffected.

The British Association for Applied Linguistics (BAAL) is a group in the UK that brings together people interested in language and applied linguistics. BAAL organizes regular meetings for its members in different places in the UK. They publish conference proceedings and send out a regular newsletter. BAAL also gives scholarships to students. There is an elected group called the Executive Committee that speaks up for the members. Dawn Knight is the current chair (2018-2021). BAAL has more than 1200 members from around the world and is a registered charity in the UK (charity number 246800).

An airliner is a plane used to carry passengers and cargo. Airlines operate most of them. Generally, an airliner is a commercial plane meant for multiple passengers or cargo. The largest airliners are wide-body jets, also called twin-aisle planes, because they have two aisles running from front to back. These are used for long flights between big cities. A smaller, more common type is the narrow-body or single-aisle plane, used for shorter or medium-length flights with fewer passengers. Regional airliners seat fewer than 100 people and might use turbofans or turboprops. These planes support major airlines by carrying passengers to big hubs. Regional routes connect to large airline hubs like spokes on a wheel. Lighter planes, called commuter aircraft or air taxis, carry fewer passengers for short trips. For example, the Beechcraft 1900 has only 19 seats.

Duck Commander is a brand for duck calls and the name of a company in West Monroe, Louisiana, United States. The company makes duck calls and other hunting items for ducks. It also makes deer-hunting items under Buck Commander and turkey-hunting items under Strut Commander. Phil Robertson, who was a football player, started the business in an old boat. He made calls for 25 years using cedar trees from Louisiana. His son Willie now leads the company and has grown it into a big business. The Robertson family and their business are shown on a TV show called "Duck Dynasty" on A&E. Before that, they were featured on a show called "Duck Commander" on the Outdoor Channel.

Halabja is a city in the Kurdistan region of Iraq. It is the capital of Halabja governorate. Located northeast of Baghdad and near the Iranian border, Halabja is part of the Greater Hewraman region, which stretches across the Iran-Iraq border. Surrounding Halabja are the Hawraman and Shnrwe ranges to the northeast, the Balambo range to the south, and the Sirwan river to the west. The people in Halabja speak the Sorani dialect of Kurdish. Some nearby villages speak the Hewrami dialect.

The Meissner effect is when a superconductor expels a magnetic field when it becomes superconducting after cooling below its critical temperature. In 1933, Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld discovered this by cooling tin and lead samples and measuring the magnetic field outside them. The samples, when cooled, canceled most of the interior magnetic fields. They saw this only because the magnetic field outside increased as the interior field decreased. This proved that superconductors are not just perfect conductors but have a unique property. The Meissner state means no magnetic field inside. Type-I superconductors stop superconducting when a certain magnetic field strength is reached. Type-II superconductors allow some magnetic field when the field is strong. Most pure superconductors, except niobium and carbon nanotubes, are type I, while most impure and compound superconductors are type II.

" Misery" is a song by the American band Maroon 5. It came out on June 22, 2010, through A&M Octone Records. This song was the first single from their album "Hands All Over," which was released in 2010.

North Macedonia has 34 cities. Five of them have more than 50,000 people, and 12 towns have fewer than 10,000. The capital, Skopje, is home to about one-quarter of the country's population. As of 2002, 59.5% of the people lived in cities. There are 12 small towns in North Macedonia with less than 10,000 people. They are called "cities" officially but are often referred to as "small towns." Five cities have over 50,000 people: Skopje with 506,926, Bitola with 74,550, Kumanovo with 70,842, Prilep with 66,246, and Tetovo with 86,580. These are the largest cities. There are 17 towns with between 10,000 and 50,000 people: Veles with 43,716, Stip with 43,652, Ohrid with 42,033, Gostivar with 35,847, Strumica with 35,311, Kavadarci with 29,188, Kočani with 28,330, Kičevo with 27,067, Struga with 16,559, Radoviš with 16,223, Gevgelija with 15,685, Debar with 14,561, Kriva Palanka with 14,558, Sveti Nikole with 13,746, Negotino with 13,284, Delčevo with 11,500, and Vinica with 10,863. These towns are usually called "medium-sized cities."
Cool is a town in Parker County, Texas, United States. In 2010, the town had 157 people.

The Russian Empire, which lasted from 1721 to 1917, covered parts of Europe, Asia, and North America. It was one of the largest empires in history, surpassed only by the British and Mongol empires. During its height, the empire's power increased as neighboring countries like Sweden, Poland, Persia, and the Ottoman Empire weakened. It played a key role in defeating Napoleon's plans in 1812-1814 and expanded its territories to the west and south. The Romanov family ruled the empire from 1721 until the end, with a branch called Holstein-Gottorp-Romanov taking over in 1762. At the start of the 19th century, the empire stretched from the Arctic Ocean to the Black Sea and covered parts of America as well. With over 125 million people in 1897, it was the third-largest in population after China and India. It had many different groups, including various economies, ethnicities, languages, and religions. There were many uprisings and assassinations, which were watched by the secret police, and thousands were sent to Siberia. The economy was mainly farming, with large farms worked by people called serfs, who were tied to the land. Serfs were freed in 1861, but the nobles still had control. The economy slowly improved with foreign help for railways and factories. Tsar Ivan III (1462-1505) started the empire, while Peter the Great (1682-1725) made it a major European power by fighting wars and moving the capital to St. Petersburg. He also modernized society to look more like Europe. Catherine the Great (1762-1796) expanded the empire through conquest and modernization. Alexander II (1855-1881) freed the serfs in 1861 and protected Orthodox Christians in the Ottoman Empire. This led Russia into World War I on the side of France and Britain. The empire was an absolute monarchy until 1905, when a constitutional monarchy was introduced. It had problems during World War I. The royal family was executed by the Bolsheviks in 1918, who took over after a civil war. They forced most of the nobles into exile or killed them, ending the Russian Empire with the formation of the Soviet Union in 1922.

Ongar railway station is on the Epping Ongar railway heritage line in Chipping Ongar, Essex. It opened in 1865 by the Great Eastern Railway. In 1949, it became part of London Transport. It closed in 1994. Until then, it was the easternmost point of the Central Line, and the eastern buffers remain the starting point for measuring distances on the London Underground.

Roberts County is in Texas, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 929 people, making it the least populous county in Texas. The county seat and only incorporated community is Miami. Roberts County was created in 1876 and organized in 1889. It is named after Oran Milo Roberts, a former governor of Texas. Roberts County is one of six counties in Texas that do not allow alcohol.

Eye contact happens when two animals look directly into each other's eyes at the same time. In humans, it's a type of nonverbal communication. People often think it shows confidence, respect, and is important for social interaction. This term was first used in the 1960s. In different cultures, eye contact means different things, often because of religious and social differences. The study of eye contact is called "oculesics."

pavement lights, also called vault lights in the US, floor lights, or sidewalk prisms, are flat-topped lights set into sidewalks or floors. They let sunlight into spaces below. Often, they use special prisms to spread light sideways under buildings. These lights were invented in the 19th century but became less popular with cheap electric lights. Many older cities and small places around the world have or had these lights. Most of the existing ones are about a century old. Some new buildings are now getting these lights too.

Lancaster is a city in Fairfield County, Ohio, in the south-central part of the state. As of the 2010 census, it had 38,780 people. The city is near the Hocking River. It is southeast of Columbus and southwest of Zanesville. Lancaster is the county seat of Fairfield County.

The Korean peninsula has many mountains along its eastern side. Most rivers flow westward into the Yellow Sea. Some rivers pass through artificial lakes on their way to the coast. There are no natural lakes on the mainland. A few rivers flow south into the Korea Strait. Others flow east to the East Korea Bay, but they are usually small streams. The rivers are listed with their smaller tributaries first, going upstream. They are listed in a counterclockwise order, starting from the Amnok to the Duman.

chopicallqui, possibly from Quechua words meaning "center ravine," is a mountain in the Cordillera Blanca in Peru's Andes. It is one of the highest peaks in the area, with a summit above sea level. The mountain is in Yungay province, in Ancash. It is located between Huascarán and Contrahierbas mountains.

Ilkka Olavi Suominen, born on April 8, 1939, in Nakkila, is a Finnish politician from the National Coalition Party. He served as the president of the Nordic Council in 1992. Suominen was a member of the parliament from 1970 to 1975 and from 1983 to 1994. He was the chairman of the National Coalition Party from 1979 to 1991 and was the speaker of the parliament twice, in 1987 and from 1991 to 1994. He was also a minister of trade and industry in the Holkeri cabinet from 1987 to 1991. After leaving the parliament, Suominen became the CEO of Alko, a state monopoly. He was elected to the European Parliament (MEP) from 1999 to 2004 and was part of the EPP. Suominen was the chairman of the parliamentary assembly of the OSCE from 1992 to 1994.

Wofford Heights is a census-designated place in southern Sierra Nevada, California. It is in Kern County and located in the West Kern River Valley, south-southwest of Kernville. The area is at an elevation. In 2010, the population was 2,200. It was 2,276 in 2000.

Shakib Khan, born on March 28, 1979, is a Bangladeshi actor, producer, singer, and media personality. Known as "King Khan" and "King of Dhallywood," he has been a major figure in the local film industry for about two decades. He is famous for his energetic performances and has made many popular films. Khan first appeared in the 1999 film "Ananta Bhalobasha," but didn't gain widespread fame until later. His breakthrough came in 2008 with "Priya Amar Priya," a commercial success where he played a college student. The film earned him a lot of money and was the second highest-grossing movie of that year. In 2016, his film "Shikari" was also a big hit, and he starred in "Swatta" and "Nabab" in 2017, which were very successful. "Swatta" won several awards, and "Nabab" was the highest-grossing film of that year. In 2019, he was the highest-paid actor in Bangladesh for his role in "Nolok." His production "Password" also performed well at the box office. Some of his notable films include "Shuva" (2006), "Amar Praner Swami" (2007), "Bhaijaan Elok Re" (2018), and "Chalbaaz" (2018). Khan also started his career as a playback singer in 2011 with the film "Moner Jala." He became a producer in 2014 with the film "Password" and went on to produce other successful films. Khan has won many awards for his work, including four National Film Awards and several Prothom Alo and Bachshas awards. He is one of the most popular and highest-paid actors in Bangladesh.

Wanrong, also known as the Xuantong Empress, lived from November 13, 1906, to June 20, 1946. She was the empress of the last Chinese emperor, Puyi, who ruled the Qing dynasty. In 1932, when Japan created a puppet state in Manchuria, named Manchukuo, and made Puyi its leader, Wanrong became the empress of this state. During the Soviet invasion of Manchuria in 1945 at the end of the Sino-Japanese War, Wanrong was captured by Chinese Communist guerrillas. She was moved to different places before being kept in a prison camp in Yanji, Jilin. She died in prison around June or August 1946, but her body was never found. On October 23, 2006, Wanrong's younger brother, Runqi, performed a burial ritual for her at the Western Qing Tombs.

Uzlomac is a long mountain in Bosnia, east of the line from Maslovare to Vrbanjci to Kotor varoš to Čelinac. It runs from southeast to northwest through the mountain area. The mountain goes from the Kruševica River (west of the Borja Mountains) to Jošavka. It has many mixed forests and hunting animals, including some unique to Bosnia. The forests include deciduous oak and deciduous beech. There are also many water sources like springs, streams, and rivers. Many smaller rivers and streams, like Usora and Ukriña, start on Uzlomac, which feed into the Vrbas and Bosna rivers.

Thixotropy is a property where certain fluids or gels become thinner over time when shaken or stressed. They then take time to get thicker again. Some fluids, like ketchup, become thinner quickly and are called pseudoplastic. Others, like yogurt, take longer to thin and can become almost solid. Gels and colloids often show this behavior, appearing solid until shaken. Thixotropy happens because particles need time to organize. Some fluids, called anti-thixotropic, get thicker when shaken.

Arjen Anthony Lucassen, born on April 3, 1960, in Hilversum, Netherlands, is a Dutch singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and record producer. He is famous for his long-running progressive metal/rock opera project called Ayreon. Lucassen started his career in 1980 as a guitarist and backup singer for a band called Bodine, using the name Iron Anthony. In 1984, he joined a band named Vengeance and stayed there for eight years. After that, he left the band to make more progressive music. In 1986, he released a solo album named "Pools of Sorrow, Waves of Joy" under the nickname Anthony, but it was not successful. In 1995, Lucassen released an album called "Ayreon: The Final Experiment" without a credited artist. He sang, wrote songs, and played most of the instruments on it. This album led to the creation of Ayreon. Despite not being very well-known at first, Ayreon gained attention and praise after the release of its third album "Into the Electric Castle." This helped Lucassen become known as a composer of rock operas. Following the success of Ayreon, Lucassen was involved in many other projects. He created and performs with bands like Star One, Guilt Machine, and The Gentle Storm. He also led Ambeon and Stream of Passion. Lucassen writes and composes most of his songs, but he lets others write lyrics in some projects. Lucassen plays many instruments. His main instruments are guitar and keyboards, but he also plays bass and banjo. Throughout his career, he has released 26 studio albums, four live albums, two EPs, and 17 singles. He has also participated in albums with other artists, appearing on over 50 albums. Since creating Ayreon, Lucassen has become well-known in the rock and metal music world. Many people call him a "genius" and praise his musical skills.

Rod Piazza, born on December 18, 1947, in Riverside, California, is an American blues harmonica player and singer. He has been playing with his band, The Mighty Flyers, since 1980. He formed the band with his pianist wife, Honey Piazza. Their music has a boogie sound that mixes jump blues, West Coast blues, and Chicago blues.

A disposable product is made to be used once and then thrown away or recycled. Sometimes, it can last for several months, like a disposable air filter. This is to distinguish it from a similar product that can be washed and used many times, like a washable air filter. The term "disposable" is not the same as "consumable." In the world of machinery, consumables are items like welding rods and tips that need to be replaced after a certain time, such as inks for printing or gas for welding. Disposables are items that can be thrown away when they are damaged or no longer useful.

Tiko, formerly known as ‘keka’ by the Bakweris, is a town and important port in Cameroon’s southwest region. It grew as a market town for Duala fishermen, Bakweri farmers and hunters from Molyko, Bwenga, Bulu, and Bokova. The main parts of Tiko include streets 1 to 7, Motombolombo, Down Beach, New Quarter, P&T Quarters, New Layout, Long Street, Likomba, Golf Club, Mutengene, and Ombe. In 2010, Tiko had around 55,914 people. It's popular for tourists visiting Cameroon. Tiko has industries, mainly run by the CDC, which make rubber, banana, and palm oil. The town hosts the Tiko Golf Club, a favorite for golfers. The Likomba golf course has 18 holes and hosts major tournaments during the dry season. Tiko also hosts special forces, ensuring peace and security for the residents. Mutengene, a small town west of Tiko, is a crossroads to Buea and Limbe, formerly called Victoria.

Hugo Boss AG, often called Boss, is a German luxury fashion company based in Metzingen, Baden-Württemberg. They make clothes, accessories, shoes, and perfumes. Boss is one of the biggest German clothing companies, with sales of €2.9 billion in 2019. Their stock is part of the MDAX. Boss was started in 1924 by Hugo Boss and first made everyday clothing. During the 1930s, with the rise of the Nazi Party, Boss began making and selling Nazi uniforms. This led to increased sales because the company supplied uniforms for groups like the Hitler Youth and Waffen-SS during World War II. After World War II and the founder's death in 1948, Boss focused on men's suits. In 1988, the company went public and launched a fragrance line. In 1997, they added men's and women's clothing lines, followed by a complete women's collection in 2000 and children's clothing in 2006-2007. Since then, Boss has grown into a major global fashion brand. As of now, they own over 1,113 stores worldwide.

Nystagmus is a condition where the eyes move involuntarily, or sometimes voluntarily. It can develop in infancy or later in life and might cause reduced or limited vision. Due to these eye movements, it is sometimes called "dancing eyes." In normal vision, when the head moves, the eyes move in the opposite direction to keep distant objects in focus. The ear's semicircular canals sense head movement and send signals to the brain. The brain then tells the eye muscles to adjust the gaze so the eyes stay on an object while the head moves. Nystagmus happens when the ear's semicircular canals are stimulated, even if the head is still. The direction of the eye movement depends on which canal is affected. There are two main types of nystagmus: pathological and physiological. Within each type, there are different kinds. Nystagmus can be caused by a birth defect, lack of sleep, certain diseases, chemicals, medicines, alcohol, or spinning. While it was previously thought to be untreatable, several drugs have recently been found to help. Nystagmus is sometimes linked to dizziness.

Starting around the middle of the 2nd century, this practice became linked with worshiping the great mother goddess. Before 159 AD, taurobolium wasn't just for her. But after 159 AD, all private taurobolium inscriptions mentioned the "magna mater."

Ugur Yucel, born on May 26, 1957, is a Turkish actor, producer, and director. He studied theater at the Istanbul Municipality Conservatory. Between 1975 and 1984, he acted in several plays at Kenter Theatre, Tef Kabare, Dormen Theatre, and Şan Musikholu. He became known for his roles in "Selamsiz Bandosu" and "Muhsin Bey" in 1987. He had more success when he acted in "Eskıya" in 1996.

The Murray was an Australian electoral division in Victoria. It was in the northern part of Victoria, next to the Murray River, which separates Victoria from New South Wales. The division included towns like Shepparton, Echuca, Cobram, Yarrawonga, Boort, and Bridgewater. In 2018, the division was renamed Nicholls. The change took effect for the 2019 federal election.
