Bradford Interchange is a transport station in Bradford, West Yorkshire, England. It includes a railway station and a bus and coach station. Designed in 1962, it opened on January 14, 1973. The interchange handles most city center bus services and National Express coaches. The railway station, one of two in the city center, serves Northern trains and also stops Grand Central services from London King's Cross.
" When the tigers broke free" is a Pink Floyd song by Roger Waters. It describes the death of his father, Eric Fletcher Waters, who died in the Battle of Anzio during World War II.

Neon Trees is an American rock band from Provo, Utah. In late 2008, they opened for the band The Killers on several North American tour dates. Soon after, they signed with Mercury Records. In 2010, they released their first album, "Habits." Their first single, "Animal," reached number 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 1 on the Alternative Songs chart.

Elbert D. Glover is a researcher and writer about tobacco addiction and helping people stop smoking. He teaches at the University of Maryland College Park School of Public Health. He is a professor and heads the Behavioral and Community Health department.

Margaret Jobeth Williams, born on December 6, 1948, is an American actress and television director. She got nominated for an Academy Award in 1994 for directing a short film called "On Hope." Since 2009, she has been the president of the Screen Actors Guild Foundation. Williams became famous for her roles in films like "Stir Crazy" (1980), "Poltergeist" (1982), "The Big Chill" (1983), "The Day After" (1983), "Teachers" (1984), and "Stuart Gordon's The Tomb of Louis XV" (1986). She was nominated for three Emmy Awards for her work in TV movies and a sitcom. Specifically, she was nominated for best lead actress in a miniseries or movie for her roles in "Adam" (1983) and "Baby M" (1988). She also had a role in the sitcom "Frasier" (1993–94). Williams also starred in the TV series "The Client" (1995–96) and appeared in recurring roles in "Dexter" (2007) and "Private Practice" (2009–11).

Versigny is a town in the Aisne department, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in northern France. It belongs to the Communauté de Communes des Villes d'Oise. Versigny is located between Saint-Quentin, Laon, and Chauny.

Forgetting Sarah Marshall is a 2008 American romantic comedy. Nicholas Stoller directed it. Jason Segel, Kristen Bell, Mila Kunis, and Russell Brand star in the film. Segel also wrote it and Judd Apatow helped produce it. Universal Pictures released it. Filming began in April 2007 at the Turtle Bay Resort in Hawaii. The story is about Peter Brett, a music composer for a TV show with his girlfriend Sarah Marshall as the main actress. They were together for five years, but Sarah suddenly broke up with Peter. Devastated, Peter went on vacation to Hawaii to move on. He ends up seeing Sarah there, who is on holiday with her new boyfriend.

Justin Marie Bomboko Lokumba was born on September 22, 1928, and died on April 10, 2014. He was a Congolese politician and important leader. Bomboko worked as the Minister of Foreign Affairs for Congo. He also led the Congolese government as the Chairman of the College of Commissioners. People often call him "the father of independence" for Congo. Bomboko was Foreign Minister three times: from 1960 to 1963, from 1965 to 1969, and again in 1981. He passed away in Brussels, Belgium, due to a long illness, at the age of 85.
Anthony Lane is a British journalist. He writes about movies for The New Yorker magazine.

Meccano is a model construction system created in 1898 by Frank Hornby in Liverpool, United Kingdom. It uses metal strips, plates, wheels, axles, gears, and plastic parts connected with nuts and bolts. You can build working models and mechanical devices with it. Meccano has a factory in Calais, France. In 2013, Spin Master, a Canadian toy company, bought the Meccano brand. In 1913, a similar construction set called Erector was introduced in the United States. In 2000, Meccano bought the Erector brand and now operates in all continents.

Red is a color at the end of the light spectrum, next to orange and opposite violet. It has a wavelength of about 625 to 740 nanometers. In the RGB and CMYK color models, red is a primary color and its opposite is cyan. Reds can be bright, like scarlet and vermillion, or darker, like burgundy, and they range from pink to crimson. The first red pigment used in prehistoric art was made from ochre. Ancient Egyptians and Mayans used red in ceremonies, and Roman generals had their faces painted red after victories. In China, red was used in early pottery and later to paint palace gates and walls. During the Renaissance, nobles wore red clothes dyed with kermes and cochineal. The 19th century brought synthetic red dyes, replacing traditional ones. Red became the color of revolution, adopted by countries like Soviet Russia and China after the Bolshevik Revolution in 1917. Red is linked to blood, symbolizing sacrifice, danger, and courage. In modern surveys in Europe and the U.S., red is often associated with heat, activity, passion, sexuality, anger, love, and joy. In Asia, particularly China and India, red symbolizes happiness and good fortune.

Timothy J. Davlin was the mayor of Springfield, Illinois, from April 2003 until his suicide in December 2010. He was 53 years old. The mayor's job is supposed to be non-partisan, but in Springfield, there is a strong tradition of political parties, including in city elections. Both major parties support candidates. Davlin was backed by the Democratic Party.
José Francisco "El Nene" Sanfilippo was born on May 4, 1935. He is a former Argentine football player who played as a striker.

Leishmania is a type of trypanosome that causes leishmaniasis. These trypanosomes are spread by sandflies. In the Old World, they are mainly spread by sandflies from the genus "Phlebotomus." In the New World, they are spread by sandflies from the genus "Lutzomyia." At least 93 sandfly species worldwide can spread leishmaniasis. Their main hosts include vertebrates like hyraxes, canids, rodents, and humans.

Mycoplasma genitalium (Mgen) is a small, sexually transmitted bacterium that lives on skin cells in the urinary and genital areas. Medical reports show it is becoming more common. It can now resist many antibiotics, including azithromycin, which was once a good treatment. Mgen was first found in 1981 and was identified as a new species in 1983. It can make both men and women sick. It also makes it easier for HIV to spread, especially in men who have sex with men and those who have taken azithromycin before. It can cause urethritis in both genders and cervicitis and pelvic inflammation in women. It often shows similar symptoms to chlamydia and has higher rates in some groups than chlamydia or gonorrhea. In 1995, its complete genome was published, with 475 genes. It was once thought to have the smallest genome but was surpassed by another organism in 2003. However, it still has the smallest genome of any naturally occurring self-replicating organism. In 2008, the first organism with a synthetic genome, named Mgen JCVI-1.0, was created. In 2014, a protein called protein M from Mgen was described.

Codename: Kids Next Door – Operation: S.O.D.A. is an American platformer video game based on the animated TV show. It came out in 2004 for the Game Boy Advance.

"Mr. Know It All" is a song by American pop singer Kelly Clarkson. It was written by Brian Kennedy, Ester Dean, Brett James, and Dante Jones, and produced by Kennedy, Dean, and Jones. Clarkson called the song "vocally raw," meaning they tried to record it as it sounds in live performances with minimal auto-tune. It was the first single from her album "Stronger," released on September 5, 2011. The song is mid-tempo and has R&B influences. It talks about heartbreak and relationships with self-important people. Critics mostly liked the song, saying it was different from her previous releases. Some compared it to other songs, like Alicia Keys' "Doesn't Mean Anything" and Bruno Mars' "Just the Way You Are." "Mr. Know It All" was a hit. It was her ninth top-ten hit on the Billboard Hot 100 and the top song on the Adult Pop Songs chart. It topped charts in Australia and South Korea and reached top-ten positions in New Zealand, Poland, and the United Kingdom. It also became a country hit, entering the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart for the first time since 2002. The video for the song, directed by Justin Francis, shows a "wall of doubt" with negative headlines about Clarkson. Clarkson performed the song in many places, including at the 2011 NRL Grand Final and on various versions of "The X Factor" and her Stronger Tour.

Huáscar Inca (Quechua: "Waskar Inca", 1503–1532) was the sapa Inca, or ruler, of the Inca Empire from 1527 to 1532. He became the leader after his father, Huayna Capac, and his brother, Ninan Cuyochi, both died from smallpox while fighting near Quito.
Cléden-Poher is a commune in Finistère, which is in Brittany, in western France.

Jacques Dupont was born on June 19, 1928, and died on November 4, 2019. He was a French racing cyclist and won an Olympic gold medal in 1948. At the 1948 Summer Olympics in London, he won the 1000m time trial event. He also won a bronze medal in the team road race, with teammates José Beyaert and Alain Moineau. Dupont won the Paris–Tours race in 1951 and again in 1955. In 1955, he won Paris–Tours with a very fast speed. He completed 253 kilometers in just over 5 hours, going an average of 43.666 kilometers per hour. For this achievement, he was given the Yellow Ribbon.
UFC 152: Jones vs. Belfort was a fight event. It happened on September 22, 2012. The event took place at the Air Canada Centre in Toronto, Canada. It was a mixed martial arts pay-per-view.

A combat sport is a competitive contact sport where one-on-one fighting occurs. In many combat sports, a contestant wins by getting more points than the opponent or by stopping the opponent. Some common combat sports include mixed martial arts, boxing, wrestling, judo, and kickboxing.

The Zitter Forest is in the Eifel region, near Euskirchen in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, and in Liège, a part of Wallonia in Belgium. It lies between Hellenthal (north), Dahlem (east), Kronenburg (south), and Büllingen (west) in the North Eifel area. This forest is part of the Hohes Venn-Eifel nature park. To the north, the Eifel National Park borders it, and to the south, the Kyll River forms the border with the Schnee Eifel. The sources of the Olef, Urft, and Kyll rivers are found in the thinly populated, mostly wooded hills of the Zitter Forest, which are between 500 and 692 meters above sea level. The highest point is at Weißer Stein (692 meters), which also has ski slopes. Other hills include Bärbelkreuz (662.8 meters), Hühnerhöhe (659.9 meters), and Kamberg (637.8 meters). Many villages in the northern part of the Zitter Forest, such as Giescheid, Miescheid, Neuhaus, Ramscheid, and Udenbreth, belong to the highest parishes in Rhineland. The Zitter Forest is also home to wildcats. There's a transmission tower called Eifel-Bärbelkreuz within the forest.

Islamgarh, formerly known as Akalgarh, is a municipal committee in Mirpur district near the Mangla Dam in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. It is situated in the southern part of the Pir Panjal range, about 28 kilometers northeast of Mirpur. In 2017, it had a population of 16,651.

Midway is a town in eastern Bullock County, Alabama, United States. In 2010, the population was 499.

Grenay is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region of France. It is part of the Lens arrondissement, the Wingles canton, and the Communaupole of Lens-Liévin. In 2013, its population was 6,899. The mayor resigned on March 31, 2019, and was temporarily replaced by his first deputy, Mathieu Feutry.

The 2011 Daytona 500, the 53rd time this race was held, took place on February 20, 2011, at Daytona International Speedway in Daytona Beach, Florida. It was the first race of the 2011 NASCAR Sprint Cup season. Trevor Bayne, driving for Wood Brothers Racing, won. He became the youngest person to win the Daytona 500. Carl Edwards came in second. David Gilliland, Bobby Labonte, and Kurt Busch finished third to fifth. Bayne took the lead just before the last restart and kept it to win his first race in the cup series and Wood Brothers' fifth Daytona 500 win. The race had 16 cautions and 74 lead changes among 22 different drivers. After the race, Carl Edwards led in the drivers' championship with 42 points, one more than David Gilliland and Bobby Labonte. Ford was in the lead in the manufacturers' championship with nine points, three more than Toyota and five more than Dodge. A total of 182,000 people attended the race, and 15.6 million people watched it on television.

A flat lens has a flat shape that lets it make images without distortion. It can also have very large openings. Sometimes, "flat lens" refers to lenses that bend light in a special way, creating a negative index of refraction. Flat lenses need a refractive index close to -1 over a wide range of angles. Recently, scientists showed that flat lenses using metasurfaces are possible.

An LC circuit, also known as a resonant circuit, tank circuit, or tuned circuit, is made up of an inductor (L) and a capacitor (C) connected together. This circuit can store and release energy as it oscillates at a specific frequency, similar to a tuning fork. LC circuits are used to create signals at a particular frequency or to filter out signals at a specific frequency from a complex mix of signals. They are important in many electronic devices, especially in radios, where they are found in oscillators, filters, tuners, and mixers. An ideal LC circuit assumes no energy is lost. In reality, some energy is always lost due to the small resistance in the components and connecting wires. To minimize this loss, the resistance is kept as low as possible. While real circuits always have some loss, studying the ideal LC circuit helps us understand how it works. For circuits that include resistance, see RLC circuit.

Ottawa is the capital city of Canada. It is located on the south bank of the Ottawa River in eastern Ontario. Ottawa borders Gatineau, Quebec, and forms the core of the Ottawa–Gatineau area and the National Capital Region. In 2016, Ottawa had 934,243 people in the city and 1,323,783 in the metropolitan area, making it the fourth-largest city and fifth-largest metropolitan area in Canada. In June 2019, the city had more than one million people. Ottawa was founded in 1826 as Bytown and was officially named Ottawa in 1855. It has become the political center of Canada. Its area has grown over time through annexations and was significantly expanded in 2001. The city name "Ottawa" comes from the Algonquin word "Odawa," meaning "to trade." Ottawa has a very educated population and includes many educational, research, and cultural institutions like the National Arts Centre, the National Gallery, and several national museums.
Der er et yndigt land" is a Danish national anthem. It is commonly translated into English as "There is a lovely country.

Young Frankenstein is a 1974 American comedy horror movie. It was made by Mel Brooks and stars Gene Wilder as Dr. Frankenstein and Peter Boyle as the monster. Other actors include Teri Garr, Cloris Leachman, Marty Feldman, Madeline Kahn, Kenneth Mars, Richard Haydn, and Gene Hackman. Brooks and Wilder wrote the script. The movie makes fun of old horror films, especially the 1930s Universal Pictures versions of "Frankenstein." Many props used in the lab were created by Kenneth Strickfaden for the 1931 "Frankenstein" film. To match the feel of the older movies, Brooks shot the film in black and white and used 1930s-style titles and transitions. The music was composed by John Morris, Brooks' longtime collaborator. "Young Frankenstein" was a hit. It's number 28 on "Total Film's" list of top comedy films, number 56 on Bravo's list of funniest movies, and number 13 on the American Film Institute's list of funniest American films. It was also chosen for preservation by the U.S. National Film Registry. A stage musical was made based on the movie. Mel Brooks thought it was his best film as a writer-director, even if it wasn't the funniest.

Olaf Marschall was born on March 19, 1966. He is from Germany. Olaf Marschall played football as a forward. He is now retired and works as a football manager.

Lafayette County is a county in Wisconsin, a U.S. state. It became part of Wisconsin when the territory was formed. In 2010, it had 16, 836 people. The main city is Darlington. The county was named after Marquis de Lafayette, a French general who helped the American army in the Revolutionary War. Scenes from the 2009 movie Public Enemies were filmed at the courthouse in Darlington.
As of October 1, 2016, the city has an estimated 65,075 people. The population density is about 7,300 people per square kilometer. The city's total area is 8.89 square kilometers.

The Pharaoh hound is a hunting dog from Malta. In Maltese, it is called "gibgus-rabbus," which means "rabbit dog." It is used to hunt rabbits in Malta's rocky areas. This dog is part of a group called "spitz and primitive" by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale. It looks like other dogs from the Mediterranean region in this group, such as the Cirneco dell'Etna, the Podenco Andaluz, the Podenco Canario, the Podenco Ibicenco, and the Portuguese Podengo. It is the only Maltese dog breed recognized internationally.

Salem is the largest city in Livingston County, but the nearby unincorporated community of Leadbetter has more people.

Gianni Infantino, born on March 23, 1970, is a Swiss-Italian football administrator. He became the president of FIFA in 2016. He was elected again as FIFA president in 2019. In 2020, he joined the International Olympic Committee.

Rav Baruch Mordechai Ezrachi is a well-known rabbi. He leads the non-Hassidic Lithuanian Jews. He is the head teacher at Ateres Yisrael yeshiva in Bayit Vegan, Jerusalem. Rav Ezrachi is also part of the Degel Hatorah Moetzas Gedolei Yisrael. His brother, Rav Yitzchok Ezrachi, is the head teacher at the Mir yeshiva in Jerusalem. Rav Ezrachi is married to the daughter of Rabbi Meir Chodosh, who was the spiritual advisor at the Hebron yeshiva.

The RSA, or Royal Society for the Encouragement of Arts, Manufactures and Commerce, is a London-based British group. It was created in 1754 by William Shipley. In 1847, it got a special charter, and in 1908, King Edward VII allowed it to use "Royal" in its name. The shorter name and RSA acronym are used more often. Famous people like Charles Dickens, Benjamin Franklin, and Stephen Hawking were once members. Today, the RSA has members from 80 countries. It gives three medals: the Albert Medal, the Benjamin Franklin Medal, and the Bicentenary Medal. Notable winners include Nelson Mandela, Sir Frank Whittle, and Professor Stephen Hawking. RSA members include people who make important discoveries. The first use of the word "sustainability" in an environmental sense was recorded in their journal in 1980.

Tokyo, the capital and most populous city in Japan, is located at the head of Tokyo Bay on Japan's main island, Honshu. It is an important political and economic center, where the Emperor and the national government work. In 2019, Tokyo had about 13.9 million people. The Greater Tokyo area has over 37 million people, making it the world's largest urban area. Tokyo used to be a small fishing village called Edo. In 1603, it became a big political center when the Tokugawa family took control. By the 1700s, Edo had grown to be one of the largest cities in the world, with over a million people. After the Tokugawa shogunate ended in 1868, the capital was moved to Edo, which was renamed Tokyo, meaning "Eastern Capital." Tokyo was damaged by an earthquake in 1923 and by bombing during World War II. Starting in the 1950s, the city was rebuilt and grew quickly. Tokyo helped Japan's economy recover after the war. Since 1943, the Tokyo Metropolitan Government has managed the city. Tokyo is Japan's top business and finance center. In 2019, it hosted 36 Fortune Global 500 companies, and in 2020, it ranked third in the Global Financial Centres Index. Tokyo has held the Summer Olympics twice and hosted several G7 summits. It was also set to host the 2020 Summer Olympics, which were delayed due to the pandemic. Tokyo is a global research and development hub, with several important universities, including the University of Tokyo. Tokyo Station is a major railway hub, and the city has a big rail and subway network. Notable areas include Chiyoda, where the Imperial Palace is, Shinjuku, which is the city's administrative center, and Shibuya, a major commercial and business district.

Clarence M. Kelley was born on October 24, 1911, and died on August 5, 1997. He was an American police officer. Kelley became the second director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The Chaldean Catholic Church uses the East Syriac rite in Syriac language for its services. It is part of Syriac Christianity and is in full agreement with the Catholic Church. The church is led by the Chaldean Catholic Patriarch of Babylon. It has its headquarters in the Cathedral of Mary, Mother of Sorrows, Baghdad, Iraq, since 1950. In 2010, the church had 490,371 members, with 310,235 (63.27%) living mainly in Iraq. The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom reported that about 80% of Iraqi Christians belong to the Chaldean Catholic Church. According to the U.S. Department of State, Chaldean Catholics make up approximately 67% of Christians in Iraq. The 2019 European Asylum Support Office guidance on Iraq confirms the same information.

Jesse Lingard, born on December 15, 1992, is an English footballer. He plays as an attacking midfielder or winger for Manchester United and the England national team. Lingard has won the UEFA Europa League, FA Cup, FA Community Shield, and EFL Cup. He scored in the finals of the FA Cup, FA Community Shield, and EFL Cup. Lingard made his debut for his team when on loan at Leicester City in 2012. He also played for Birmingham City and Brighton & Hove Albion on loan during the 2013–14 season and Derby County in 2015. Lingard first played for England at the under-17 and under-21 levels. He made his senior debut in October 2016 and participated in the 2018 FIFA World Cup. In the World Cup, England reached the semi-finals and finished in fourth place.

Racewalking is a long-distance event in athletics. Unlike running, racewalkers must keep one foot on the ground at all times. Race judges check this. The events are usually held on roads or tracks, with distances from 100 kilometers. At the Olympics, there are 20 km racewalks for both men and women, and 50 km for men only, always on roads. The World Athletics Championships also includes these, plus a 50 km walk for women. The IAAF World Race Walking Cup, started in 1961, features 10 km racewalks for juniors, plus 20 and 50 km events. In the past, the IAAF World Indoor Championships had 5000 m and 3000 m racewalks, but they stopped in 1993. Top championships often include 20 km racewalking. This sport came from British long-distance walking, which developed rules in the mid-1800s. Since the mid-20th century, Russian and Chinese walkers have been very successful, with Europeans and some Latin Americans also doing well. Racewalkers take shorter steps but run at speeds similar to top 800 meters runners.

Timpani, or kettledrums, are drums in the percussion family. They have a membrane called a head stretched over a large bowl, usually made of copper. Modern timpani can be tuned quickly by skilled players using a foot-pedal. They are played with special sticks called timpani sticks. Timpani were originally military drums but became a common part of classical orchestras by the late 1700s. Today, they are used in various types of music groups, such as concert bands, marching bands, and orchestras, and even some rock bands. "Timpani" is Italian and plural; its singular form is "timpano." However, in English, they are often called kettledrums, timps, or timpani. A player of timpani is called a timpanist.

Ricardo Montaner is a singer-songwriter from Argentina and Venezuela. His first album, also named after him, was released in 1986. It was called "Ricardo Montaner." This album became number one on the Billboard Latin Pop Albums chart.

Orangeburg County is in South Carolina, U.S. In 2010, it had 92, 501 people. Orangeburg is the main city in the county. Orangeburg County was formed in 1769. It is part of the Orangeburg, SC micropolitan area and the Columbia-Orangeburg-Newberry, SC combined area. The county is in South Carolina's Midlands region. Orangeburg County has South Carolina State University, the only public four-year historically black college in the state. It also has Claflin University, the oldest historically black college in South Carolina.

Jasonville is a city in Greene County, Indiana, United States. In 2010, it had 2,222 people. It is the westernmost part of the Bloomington, Indiana, metropolitan area. It is about 15 miles closer to Terre Haute than to Bloomington.

Ganderbal is a town and a municipality committee located in the Ganderbal district. This district is part of the Jammu and Kashmir union territory in India. Ganderbal has an average elevation of 1,619 meters (5,312 feet). It is surrounded by different areas: to the south is the district Srinagar, to the north is Bandipore, to the northeast is Kargil, to the southeast is Anantnag, and to the southwest is Baramulla.
Lupsingen is a municipality in the district of Liestal, in the canton of Basel-Country, in Switzerland.
Västerfärnebo is a place in Sala municipality, Västmanland county, Sweden. It had 477 people living there in 2010.

Alejo Carpentier y Valmont, born on December 26, 1904, and died on April 24, 1980, was a Cuban writer who influenced Latin American literature. He was born in Lausanne, Switzerland, but grew up in Havana, Cuba. He strongly identified as Cuban throughout his life. Carpentier traveled a lot, especially in France and South America, where he met important cultural and artistic figures. Carpentier was interested in Latin American politics and supported revolutionary movements, like Fidel Castro's communist revolution in Cuba. He was imprisoned and went into exile because of his left-wing ideas. Carpentier knew a lot about music and wrote about it. He published a book on Cuban music called "La Música en Cuba" and used music themes in his works. He also wrote about African influences in Cuba. Carpentier is best known for his novels. He used a style called "magical realism" to explore the magical quality of Latin American history and culture. His most famous novel, "El Reino de Este Mundo" (The Kingdom of This World), from 1949, tells the story of the Haitian revolution in the late 1700s. Carpentier mixed the Baroque style with new elements from Europe and adapted Surrealist ideas to Latin American literature. His writings included information about Latin American political history, music, social problems, and art. Many younger Cuban and Latin American writers, like Lisandro Otero, Leonardo Padura, and Fernando Velázquez Medina, were influenced by his work. Carpentier died in Paris in 1980 and was buried in Havana's Colon Cemetery with other important Cuban artists and political figures.

On March 27, 2014, the United Nations General Assembly passed a resolution during its 68th session. This resolution, called 68/262, was about Ukraine's territorial integrity. It was adopted by 100 countries. The resolution said that the internationally recognized borders of Ukraine are important and that the 2014 Crimean referendum was not valid. Eleven countries voted against the resolution. Fifty-eight countries did not vote. Another 24 countries were not present when the vote happened. The resolution was proposed by Canada, Costa Rica, Germany, Lithuania, Poland, and Ukraine. Before this resolution, the United Nations Security Council had seven meetings to discuss the Crimean crisis. However, they could not agree and Russia vetoed a draft resolution.
Lavau is a commune in the Yonne department, which is in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté in central France.
Forbing is a community in Caddo Parish, Louisiana, United States. It is part of the Shreveport-Bossier City area.
Laurie Brokenshire, born in 1952 and died in 2017, was a Royal Navy officer, magician, and expert puzzle solver.

Saydabad district is in Maidan Wardak province, Afghanistan. It has a pleasant climate with hills, streams, and orchards. The district was popular for Kabul residents to visit until violence increased in the late 2000s. Saydabad city is the capital of the district. It has a population of 114,793, which is the largest in the province. The district is in the heart of the Wardak tribe area.

Nigel David Short, born on June 1, 1965, is an English chess grandmaster. He is also a columnist, coach, and commentator. Since October 2018, he has been FIDE's vice-president. Short became a grandmaster at 19. He was the world's third-ranked chess player from January 1988 to July 1989. In 1993, he played in the World Chess Championship for the first time as an English player. He played against Garry Kasparov in the 1993 World Chess Championship in London. Kasparov won with a score of 12½ to 7½.

Nicole Sinclair, born on July 26, 1968, is a British politician. She used to lead the We Demand a Referendum party. From 2009 to 2014, she was a member of the European Parliament for the West Midlands. She was elected in June 2009 as a candidate for the UK Independence Party (UKIP). However, she left the Europe of Freedom and Democracy group, where UKIP sat, because some members had extreme right-wing views. She thought these views were not good, especially as they criticized homosexuals and migrants. After leaving the group, Sinclair worked as an independent MEP from January 2010 to September 2012. During this time, she started the We Demand a Referendum party. In the 2014 elections, she lost and said on her website, "The people who work for me have spoken, and it seems I was unsuccessful in trying to be re-elected as an MEP for the West Midlands region." Sinclair was the first transgender person to be in the British Parliament.

In physics, a shock wave is a type of disturbance that travels faster than the speed of sound in the medium it moves through. Like other waves, it carries energy and can move through a medium, but it has a sudden, sharp change in pressure, temperature, and density. In supersonic flows, an expansion fan, also called a Prandtl–Meyer expansion fan, can increase the flow's expansion. This expansion wave can interact with the shock wave, causing interference. A sonic boom from a supersonic aircraft is a type of sound wave caused by this interference. Unlike solitons, which maintain their shape and energy over long distances, a shock wave's energy and speed decrease quickly as it travels. When a shock wave passes through matter, the energy is kept, but the disorder (entropy) increases. This means the matter loses some of its ability to do work and creates a drag force on supersonic objects. Shock waves are irreversible processes.

Lewis Collins was born on May 27, 1946, and died on November 27, 2013. He was an actor in films and theater. He is best known for playing the character Bodie in a British TV show called "The Professionals" from the late 1970s to the early 1980s.

Summerland, with a population of 11,615 in 2016, is a town on the west side of Okanagan Lake in British Columbia, Canada. It is between Peachland to the north and Penticton to the south. The biggest town nearby is Kelowna, which is about 97 kilometers north. Vancouver is about 322 kilometers west. Summerland is known for "bottleneck drive," a route connecting wineries.

Northeastern University (NU or NEU) is a private research university in Boston, Massachusetts. It was founded in 1898. The main campus offers undergraduate and graduate programs. There are smaller campuses in Charlotte, North Carolina; Seattle, Washington; San Jose and San Francisco, California; Toronto, Vancouver, and Portland, Maine. These smaller campuses mainly offer graduate programs. In 2019, NU bought a college in London, England. Currently, there are about 18,000 undergraduate students and 8,000 graduate students. NU is known for its "co-op" program, which mixes classroom study with real-world work. Over 3,100 companies around the world are partners. The program has been part of the university for over 100 years. Almost all undergraduate students participate, which makes their experience different from other schools. The university also has a big program for studying abroad at over 170 schools. Northeastern is a large, mainly on-campus university. Most students live on campus, but older students can live off campus. More than 76% of students get financial help. In the 2019-2020 school year, the university gave out $296.2 million in scholarships. The university's sports teams, the Huskies, play in the NCAA Division I and the Colonial Athletic Association. They compete in 18 different sports. The men's and women's hockey teams play in Hockey East, and the rowing teams in the Eastern Association of Rowing Colleges and Eastern Association of Women's Rowing Colleges. The men's track and field team won back-to-back championships in 2015 and 2016. In 2013, the men's basketball team won their first regular season championship, the men's soccer team won their first title, and the women's ice hockey team won their 16th Beanpot championship. The men's hockey team won the Beanpot three times in 2018, 2019, and 2020, beating Boston University, Boston College, and Harvard.

Esther Salas was born on December 29, 1968. She is a judge in the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey, based in Newark, New Jersey. Before becoming a district judge, she served as a United States magistrate judge from 2006 to 2011. Salas is the first Hispanic woman to hold both positions in New Jersey.

Trapani is a city and "comune" on Sicily's west coast in Italy. It is the capital of the Trapani province. Trapani was founded by Elymians and is still an important fishing port. It is also the main entrance to the nearby Egadi Islands.

Christian Karembeu, born on December 3, 1970, is a former French professional footballer. He is now a strategic advisor for Olympiacos. During his playing career, he played for Nantes, Sampdoria, Real Madrid, Middlesbrough, Olympiacos, Servette, and Bastia. Karembeu also played for France. He was born in New Caledonia, an overseas territory. He was a key player in France's 1998 FIFA World Cup win, which took place in France. He also played in one match in France's UEFA Euro 2000 tournament. He is part of a group based in Paris that wants to add a Pacific island team to the A-League.

Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was the king of Saudi Arabia and the custodian of the two holy mosques. He became king in 2005 after his half-brother King Fahd died. Like King Fahd, Abdullah was one of the many sons of Ibn Saud, who founded modern Saudi Arabia. Throughout his life, Abdullah held important jobs in politics. He became the mayor of Mecca in 1961 and later the commander of the Saudi Arabian National Guard. He was also the deputy defense minister and a crown prince. When King Fahd had a serious illness in 1995, Abdullah started ruling Saudi Arabia unofficially until he became king in 2005. During his rule, Abdullah had good relationships with the United States and the United Kingdom. He allowed women to vote and compete in the Olympics. He also kept things the same during the Arab Spring protests. In 2013, a BBC report said that Saudi Arabia could get nuclear weapons from Pakistan. Abdullah's half-brother Sultan bin Abdulaziz died in October 2011, and Interior Minister Nayef bin Abdulaziz was named the new heir. However, Nayef died in June 2012. Abdullah then chose 76-year-old Defense Minister Salman bin Abdulaziz as his heir. Abdullah married many times and had more than 30 children. He was worth about $18 billion, making him the third-wealthiest leader in the world. Abdullah passed away in January 2015 due to pneumonia, and his half-brother Salman became the new king.

A community is a group of people who share common things like rules, beliefs, and values. They might live in the same area, like a town or neighborhood, or connect through talking online. People in a community often have strong ties that go beyond just family relationships. These ties help them work together in places like families, homes, jobs, and governments. While a community usually means a smaller group compared to personal relationships, it can also mean larger groups like countries or groups connected online. The word "community" comes from Latin and means sharing common things. People in a community often share goals, beliefs, and worries, which helps them feel connected.
Laigné was a small town in the Mayenne department of northwest France. On January 1, 2018, Laigné joined with Prée-d'Anjou to form a new town.

Shaw is a city in Bolivar and Sunflower counties, Mississippi, United States. It is in the Mississippi Delta region. The name came from an old Indian tribe to the northeast. In 2010, the population was 1,952.

Cantabria is an autonomous community in northern Spain, with its capital city being Santander. It is known as a historic community. Cantabria is bordered on the east by the Basque Autonomous Community (Province of Biscay), on the south by Castile and León (Provinces of León, Palencia, and Burgos), on the west by the Principality of Asturias, and on the north by the Cantabrian Sea (Bay of Biscay). Cantabria is part of "Green Spain," a region between the Bay of Biscay and the Cantabrian Mountains. This area has lots of plants due to its wet and mild ocean climate. The climate is heavily influenced by winds from the Atlantic Ocean, which are held back by the mountains. On average, it gets about 2,000 millimeters of rain each year. Archaeological sites from the Upper Paleolithic period can be found in Cantabria. The most famous site for cave paintings is the Altamira Cave, which dates back to around 37,000 BC. This cave, along with nine other Cantabrian caves, was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cantabria's modern province was created on July 28, 1778, in Puente San Miguel, Reocín. This date is celebrated annually as the Provincial Institutions Day on July 28. The Organic Law of the Autonomy Statute of Cantabria was approved on December 30, 1981, which gave the region its own self-governing institutions.

James John Benzelock was born on June 21, 1947. He played as a right winger in ice hockey. He was chosen in the first round, fifth overall, by the Minnesota North Stars in the 1968 NHL amateur draft. He never played in the National Hockey League. However, he played in 166 games in the World Hockey Association with the Alberta Oilers, Chicago Cougars, and Quebec Nordiques. Benzelock mostly played for teams in minor professional leagues like the CHL, IHL, and Nahl.

Imperia Tower is a complex in Moscow, Russia, located on plot 4 of the Moscow International Business Center. The complex has two buildings: a 60-story skyscraper and a 14-story building that is being constructed. The skyscraper is complete. It started being built between 2001 and 2002, stopped in 2003, and then resumed in 2006. It was finished in 2011. The 14-story building began construction in 2013 and is expected to be completed by 2018.

Chess was an American record company started in 1950 in Chicago. They focused on blues and rhythm and blues music. Over time, they added soul, gospel, early rock and roll, and some jazz and comedy recordings. They released music on the Chess label and its subsidiary labels Checker, Argo/Cadet, and Cadet Concept. Universal Music Group now owns Chess's entire catalogue and manages it through Geffen Records. Leonard and Phil Chess, Jewish immigrant brothers from Poland, founded and ran the company. They produced and released many important singles and albums. Musician and critic Cub Koda called Chess "America's greatest blues label." Chess was based in several locations on Chicago's South Side. Their most famous location was 2120 S. Michigan Avenue from 1957 to 1965. The Rolling Stones recorded there in 1964, and later in 1965 and 1968. This building, officially named Ter-Mar Studios, was commonly known as Chess Studios. It is now home to Willie Dixon's Blues Heaven Foundation. In the mid-1960s, Chess moved to a bigger building at 320 E. 21st Street, which used to be Revere Camera Company. Leonard Chess died in 1969, and the brothers sold the company shortly before his passing.
Raspberry is a color like the color of raspberries. The word "raspberry" as a color name was first used in English in 1892. A book about the "raspberry" color was published in 2018 by Coloratura.

Chondrostei is a group of fish that have some bones but mostly cartilage. Their ancestors were bony fish with fully formed bones. These fish share some features with elasmobranchs, like having spiracles, a tail that is not symmetrical, and no scales. However, the fossil record suggests they are more similar to teleosts. The living chondrostei fish are divided into two groups: sturgeons and paddlefishes, and reedfishes and bichirs.

Retalhuleu is a department in southwestern Guatemala, stretching from the mountains to the Pacific Ocean. It covers an area of 1,856 square kilometers. In 2018, the department had 326,828 people. The capital is the city of Retalhuleu. The K'iche' Maya people are the largest native group. The department has some ancient ruins, like Takalik Abaj.

Typesetting involves arranging physical letters or digital equivalents to create text. In mechanical systems, letters are called sorts, while in digital systems, they are called glyphs. These are arranged based on a language's writing rules for display. Typesetting needs one or more fonts, which are often mistakenly called typefaces. A major effect of typesetting was that it became easier to recognize who wrote a work, making it harder for people who copied without permission.

"Color of Night" is a 1994 American erotic mystery movie. It was made by Cinergi Pictures and released in the U.S. by Hollywood Pictures. The director is Richard Rush, and Bruce Willis and Jane March are the main actors. Other actors include Ruben Blades, Lesley Ann Warren, Brad Dourif, Lance Henriksen, Kevin J. O’Connor, and Scott Bakula. This is one of two famous films directed by Rush, the other being "The Stunt Man," which came out 14 years earlier. The movie did not do well at the box office and won a Golden Raspberry Award as the worst film of 1994. However, it became one of the 20 most-rented films in the U.S. home video market in 1995. "Maxim" magazine said it had the best sex scene in film history. In 2018, Kino Lorber (with Disney’s permission) released a special edition Blu-ray of the film, which includes an audio commentary by director Richard Rush.
Stora Vika is a small place in Nynäshamn municipality, in Stockholm county, Sweden. It had 651 people living there in 2010.

Marie Eugène François Thomas Dubois lived from January 28, 1858, to December 16, 1940. He was a Dutch paleoanthropologist and geologist. Dubois became famous for finding "Pithecanthropus erectus," later called "Homo erectus," or "Java Man." Before Dubois, other fossils had been found, but he was the first to look for them on purpose.

Charles Frederick "Karch" Kiraly, born on November 3, 1960, is an American volleyball player, coach, and broadcaster. In the 1980s, he was a key player for the U.S. national team, winning gold medals at the 1984 and 1988 Olympic Games. He also won a gold medal at the 1996 Olympic Games, which was the first to include beach volleyball. Kiraly is the only person, male or female, to win Olympic gold medals in both indoor and beach volleyball. He played volleyball in college for UCLA, where his teams won three national championships under Coach Al Scates. Currently, Kiraly coaches the United States women's national volleyball team.

Snap! is a German eurodance group formed in 1989. It was created by producers Michael Münzing and Luca Anzilotti. The group has had many changes in its lineup over the years, including American singers, songwriters, and rappers like Thea Austin, Turbo B, and Penny Ford. Their most famous songs are "The Power" and "Rhythm Is a Dancer." Both of these songs reached number one in many countries.

Glass frogs belong to the centrolenidae family of frogs, which are part of the order anura. Most glass frogs are green, but some have transparent skin on their bellies. You can see their insides, like their heart and stomach, through this skin. This is why they are called glass frogs. Glass frogs live mainly in trees and only come down during mating season.

Benthos refers to the community of organisms living on, in, or near the ocean, river, lake, or stream bottom. These organisms live in marine or freshwater environments, from tidal pools to the continental shelf and deep into the abyss. Many deep-sea creatures cannot survive in the upper water parts due to high pressure. Pressure increases about one atmosphere for every 10 meters of water depth. Deep ocean benthic ecosystems get their energy from organic matter drifting down from above. Most benthic zone organisms are scavengers or feed on decaying matter. The term "benthos" was created by Haeckel in 1891. It comes from the Greek word meaning "depth of the sea." In freshwater biology, "benthos" means organisms at the bottom of lakes, rivers, and streams. The term "benthon" is sometimes used but is unnecessary.

Monday is the day between Sunday and Tuesday. In many countries, it is considered the first day of the week. According to ISO 8601, Monday is the first day. In some countries that follow a "Sunday-first" convention, Monday is the second day. The name "Monday" comes from Old English "mōnandæg" and Middle English "monenday." This name originally meant "day of the moon."

Development started in 1994 for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System. Square faced delays and technical issues while testing real-time rendering platforms, so they switched to pre-rendered video. This change required more space, leading them to leave Nintendo for the PlayStation. Veteran "Final Fantasy" team members, including Hironobu Sakaguchi, Yoshinori Kitase, and Nobuo Uematsu, returned. "Final Fantasy VII" was the first game in the series to use full-motion video and 3D computer graphics, with 3D character models on 2D backgrounds. It introduced science fiction elements, a more realistic look, and new features like materia, limit breaks, and mini-games. The large team had a big budget for development and marketing. Supported by a big promotion, "Final Fantasy VII" was both a commercial and critical success. It is considered a landmark game, one of the most influential and greatest of all time. It won many game of the year awards and helped sell more PlayStation systems. People praised its graphics, gameplay, music, and story, but criticized the English version. Its success led to better versions on other devices, a multimedia sub-series, and a high-definition remake that started in 2020.

Melide is a town in the Lugano district of Ticino, Switzerland. It is near Monte San Salvatore mountain and sits right next to Lake Lugano. To the east, the Melide causeway was built so people could go to Bissone. It also allowed a north-south highway to be constructed. Melide is famous for the Swissminiatur museum, which shows tiny versions of famous Swiss buildings.

Ullared is a small town in Falkenberg municipality, Halland county, Sweden. In 2010, it had 791 people living there. Ullared has a big department store called Gekås. This store is the largest in Sweden and Scandinavia. Its low prices have made Ullared known as a place with good deals. Many stores, mostly with lower prices, have opened in Ullared since the early 1990s.

The Durrells, known as The Durrells in Corfu in North America, is a 26-episode British comedy-drama series. It is based on Gerald Durrell's three autobiographical books about his family's time on the Greek island of Corfu from 1935 to 1939. The series began airing on April 3, 2016, and ended on May 12, 2019. Simon Nye wrote the series, and Steve Barron and Roger Goldby directed it. Christopher Hall produced it, and Lee Morris and Sally Woodward Gentle were the executive producers. Lee Durrell, the widow of Gerald Durrell and director of the Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust, acted as a consultant. Some filming took place at Ealing Studios and Twickenham Studios in London.

Reading Rainbow was a 30-minute educational TV show for kids that started on PBS Kids on July 11, 1983, and ended on August 28, 2009. It had 155 episodes over 21 seasons. The show encouraged kids to read and featured topics from children's books. It ended on November 10, 2006, but reruns continued until 2009. In 2012, an app with the same name was released for iPads and Kindle Fire, offering interactive book reading and video field trips. The show won many awards, including Peabody and Emmy awards. Reading Rainbow was created by Twila Liggett and her partners at Lancit Media Productions. Each episode explored a book's topic through segments. It was one of the longest-running kids' shows on PBS after "Sesame Street" and "Mister Rogers' Neighborhood." In 2013, it celebrated its 30th anniversary. A Kickstarter campaign in 2014 raised $5.4 million to make the app available on more devices and provide free access to 13,000 disadvantaged classrooms.

Paul Anthony Samuelson was an American economist born on May 15, 1915, and died on December 13, 2009. He won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1970. The Swedish Royal Academy said he raised the level of scientific analysis in economic theory more than any other economist of his time. Samuelson was seen as the top academic economist of the 20th century. He was highly influential in the latter part of the 20th century. President Bill Clinton awarded him the National Medal of Science in 1996, America's top science honor, for his work over 60 years. Samuelson thought math was the language of economics and wrote a book called "Foundations of Economic Analysis." His best-selling book, "Economics: An Introductory Analysis," was published in 1948 and is now in its 19th edition, sold in 40 languages. MIT's former head of the department of economics, James Poterba, said Samuelson's book left a great legacy, as a researcher and teacher. Samuelson joined the University of Chicago at 16 during the Great Depression and got his PhD from Harvard. At 25, he became an assistant professor at MIT and a full professor at 32. In 1966, he became MIT's highest faculty honor, the Institute Professor. He helped MIT's economics department become a top institution by bringing in other famous economists. Samuelson advised presidents John F. Kennedy and Lyndon B. Johnson and worked for the U.S. Treasury and other economic groups. He wrote a weekly column for Newsweek with Milton Friedman, where they discussed opposing economic ideas. Their columns won the magazine an award.

Richard Benaud, born on October 6, 1930, and who passed away on April 10, 2015, was an Australian cricketer. After retiring from international cricket in 1964, he became a well-known commentator. Benaud was a test cricket all-rounder, combining leg spin bowling with aggressive batting. He worked with another bowler all-rounder, Alan Davidson, to help Australia return to the top of world cricket in the late 1950s and early 1960s. In 1958, he became Australia's test captain, serving until 1964. Benaud was the first player to reach 200 wickets and 2,000 runs in test cricket, achieving this milestone in 1963. Cricket writer Gideon Haigh said Benaud was "perhaps the most influential cricketer and personality since World War II." In his review of Benaud's autobiography "Anything But," Sri Lankan cricket writer Harold de Andrado described Benaud as "possibly next to Sir Donald Bradman, one of the greatest cricketing personalities as a player, researcher, writer, critic, author, organizer, adviser, and student of the game."

"The Loud House" is an American animated comedy show. It started on Nickelodeon on May 2, 2016. The show is about Lincoln Loud. He is the only boy and the middle child in a family of girls. Lincoln often talks directly to viewers to explain the messy and funny situations at home and how his siblings get along.

Most old Japanese provinces had one or more "ichinomiya." These "ichinomiya" shrines gave rise to place names, like the city of Ichinomiya in Aichi. Shrines of a lower rank are called "ninomiya" (second), "sannomiya" (third), "shinomiya" (fourth), and so on.

Jed Allan Brown, born on March 1, 1935, and known professionally as Jed Allan, was an American actor and TV host. He was famous for his roles as C.C. Capwell in "Santa Barbara," Don Craig in "Days of Our Lives," Rush Sanders in "Beverly Hills, 90210," Scott Turner in "Lassie," and Harold Johnson in "The Bay." He also hosted "Celebrity Bowling." He passed away on March 9, 2019.

Gliese 667Cc, also called GJ 667Cc, HR 6426Cc, or HD 156384Cc, is an exoplanet in the habitable zone of the red dwarf star Gliese 667C. Gliese 667C is part of a triple star system. Gliese 667Cc is about 23.62 light-years away, which is roughly 6.8 parsecs or 217 billion kilometers in the constellation Scorpius. This exoplanet was found using the radial velocity method. Scientists found it by looking at changes in the spectrum of the star, caused by the star's movement due to the planet's gravitational pull.
Neumarkt is a "landkreis" (district) in Bavaria, Germany. It borders several districts: Nürnberger Land, Amberg-Sulzbach, Schwandorf, Regensburg, Kelheim, Eichstätt, and Roth.

Caryophyllaceae, also known as the pink family or carnation family, is a group of flowering plants. This family, part of the dicotyledon order called Caryophyllales, includes 33 other families such as amaranthaceae, cactaceae, and polygonaceae. Caryophyllaceae is a large family, with about 81 genera and 2,625 species. Most plants in this family are herbaceous and grow best in temperate climates, though some species are found on tropical mountains. Common examples include pinks and carnations, firepink, and campions. Many of these plants are grown as ornamental plants, and some are considered weeds. Most species are found in the Mediterranean region and surrounding areas of Europe and Asia. In the southern hemisphere, the number of genera and species is smaller, but the family includes Colobanthus quitensis, an Antarctic plant that is one of only two flowering plants found in Antarctica. The name "Caryophyllaceae" comes from "caryophyllus," an old name for "dianthus."

Terrel Howard Bell was the secretary of education under President Ronald Reagan. He served as the second secretary of education, after Shirley Hufstedler. He was born on November 11, 1921, and died on June 22, 1996.

Oberstrass is a quarter in district 6 of Zürich. It used to be its own municipality but became part of Zürich in 1893. The quarter has 9,494 people living there. Oberstrass covers a small area. It has one of two funiculars in the city of Zürich, called the Rigiblick funicular. This funicular was first built in 1901 as a restaurant. Later, in 1984, it was turned into a theater called Theater Rigiblick.

Hemphill is a city in Sabine County, Texas, United States. It had 1,198 people in 2010. Hemphill is the county seat. It is on State Highway 87 where State Highway 184 meets. Hemphill is surrounded by the Sabine National Forest and Toledo Bend Reservoir.

Carla Ragin Bozulich, born on December 24, 1965, is an American musician from Los Angeles. She is known as the lead singer, lyricist, and founder of the Geraldine Fibbers and Evangelista. She was also a founding member of Ethyl Meatplow and Scarnella. The Geraldine Fibbers recorded two albums for Virgin Records. Their first album, "Lost Somewhere Between the Earth and My Home," was called "a country feedback masterpiece" by Vice. Bozulich started her Evangelista project in 2006. The album was released under her own name and called "Evangelista." It was from Montreal, Quebec's Constellation Records and was the first release by a non-Canadian artist. In 2007, The Sunday Times praised "Evangelista," saying it was "a vivid inner darkness which shames rock's weeping millionaires." Bozulich used the name Evangelista for albums "Hello, Voyager" (2008), "Prince of Truth" (2009), and "In Animal Tongue" (2011). Some regular members include Tara Barnes (bassist), Dominic Cramp (keyboardist/sampler), Nels Cline (guitarist), Jessica Moss (violinist), Nadia Moss (organist), Ches Smith (drummer), and a multi-instrumentalist and co-producer. Musicians from Godspeed! You Black Emperor helped with arranging, recording, and writing songs. The line-up for Evangelista changes each time they play or record. The "Hello, Voyager" album featured 14 musicians. In 2014, Constellation released "Boy," a solo album by Bozulich. Her most recent album, "Quieter," was released in May 2018 and collected previously unreleased recordings. Bozulich has also worked on other projects, including collaborations with Francesco Guerri, Novariant/Sarah Lipstate, and Devin Sarno.
Arkelstorp is a small place in Kristianstad municipality, Skåne county, Sweden. In December 2010, it had 768 people living there.
