A leaf blower, also called a blower, is a tool used in gardening. It blows air out of a nozzle to move things like leaves and grass cuttings. Leaf blowers can be powered by electricity or gasoline. Some old gasoline models use two-stroke engines, but newer ones use four-stroke engines to help reduce air pollution. Leaf blowers are usually small, handheld devices or backpack units with a wand. The backpack models are easier to use for long periods. Larger models might have wheels and use a motor for movement. They are sometimes called "walk behind leaf blowers" because they are pushed while being used. Some units can also suck in leaves and small twigs with a vacuum, then shred and collect them in a bag. In this case, they are known as blower vacs.

Sheyi Emmanuel Adebayor, born on February 26, 1984, is a professional footballer from Togo. He plays as a striker. He has played for several clubs, including Arsenal, Manchester City, Tottenham Hotspur, and Crystal Palace in England. He also played for Metz in France, Monaco, Real Madrid in Spain, and Istanbul Başakşehir and Kayserispor in Turkey. Additionally, he played for Olimpia Asunción in Paraguay. In 2008, while playing for Arsenal, he was voted African Footballer of the Year. In his later career, he became the most famous player and the highest-paid in Paraguay when he joined Olimpia Asunción in 2020. Adebayor played for Togo in the 2006 FIFA World Cup in Germany. It was Togo's first and so far only appearance in the World Cup. In January 2010, during the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations in Angola, his team's bus was shot at, and he retired from playing for the national team. In 2013, he returned to the Togo team for the 2013 African Cup of Nations in South Africa, helping them reach the quarter-finals. Currently, he is Togo's top goalscorer with 32 goals.

Andrzej Wojciech Suski, born on December 24, 1941, is a retired Polish Roman Catholic prelate. He was born in Płock. Suski became a priest in 1965. From 1986 to 1992, he worked as an auxiliary bishop in Płock. Then, he became the bishop of Toruń. He retired in November 2017.

RMJM, led by Robert Matthew Johnson Marshall, is a large architecture and design company. They offer services like architecture, development management, engineering, interior and landscape design, urban design, and consultancy. RMJM works with many types of clients, including mixed-use, education, healthcare, energy, residential, government, and hospitality sectors. Specialized services are available through divisions like RMJM Sport, RMJM Healthcare, RMJM DX, and RMJM PIM. RMJM was started in 1956 by architects Robert Matthew and Stirrat Johnson-Marshall. Their first offices were in London and Edinburgh. Since its start, RMJM has supported modern and contemporary architecture inspired by global cultures.

Herbert Eser "Herb" Gray was a Canadian politician. He was a Member of Parliament for Windsor West from 1962 to 2002, making him the longest-serving member of parliament in Canadian history. Gray also worked as a cabinet minister under three prime ministers and was Deputy Prime Minister from 1997 to 2002. He was Canada's first Jewish federal cabinet minister. Gray was one of the few Canadians honored with the title "The Right Honourable," but not because of his position.
Bodcaw is a town in Nevada County, Arkansas, United States. The 2000 census showed it had 154 people. It is part of the Hope micropolitan statistical area.
Serres-Morlaàs is a town in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, which is in southwestern France.

Pauline Hanson's One Nation, also called One Nation or One Nation Party, is an Australian political party. It was created in 1997 by Pauline Hanson and her advisors David Ettridge and David Oldfield after Hanson was no longer chosen as a candidate for the Liberal Party. This happened before the 1996 election because of things she said about Aboriginal Australians. Before forming One Nation, Hanson was an independent for a year. One Nation candidates have never been elected to the House of Representatives, but they did win a Senate seat in 1998 and four in 2016. In state politics, One Nation did better. In the 1998 Queensland election, they got over 22% of the vote and won 11 out of 89 seats. In 2016, the party got 4.3% of the vote nationally and 9.2% in Queensland. Hanson, Roberts, Burston, and Culleton were elected to the Senate. Culleton lost his seat in 2017 due to bankruptcy and a criminal conviction. A court replaced him with Peter Georgiou. Mark Latham, a former Labor leader, joined One Nation in 2018 as New South Wales leader. He won a Legislative Council seat in 2019. One Nation has a strong nationalist platform. Hanson and other members say the party is not racist. Hanson said criticism is not racism; real racism is when people get help just because of their skin color. A 2001 study showed One Nation has no official ties to racist groups but has informal ties due to shared interests. These include the League of Rights, Australians Against Further Immigration, the Confederate Action Party, and some militia groups. Members of a militant white supremacist group, True Blue Crew, were linked to One Nation candidate Nikhil Reddy.

Interstate 69 (I-69) is a highway in the United States. Currently, it is made up of ten separate parts. The original continuous part runs from Indianapolis, Indiana, to Port Huron, Michigan, on the Canada–US border. Other parts extend southwest to the Mexican border in Texas. Five segments, including areas near Corpus Christi, Houston, Mississippi, Memphis, and Evansville, have been built or upgraded. In Kentucky, a new section uses existing parkways and a part of I-24. This brings the total length to about 1,200 miles. I-69 was chosen in 2007 as one of six key routes by the US Department of Transportation. This made it eligible for extra federal money and quicker planning. However, funding was later stopped, leading some states to pause construction indefinitely. The proposed extension combines old highway corridors 18 and 20. It also includes connections to existing infrastructure like I-94 between Chicago and Port Huron, and various other routes. These include extending I-530 in Arkansas, upgrading US Route 59 in Texas, and adding new routes in southern Texas to serve border crossings in Laredo, Pharr, and Brownsville.

An observation deck is a raised platform for viewing. It is usually on a tall building like a skyscraper or an observation tower. Sometimes, it is protected from the weather. Some decks also have coin-operated telescopes for seeing distant things.

Khufu, also known as Cheops to ancient Greeks, was a king of ancient Egypt. He was the second ruler of the Fourth Dynasty, during the Old Kingdom period around 2600 BC. Khufu became king after his father, Sneferu. He is famous for building the Great Pyramid of Giza, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. However, not much is known about his reign. The only clear image of him is a small ivory figurine found at Abydos in 1903. Most other pictures and statues were found in pieces, and many of his buildings are gone. We mostly know about Khufu from inscriptions in his burial complex and some later writings. For example, he is mentioned in the Westcar Papyrus from the 13th Dynasty. The ancient historians Manetho, Diodorus, and Herodotus wrote about Khufu around 300 BC, giving him a negative image. Thanks to these documents, Khufu is remembered as an unclear and criticized figure.

Selena etc. was a boutique, salon, and clothing store in South Texas. Founded by the famous Latin singer Selena, it opened on January 27, 1994, in Corpus Christi. Selena also opened another boutique in San Antonio around the same time. Both stores had in-house beauty salons. Selena and designer Martin Gomez created Latin American-style clothing. These boutiques earned Selena over $5 million, according to Hispanic Business Magazine. Another store planned for Monterrey, Mexico, was never opened due to Selena's murder. The San Antonio boutique closed around 1999. After Selena's death, her husband Chris Pérez took over the business. The Corpus Christi store closed in July 2009, 16 years after opening. Chris Pérez sold the store for $165,000. The Selena etc. store had a full-service salon and sold Selena's memorabilia, jewelry, hats, and accessories. All items were later sold at the Selena Museum.

Cardi B, born Belcalis Marlenis Almánzar on October 11, 1992, is an American rapper, songwriter, TV personality, and actress. She grew up in New York City, in Manhattan and the Bronx. Cardi B became famous online after her videos went viral on Vine and Instagram. From 2015 to 2017, she was on a TV show called "Love & Hip Hop" where she tried to become a rapper. She released two mixtapes, "Gangsta Bitch Music, Vol. 1" and "Vol. 2." In early 2017, she joined a record label called Atlantic Records. Her first big album, "Invasion of Privacy," came out in 2018 and was very successful. It was the number-one album on the Billboard 200 chart, broke streaming records, and was named the best female rap album of the 2010s. The album won the Grammy Award for Best Rap Album, and Cardi B was the first woman to win this award alone. It also had two number-one songs on the Billboard Hot 100: "Bodak Yellow" and "I Like It." Her collaboration with Maroon 5, "Girls Like You," topped the chart too. The song "Wap" from her second album was a hit, making Cardi B the first female rapper to top the chart in two different decades. Cardi B is recognized as one of the most influential female rappers. She is known for her strong style and honest songs. She has won many awards, including a Grammy, Billboard Music Awards, Guinness World Records, and ASCAP Songwriter of the Year awards. In 2018, she was named one of the 100 most influential people in the world by Time magazine.
Gothenburg Cathedral is in Gothenburg, Sweden's second-largest city. It is where the bishop of the Gothenburg diocese works in the Church of Sweden.
William Thomas Hart was born on February 4, 1929. He is a judge in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.

Kahuta tehsil is one of eight subdivisions in the Rawalpindi district of Punjab, Pakistan. Kallar Sayedan used to be part of Kahuta but became a separate tehsil later. The name Kahuta comes from "koh," a local medicinal tree (with leaves similar to olive), and "boota." Over time, "koh boota" may have been shortened to Kahuta.

Richard John Hadlee, born on July 3, 1951, is a former New Zealand cricketer. He is considered one of the best fast bowlers and all-rounders in cricket history. Hadlee received an MBE in 1980 and was knighted in 1990 for his contributions to cricket. He once led the New Zealand selectors. In December 2002, Wisden ranked him as the second-best test bowler of all time. In March 2009, Hadlee was honored as one of the twelve local heroes, with a bronze bust unveiled outside the Christchurch Arts Centre. On April 3, 2009, Hadlee was inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame. Richard Hadlee is the most famous player in the Hadlee cricket family.

Japan surrendered on August 15, 1945, after Emperor Hirohito announced it. The formal surrender happened on September 2, 1945. By July 1945, Japan's navy could not fight anymore, and an Allied invasion was likely. In July 1945, the United States, Britain, and China asked Japan to surrender. Japan's leaders secretly asked the Soviet Union to help in peace talks. The Soviet Union was ready to attack Japanese forces in Manchuria and Korea, as agreed with the United States and Britain. On August 6, 1945, the United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima. The next day, the U.S. asked Japan to surrender again. On August 8, 1945, the Soviet Union declared war on Japan and invaded Manchuria. The next day, the United States dropped a second atomic bomb on Nagasaki. Emperor Hirohito then ordered Japan to surrender. On August 15, 1945, he made a radio announcement to the Japanese people. On September 2, 1945, the Japanese signed the surrender document on a U.S. battleship. V-J Day, celebrating the end of World War II, was marked. However, some Japanese soldiers in other parts of Asia and the Pacific did not surrender until much later. The war ended officially in 1952, and relations with the Soviet Union were normalized in 1956.

Kathleen Rachel Makinson, born White, was born on February 15, 1917, and died on October 18, 2014. She was an Australian physicist. Makinson was the first woman to become a chief research scientist at CSIRO, Australia's research organization.

Heian-kyō was one of the names for the city now called Kyoto. It was Japan's capital for over 1,000 years, from 794 to 1868, with a brief break in 1180. Emperor Kanmu made Heian-kyō the capital in 794, after getting advice from Wake no Kiyomaro. This move marked the start of the Heian period in Japanese history. Heian-kyō was modeled after the Chinese capital Chang'an (now Xi'an). The city was the main political center until 1185, when the samurai clan led by Minamoto defeated the Taira clan in the Genpei War. After this, national affairs were managed from Kamakura, and the Kamakura Shogunate was established. Even though the samurai controlled the government for three shogunates, Heian-kyō remained the place of the imperial court and the seat of power, so it kept being the official capital. Even after the imperial court moved to Tokyo in 1868, some people think Kyoto is still the official capital because there is no law saying Tokyo is the capital. In 1994, Kyoto city celebrated its 1,200th anniversary with various events.

The globe artichoke, also called French artichoke or green artichoke in the U.S., is a type of thistle grown for food. People eat the flower buds before the flowers open. These buds are many small flowers and bracts on an edible base. Once the buds bloom, the plant becomes tough and not very tasty. Another type, cardoon, is also a species of thistle native to the Mediterranean. Wild and cultivated forms of both plants exist.

Sportverein Grödig is an Austrian football club from Grödig. They play in the Austrian Regional League West, which is the third level of Austrian football. Grödig were moved from the Austrian Bundesliga at the end of the 2015–16 season. They went down two levels to the Austrian Regional League West because of money problems.

Singapore started sending athletes to most summer Olympics after 1948. In 1948, Singapore became a separate British colony just before the Olympics. They kept sending teams until 1964, when Singapore was part of Malaysia, which sent a combined team. After becoming fully independent in 1965, Singapore continued to join the summer Olympics except in 1980, when they joined a boycott. Singapore first joined the winter Olympics in 2018, with Cheyenne Goh competing in short track speed skating. They have won five Olympic medals in total: one in 1960, one in 2008, two in 2012, and a gold in 2016.

Donnal Alan Pennebaker, often known as D.A. Pennebaker, was an American documentary filmmaker who lived from July 15, 1925, to August 1, 2019. He made films about performing arts and politics. He was one of the first people to use direct cinema. In 2013, he was given an Academy Honorary Award by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Pennebaker is considered one of the best people to document the counterculture of the 1960s.

Pullman is the biggest city in Whitman County, in southeastern Washington State, within the Palouse region of the Pacific Northwest. In 2010, it had 29,799 people, and in 2019, it was estimated to have 34,506. The city was originally called Three Forks but was renamed Pullman in 1884 after industrialist George Pullman. Known for its rich farmland, Pullman has many rolling hills and grows wheat and legumes. It is also home to Washington State University, a public university that does research. The city has Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories' main office. Pullman is close to Moscow, Idaho, where the University of Idaho is located. People can use the Pullman-Moscow Regional Airport to travel.

International Left Handers Day is celebrated on August 13 each year. The day honors left-handed people and was first observed in 1976 by Dean R. Campbell. It aims to celebrate being left-handed and raise awareness about the challenges and advantages of being left-handed in a right-handed world. The day highlights that about 7 to 10 percent of the world's population is left-handed. It also brings attention to issues faced by left-handers, such as special needs for left-handed children, and the higher chance of developing schizophrenia. There are roughly 708 million left-handed people globally. More men are left-handed than women. In the past, left-handers were forced to use their right hands. Former U.S. President Harry S. Truman used to write with his left hand but was made to write with his right hand by his parents. On International Left Handers Day, we can help raise awareness of the difficulties left-handers face.

Bayzo was born on April 3, 1947, in St. Paul's Bay, Malta. He died on February 1, 2018. Bayzo was a singer known for his special voice and for a song called "Qalu Li Raw." This song was performed at the Malta Song Festival in 1986.

Jiang Yi-huah, born on November 18, 1960, is a Taiwanese politician. He was once the premier of the Republic of China. On November 29, 2014, he resigned, and Mao Chi-kuo took over on December 8, 2014. Before becoming premier, Jiang was the vice premier from 2012 to 2013. He was minister of the interior from 2009 to 2012. From 2008 to 2009, he worked as minister of the Research, Development, and Evaluation Commission in the executive yuan.

Iran is divided into thirty-one provinces. Each province has a local center, usually the largest city, called the capital (Persian: “markaz”). The governor-general (Persian: “ostāndār”) leads each province. This governor-general is chosen by the minister of the interior and needs approval from the cabinet.

Voltage, also known as electric potential difference or electric pressure, is the difference in electric potential between two points. In a static electric field, it is the work needed to move a test charge between these two points. In the International System of Units (SI), voltage (potential difference) is measured in volts. The unit of voltage is expressed as joules per coulomb, where 1 volt equals 1 joule per coulomb. Since 1990, voltage is defined using the quantum Hall and Josephson effects, and in 2019, fundamental physical constants were used for defining all SI units and derived units, including voltage. Voltage or electric potential difference is denoted by "V" or "U" in circuit laws like Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws. Voltage differences between points can be caused by electric charge, electric current through a magnetic field, time-varying magnetic fields, or a combination of these. A voltmeter measures the voltage (potential difference) between two points in a system, often using ground as one of the points. Voltage can represent a source of energy (electromotive force) or energy that is lost, used, or stored.

Wisconsin's 8th congressional district is in the northeastern part of the state. Currently, it is represented by Mike Gallagher, a Republican. Gallagher won the seat in 2016 when Reid Ribble left. It is also known for electing a Catholic priest, Robert John Cornell, as a representative. For many years, the district voted for Republicans. Only four Democrats represented it in the 20th century. However, it became more competitive in the 1990s. In 2004, George W. Bush got 55% of the votes, but in 2008, Barack Obama won with 53.6%. Steve Kagen, a Democrat, was the last to represent this district from 2007 to 2011. Republicans have won the seat since then, getting over 10% more votes than Democrats in each election since 2012. The district includes Green Bay, Appleton, Door County, and most of the counties bordering Michigan since 2010.

Merced County is in the northern San Joaquin Valley of California. The 2010 census showed a population of 255,793. The county seat is Merced. The county is named after the Merced River. Merced County is part of the Merced, CA metropolitan area, which is part of the Modesto-Merced, CA combined statistical area. It is north of Fresno County and Fresno, and southeast of Santa Clara County and San Jose.

Fish processing involves handling and preparing fish from when they are caught until they reach the customer. This term usually refers to fish, but it also covers other aquatic animals harvested for sale. Big fish processing companies may have their own fishing or farming operations. Their products go to grocery stores or middlemen. Fish can go bad quickly, so a key part of processing is keeping them fresh. This is important throughout other processing steps too. Fish processing can be split into two main parts: first, preliminary processing of raw fish, and second, making fish products like frozen or canned goods. People have been processing fish for a long time. Now, it happens on fishing boats or in fish processing plants.

Lars Mortimer was born on March 22, 1946, and died on August 25, 2014, at the age of 68 in Alfta, Hälsingland. He was a Swedish comic artist who created many comic strips. Some of his works include "Bobo" and "Hälge." Mortimer passed away after a short illness.

Cagliari was a province in Sardinia, an autonomous region in Italy. The capital city was Cagliari. The province had an area and a population of 543,310 in 2001. It included 71 "comuni" (singular: "comune"). In 2016, the province was changed by a regional decree and replaced by the metropolitan city of Cagliari.

A blast injury is a type of physical damage caused by an explosion. It can happen when someone is close to or affected by the explosion. These injuries are worse when the explosion happens in a small space.

Rachel Emily Nichols, born on January 8, 1980, is an American actress and model. She started modeling while studying at Columbia University in New York City in the late 1990s. By the early 2000s, she began acting. She appeared in the movie "Autumn in New York" in 2000 and in one episode of "Sex and the City" in 2002. Her first big role was in the comedy film in 2003. She was well-known for playing Rachel Gibson in the final season of the show "Alias" from 2005 to 2006. She also starred in the horror film "The Amityville Horror" in 2005. Nichols got her first leading role in the thriller "P2" in 2007. She became more popular with the science-fiction action films "Star Trek" and "Star Trek Into Darkness" both in 2009. Other notable films include "The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants 2" (2008), "Conan the Barbarian" (2011), "Alex Cross" (2012), "Raze" (2013), and "Inside" (2016). She was in the TV series "Continuum" from 2012 to 2015. She appeared in the sixth season of "Criminal Minds" from 2010 to 2011, and in the fourth seasons of "Chicago Fire" from 2015 to 2016 and "The Librarians" from 2017 to 2018. She also played a Gestapo officer named Martha in five episodes of "The Man in the High Castle."

Mullsjö AIS is a floorball club in Mullsjö, Sweden. It was founded on November 1, 1989, by a group from the Mullsjö Mission Covenant Church. In March 2008, the men's team reached the Swedish top division.

Atlantis is a made-up island from an old story by Plato. In Plato's work, "Timaeus" and "Critias," Atlantis is described as a powerful navy that attacks a city called ancient Athens. Athens defeats the Atlantis navy. Plato used Athens to show his idea of a perfect state. The story ends with Atlantis being punished by the gods and sinking into the Atlantic Ocean. Although Atlantis is only a small part of Plato's work, it has inspired many writers. For example, Francis Bacon wrote "New Atlantis" and Thomas More wrote "Utopia," both based on Plato's ideas. Later, people who weren't experts wrongly thought Plato's story was based on real events. One person, Ignatius L. Donnelly, wrote a book about Atlantis being real. Plato said the events happened more than 9,000 years ago, and that Atlantis was beyond a place called the Pillars of Hercules. This led to many people making unfounded guesses about Atlantis. Today, people still use "Atlantis" to talk about lost civilizations from long ago. While experts agree Atlantis is a fictional place, they still wonder what inspired Plato. Some think he got ideas from older stories, like the tale of Gyges. Other ideas suggest Atlantis might be based on events like the eruption of Thera, the attack of the Sea Peoples, or even the Trojan War. Some scholars say Plato made Atlantis up, using stories from his time as inspiration, like the failed invasion of Sicily by Athens in 415-413 BC or the destruction of Helike in 373 BC.

Jose C. Vitug, born on July 15, 1934, is a Filipino lawyer and judge. He became an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the Philippines in 1993. President Fidel Ramos appointed him. Vitug stopped working at the Supreme Court in 2004. He also started the Angeles University Foundation School of Law as its first dean. Currently, he is an independent director for Abottiz Equity Ventures.

Monster Buster Club is a French-Canadian children's science fiction TV show. It was made by Marathon Media, an French company, and Image Entertainment Corporation, a Canadian animation studio. Jetix Europe also helped make it. The show started on June 2, 2008, in Europe on Jetix. It came out on June 9, 2008, in the United States and Asia on May 3, 2008. It first appeared on YTV in Canada. In total, 52 episodes were made.

The Caledonian Railway (CR) was a big Scottish train company. It was started in the early 1800s. Its goal was to connect English railways with Glasgow. Over time, it built more tracks and reached Edinburgh and Aberdeen. It had many smaller lines around Glasgow too. In 1923, it became part of the London, Midland and Scottish Railway. Many of its main routes are still used today. The big line between Carlisle and Glasgow is now part of the West Coast Main Line.

The British Rail Class 304 electric multiple units were made for use in suburbs on the first parts of the West Coast Main Line that got electricity between Crewe and Manchester/Liverpool/Rugby. They were first called AM4 units, then became Class 304 under the TOPS numbering system. These units ran on most of the West Coast Main Line. They followed the 1959 design for alternating current (AC) electric trains. Externally, they looked similar to Class 305, Class 308, and 1,200 V DC Class 504 units. None of these trains are preserved, and all were eventually scrapped.

Sir Herbert Benjamin Edwardes was a British official and soldier who lived from November 12, 1819, to December 23, 1868. He worked in the Punjab area of British India. He is famous as the "Hero of Multan" for his key role in winning the Second Anglo-Sikh War.

STS-122 was a NASA space shuttle mission to the International Space Station. This was the 24th shuttle mission to the ISS and the 121st overall space shuttle flight. The mission was also known as ISS-1E. Its main goal was to bring the European "Columbus" science lab to the station. It also brought back to Earth an astronaut named Daniel M. Tani. Tani was replaced by another astronaut named Léopold Eyharts, representing ESA. After landing, the shuttle "Atlantis" was prepared for its next mission, STS-125, which was to fix the Hubble Space Telescope. The original plan was to launch on December 6, 2007, but problems delayed the launch. The sensors failed twice, and the launch was stopped. A test on December 18, 2007, found the problem was with a connector between the fuel tank and the shuttle. The connector was replaced, and the shuttle finally launched on February 7, 2008.
The Cathedral of Solsona is in Solsona, Catalonia. The apse, which is in a Roman style, likely dates from the 12th century.

In mathematics, a continuous function is one that has no sudden changes. Small changes in input lead to small changes in output. Functions that aren't continuous are called "discontinuous." Before the 19th century, mathematicians used simple ideas about continuity, but later, they tried to make it more precise with rules like the epsilon–delta definition. In topology, continuity is a key concept, though this article focuses on functions that take and give real numbers. A stronger kind of continuity is called uniform continuity. In this article, we also look at how continuity works for functions between metric spaces. In order theory, particularly domain theory, there's a type of continuity known as Scott continuity. The article doesn't cover other forms of continuity. For example, a function showing a flower's height as it grows would be continuous. In contrast, a function showing money in a bank account would be discontinuous because it changes suddenly at specific times when money is added or taken out.

Harads is a small village in Boden Municipality, Norrbotten County, Sweden, about 50 kilometers south of the Arctic Circle. It had 501 people living there in 2010. The main village is in the area called Edefors. There is a church in Edefors from 1928. A famous architect, John Åkerlund, designed it. The church mixes Nordic classicism with national romantic style. It replaced an older church from 1888 that was destroyed in a fire in 1918. Harads also has the Treehotel, created by entrepreneur Kent Lindvall in 2010. The hotel rooms are in the forest, high up in the trees. You can walk between them using walkways. Each room, designed by a different architect, has a special name, like Mirrorcube, UFO, Blue Cone, and Bird's Nest. Lindvall believes the hotel design follows the idea of sustainability.

Angelo Peruzzi, born on February 16, 1970, is an Italian football coach and former goalkeeper. He has won the Serie A Goalkeeper of the Year award three times. Currently, he works as a team manager for Lazio. Peruzzi is considered one of the best Italian goalkeepers of all time. He played for several Italian clubs: Roma, Hellas Verona, Juventus, Inter, and Lazio. During his time with Juventus, Peruzzi was very successful, winning three Serie A titles, the Coppa Italia, the UEFA Cup, and the UEFA Champions League. Before retiring in 2007 with Lazio, he won another Coppa Italia. Internationally, Peruzzi played 31 times for Italy. He started his international career in 1995. He was part of the Italian team that won the 2006 FIFA World Cup. He also played in the 1992 Olympics and in UEFA Euro 1996 and 2004.

Alfred A. Bianchi was born on March 26, 1932, and died on October 28, 2019. He was an American who worked in basketball in many roles. He played basketball professionally. He also coached basketball teams. Bianchi was a general manager, consultant, and scout in basketball.
Ambrières-les-Vallées is a town in the Mayenne department in Northwestern France. It is near Normandy.

Fernando James Ferrer was born on April 30, 1950. He is an American politician. From 1987 to 2001, he was the borough president of the Bronx. In 2001, he ran for mayor of New York City. In 2005, he was chosen as the Democratic Party's candidate for mayor.

Montluçon is a town in central France, located on the Cher River. It is the biggest town in the Allier department, though the department's main town, Moulins, is smaller. People who live there are called "montluçonnais." Montluçon is in a region called Bourbonnais and was once part of a medieval duchy called Bourbon.

Hurricane Erin was the first hurricane to hit the United States since Hurricane Andrew in 1992. It was the fifth tropical cyclone, fifth named storm, and second hurricane of the 1995 Atlantic hurricane season. Erin formed near the southeastern Bahamas on July 31 and moved northwest, becoming a Category 1 hurricane near Rum Cay on August 1. The cyclone moved over the northwestern Bahamas, including the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama. On August 2, it hit Vero Beach, Florida, with winds of 85 mph (140 km/h). Erin weakened as it crossed Florida but re-intensified into a Category 1 hurricane early on August 3, briefly becoming a Category 2 hurricane before hitting Fort Walton Beach with winds of 100 mph (155 km/h). The hurricane then weakened slightly and hit Pensacola Beach, Florida, with 85 mph (140 km/h) winds. Erin caused power outages for over a million people in Florida and damaged about 5,000 homes and buildings, mostly in Brevard County and the western Florida Panhandle. Nine people died in Florida, mostly from drowning. The storm also damaged 100 homes and 17 schools in Alabama and affected pecan crops in Baldwin County. In total, Hurricane Erin caused about $700 million in damage, most of which was in Florida.

The Sea of Marmara, also called the Marmora Sea, connects the Black Sea to the Aegean Sea and is entirely within Turkey. It separates Turkey's Asian and European parts. The Bosphorus strait links the Sea of Marmara to the Black Sea, and the Dardanelles strait connects it to the Aegean Sea. This sea is small, with an area of a certain size and certain dimensions. Its deepest part is a specific depth.

Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal is an expansion for a real-time strategy game made by Blizzard Entertainment and Cyberlore Studios. It came out in 1996. You need the original game to play this expansion.

Jean-Michel Larrasket, born on May 22, 1950, and passed away on March 19, 2018, was a French professor and engineer. He was also the vice president of the French Basque Country in the Basque Studies Society. Larrasket promoted projects to help the social and economic growth of the French Basque Country. He was one of the founders of the "Eticoop" cooperative, which encourages business in that area.

Ingram Olkin was born on July 23, 1924, and passed away on April 28, 2016. He was a professor emeritus and the chair of statistics and education at Stanford University and the Stanford Graduate School of Education. Olkin is famous for creating statistical methods to evaluate policies, especially in education, and for his work in meta-analysis, statistics education, multivariate analysis, and majorization theory.

The People's Party was a political party in the United States. It was formed in 1971 by several groups, including the Peace and Freedom Party, Common Good People's Party, Country People's Caucus, Human Rights Party, Liberty Union, New American Party, New Party (Arizona), and No Party. Their main goal was to present an anti-war platform for elections. In 1972, Dr. Benjamin Spock, an American pediatrician, was the party's presidential candidate. Margaret Wright was the party's candidate in the 1976 presidential election. Dr. Spock was also the party's vice-presidential candidate in 1972. After the 1976 election, the party became less organized and soon stopped existing. Many of the groups that started the People's Party also dissolved. The party's records are now kept at the Western Historical Manuscript Collection in the University of Missouri–St. Louis, where they used to hold their conventions.

Ramo Peter (Ray) Ceresino was born on April 24, 1929, and passed away on May 1, 2015. He was a Canadian ice hockey player who played as a left winger. He played for the Toronto Maple Leafs, an NHL team. On June 2, 1953, he married Lorraine Giardetti, and they stayed married for 62 years. In 1962, he moved his family to California and settled in Los Angeles. There, he worked as a mortgage broker. Later, he retired to San Diego. He had three children, one of them being Gordon Ceresino.

tagetes is a group of plants that are either annuals or perennials. Most of them are herbaceous. They belong to the sunflower family. Carl Linnaeus described this group in 1753. Tagetes is originally from southern Mexico, but some species have become naturalized in other parts of the world. One species, "T. minuta," is considered a noxious invasive plant in some areas.

China uses one time zone, which is eight hours ahead of UTC. Even though China covers five geographical time zones, it follows the same time. This time is called "Beijing time" in China and "China Standard Time" (CST) internationally. China stopped using daylight saving time in 1991.

Allosaurus is a type of meat-eating dinosaur that lived about 155 to 145 million years ago during the Late Jurassic period. Its name means "different lizard," referring to its unique vertebrae when discovered. Allosaurus belongs to a group of dinosaurs called theropods. The first fossils that could be identified as Allosaurus were found in 1877 by Othniel Charles Marsh. As one of the earliest known theropods, it has long been popular outside paleontological circles. Allosaurus was a large, two-legged predator with a large skull filled with sharp, serrated teeth. It measured around 9 meters long. Its three-fingered forelimbs were small compared to its strong hind legs, and it had a long, muscular tail for balance. It is part of the Allosauridae family, a group of Carnosaurian theropod dinosaurs. Allosaurus includes three valid species, with the best-known one being A. fragilis. Most fossils have been found in the Morrison Formation in North America, with some also discovered in Portugal. For most of the 20th century, it was known as Antrodemus, but recent studies from the Cleveland-Lloyd dinosaur quarry brought the name Allosaurus back to the spotlight, making it one of the best-known dinosaurs. As the most common large predator in the Morrison Formation, Allosaurus likely preyed on large plant-eating dinosaurs such as ornithopods, stegosaurids, and sauropods. Some researchers think Allosaurus might have hunted in groups, while others believe they were aggressive towards each other, and groups formed around feeding on the same carcasses.

Joseph Thomas Elliott Jr., born on August 1, 1959, is an English singer-songwriter, musician, record producer, and radio presenter. He is famous for being the lead singer and one of the founding members of the English rock band Def Leppard. Elliott has also sung as the lead in tribute bands for David Bowie and Mott the Hedleep. He is one of the original members of Def Leppard and has sung on every Def Leppard album. Elliott is known for his special, raspy singing voice.

White Colne is a village and parish in Essex, England. It is located on the north side of the River Colne, opposite Earls Colne, and on the Colchester road. It is 4 miles east southeast of Halstead. White Colne's history goes back to the Domesday Book. There is evidence of people living in the area during the Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods. White Colne had a railway station on the Colne Valley and Halstead railway. The village church honors St. Andrew. The German actor Anton Diffring is buried in the churchyard.
Stapleford Tawney is a village and civil parish in Epping Forest District, Essex, England. It is roughly southwest of Chipping Ongar and south of Chelmsford, the county town.
lignerolles is a commune in central France. It is in the Allier department.

Nadine Vanessa Dorries, born on May 21, 1957, is a British politician who has been serving as the minister for mental health, suicide prevention, and patient safety since 2019. She is a member of the Conservative Party and has been the Member of Parliament (MP) for Mid Bedfordshire since 2005. Dorries is considered to be on the right side of the Conservative Party. Born in Liverpool to a working-class family, Dorries started her career as a nurse and later became a medical representative. She spent a year in Zambia as the head of a community school. After returning to the UK, she founded a company called Kids Ltd, which provided day-care services for working parents. She sold the company in 1998. Dorries was elected to Parliament in the 2005 general election for the safe Conservative seat of Mid Bedfordshire. She won with a majority of 11,355 votes. As a backbencher, she tried to pass several unsuccessful private member’s bills, such as reducing the time limit for abortions in the UK and changing rules for counseling women. She also advocated for sexual abstinence for girls in sex education. Dorries was against John Bercow and tried to remove him as the Speaker of the House of Commons. She also had disagreements with David Cameron and George Osborne, calling them "arrogant posh boys." In November 2012, she was suspended from the Conservative whip for participating in the reality TV show "I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!" without informing the chief whip. In May 2013, she was allowed back into the Conservative whip and re-admitted to the parliamentary party. In July 2019, Boris Johnson appointed Dorries as the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State at the Department of Health and Social Care, focusing on mental health, suicide prevention, and patient safety. In February 2020, she became the first MP to be diagnosed with COVID-19 during the pandemic. In May of the same year, she was promoted to the rank of Minister of State.

Abel Ferrara, born on July 19, 1951, is an American filmmaker. He is known for making movies with shocking and sometimes controversial content. He uses a style called neo-noir in his films and often shows urban settings that are rough and real. As an independent filmmaker, some of his famous movies are "Ms. 45" (1981), "King of New York" (1990), "Bad Lieutenant" (1992), and "The Funeral" (1996).

Minnie Mouse is one of the cartoon characters created by Ub Iwerks and Walt Disney. She and Mickey Mouse were first drawn in 1928 by Iwerks. In a comic strip called "The Gleam" published in 1942, her full name was given as Minerva Mouse, but this name is not often used. The comic strip "Mr. Slicker and the Egg Robbers," published in 1930, introduced Minnie's father, Marcus Mouse, and her unnamed mother. It also showed photographs of Minnie's uncle, Milton Mouse, his family, and her grandparents, Marvel Mouse and Matilda Mouse. Minnie's best-known relatives are her uncle Mortimer Mouse and her twin nieces, Millie and Melody Mouse. Usually, only Melody appears. Minnie is often shown as Mickey Mouse's girlfriend, a close friend of Daisy Duck, and a friend of Clarabelle Cow. On January 22, 2018, she got her own star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, like Mickey Mouse.
Louis Réard, a French engineer and clothing designer, introduced the modern bikini in July 1946. He opened a bikini shop and ran it for 40 years until 1984.

Manchukuo was a puppet state in Northeast China and Inner Mongolia from 1932 to 1945. Japan controlled it. Before 1934, it was called the State of Manchuria. After 1934, it became the Empire of Manchuria. It was created after Japan invaded Manchuria in 1932. In 1934, it became a monarchy. Puyi, the last Qing emperor, was made the nominal leader. The region was seized by Japan in 1931 following the Mukden Incident. Manchuria was mostly Han Chinese. Koreans and Japanese also lived there. Mongolia's western regions had a different system. The southern part of the Liaodong peninsula was ruled directly by Japan. Manchus were not the main ethnic group. Manchukuo ended in 1945 after Japan lost World War II.

Jane Child, born on February 15, 1967, is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and record producer. She is famous for the song "Don't Want to Fall in Love." Jane is also known for her special and unusual fashion. Her hairstyle had spikes and long braids reaching her ankles. She also wore a nose chain.

Pope Gregory XVI, born Bartolomeo Alberto Cappellari on September 18, 1765, died on June 1, 1846. He led the Catholic Church and the Papal States from February 2, 1831, until his death. He chose the name Mauro when he joined the Camaldolese religious order. Gregory XVI was very traditional and did not like new ideas. He did not want democratic and modern changes in the Papal States or in Europe because he thought they were dangerous. Instead, he tried to make the Church more powerful. In a document called "Mirari Vos," he said that giving people freedom to think what they want about religion is wrong. He supported sending Church workers to other countries and fighting against slavery. But, he was not popular because of his strict rules, spending too much money, and not taking care of people's needs. He was the last pope to use the name "Gregory" and the last non-bishop to become pope. He was also the last pope who was a member of a religious order, until Pope Francis became pope in 2013.
returns, in economics and political economy, are the payments given to people who provide goods or services.

Patrik Jonas Andersson, born on August 18, 1971, is a Swedish former football player who played as a defender. His father, Roy Andersson, and his younger brother, Daniel Andersson, also played professional football.

Colonization is a global and long-lasting phenomenon. Ancient and medieval colonizers, like the Phoenicians, Greeks, and Crusaders, established colonies. Modern colonialism started with the "Age of Discovery," led by Portugal and Spain. They explored America, Africa, the Middle East, India, and East Asia, creating the first global empires. From 1580 to 1640, Spain ruled both empires. Later, England, France, and the Dutch also created their own overseas empires, competing with each other. By the late 18th and early 19th centuries, most American colonies gained independence. During the 19th century, especially after the Industrial Revolution, there was a new imperialism phase, with rapid colonization and the Scramble for Africa involving Belgium, Germany, and Italy. Conflicts with colonizers and revolutions by colonized people changed control and led to independent nations. After World War I, the colonies of defeated countries were given to winners as mandates, but major decolonization began after World War II.

World music, also called global or international music, is a category in Western music that includes many different types of music from other parts of the world. It covers ethnic, indigenous, folk, and neotraditional music, as well as music where non-Western and Western popular traditions mix. World music doesn't have a single definition because it's so diverse, but it's about showing interest in different cultures. A magazine called "Froots" describes it as "local music from far away." The term "world music" became popular in the 1980s to market non-Western traditional music. Now, it includes subgenres like ethnic fusion and worldbeat.

Ophthalmosauridae is an extinct family of ichthyosaurs from the middle Jurassic to the early Late Cretaceous. They lived in Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America. The oldest known ophthalmosaurid is "Mollesaurus" from Argentina, from the early Bajocian period. It was named by George H. Baur in 1887. This species includes early forms like "Ophthalmosaurus". In 1956, Appleby named the taxon Ophthalmosauria, but Ophthalmosauridae is the preferred term because it was named first.

Everett Lee, born on August 31, 1916, is an American conductor and violinist. He was the first African American to lead a Broadway musical. He was also the first to direct an established symphony orchestra in the southern United States. Additionally, he conducted a major American opera company's performance for the first time.

Rodney Adolphus Wilkes, born on March 11, 1925, and died on March 24, 2014, was a weightlifter from Trinidad and Tobago. He was called "the mighty midget." He was not famous outside his local area until he won a gold medal at the 1946 Central American and Caribbean games in Barranquilla, Colombia. His best lifts were in the press, snatch, and clean and jerk. He went to the 1948 Olympics in London and got a silver medal, making him the first athlete from Trinidad and Tobago to win one. In 1951, he won a gold medal at the first Pan American Games in Buenos Aires. The next year, he went to the Olympics in Helsinki and got a bronze medal. He was behind two Soviet athletes. Wilkes stopped lifting for a short time in 1953 but came back to win gold at the 1954 British Empire and Commonwealth Games in Vancouver. Four years later, he got a bronze medal at the games in Cardiff. His last Olympic appearance was in Melbourne in 1956. He came in fourth place but missed the medal by one position and 5 kilograms. He kept lifting until 1960 but quit when he couldn't make the West Indies team for the Rome Olympics. After stopping, Wilkes worked as an electrician in San Fernando, Trinidad and Tobago. He passed away from prostate cancer in a San Fernando hospital in 2014 at the age of 89.

Gorillaz are a British virtual band created in 1998 by musician Damon Albarn and artist Jamie Hewlett. They have four animated members: 2-D, Murdoc Niccals, Noodle, and Russel Hobbs. The band's world is shown in music videos, interviews, and short cartoons. Albarn is the only permanent musician. Gorillaz often works with other artists. Remi Kabaka Jr. joined as a producer in 2016 and was listed as an official member in 2019. Albarn started Gorillaz differently from his previous band Blur, using many music styles like hip hop, electronic, and world music. Their first album "Gorillaz" (2001) was very popular, selling many copies in the UK and Europe. "Demon Days" (2005) was darker and also very successful. "Plastic Beach" (2010) talked about the environment and used electropop. "The Fall" (2010) came from touring. "Humanz" (2017) took a 7-year break. "The Now Now" (2018) had simpler music and focused on Albarn. Gorillaz share new songs every month on a project called "Song Machine." They have performed in different ways, hiding the band members or using real ones. Gorillaz won a Grammy, two MTV Video Music Awards, an NME Award, and three MTV Europe Music Awards. They also won best British group at the 2018 Brit Awards. Gorillaz have sold over 20 million records worldwide and are considered the world's most successful virtual band by Guinness World Records.

Mortality rate is a way to measure how many people die in a group, per year. It is shown as deaths out of 1,000 people. For example, a mortality rate of 9.5 per 1,000 in a population of 1,000 means 9.5 deaths per year, or 0.95%. It's different from "morbidity," which is about being sick, and from the incidence rate, which is about how many new cases of a disease appear. A key measure is the crude death rate, which looks at deaths from all causes in a certain time for a given population. For instance, the CIA predicts the global crude death rate will be 7.7 deaths per 1,000 people per year. Mortality rates can be calculated using the formula: (number of deaths / population size) × conversion factor.

The Kama is a long river in Russia. It is the longest left tributary of the Volga and the largest in terms of water flow. At the point where it meets the Volga, the Kama is even larger than the Volga itself. The Kama starts in the Udmurt Republic, near Kuliga. It flows northwest for a distance, then turns northeast near Loyno for another stretch. It then goes south and west through Perm Krai, flowing through the Udmurt Republic and the Republic of Tatarstan before joining the Volga. Before trains, important paths existed that connected the Kama with the rivers of the Northern Dvina and the Pechora. In the early 1800s, a canal called the Northern Ekaterininsky connected the upper Kama with the Vychegda River (a tributary of the Northern Dvina). However, it was mostly abandoned after just a few years because not many people used it. The Kama is featured in a 2013 Russian film called "The Geographer Drank His Globe Away," particularly in a scene with rapids.

William Edgar Buchanan II was born on March 20, 1903, and died on April 4, 1979. He was an American actor with a long career in films and TV shows. He is best known today for his role as Uncle Joe Carson in the TV sitcoms "Petticoat Junction," "Green Acres," and "The Beverly Hillbillies" from the 1960s.

Steven Ralph Schirripa, born on September 3, 1957, is an American actor, producer, author, and voice artist. He is famous for playing Bobby Baccalieri in "The Sopranos" and Detective Anthony Abetemarco in "Blue Bloods." Schirripa also produces and hosts two Investigation Discovery shows: "Karma's a B*tch!" and "Nothing Personal." He was a regular on "The Secret Life of the American Teenager" and voiced Roberto in the "Open Season" movies. He has also appeared in ads for Lamisil, Dick's Sporting Goods, and McDonald's.

Mamasani County is in Fars Province, Iran. Its capital is Nurabad, 180 kilometers from Shiraz. The people there speak Luri, a southern Luri dialect. In 2006, including parts that became Rostam County, the county had 162,694 people in 45,145 families. Excluding those parts, it had 166,317 people in 26,011 families. Mamasani County has three districts: Central, Mahvarmilani, and Doshman Zari. It includes three cities: Nurabad, Khumeh Zar, and Baba Monir. Mamasani is home to an ancient tribe, also called Muhammad Hasni, with many sub-tribes. Parts of this tribe live in Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Iraq. The main tribe is in Mamasani County, Fars Province, Iran, and speaks Luri. Another group, Sistan Mamasanis, live in Sistan and Baluchistan. Muhammad Hasni Brahui and Baluchi live in Baluchistan, Iran and Pakistan, and Nimrus and Helmand in Afghanistan.
The Perpignan arrondissement is in France, in the Pyrénées-orientales department (Northern Catalonia) in the Occitanie region. It includes 39 towns. In 2016, it had 285,077 people.

Rameswaram is a town in Tamil Nadu, India. It is on an island called Pamban, separated from mainland India by the Pamban Channel. Pamban Island is connected to mainland India by the Pamban Bridge. Rameswaram is at the tip of the Indian peninsula, near Mannar Island in Sri Lanka. It is an important holy place for Hindus and is part of the Char Dham pilgrimage. According to the Ramayana, Rama and Hanuman built a bridge to Sri Lanka from here to save Rama's wife, Sita. The Ramanathaswamy temple, dedicated to Shiva, is central to the town. Rameswaram is close to Sri Lanka and has been involved in projects like the Setusamudram shipping canal and issues with Tamil refugees and fishing. The town has a population of about 44,856 and is run by a municipality established in 1994. Most people in Rameswaram work in tourism or fishing.
Wolfgang Feiersinger was born on January 30, 1965. He is from Austria. He played soccer as a defender and is now retired.

Lil' Kim's "La Bella Mafia" is her third album. It came out on March 4, 2003, through Atlantic Records. The album did well, starting at number five on the US Billboard 200. It sold more than one million copies in the US and over two million worldwide, getting platinum certification from the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Critics liked the album, praising Lil' Kim's skills and presence. Two singles were released. "The Jump Off" reached number 17 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number 16 in the UK. "Magic Stick," featuring 50 Cent, peaked at number two on the Billboard Hot 100. The singles "Magic Stick" and "Come Back for You" got Lil' Kim nominated for Grammy Awards.

Priscilla Moran was an American actress who worked in silent films. She was born on November 23, 1917, in Sedalia, Missouri. She began acting in movies in 1922. Priscilla stopped acting in 1937, when she was 20 years old. She appeared in 14 films during her career.
This is a list of NHL players who played at least one game from 1917 to now and have last names starting with "M". The list was updated for the 2018-19 NHL season.

Arianism is a belief that Jesus Christ is the son of God, born by God the Father, and different from the Father (though not inferior). This belief was first linked to Arius, a priest in Alexandria, Egypt, in the 300s. The term "Arian" came from his name, not something he chose for himself. Arians had different views on God's nature compared to those who believed in the Trinity. The main argument between Arians and others was about Jesus's divinity. Arians believed Jesus did not always exist, but was begotten by God the Father. This belief caused a big argument within Christianity. Trinitarian or homoousian views were officially supported by early councils. Arianism was seen as wrong by most Christians for many years. Athanasius of Alexandria argued that God and Jesus were one in nature. Arianism was declared heretical at the Council of Nicaea in 325. Ten years later, Emperor Constantine allowed arian leaders to meet. He then exiled Athanasius and restored Arian bishop Eusebius. However, Athanasius returned in 346 after Arianism declined. He and other leaders fought against Arian beliefs. Arianism spread to some emperors and kings, including Constantius II, Valens, and Odoacer. The Visigoths, Vandals, and Lombards also practiced Arianism for a time. In the 400s, Arianism was challenged again at the Council of Constantinople. While some nontrinitarian beliefs are similar to Arianism, they differ in how they view Jesus.

Marc Angéle Vanderlinden, or van der Linden, was born on February 4, 1964, in Merksem. He played football as a professional. He started his career with SC Merksem. In 1982, he moved to Royal Antwerp FC. He stayed there for seven seasons. In 1989, he joined RSC Anderlecht. Two years later, he went to KAA Gent. In 1995, he played for Hapoel Ironi Rishon Lezion FC and then for Hapoel Herzliya FC in Israel. He returned to Merksem in 1997 and continued playing there until 2002 when he retired. He also played 19 times for the Belgium national team, scoring nine goals, and appeared in the 1990 FIFA World Cup.

In physics, specifically in celestial mechanics, escape velocity is the minimum speed needed for an object to escape the gravitational pull of a large body, reaching an infinite distance from it. Escape velocity depends on the mass of the body and the distance to its center. A rocket can escape without reaching escape velocity because it keeps getting energy from its fuel as it moves. It can leave at any speed with enough fuel and propulsion. Earth's escape velocity from its surface is about. More generally, escape velocity is the speed where the object's kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy equal zero. Once an object leaves a body with escape velocity, it moves away, slowing down forever but never stopping. If an object reaches escape velocity and heads away from a large body, it will keep moving away, slowing down continuously, and approach zero speed as it gets very far away. No further force is needed after reaching escape velocity. The minimum escape velocity doesn't consider friction or future changes in speed due to other forces. For a spherical, massive body like a planet or star, the escape velocity at a certain distance is calculated as: Where "G" is the universal gravitational constant, "m" is the mass of the body, and "r" is the distance from the body's center. The escape velocity doesn't depend on the escaping object's mass. An object starting from infinity and falling due to gravity will hit the body with the same escape velocity. If an object's initial speed is more than the escape velocity, it will approach a "hyperbolic excess speed" as it moves away.

Lichtervelde is a municipality in the Belgian province of West Flanders. Lichtervelde consists of only one town. On January 1, 2006, the town had 8,400 people. The area of Lichtervelde is 25. 93 square kilometers, making the population density 324 people per square kilometer. There is a church that is 64 meters high. The inventor Charles Joseph van Depoele was born in this town.
Plains is a town and the county seat of Yoakum County in Western Texas, United States. It is in the south part of the Panhandle. The town's population was 1,481 in the 2010 census.
Gillespie is a city in Macoupin County, Illinois, United States. It is part of the Metro East region of the St. Louis area. The population was 3,319 in 2010.

Bernard Verlhac, known as Tignous, was a French cartoonist born on August 21, 1957. He worked as a long-time cartoonist for the French satirical magazine "Charlie Hebdo." Tignous died on January 7, 2015, during the "Charlie Hebdo" shooting.

This list includes only domestic cat breeds and some domestic hybrids. It covers recognized breeds by registries, new breeds, and those being developed into official breeds. It also includes distinct domestic cat groups and extinct breeds. As of 2019, TICA recognizes 71 breeds, CFA 44, and FIFE 43. Different registries sometimes classify the same animal as different breeds. For example, TICA’s Himalayan is seen as a type of Persian by CFA, and the Javanese in both TICA and CFA is a variation of the Balinese. WCF combines them into a single "mega-breed" called the Colorpoint. Other registries have different names for these breeds. Many cat breed names are made up to sound exotic, like Balinese, Javanese, and Himalayan, which don’t match their origins. Domestic short-haired and long-haired cats are not breeds but terms used to describe mixed breeds based on coat length. Some registries can register them and they were used to create new breeds. They should not be confused with official breeds with similar names, such as the British Shorthair and Oriental Longhair.

The Rubik's Revenge, also known as the Master Cube, is a 4×4×4 version of the Rubik's cube. It came out in 1981. Peter Sebesteny invented it. Initially, it was almost called the Sebesteny Cube, but they decided to change the name to attract people who liked the original Rubik's cube. Unlike some other puzzles like the 5×5×5 cube, the Rubik's Revenge has moveable center pieces. Solving methods for the 3×3×3 cube can work for the edges and corners of the 4×4×4 cube, as long as you correctly identify the colors since the center pieces can't be used for this.
The middle angles were an important group in Mercia, a large kingdom in England during the Anglo-Saxon period.

Robert Michael Schneider, born on October 31, 1963, is an American actor, comedian, writer, and director. He performed stand-up comedy and was on a TV show called "Saturday Night Live." Later, he acted in movies like "The Animal," "The Hot Chick," "The Benchwarmers," and "Grown Ups." Schneider has a daughter who is a singer named Elle King.

Alexander Smart was born on May 29, 1918, and died on April 18, 2005. He was a Canadian ice hockey player who played as a forward. He played one season for the Montreal Canadiens in the National Hockey League. Most of his career was in the Quebec Senior Hockey League.

Charles Anthony Ryan Silvera, nicknamed Swede, was an American baseball player and coach. He was born on October 13, 1924, and died on September 7, 2019. Silvera played for the New York Yankees and was part of six World Series championships with the team.

Hamilton County is in the southwestern part of Ohio. In 2010, it had 802, 374 people, which made it the third largest county in Ohio. The county seat and biggest city is Cincinnati. Hamilton County is named after Alexander Hamilton, the first U.S. Secretary of the Treasury. This county is part of the Cincinnati-Middletown, Ohio-Kentucky-Indiana metropolitan area.
Palmer is a city in Washington County, Kansas, United States. In 2010, the city had 111 people living there.

Norman Steven Maciver, born on September 1, 1964, is a Canadian. He used to play ice hockey professionally and is now an assistant general manager for the Chicago Blackhawks in the NHL. During his playing career, which lasted 13 years, he played defense for six different NHL teams.

Hiragana and katakana are both kana systems. Each syllable, or mora, in Japanese is represented by one or two characters in each system. These characters can be vowels like "あ" (a), consonants followed by vowels like "か" (ka) or "ん" (n), or nasal sounds like "ん" that can sound like English "m", "n", or "ng", or like nasal vowels in French, Portuguese, or Galician. The characters in kana are called syllabic symbols, not letters. Hiragana is used for "okurigana" (suffixes following a kanji root, like verb and adjective endings), some grammatical words like particles, and other native words without kanji or where the kanji is too formal. Authors might also use hiragana for these words to make the text feel more informal. Hiragana is also used for "furigana", which are small characters showing how to read kanji. Hiragana has two main ordering systems: the old-fashioned iroha order and the more common gojūon order.
San Diego is a city in Texas, United States. It is mainly in Duval County and is the county seat. The population was 4,488 in 2010.

Michel Suleiman was born on November 21, 1948. He was the president of Lebanon from 2008 to 2014. Before becoming president, he was the commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces from 1998 to 2008. After Emile Lahoud became president in November 1998, Suleiman took his place as commander in December 1998. Later, Suleiman was elected as president and took office on May 25, 2008.

Ivan's Childhood, sometimes called My Name Is Ivan in the US, is a 1962 Soviet war film. It was the first movie directed by Andrei Tarkovsky. Tarkovsky and Mikhail Papava co-wrote the film, which is based on Vladimir Bogomolov's 1957 short story "Ivan." The film features Nikolai Burlyayev as Ivan, an orphan whose parents died in World War II, and other actors like Valentin Zubkov, Evgeny Zharikov, Stepan Krylov, Nikolai Grinko, and Tarkovsky's wife Irma Raush. "Ivan's Childhood" shows Ivan's life during World War II. It was one of several Soviet films, including "The Cranes Are Flying" and "Ballad of a Soldier," that focused on the human cost of war rather than glorifying it, unlike earlier films. Tarkovsky said he wanted to show his hatred of war and chose children because their experiences contrast sharply with war. This was Tarkovsky's first feature film. He gained critical praise and became internationally known for it. The film won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and the Golden Gate Award at the San Francisco International Film Festival in 1962. It was also considered for an Academy Award but was not nominated. Ingmar Bergman, Sergei Parajanov, and Krzysztof Kieślowski admired the film and were influenced by it.
Sannes is a commune in the Vaucluse department, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur region in southeastern France.

Linux Mint is a community-driven Linux distribution based on Ubuntu or Debian. It comes with many free and open-source applications. You can get full multimedia support by ticking one box during installation. This includes some proprietary software, like multimedia codecs. Linux Mint was created by Clément Lefèbvre and is actively developed by the Linux Mint team and community.

Crooked Island is an island and district. It is part of a group of Bahamian islands. These islands surround a large, shallow lagoon called the Bight of Acklins. The largest islands in this group are Crooked Island in the north and Acklins in the southeast. Other smaller islands are Long Cay, which used to be known as Fortune Island, in the northwest, and Castle Island in the south.

Vientiane is the capital and largest city of Laos. It is located on the banks of the Mekong River near the border with Thailand. Vientiane became the capital in 1573 because people were afraid of a Burmese invasion. Later, it was looted and destroyed by the Siamese (Thais) in 1827. During French rule, Vientiane was the administrative capital. Now, it is also an important economic center for Laos. As of the 2015 census, the city had 820,000 people. Vientiane is famous for the That Luang, a major national monument in Laos. This monument is a symbol of Laos and represents Buddhism in the country. Other important Buddhist temples, like Haw Phra Kaew, are also in Vientiane. Haw Phra Kaew used to have the Emerald Buddha. Vientiane hosted the 25th Southeast Asian Games in December 2009, to celebrate 50 years of the Southeast Asian Games.
A crescent is a shape that represents the moon. It may also refer to:

Our Band Could Be Your Life: Scenes from the American Indie Underground, 1981-1991 is a book by Michael Azerrad. It tells the stories of several underground rock bands. These bands didn't become famous, but they were very important in making American alternative and indie rock popular. They did this by touring a lot and releasing records on small, local independent record labels. Azerrad talked to many band members and also read old fanzines, as well as mainstream newspapers and books.

Everland is South Korea's biggest theme park. It is in Yongin, a city in Gyeonggi-do. Everland has 5.85 million visitors each year. In 2018, it was ranked 19th in the world for the most visitors. Everland has a zoo and a water park called Caribbean Bay. The park is run by Samsung C&T Corporation, which used to be called Samsung Everland and Cheil Industries. Everland used to be called "Jayeon Nongwon," which means "Natural Farm" in Korean. Its old English name was "Farmland."

Dr. Strangelove, or How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb, is a 1964 movie. It is a funny film that makes fun of the fear of a nuclear war between the Soviet Union and the United States during the Cold War. The film was directed, produced, and co-written by Stanley Kubrick. It stars Peter Sellers, George C. Scott, Sterling Hayden, and Slim Pickens. Filming happened in the United Kingdom. The movie is based on a novel called "Red Alert" by Peter George. The story is about an unstable U.S. air force general who orders a nuclear attack on the Soviet Union. Meanwhile, the U.S. president, his advisors, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and a Royal Air Force officer try to stop the B-52 bomber crew from carrying out the attack. "Dr. Strangelove" is often seen as one of the best comedies ever made and one of the greatest films of all time. In 1998, it was ranked 26th in a list of the best American movies by the American Film Institute. In 2000, it was listed as the third funniest American film. In 1989, the United States Library of Congress added the film to the National Film Registry because it is considered very important.
Warendorf is a district in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, located in the north. It borders the districts of Steinfurt, Osnabrück, Gütersloh, Soest, Hamm, Coesfeld, and Münster.

Frank Cloud Cooksey was born on June 3, 1933. He is an American public servant. In the 1950s, he was the president of the student body at the University of Texas. He worked as an attorney in different places. He was part of the civil rights division of the U.S. District Attorney. He also worked at the Texas Attorney General's office, where John Hill was the attorney general. He had his own law practice. From 1985 to 1988, he was the mayor of Austin, Texas. He is known for being an environmental activist and for his progressive views while mayor.

Zonia Baber, born Mary Arizona Baber on August 24, 1862, in Clark County, Illinois, lived until January 10, 1956. She was an American geographer and geologist. Zonia is famous for creating methods to teach geography. Her teaching focused on learning by doing, using field work and experiments.

José Hugo Garaycoa Hawkins was born on June 2, 1930, in Peru. He became a priest in 1961. From 1982 to 1991, he was the titular bishop of Hora and an auxiliary bishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Lima in Peru. Then, from 1991 to 2006, he served as the bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Tacna y Moquegua in Peru. He passed away on March 27, 2018.

The London, Brighton and South Coast Railway (LB&SCR) was a train company in the UK from 1846 to 1922. It covered a rough triangular area, with London at the top, the entire Sussex coastline as the base, and a large part of Surrey. On its western side, it bordered the London and South Western Railway (L&SWR), which offered an alternative route to Portsmouth. On its eastern side, the LB&SCR bordered the South Eastern Railway (SER), later part of the South Eastern and Chatham Railway (SE&CR), providing an alternative route to towns like Bexhill, St Leonards, and Hastings. The LB&SCR had the most direct paths from London to popular seaside towns like Brighton, Eastbourne, Worthing, Littlehampton, and Bognor Regis, as well as to ports like Newhaven and Shoreham-by-Sea. It also served inland towns such as Chichester, Horsham, East Grinstead, and Lewes, and shared lines with Croydon, Tunbridge Wells, Dorking, and Guildford. The LB&SCR started as five separate companies that merged in 1846. In 1921, under the Railway Act, it merged with the L&SWR, the SE&CR, and several smaller railway companies in southern England to form the Southern Railway, which began operating on January 1, 1923.

The Colombo crime family is one of the five main families that control organized crime in New York City. It started as a bootlegging gang in 1928 led by Joseph Profaci. Profaci ruled the family without problems until the 1950s. During the late 1950s, a war broke out when Joe Gallo revolted against Profaci. This war stopped when Gallo was arrested and Profaci died of cancer. In the early 1960s, Joseph Colombo took control. A second war began in 1971 when Gallo came out of prison and shot Colombo. After Gallo’s crew left for the Genovese family, Colombo’s supporters, led by Carmine Persico, won. The family was peaceful under Persico until 1991. Then, a third war started when Acting Boss Victor Orena tried to take power from the imprisoned Persico. The family split into two groups loyal to Orena and Persico. Two years of fighting ended in 1993 with 12 family members dead and Orena in prison. Persico then ruled the family until 2019. In the 2000s, the family suffered more due to members being convicted and becoming government informants. Many think the Colombo family is the weakest of the five. Carmine Persico died in prison in 2019.

Prunella Margaret Rumney West Scales, born on June 22, 1932, is an English actress. She is famous for playing Sybil, the wife of Basil Fawlty, in the BBC comedy "Fawlty Towers." She was also nominated for a BAFTA award for her role as Queen Elizabeth II in "A Question of Attribution," a Screen One episode on BBC 1 in 1991, written by Alan Bennett.
Beyrie-en-Béarn is a village in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department in southwestern France.

Achim Mentzel was born on July 15, 1946, in Berlin and died on January 4, 2016, in Cottbus. He was a German musician, TV presenter, and actor. He is most famous for hosting "Achim's Hitparade" from 1989 to 2006. He also worked with Oliver Kalkofe on "Kalkofe's Record." He made 23 singles and seven albums between 1978 and 2010. He was part of a cover band called Fritzens Dampferband, which included Nina Hagen. He appeared in films like "The Legend of Paul and Paula" (1973) and "Der Wixxer" (2004), and in TV shows such as "Das Amt" and "Leipzig Homicide." Mentzel got married four times and had eight children.

Age Fridtjof Hareide, born on September 23, 1953, is a Norwegian football manager who recently led the Denmark national team. In his playing career, he played for Hødd and Molde in Norway, and Manchester City and Norwich City in England. Hareide earned 50 caps playing for Norway. As a coach, he won league titles in all Scandinavian countries. He won with Helsingborgs IF in Sweden in 1999 and Malmö FF in 2014. He also won with Brøndby in Denmark in 2001-2002, and Rosenborg in Norway in 2003. Hareide managed the Norway national team from 2003 to 2008.

Arsène Lupin is a fictional gentleman thief and master of disguise created in 1905 by French writer Maurice Leblanc. The character's name was originally Arsène Lopin, but it was changed after a local politician with the same name objected. Leblanc first introduced Lupin in a series of short stories in the magazine "Je Sais Tout" in 1905. The first story, "The Arrest of Arsène Lupin," came out on July 15, 1905. Lupin appeared in 17 novels and 39 novellas by Leblanc, making a total of 24 books. If the 1923 novel "The Secret Tomb" is counted, the total becomes 25 books. In this novel, Lupin does not appear, but the main character, Dorothée, solves one of his secrets. The character has also appeared in books by other writers and been adapted into films, TV shows, stage plays, and comic books. In the 1970s, the mystery writing team Boileau-Narcejac wrote five authorized sequels.

Tuili is a "municipality" in the province of South Sardinia, in the Italian region of Sardinia. It is located north of Cagliari and northeast of Sanluri. Tuili borders the following municipalities: Barumini, Gesturi, Las Plassas, Pauli Arbarei, Setzu, and Turri.

Bussigny-sur-Oron was a former municipality in the district of Lavaux-Oron, in the canton of Vaud, Switzerland. On January 1, 2012, Bussigny-sur-Oron merged with several other municipalities. These municipalities were Châtillens, Chesalles-sur-Oron, Ecoteaux, Oron-la-Ville, Oron-le-Châtel, Palézieux, Les Tavernes, Les Thioleyres, and Vuibroye. After the merger, they formed a new municipality called Oron.

Jack Klugman, born on April 27, 1922, and died on December 24, 2012, was an American actor. He started his career in 1950 and appeared in movies and on TV.
